name: How to Find Diamonds in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Diamond ore generates in the Overworld from Y=16 down to Y=-63 and gets more common the lower you go. Deepslate diamond ore is most common at Y=-58 and Y=-59. Mine it with an iron pickaxe or better; it drops 1 diamond and 3-7 XP.
steps: Craft an iron pickaxe or better: diamond ore needs it to drop anything useful.
Dig down to around Y=-58 or Y=-59, where deepslate diamond ore is most common. Check your Y level with coordinates (F3 in Java).
Branch mine through stone and deepslate to expose as many blocks as you can.

Look near aquifers and lava: ore does not get a reduced chance to generate when exposed to water or lava, so it appears more often on aquifer walls. Some ore blocks have a chance not to generate when next to air.
Mine the ore: it drops 1 diamond and 3-7 XP. Fortune I gives a 1/3 chance of 2 diamonds (average 1.33), Fortune II averages 1.75 and Fortune III averages 2.2.
Silk Touch drops the ore block itself instead of a diamond.
materials: Fortune III pickaxe for best yield (optional)
editionNote: Per the wiki, diamond ore replaces stone, andesite, diorite, granite, tuff and deepslate, and the version that replaces deepslate or tuff becomes deepslate diamond ore. It also appears in fossils below Y=0 as deepslate diamond ore replacing some bone blocks.
versions: Per the Minecraft Wiki Diamond Ore page: current generation features run from Y=16 to Y=-63, with an extra feature from Y=-4 to Y=-63.

faq.q: What is the best Y level for diamonds?
faq.a: Around Y=-58 to Y=-59, where deepslate diamond ore is most common.

faq.q: Do diamonds spawn more near lava?
faq.a: Ore is not less likely to generate when exposed to water or lava, so it shows more on the walls of aquifers. Ore touching air has a chance not to generate.

faq.q: How much does Fortune give?
faq.a: Fortune I averages 1.33 diamonds, Fortune II 1.75 and Fortune III 2.2.

faq.q: What tool do I need?
faq.a: An iron pickaxe or better.

keywords: how to find diamonds best y level diamond mining

name: How to Make a Nether Portal in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Build a vertical frame of obsidian at least 4 blocks wide and 5 blocks tall (10 obsidian minimum, corners optional) and light the inside with flint and steel. A full frame with corners uses 14 obsidian.
steps: Get obsidian: pour water over lava source blocks, then mine it with a diamond or netherite pickaxe. You need 10 (economy frame) or 14 (full frame).
Build the frame upright: two obsidian columns 3 blocks tall, joined by 2 obsidian at the top and 2 at the bottom. Interior space: 2x3.
Corners are optional - leave them empty to save 4 obsidian.

Light it: fire placed inside the frame activates it, for example with flint and steel or a fire charge. A fireball, a lightning strike or fire spreading to flammable material next to the portal also works. Portals cannot be activated in the End.
The interior fills with portal blocks. Stand inside for 80 game ticks (4 seconds) in Survival, or 1 tick in Creative, to teleport.
No diamond pickaxe? Cast the portal in place: make a mold, place lava source blocks where the frame goes, then pour water on each to turn them into obsidian one by one.
materials: Diamond/netherite pickaxe OR water bucket + lava for casting
editionNote: The wiki gives a 4x5 minimum and a 23x23 maximum frame, and the four corners are not required. Portals the game creates always include the corners. In Java Edition the teleport delay can be changed with the gamerules playersNetherPortalDefaultDelay and playersNetherPortalCreativeDelay.
versions: Per the Minecraft Wiki Nether Portal page: frame limits of 4x5 minimum and 23x23 maximum were introduced in a past update, and the portal delay gamerules arrived in 1.20.3 (23w42a).

faq.q: How much obsidian do you need for a nether portal?
faq.a: 10 blocks minimum if you skip the four corners, or 14 for the complete 4x5 frame.

faq.q: Why won't my nether portal light?
faq.a: Check the frame is complete obsidian with a 2x3 empty interior, that you are not in the End (portals cannot be activated there), and that fire is placed inside the frame.

faq.q: How do portals link between dimensions?
faq.a: Each Overworld block equals 8 Nether blocks on X and Z. A portal at Overworld 800, 64, 800 links near Nether 100, ~64, 100. Y is not scaled.

keywords: nether portal how to make obsidian flint steel

name: How to Find an Ancient City in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Ancient cities only generate in the deep dark biome, with the city floor at Y=-51. The deep dark forms deep underground beneath low-erosion areas such as mountains. Look for sculk, or use a "buried ancient city" explorer map from a secret chest in an abandoned camp.
steps: Prepare: bring lots of wool, food, light and good gear. The deep dark has no regular mob spawning, but the warden can appear.
Go deep: the city floor is always at Y=-51. Because ancient cities only generate in the deep dark, they are often found under mountains and other low-erosion areas.
Recognize the biome: it is covered in sculk, and the only natural light comes from sculk catalysts and lava.
Move quietly: sneaking prevents vibrations while you move, and wool or carpet placed between a sculk sensor and a vibration source blocks it. The city corridors have wool floors for this reason.

Avoid sculk shriekers: each one you trigger raises your warning level, and at level 4 the shrieker tries to summon a warden. Naturally generated shriekers are much more common in ancient cities. Each shrieker has a 10-second cooldown per player.
Loot the chests: the wiki says ancient cities hold disc fragments, armor trims and echo shards that cannot be found anywhere else.
Alternative: a "buried ancient city" explorer map, found in secret chests in abandoned camps, can lead you to one.
materials: Lots of wool blocks or carpets
Good armor and weapons (in case a warden appears)
Optional: a buried ancient city explorer map
editionNote: Both editions generate ancient cities only in the deep dark at Y=-51. In Bedrock Edition a warden summoned by a shrieker gets the emerging spawn event so it plays its emerging animation.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.q: What Y level are ancient cities at?
faq.a: The city floor always generates at Y=-51 and the structure is about 20 blocks high, with a footprint of around 220 blocks on each horizontal axis.

faq.q: How many shrieks summon the Warden?
faq.a: When a player's warning level reaches 4, the shrieker tries to summon a warden after it finishes shrieking, up to 20 attempts within an 11x13x11 box. If no other warden is within 24 blocks, one emerges from the ground.

faq.q: Is it worth looting an ancient city?
faq.a: The wiki lists disc fragments, armor trims and echo shards as items that cannot be found anywhere else. Ancient cities are also one of only two places where sculk generates.

faq.q: Do shriekers I place summon wardens?
faq.a: No. Only naturally generated shriekers can summon wardens. Shriekers placed by players or made by sculk catalysts are inert.

keywords: ancient city deep dark how to find Y=-51 warden sculk shrieker echo shard

name: How to Breed Villagers in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Villagers breed when they are willing and an unclaimed bed with at least 2 empty blocks above it is reachable. A villager becomes willing with 3 bread, 12 carrots, 12 potatoes or 12 beetroots in one inventory slot. Throw food at two villagers and wait.
steps: Enclose the area so villagers cannot wander off or be killed. Job sites are not required for breeding.

Place beds with at least 2 empty blocks above each. Slabs, trapdoors and similar blocks above a bed invalidate it, because mobs treat them as full blocks for pathfinding. Each baby needs a free bed the villager can reach.

Make them willing: throw bread, carrots, potatoes or beetroots at the villagers. They need 3 bread or 12 of the others in one slot. Villagers with spare food, usually farmers, also throw food to others.
Wait. Two willing villagers nearby breed and a baby appears. Becoming willing uses up the food even if no baby is born.
After breeding, villagers stop being willing for 5 minutes until they gather enough food again.
A baby villager becomes an adult 20 minutes after birth.
materials: Beds, with 2 empty blocks above each
editionNote: Java: breeding fails if no unclaimed bed can be reached by pathfinding within 48 blocks, and beds must be within village bounds. Bedrock: a periodic census of the village population decides whether mating continues, and the child's appearance depends on the biome where breeding happens.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.q: Why won't my villagers breed?
faq.a: The usual causes on the wiki: no unclaimed bed they can pathfind to, a bed with a block (like a slab or trapdoor) less than 2 blocks above, not enough food, or the mobGriefing gamerule set to false, which stops villagers picking up food.

faq.q: What food makes villagers willing to breed?
faq.a: 3 bread, 12 carrots, 12 potatoes or 12 beetroots in one slot of the villager's inventory. Throw it at them so they pick it up. The food is used up when they become willing.

faq.q: How often can villagers breed?
faq.a: After a successful breeding, they stop being willing for 5 minutes, until they gather enough food again.

keywords: how to breed villagers beds food willing bread carrots potatoes beetroots

name: How to Get Elytra in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Elytra come only from End ships: beat the dragon, pearl through an End gateway to the outer islands, find an End city with a ship floating beside it, and take the elytra from the item frame in the ship's treasure room.
steps: Defeat the Ender Dragon and enter an End gateway with an ender pearl.
Search the outer islands for an End city.
Look for the End ship, a boat-shaped structure floating beside some cities; cities without a ship have no elytra.
Board the ship via the tower bridge or by throwing an ender pearl.
Fight the shulker guarding the treasure room inside the hull.
Take the elytra from the item frame on the wall, and grab the dragon head from the bow.
materials: Slow falling potions or water bucket
Food and armor for shulker fights
Ender chest to bank the elytra safely
editionNote: Elytra cannot be crafted; the End ship item frame is the only source in Java and Bedrock. Each ship holds exactly one pair. Equip them in the chestplate slot, jump, and press jump again midair to glide; firework rockets boost flight. Repair elytra with phantom membranes on an anvil (or two damaged pairs combined), and put Mending and Unbreaking III on them immediately, because a broken pair is gone until you find another ship.

faq.q: Can you craft elytra in Minecraft?
faq.a: No. Elytra are found only in an item frame inside End ships on the outer End islands, one pair per ship. There is no recipe and no villager trade.

faq.q: Why does the End city I found have no elytra?
faq.a: Only End cities with an End ship floating beside them hold elytra. If your city has no ship, keep searching other cities across the outer islands.

faq.q: How do you fly with elytra?
faq.a: Equip them in the chest slot, jump from height, and press jump again while falling to open the wings. Look up to trade speed for altitude, and use firework rockets (without stars) for thrust.

faq.q: How do you repair elytra in Minecraft?
faq.a: Combine them with phantom membranes on an anvil, or combine two damaged pairs. The cheap long-term answer is Mending plus Unbreaking III, applied before the first pair wears down.

name: How to Enchant in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft an enchanting table (book + diamonds + obsidian), put an item that is not already enchanted in it with lapis lazuli, and pick one of three offers. Surround the table with 15 bookshelves, each with one block of air or a replaceable block between it and the table, to unlock level 30 offers. A level 30 offer charges only 3 levels and 3 lapis.
steps: Craft an enchanting table from a book, diamonds and obsidian.

Build the library: bookshelves go next to the table with one block of air (or a replaceable block like snow or grass) between them. Most other blocks, even torches, stop a bookshelf from connecting. A 1-block-high square of bookshelves with an empty space on the perimeter is the simple layout. 15 bookshelves are needed for level 30 enchantments.
Get lapis lazuli and experience levels. You need at least the level requirement of the offer.
Open the table, put the item in the item slot and lapis in the lapis slot. Three offers appear. Hover over one to see one of its enchantments.
Pick an offer. You are charged levels and lapis equal to its lapis requirement: a level 30 offer needs 30 levels but costs only 3 levels and 3 lapis.
To refresh the offers, enchant anything: it changes your enchantment seed, so the possible enchantments change. The wiki suggests spending 1 lapis and 1 level on a book or another item.
Treasure enchantments (such as Mending) are not available at the table. Use an anvil and enchanted books for exact enchantments.
materials: Lapis lazuli (3 at most per enchantment)
Anvil and enchanted books for targeted enchantments
editionNote: The wiki's enchanting pages describe the same table, bookshelf limit and 3-offer system for both editions. Naming the table in an anvil changes the GUI title; the /data CustomName route is Java only.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.q: How many bookshelves do I need for level 30 enchantments?
faq.a: 15 bookshelves, each with one block of air or a replaceable block between it and the table. Most other blocks, even torches, break the connection.

faq.q: Why can't I get Mending from the enchanting table?
faq.a: Mending is a treasure enchantment, and treasure enchantments cannot be obtained through an enchanting table.

faq.q: How do I reroll the offers?
faq.a: Enchanting any item changes your enchantment seed and the possible enchantments. The wiki suggests spending 1 lapis and 1 level on a book or another item to refresh the list.

faq.q: Can I enchant an item that is already enchanted?
faq.a: No. The table only enchants items that are not already enchanted.

keywords: how to enchant minecraft enchanting table bookshelves level 30 lapis lazuli reroll

name: How to Make an Iron Golem in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Place 4 blocks of iron in a T shape (3 across the top, 1 below the middle one) and put a carved pumpkin or jack o'lantern on top of the center upper block, last. An iron golem with 100 HP appears. A player-built golem is passive toward players and attacks hostile mobs.
steps: Craft 4 blocks of iron (36 iron ingots) and get a carved pumpkin (shear a pumpkin) or a jack o'lantern.
Place 3 iron blocks in a row, then 1 more below the middle block, forming a T.

Place the carved pumpkin or jack o'lantern on the center upper block. It must go last (a dispenser or an enderman can place it too). Alternatively, place an uncarved pumpkin and shear it to spawn the golem.
The iron golem appears: 100 HP at full health. It attacks hostile mobs and knocks them into the air, and never directly attacks you.
To heal it, use an iron ingot on it: each ingot restores 25 HP. Cracks show its health: none at 75% or more, then more cracks below 75%, 50% and 25%.
You can put a lead on it to move it. It drops 3-5 iron ingots and 0-2 poppies when killed.
editionNote: Same T-shaped build in Java and Bedrock. Differences on the wiki: villages spawn golems by different rules (Java: villagers summon them when gossiping or panicking; Bedrock: villages with at least 20 beds and 10 villagers), and the hitbox is 2.7 blocks tall in Java and 2.9 in Bedrock.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.q: Why won't my iron golem spawn?
faq.a: Check that you built a T of exactly 4 iron blocks and that the carved pumpkin or jack o'lantern is the last block placed, on top of the center upper block.

faq.q: Will a golem I build attack me?
faq.a: No. A player-built iron golem is passive toward players and never directly attacks you. It attacks hostile mobs. Naturally spawned golems are neutral and retaliate if attacked, and are hostile to players with low village popularity.

faq.q: How do I heal an iron golem?
faq.a: Use an iron ingot on it. Each ingot heals 25 HP and is consumed.

keywords: how to make iron golem build iron blocks pumpkin T shape heal iron ingot

name: How to Beat the Wither in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Build the Wither with 4 soul sand or soul soil in a T shape and 3 wither skeleton skulls on top (place a skull last). After its charge-up it explodes, then fights. It has 300 HP in Java (Bedrock: 300 Easy, 450 Normal, 600 Hard), becomes immune to arrows at half health, and always drops one nether star.
steps: Get 3 wither skeleton skulls and 4 blocks of soul sand or soul soil. Soul soil can be used interchangeably with soul sand.
Choose an arena with air on both sides of the base block. The structure can be built upright, lying down or upside-down, and the skull orientation does not matter.
Build the T of 4 soul sand/soil blocks, then place the 3 skulls on the three upper blocks. The last block placed must be a skull.
The Wither is invulnerable and does not move or attack during its charge-up (about 11 seconds), then makes a large explosion centered on itself. Stay far away until it ends.

It flies about 5 blocks above its target and fires black skulls, and sometimes blue ones. Skulls deal 5 HP on Easy, 8 on Normal and 12 on Hard, and cause the Wither effect on Normal and Hard. Milk cures the Wither effect.
At half health it crashes into the ground in a large explosion, spawns 3 wither skeletons (not on Easy), and gains wither armor that makes it immune to arrows. Use melee from then on.
Kill it to get 1 nether star, needed to craft beacons. The Wither also drops 50 XP (Java: only when killed by a player or tamed wolf).
materials: Milk to cure the Wither effect
A melee weapon (arrows stop working at half health)
editionNote: Health: Java 300 HP at all difficulties; Bedrock 300 / 450 / 600 HP on Easy / Normal / Hard. Bedrock only: dash attacks, and the blue skull can be deflected by hitting it. Java: nether star despawns after 10 minutes; Bedrock: it never despawns.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.q: When is the Wither immune to arrows?
faq.a: Below half health, when it gains wither armor. The wiki notes it keeps this armor if it regenerates above half health.

faq.q: What does the Wither drop?
faq.a: One nether star every time (100%), plus 50 XP. In Java the XP only drops when a player or tamed wolf kills it; in Bedrock it always drops.

faq.q: How do I cure the Wither effect?
faq.a: Drink milk. On Easy difficulty the Wither does not inflict the effect at all.

faq.q: Can I spawn it in an enclosed space?
faq.a: It needs air blocks on either side of the base soul sand/soil. Remember its spawn explosion and its half-health dash can destroy the blocks around it.

keywords: beat wither boss fight nether star wither skeleton skull soul sand T shape wither armor

name: How to Find an End City in Minecraft
quickAnswer: End cities generate on the large outer islands of the End, in the midlands and highlands, where chorus trees grow. You reach the outer islands through an End gateway. Only End ships, found at some cities, contain elytra and dragon heads.
steps: Reach the outer End islands: End cities are easily accessed by entering the End gateway. If it drops you on a small island, build, use an elytra or throw ender pearls to reach the nearest large island.
Look on the large islands where chorus trees grow. End cities usually generate in flat midlands or highlands areas.
Search in a grid: End cities only generate in chunks numbered 0-8 plus or minus a multiple of 20. You may find several clustered together or travel thousands of blocks without finding one.
Spot the towers: they are tall skyscrapers of end stone bricks and purpur blocks, lit only by end rods and ender chests, and guarded by many shulkers.

Loot the rooms: loot rooms have two chests with valuable loot at the end of a small parkour area, and some have one normal chest next to an ender chest. Loot includes enchanted iron and diamond tools, weapons and armor.

Check for an End ship: each tower direction has a 50% chance of a bridge, and each bridge has a 12.5% chance of an End ship, with at most one ship per city. The ship holds an elytra in an item frame and a dragon head, and three shulkers spawn on it.
materials: Slow Falling potions or water bucket
editionNote: The wiki lists the End Midlands and End Highlands biomes for Java Edition and the End biome for Bedrock Edition.
versions: Per the Minecraft Wiki End City page.

faq.q: How rare are End cities?
faq.a: You may find several clustered together or travel thousands of blocks before finding one. They generate on a noticeable grid in chunks numbered 0-8 plus or minus a multiple of 20.

faq.q: Does every End city have an elytra?
faq.a: No. Only End ships contain elytra, and each bridge has a 12.5% chance of one, with at most one ship per city.

faq.q: What can I find in an End city?
faq.a: Enchanted iron and diamond tools, weapons and armor, shulkers and, in End ships, elytra and dragon heads.

faq.q: What lights an End city?
faq.a: End rods and ender chests are the only light sources.

keywords: end city find elytra end ship gateway shulker outer islands

name: How to Make and Use a Beacon in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft a beacon from glass, a nether star and obsidian. Place it on a pyramid of 1 to 4 layers of iron, gold, emerald, diamond or netherite blocks (9 to 164 blocks), then feed it one iron ingot, gold ingot, emerald, diamond or netherite ingot to pick its powers.
steps: Get a nether star and craft the beacon with glass, a nether star and obsidian.
Build the pyramid: layer 1 is 3x3 (9 blocks), a 3-layer pyramid is 7x7, 5x5, 3x3 (83 blocks), and a 4-layer pyramid is 9x9, 7x7, 5x5, 3x3 (164 blocks, 1,476 ingots or gems). The beacon sits on top.
Use iron, gold, emerald, diamond or netherite blocks, alone or mixed. The block type is purely cosmetic.
Keep the beam clear: it deactivates if it intersects any fully opaque block, except bedrock. Stained glass above the beacon colors the beam.
Right-click the beacon, place one iron ingot, gold ingot, emerald, diamond or netherite ingot, pick a Primary Power and confirm. Which item you feed does not matter.
Powers: Resistance and Jump Boost need a 2-layer pyramid, Strength needs 3 layers. On a 4-layer pyramid you can also pick a Secondary Power: Regeneration, or raise the primary power to level II.
If the pyramid breaks, the chosen power returns when you rebuild it, with no new item needed.
materials: 164 mineral blocks for a max pyramid (iron recommended)
editionNote: Per the wiki, a beacon beam is visible from any loaded chunk: up to 512 blocks in Java Edition and 2048 blocks in Bedrock Edition. In Bedrock Edition the beam updates every 80 ticks (4 seconds). In Java Edition another beacon above can change the beam color.
versions: Per the Minecraft Wiki Beacon page.

faq.q: How many blocks do you need for a full beacon?
faq.a: 164 blocks for a 4-layer pyramid, which is 1,476 ingots or gems.

faq.q: Do different pyramid materials give better effects?
faq.a: No. The block type is cosmetic, and you can mix iron, gold, emerald, diamond and netherite blocks.

faq.q: Why is my beacon not working?
faq.a: Its beam is probably blocked by a fully opaque block above it, or the pyramid is incomplete.

faq.q: What do I feed a beacon?
faq.a: One iron ingot, gold ingot, emerald, diamond or netherite ingot. It does not matter which.

keywords: beacon pyramid powers haste speed regeneration nether star

name: How to Make and Use a Conduit in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft 1 conduit with 1 heart of the sea surrounded by 8 nautilus shells. Waterlog it at the center of a 3 by 3 by 3 water volume, then add 16-42 full prismarine-family blocks or sea lanterns in valid frame positions. Its player-effect radius is 32-96 blocks; only a complete 42-block frame attacks wet hostile mobs within 8 blocks.
steps: Get a heart of the sea: it is found only in buried treasure chests, whose location is marked with a red X on a buried treasure map from ocean ruins and shipwrecks.
Get nautilus shells: drowned holding one always drop it (3% in Java, 8% in Bedrock), nautiluses rarely drop it, and you can fish it up.
Craft 1 conduit: place 1 heart of the sea in the center of a crafting table and 1 nautilus shell in each of the 8 surrounding slots.
Place the conduit in the center of a 3x3x3 volume of water (the conduit waterlogged too), enclosed by a frame of three 5x5 open squares, one around each axis.

Use full prismarine, dark prismarine, prismarine bricks or sea lantern blocks in valid frame positions. Slabs, stairs and walls do not count. At least 16 blocks activate a 32-block radius; the complete frame has 42.
Range grows 16 blocks for every 7 frame blocks: 48 at 21, 64 at 28, 80 at 35 and 96 with all 42. A lit orange iris shows when the frame is complete.
Conduit Power works on players touching water or rain, with the benefits of Water Breathing, Night Vision and Haste (it does not stack with them).
A complete frame attacks one hostile mob at a time within 8 blocks, such as drowned, guardians and elder guardians, for 4 HP magic damage every 2 seconds if the mob touches water or rain.
materials: 16-42 prismarine / sea lantern / dark prismarine blocks
editionNote: Drowned spawn holding a nautilus shell 3% of the time in Java Edition and 8% in Bedrock Edition. In Bedrock Edition zombies converted into drowned count too.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.q: Where do you find a heart of the sea?
faq.a: Only in buried treasure chests. A buried treasure map from ocean ruins or shipwrecks marks the spot with a red X.

faq.q: How big is the conduit range?
faq.a: The effect has a spherical radius of 32 blocks with 16 frame blocks, 48 with 21, 64 with 28, 80 with 35 and 96 with all 42. Fewer than 16 valid frame blocks do not activate it.

faq.q: Do conduits work out of water?
faq.a: Conduit Power only affects players in contact with water or rain, and the conduit must sit in water inside its frame.

faq.q: Which blocks count for the frame?
faq.a: Full prismarine, dark prismarine, prismarine bricks and sea lantern blocks in valid frame positions. Prismarine slabs, stairs and walls do not count, and blocks outside the frame positions do not increase its range.

keywords: conduit heart of the sea nautilus shell underwater breathing prismarine frame

name: How to Build a Villager Trading Hall
quickAnswer: Give each adult unemployed villager a job site block, check its offers before trading, and trade once to lock its profession and offers. Keep access to the claimed workstation for restocking. Curing can reduce prices, but does not guarantee 1-emerald trades, and repeated cures do not add discounts.
steps: Choose a secure site and bring adult unemployed villagers. A breeder is optional; protect the hall from zombies and leave room to expand.
Build separate trading spaces with a walkway for the player. Each villager must be able to work at its claimed job site block. Test the first cell before repeating the design.

Assign professions: lectern for librarian, composter for farmer, blast furnace for armorer, smithing table for toolsmith, grindstone for weaponsmith, fletching table for fletcher, cartography table for cartographer or stonecutter for mason.
Check offers before trading. For an untraded novice, remove and replace its claimed job site block to change the offers. Nitwits and baby villagers cannot take jobs.
Trade once when you want to keep the offers. That villager keeps its profession and offers even if you remove the workstation later, but needs its workstation to restock.
Check restocking: villagers can replenish trades up to twice per day while working. In Bedrock, keep the villagers linked to beds as well; they do not need to sleep to restock.

Optional curing supplies: a splash Potion of Weakness and 1 golden apple. Craft 1 golden apple with 1 apple in the center of a crafting table and 8 gold ingots in the surrounding slots. A fermented spider eye uses 1 spider eye, 1 brown mushroom and 1 sugar in any arrangement.

If converting your own villager, check difficulty first: death from a zombie converts it on Hard (100%) or sometimes on Normal (50%); on Easy it dies instead. Keep the zombie isolated from the rest of the hall.
Cure a zombie villager by giving it Weakness, then using a golden apple on it. Protect it from sunlight and other threats while it converts. Keep the curing setup separate from other villagers.
Do not repeat zombification to stack discounts. Current curing gives no extra discount for curing the same villager again, and prices can still vary with demand and reputation.
Keep the hall lit and enclosed. Move unwanted traders elsewhere rather than building a killing route; attacking villagers harms your reputation.
materials: Job site blocks for the professions you want
Optional: splash Potions of Weakness and golden apples
editionNote: Villagers need access to their claimed job site blocks to restock in both editions. Bedrock also requires a bed link, not sleep; Java does not require beds for trading and restocking. Repeated cures do not add discounts in current releases.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.q: How do you get Mending from villagers?
faq.a: Check librarian book offers before trading. In standard trading, you can reroll an untraded librarian by removing and replacing its lectern until it offers Mending, then trade once to keep the offers. Curing does not guarantee a 1-emerald price. Experimental trade-rebalance worlds use different book rules.

faq.q: Why won't my villager take a profession?
faq.a: It cannot pathfind to the workstation, or it already locked a profession by trading. Break the old workstation, place the new one within reach, and never trade before you like the offers. Nitwits (green coats) never take jobs.

faq.q: Do villagers need beds to trade?
faq.a: Java villagers do not need beds to trade or restock. In Bedrock, villagers need a bed link to restock, though they do not need to sleep. Both editions require access to the claimed workstation for restocking.

faq.q: How do I reroll a villager's trades?
faq.a: Break its job site block and place it back - as long as you have never traded with that villager, it loses and reclaims the profession with fresh offers. Once you trade even once, the trades are locked forever, so reroll first, trade after.

faq.q: Why did my villager lose its profession?
faq.a: It lost access to its claimed job site block - broken, moved or blocked. If it has never traded, it simply becomes unemployed and can claim a new station. A traded villager keeps its profession even without a station, but cannot restock.

faq.q: Is killing bad traders bad for me?
faq.a: Attacking or killing villagers harms your reputation. Move traders you do not want to another safe area instead. Do not assume a low price will stay fixed: demand and reputation affect prices.

keywords: trading hall villager cure zombie weakness mending librarian 1 emerald discount

name: How to Upgrade to Netherite
quickAnswer: Mine ancient debris in the Nether (most common around Y=16) with a diamond or netherite pickaxe, smelt it into netherite scrap, craft 4 scrap + 4 gold ingots into a netherite ingot, then upgrade diamond gear at a smithing table with a Netherite Upgrade template. Enchantments, name and durability use are kept.
steps: Mine ancient debris with a diamond or netherite pickaxe: other tools drop nothing. It replaces netherrack, plus basalt and blackstone in Java. Generation avoids air exposure, although later generation can occasionally expose it.

Search around Y=16. Java attempts one cluster of 0-3 debris between Y=8 and Y=24 and another of 0-2 between Y=8 and Y=119. Bedrock attempts two clusters of 0-3 between Y=8 and Y=23 and three of 0-2 between Y=8 and Y=119.
Smelt the ancient debris into netherite scrap.
Craft 1 netherite ingot from 4 netherite scrap and 4 gold ingots in a crafting table. This recipe is shapeless, so any arrangement works.
Find a Netherite Upgrade smithing template in a bastion remnant: the treasure chest always holds one (100%), and bridge, hoglin stable and generic chests have a 10% chance.

Duplicate a template before using your last one: put 1 Netherite Upgrade template in the top-center slot, 1 netherrack in the center and 7 diamonds in all remaining slots. This produces 2 templates, consuming the original, for a net gain of 1.

At a smithing table put 1 Netherite Upgrade template on the left, 1 diamond item in the middle and 1 netherite ingot on the right. The upgrade consumes the template and ingot. It costs no experience and keeps enchantments, custom names and the number of durability points already lost.
materials: 4 ancient debris + 4 gold ingots per netherite ingot
For each duplication: 1 existing template, 7 diamonds and 1 netherrack
Smithing table and furnace or blast furnace
Fire resistance potions for Nether exploration
editionNote: Ancient debris cluster generation differs: Java attempts up to two clusters per chunk and Bedrock up to five. Only Java replaces basalt and blackstone as well as netherrack.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.q: What is the best Y level for ancient debris?
faq.a: Y=16 has the most on average. Clusters generate between Y=8 and Y=24, plus a smaller chance up to Y=119.

faq.q: Do enchantments transfer to netherite?
faq.a: Yes. A smithing table upgrade preserves enchantments, custom names and durability use, and costs no experience.

faq.q: Where is the Netherite Upgrade template?
faq.a: In bastion remnant chests. The treasure chest always has one; other chests have a 10% chance.

faq.q: Does ancient debris survive explosions?
faq.a: Yes. Its blast resistance of 1,200 makes it immune to normal explosions.

keywords: netherite upgrade smithing template ancient debris y15 bastion armor

name: How to Do Archaeology in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft a brush (feather + copper ingot + stick) and use it on suspicious sand (desert temples, wells, warm ocean ruins) or suspicious gravel (trail ruins, cold ocean ruins) - brushing slowly reveals pottery sherds, armor trims, sniffer eggs and loot instead of breaking the block.
steps: Craft 1 brush: put 1 feather at the top, 1 copper ingot in the middle and 1 stick at the bottom of one vertical column in a crafting table.

Learn the sites: suspicious sand generates in desert pyramids, desert wells and warm ocean ruins; suspicious gravel generates in trail ruins and cold ocean ruins. Trial chambers contain decorated pots with some sherd patterns, not a suspicious-gravel excavation site.

Excavate carefully around suspicious blocks: mining, explosions or a fall can destroy their loot. Keep a supporting block below them and use the brush rather than a shovel on the suspicious block itself.

Hold the use button with the brush on a suspicious block for 4.8 seconds (96 game ticks). The item emerges and the block becomes normal sand or gravel. Stopping too soon lets the excavation progress fade.
Warm ocean ruins: brush suspicious sand for a 1 in 15 chance of a sniffer egg per block. Place the egg on a moss block for a 10-minute hatch time; other blocks take 20 minutes.
Trail ruins: brush suspicious gravel for exclusive pottery sherds and 4 armor trims (Host, Raiser, Shaper, Wayfinder).
Cold ocean ruins: suspicious gravel gives sherds and loot; watch for drowned.

Collect pottery sherds: there are 23 patterns, including 3 from decorated pots in trial chambers. Craft a decorated pot from any combination of 4 sherds or bricks, arranged in a diamond in a crafting table.
materials: Shovel for normal blocks around the suspicious ones
editionNote: Archaeology sites and the 4.8-second brushing time apply in both editions. Brush durability differs: 64 in Java and 65 in Bedrock. Mining a suspicious block destroys its loot in either edition.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.q: How do you get a sniffer egg?
faq.a: Brush suspicious sand in warm ocean ruins: each block has a 1 in 15 chance of containing a sniffer egg. An egg hatches in 10 minutes on a moss block or 20 minutes on other blocks, including pale moss.

faq.q: What happens if you mine suspicious sand?
faq.a: Mining destroys the loot, even with Silk Touch. Brush the block instead, and keep it supported so it does not fall.

faq.q: How many pottery sherds are there?
faq.a: There are 23 pottery sherd patterns. Archaeology provides 20; the Flow, Guster and Scrape patterns come from decorated pots in trial chambers. Any combination of 4 sherds or bricks makes a decorated pot.

keywords: archaeology brush suspicious sand gravel sniffer egg pottery sherds armor trim

name: How to Beat the Ender Dragon in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Enter the End through a stronghold portal with a bow, plenty of arrows, slow falling potions and a water bucket. Destroy the 10 End Crystals on the obsidian pillars first (some are caged in iron bars), then hit the dragon when it perches over the exit fountain. Avoid its breath clouds and collect the experience and the dragon egg when it dies.
steps: Gear up: full diamond or netherite armor (Protection IV ideal), a Power bow with 2+ stacks of arrows (or Infinity), a strong sword, slow falling potions, a water bucket, food, ender pearls and 2-3 stacks of blocks. A carved pumpkin on your head prevents Enderman aggro but limits vision.
Find and activate the End portal in a stronghold (see the stronghold guide), and consider setting your spawn at a bed nearby before jumping in.
On arrival you may spawn in an obsidian room inside the island: dig up and out. Do not look at Endermen.

Destroy the End Crystals on top of the obsidian pillars: shoot them with the bow. Some pillars cage their crystal in iron bars - pillar up with blocks and break the bars, or shoot through the gap at the base.
While circling, dodge the dragon's charges and never stand in the purple breath clouds (bottle them for Dragon's Breath instead).
When the dragon flies to the exit fountain and perches, run in and hit its head with your sword (or detonate beds next to it, speedrun style: beds explode in the End and deal massive damage).
Repeat bow phase and perch phase until it dies: it explodes into 12,000 XP (first kill), opens the exit portal, spawns the dragon egg and activates an End gateway to the outer islands.
editionNote: The fight is the same on Java and Bedrock: 10 crystals, the same perch cycle and the same breath attack, and beds explode in the End on both. On Bedrock the dragon's direct hits knock you around harder, so Slow Falling matters even more. Respawning the dragon with 4 End Crystals on the fountain works identically on both.
versions: The current fight (circling dragon, perches, breath attack) has been in place since 1.9 and is unchanged in current versions. Current as of 26.3.

faq.q: How do you respawn the Ender Dragon?
faq.a: Craft 4 End Crystals (7 glass + 1 eye of ender + 1 ghast tear each) and place one on each side of the exit fountain. The dragon respawns and the crystals on the pillars regenerate. Later kills give only 500 XP and no new egg.

faq.q: Why should I bring beds to the dragon fight?
faq.a: Beds explode when you try to sleep in the End. Detonating a bed next to the perched dragon's head is the fastest way to kill it, but the blast hurts you too - block partially behind the fountain and wear blast protection.

faq.q: What do you get for killing the Ender Dragon?
faq.a: 12,000 XP (first kill), the dragon egg (one per world), access to the End gateway portals leading to the outer islands, End cities and Elytra, plus the Free the End advancement.

keywords: ender dragon kill beat boss end crystals perch bed explode respawn

name: How to Find a Stronghold in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft Eyes of Ender (blaze powder + ender pearls) and throw them: each flies about 12 blocks toward the nearest stronghold. Follow the throws until the eye travels downward instead of up - then you are above the stronghold, so dig down. The End portal room has a silverfish spawner and a ring of 12 frames that all need an eye.
steps: Craft Eyes of Ender from Ender Pearls (dropped by Endermen) and Blaze Powder (from Blaze Rods). Bring plenty: you need 12 for the frame minus any that are pre-filled, plus spares for the search.
Throw an eye (use). It flies about 12 blocks toward the nearest stronghold, then either falls to be picked up again (80%) or shatters (20%).
Walk in that direction and throw again. While you are more than 12 blocks from the stronghold's start chunk corner the eye rises; when you are closer than that it travels downward.
To triangulate, throw from two far-apart spots, note the direction each time, and head to where the two lines cross.
When the eye goes down, you are above a stronghold. Dig down carefully with a staircase and light your way - strongholds generate at any Y level and can be cut into by caves or other structures.

Find the End portal room: the frames sit in a 5x5 ring (3 per side, no corners) over a lava pool, with a staircase holding a silverfish monster spawner. Each frame has a 10% chance of already holding an eye; use eyes on the empty ones until all 12 are filled.
materials: 12-15 Eyes of Ender (pearls + blaze powder), plus spares for the portal
Pickaxe and torches for the dig
editionNote: Java Edition: every world has exactly 128 strongholds in 8 rings around the origin; the first ring has 3 strongholds between 1,280 and 2,816 blocks from the origin. Bedrock Edition: strongholds generate at least 160 blocks from the origin with no fixed limit, plus 3 extra ones at least 453 blocks away.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.q: Why did my Eye of Ender go down into the ground?
faq.a: Within about 12 blocks of the corner of the stronghold's starting chunk, the eye travels downward instead of up. That means you are above the stronghold: dig down and explore, since the portal room can be several rooms away from the start.

faq.q: Can a stronghold lack a working End portal?
faq.a: Most of a stronghold can be overwritten by caves, mineshafts, ancient cities, trial chambers and other features. It is rare for the End portal to be replaced, but if it happens you need to find another stronghold, because a portal only works with all 12 frames present.

faq.q: How many Eyes of Ender do I need?
faq.a: The portal needs 12 eyes in total, and each frame has a 10% chance of coming pre-filled, so expect to supply about 11. Each throw has a 20% chance to shatter the eye, so carry extras for the search.

keywords: find stronghold eye of ender end portal frame triangulate silverfish spawner 128 strongholds

name: How to Fly with Elytra in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Wear the Elytra in the chestplate slot, then press jump while in mid-air to spread the wings. Aim down to gain speed and up to lose it, and use firework rockets while gliding to boost. Each second of gliding costs 1 durability, and a pair has 432 (7 minutes 12 seconds).
steps: Get an Elytra: it is found in an End ship's item frame, in an End city in the outer End islands, guarded by a shulker. Equip it in the chestplate slot (you give up chest armor).
Jump off a height and press jump again while in mid-air. The wings open and you glide. You steer by turning; moving your aim up and down changes pitch.
Losing altitude increases speed and gaining altitude decreases it. Sharp turns lose speed quickly.
For the longest cruise without rockets, aim straight at the horizon: the wiki gives about 10.06 blocks traveled horizontally per block of starting altitude.

Use a firework rocket while gliding to be pushed in the direction you face. Rockets with firework stars explode at the end of their flight and can damage you, so use rockets without stars for flying. Rockets do not use up elytra durability.

Land carefully: hitting a wall at high speed deals kinetic damage ("experienced kinetic energy"), while hitting a ceiling does not. Landing at an angle steeper than about 50 degrees can cause fall damage.

Repair in an anvil with phantom membranes (each restores 25% of durability, 108 points) or combine two pairs. You cannot enchant elytra at an enchanting table, but an anvil can add Unbreaking or Mending.
materials: Phantom membranes and an anvil for repairs
Optional: Unbreaking or Mending books (applied at an anvil)
editionNote: Gliding, pitch and rockets work in both editions. Bedrock differences on the wiki: touching water or vines stops flight, pressing jump mid-flight cancels it, and in Creative (or with the mayfly ability) you can hold jump to fly up while gliding.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.q: Why do fireworks hurt me while I fly?
faq.a: A rocket with firework stars explodes at the end of its flight and damages you based on the number of stars. Use rockets without stars for boosting.

faq.q: Can elytra break permanently?
faq.a: No. When durability reaches 1 they stop working (tattered texture) until repaired, but they never fully break. Repair with phantom membranes in an anvil or combine two pairs.

faq.q: How long do elytra last?
faq.a: 432 durability, lost at 1 per second of gliding: 7 minutes 12 seconds. Unbreaking III raises that to about 28 minutes 48 seconds. Rockets do not reduce durability.

faq.q: How do I gain altitude without rockets?
faq.a: The wiki describes a pitch cycle: from at least 50 blocks up (about 80 is ideal), dive at a pitch of 32-33 degrees until you lose about 60-70 blocks, pitch up to about -50 degrees, then slowly ease back down to 32 degrees and repeat. Done right it gains about 3 blocks per cycle.

faq.q: What does "experienced kinetic energy" mean?
faq.a: You died from kinetic damage by hitting a block at high speed. Horizontal surfaces such as ceilings do not cause it.

keywords: elytra fly glide fireworks boost rocket mending phantom membrane

name: How to Find and Beat Trial Chambers in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Trial chambers generate underground in the Overworld in any biome except the deep dark. The starting room is between Y=-40 and -20. Buy a trial explorer map from a journeyman cartographer (12 emeralds and a compass). They are made of tuff bricks and copper blocks, and hold trial spawners, vaults and the only breezes.
steps: Get a trial explorer map: a journeyman-level cartographer sells it for 12 emeralds and a compass. It points to the nearest trial chamber that does not already have a map pointing to it. Maps from the same cartographer always point to the same structure.

Without a map, look for exposed caves with odd shapes and tuff bricks and copper blocks. The wiki says the starting room sits between Y=-40 and -20, and trial chambers only generate in chunks created in 1.21 or later.

Trial spawners activate when a Survival or Adventure player is within 14 blocks with line of sight. With 1 player the spawner spawns 1 mob every 2 seconds, keeps at most 2 alive, and spawns 6 in total. More players nearby means more mobs and more rewards.
After the mobs are defeated, the spawner ejects rewards, including trial keys, and goes on a 30-minute cooldown.
Use trial keys on vaults. Each player can unlock a given vault only once, and it ejects 2 to 5 stacks of loot.

For ominous trials, drink an ominous bottle (a raid captain outside a raid always drops one) to get Bad Omen, which becomes Trial Omen in the chamber and turns trial spawners ominous. Ominous trial spawners give ominous trial keys, which open ominous vaults.
The wiki lists heavy cores and breeze rods as obtainable only from trial chambers, which makes them the only place to get the mace.
materials: Trial explorer map (12 emeralds and a compass at a journeyman cartographer)
Armor, a shield, a melee weapon and a bow
An ominous bottle for an ominous trial (optional)
editionNote: The wiki treats trial chambers as the same structure in both editions. Generation follows a grid of 34x34 chunk regions with one chamber per region, unless a deep dark biome cancels it. In Java, a given villager always trades the same map, set when the trade unlocks.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.q: How do you get the mace?
faq.a: The wiki says heavy cores and breeze rods can only be obtained in trial chambers, so that is the only place to get a mace. Breezes spawn only in trial chambers.

faq.q: What is the difference between a vault and an ominous vault?
faq.a: Standard vaults open with a trial key. Ominous vaults open with an ominous trial key, which only comes from ominous trial spawners. Each player can unlock each vault only once.

faq.q: Do trial spawners ever reset?
faq.a: After the mobs are defeated, a trial spawner ejects its rewards and deactivates for 30 minutes.

faq.q: Can a trial chamber generate in the deep dark?
faq.a: Its origin point cannot generate in a deep dark biome, and a deep dark can cancel the chamber in a region, but other parts can intersect a deep dark.

keywords: trial chambers find map cartographer trial spawner vault ominous key heavy core mace breeze

name: How to Get Mending in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Mending is a treasure enchantment, so it cannot come from an enchanting table. Librarian villagers can sell it as an enchanted book (treasure enchantments cost double a normal one, capped at 64 emeralds). Put a lectern next to an unemployed villager, check its book trade, and re-place the lectern until it offers Mending. Apply the book at an anvil.
steps: Treasure enchantments cannot be obtained through an enchanting table. Most of them, including Mending, can appear on enchanted books sold by librarians.
Place an unclaimed lectern near an unemployed villager. It claims the lectern and becomes a librarian. Novice villagers who have not traded can lose their profession again.

Open its trades and look at the enchanted book. If it is not Mending, break the lectern; the villager loses the profession. Place the lectern again to get new trades. Do not trade before you have the book you want: trading locks in the villager's profession and trades.
When the book is Mending, buy it. Mending has only level I. The price is 5 to 64 emeralds plus a book, and treasure enchantments cost double before the 64-emerald cap.
Apply the book to a tool, weapon or armor piece at an anvil. Mending is incompatible with Infinity.

With Mending, any experience orb you collect repairs items in your main hand, offhand or armor slots that are damaged, at 2 durability per XP point. If several qualify, one is chosen at random per orb. Items in the rest of your inventory are not repaired.
materials: Emeralds and a book for the trade (5-64 emeralds)
An anvil and the item to enchant
editionNote: Mending repairs only damaged items in the hands and armor slots in both editions. In the Villager Trade Rebalance experiment (Java 1.20.2 experiment, Bedrock 1.20.30 experiment), Mending books come only from master-level librarians in the swamp outfit, and the wiki says ancient city chests have a higher chance of Mending books. That experiment is not part of the default trades.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.q: Why won't the enchanting table give me Mending?
faq.a: Mending is a treasure enchantment. Treasure enchantments cannot be obtained through an enchanting table.

faq.q: Does Mending repair items in my inventory?
faq.a: No. Only damaged items in your main hand, offhand or armor slots are repaired, 2 durability per XP point. If several are damaged, one is chosen at random for each orb.

faq.q: Can I put Mending on an item with Infinity?
faq.a: No. Mending and Infinity are incompatible.

faq.q: What if the trade rebalance experiment is on?
faq.a: Then Mending books come only from master-level librarians in the swamp outfit, as the wiki describes for the experiment.

keywords: mending enchantment librarian lectern treasure enchanted book anvil emeralds

name: How to Get a Happy Ghast in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Waterlog a dried ghast block for about 20 minutes: it hatches into a ghastling, which needs another 20 minutes (or snowballs) to grow into a happy ghast. Dried ghasts generate next to Nether fossils in soul sand valleys (1 in 3 chance), can be crafted from 8 ghast tears plus soul sand, or bartered from piglins (~2.13%). Equip the adult with a harness to fly with up to four players.
steps: Get a dried ghast: loot one next to a Nether fossil in a soul sand valley (1/3 of fossils), craft it with 8 ghast tears around 1 soul sand, or barter gold ingots with piglins (~2.13% each).
Place the dried ghast in water or use a water bucket to waterlog it. Keep it waterlogged until it transforms.

Wait about 20 minutes while it hydrates in visible stages and becomes a ghastling. The timing varies. Removing water makes hydration reverse gradually; breaking the block resets it to the dried state.

The ghastling normally takes 20 minutes to grow. Feed it snowballs to speed this up: each snowball cuts the remaining time by 10% in Java, while 10 snowballs grow a newly spawned ghastling into an adult in Bedrock.
Craft 1 harness: put 3 leather across the top row and glass, wool, glass across the middle row, leaving the bottom row empty. The wool color determines the harness color.
Use the harness on the adult happy ghast. Up to four players can now mount; the first rider pilots with normal movement keys.
Use shears on the adult to remove and retrieve its harness. Keep the ghast safe and use leads when you need to keep it nearby.
materials: Dried ghast (fossil loot, ghast tear crafting, or piglin bartering)
editionNote: Snowball growth differs: Java reduces the remaining growth time by 10% per snowball; Bedrock needs 10 snowballs for a newly spawned ghastling. In both editions, breaking a hydrating dried ghast resets its hydration.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.q: Can you breed happy ghasts?
faq.a: No. Happy ghasts cannot be bred. Hatch more dried ghasts if you want more happy ghasts.

faq.q: How many players can ride a happy ghast?
faq.a: Four at once. The first player to mount pilots from the front seat; the others fill the remaining sides clockwise.

faq.q: Can a happy ghast carry mobs or boats?
faq.a: Yes. Use leads to attach boats or leashable mobs to the happy ghast for air transport. Some carried entities appear suspended by four ropes, but that is a visual design, not an instruction to use four leads per entity.

keywords: happy ghast how to get dried ghast ghastling harness fly mount waterlog snowball golden dandelion

name: How to Find a Nether Fortress in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Nether fortresses can generate in every Nether biome. Search for nether brick bridges, corridors and towers, including structures partly buried in netherrack. Nether structure regions are 432 by 432 blocks in Java and 480 by 480 in Bedrock; a region can generate a fortress or a bastion, not both.
steps: Enter the Nether with armor, a weapon, food and blocks for bridging.
Explore across multiple structure regions: each can generate a fortress or a bastion remnant, not both. They do not alternate in a fixed sequence. Keep a safe route back to your portal.
Remember the generation area: each region has a four-chunk separation on its south and east borders, leaving a 368x368 (Java) or 416x416 (Bedrock) area where a structure can generate.
Scan for large nether brick complexes of bridges, corridors and towers on pillars above the lava seas. They can also be buried in netherrack, but hallways and passages stay clear.

If you find a bastion remnant, expand your search to other regions. The fortress-versus-bastion selection chance is 2/5 (40%) in Java and 1/3 (about 33.3%) in Bedrock. In basalt deltas, a selected bastion is replaced by a fortress.

Inside, look for nether wart growing next to the stairs, and for up to 2 blaze spawner platforms: three full-block stairs lead to a small platform fenced with nether brick fence, with the blaze spawner in the center.
Fortresses are the only place where wither skeletons and blazes spawn.
materials: Bow and arrows (for ghasts on the way)
Food, building blocks, and ideally Fire Resistance potions
A flint and steel spare, in case a ghast deactivates your portal
editionNote: Structure regions are 432 by 432 blocks in Java and 480 by 480 in Bedrock. Fortress selection is 2/5 in Java and 1/3 in Bedrock before the basalt-deltas replacement rule. This does not mean every location in basalt deltas contains a fortress.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.q: Which direction should I travel to find a fortress?
faq.a: There is no required compass direction. Expand your search across structure regions and scan for nether brick bridges and towers. A bastion in one region does not guarantee a fortress in the next.

faq.q: Can fortresses generate buried in netherrack?
faq.a: Yes. The interior is not filled with netherrack, and hallways and passages stay clear except for open walkways and bridges.

faq.q: What is the chance of a fortress in a region?
faq.a: The selection chance is 2/5 (40%) in Java and 1/3 (about 33.3%) in Bedrock. If a bastion is selected in basalt deltas, a fortress generates instead. These are structure-selection rules, not a guarantee of a fortress at every search location.

faq.q: What mobs spawn only in fortresses?
faq.a: Wither skeletons and blazes.

keywords: nether fortress how to find blaze rod wither skeleton nether wart basalt deltas bastion locate

name: How to Make a Mace in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft a mace with 1 heavy core and 1 breeze rod. Heavy cores only drop from ominous vaults (7.5% chance), and breeze rods come from breezes. After falling 1.5 blocks or more, a hit becomes a smash attack that deals extra damage by distance fallen and cancels your fall damage.
steps: Get a breeze rod: breezes are found in trial chambers (see the trial chambers guide).
Get a heavy core: it only drops from ominous vaults, with a 7.5% chance. Ominous vaults need ominous trial keys from ominous trial spawners.
Craft the mace: heavy core plus breeze rod in the crafting grid.

Smash attack: fall 1.5 blocks or more and hit an entity while not on the ground. Extra damage is 4 per block for the first 3 blocks fallen, 2 per block for the next 5, and 1 per block after that. Smash attacks are usually critical hits.
A successful smash attack lets you land without the fall damage you built up, and knocks back everything within 2.5 blocks (not you). It does not work while you have Slow Falling.
A normal attack on the ground deals 6 damage, and every attack costs 1 durability (500 in Java, 501 in Bedrock).
Enchantments: Density adds 0.5 damage per level for each block fallen. Breach and Wind Burst also work on the mace; Wind Burst can launch you after a smash.
materials: Gear and keys for trial chambers
editionNote: Java: attack speed is 0.6, the slowest in the game, and a mace hit on a boat or minecart destroys it. Bedrock: no attack cooldown, so a Breach IV mace has the highest damage per hit and the highest DPS against diamond or netherite armor. In Java, elytra must be unequipped for a smash attack; in Bedrock a smash works even during elytra flight.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.q: How rare is the heavy core?
faq.a: 7.5% from ominous vaults. Each player can unlock a given vault only once.

faq.q: How does the smash attack work?
faq.a: Hit while falling 1.5 blocks or more and not on the ground (and without Slow Falling). Extra damage grows with the distance fallen, the attack lands without fall damage, and entities within 2.5 blocks are knocked back.

faq.q: How much does Density help?
faq.a: Each level adds 0.5 damage for each block fallen. The wiki compares kills on a player in full Protection IV netherite armor: an unenchanted mace needs a critical hit after falling 30 blocks, Density V needs 10.

faq.q: How many times can I use a mace?
faq.a: It has 500 durability in Java and 501 in Bedrock, and every attack uses 1.

keywords: mace how to craft heavy core breeze rod ominous vault smash attack density breach wind burst

name: How to Find a Woodland Mansion in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Woodland mansions generate rarely in dark forests and pale gardens, often far from spawn. Buy a woodland explorer map from a master-level cartographer (14 emeralds and a compass), or find one in an abandoned camp secret chest. Inside are vindicators, evokers (the only source of totems of undying) and imprisoned allays.
steps: Get a woodland explorer map: a master-level cartographer sells it for 14 emeralds and a compass. Abandoned camp secret chests can also hold one. A map may not point to the nearest mansion.
With cheats on, /locate structure mansion finds the nearest one.
Travel there prepared. The mansion generates only in dark forests and pale gardens (in Bedrock also lush caves, dripstone caves, sulfur caves and dark forest hills).

Inside, the first floor only has rooms with vindicators. From the second floor up, some large rooms hold both evokers and vindicators. The interior is dark enough for other Overworld monsters to spawn, and some come in through the entrance at night.
Kill the evokers: each always drops a totem of undying. Vindicators and evokers do not respawn once killed.
Free the imprisoned allays. Some rooms are sealed and secret rooms have no entrance at all, so look for hidden spaces and chests.
materials: Woodland explorer map (master cartographer: 14 emeralds and a compass, or an abandoned camp secret chest)
Armor, a shield, a weapon and food
editionNote: Dark forests and pale gardens are the biomes in both editions. In Bedrock the wiki also lists lush caves, dripstone caves, sulfur caves and dark forest hills. Mansions only generate in new chunks, never in already-generated ones.

faq.q: Do evokers and vindicators respawn?
faq.a: No. Once all vindicators and evokers are killed they do not respawn, unlike pillagers at outposts.

name: How to Find Slimes in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Slimes spawn in swamps and mangrove swamps between Y=51 and Y=69 at light level 7 or less (most often on a full moon, never on a new moon), or in slime chunks below Y=40 regardless of light or weather. About 1 in 10 chunks is a slime chunk.
steps: Swamps: go to a swamp or mangrove swamp. Slimes spawn there between Y=51 and Y=69 (inclusive) when the light level is 7 or less, which also lets them spawn in dim areas where most hostile mobs cannot.
Watch the moon: swamp slimes spawn most often on a full moon and never on a new moon.
Slime chunks: below Y=40 in the Overworld, slimes spawn in groups of four in Java Edition or individually in Bedrock Edition, regardless of lighting or weather.
About 1 in 10 chunks is a slime chunk, determined by an algorithm. In Java Edition it depends on the world seed; in Bedrock Edition they are at the same coordinates in every world.
Give them room: a slime needs a clear space of about 2.04x2.04x2.04 blocks to spawn, and any block in that space, even a glass pane, can stop a spawn.
Slimes split into smaller slimes on death, and slimes are a major source of slimeballs.
materials: Torches (they do not stop slimes, but stop everything else)
A decent sword - big slimes hit hard
Optional: iron golem + name tag for a farm
editionNote: In Java slimes spawn in groups of four in slime chunks; in Bedrock they spawn individually, and slime chunks are at the same coordinates in every world. Swamp spawning works in both.
versions: Per the Minecraft Wiki Slime page.

faq.q: What Y level do slimes spawn at?
faq.a: In swamps and mangrove swamps: Y=51 to Y=69 at light level 7 or less. In slime chunks: below Y=40, regardless of light or weather.

faq.q: How big a space does a slime need?
faq.a: About 2.04x2.04x2.04 blocks, clear of solid and liquid blocks.

faq.q: Do slimes spawn on a new moon?
faq.a: Not in swamps: they never spawn on a new moon and spawn most on a full moon. Slime chunks ignore light and weather.

faq.q: How common are slime chunks?
faq.a: About 1 in 10 chunks. In Java Edition it depends on the world seed; in Bedrock Edition it is the same for every world.

name: How to Get Wither Skeleton Skulls in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Wither skeleton skulls only drop from wither skeletons, which are found exclusively in nether fortresses. The drop chance is 2.5% per kill, rising 1% per Looting level to 5.5% at Looting III. You need 3 skulls to summon the Wither.
steps: Find a nether fortress: wither skeletons spawn only there, at light level 0 to 7. In Java they spawn in groups of 5, in Bedrock in groups of 2-3.
Know where they spawn: inside the bounding box of any single fortress piece they spawn on any block; in the wider fortress area only on nether bricks.
Use a sword with Looting: the skull chance is 2.5% by default and 3.5%, 4.5% and 5.5% with Looting I, II and III.
Kill them yourself. The wiki says the skull drops only when a player kills the wither skeleton (in Java a tamed wolf also counts).
A wither skeleton killed by a charged creeper always drops its skull.
Expect a grind: at 2.5% the average is 40 kills per skull, and at 5.5% about 18. Wither skeletons inflict the Wither effect, and drink milk to cure it.
Wither skeletons also drop coal and bones, and they are the only renewable source of coal.
materials: Food and milk (wither skeletons inflict the Wither effect)
editionNote: Java wither skeletons spawn in groups of 5, Bedrock in groups of 2-3. In Java a tamed wolf's kill also drops a skull; the Bedrock table lists only player kills. The Wither itself spawns 3-4 wither skeletons below half health on Normal and Hard.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.q: What is the drop rate for wither skeleton skulls?
faq.a: 2.5% with no Looting, 3.5% with Looting I, 4.5% with Looting II and 5.5% with Looting III.

faq.q: Where do wither skeletons spawn?
faq.a: Only in nether fortresses, at light level 0 to 7. Inside a fortress piece's bounding box they spawn on any block; elsewhere in the fortress area only on nether bricks.

faq.q: How many kills do I need for 3 skulls?
faq.a: On average 40 kills per skull at 2.5% (about 120 for three) or about 18 per skull at 5.5% (about 55 for three). It is chance, so it can take more or fewer.

faq.q: Can a charged creeper get me a skull?
faq.a: Yes. A wither skeleton killed by a charged creeper always drops its skull.

name: How to Get a Blue Axolotl in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Blue axolotls never spawn naturally - the only way is breeding: feed two axolotls buckets of tropical fish and each baby has a 1 in 1200 (0.083%) chance to be blue. Build a breeding pool, mass-produce babies, and accelerate their growth with more tropical fish.
steps: Find axolotls: they spawn underwater in lush caves, only where there is a clay block less than five blocks below the water.
Catch them with a water bucket (bucket of axolotl) and carry them to a safe breeding pool near your base - axolotls die after 5 minutes out of water.
Stock up on buckets of tropical fish: scoop tropical fish from warm oceans with buckets. This is the only food that breeds axolotls.
Breed pairs nonstop: each baby has a 1/1200 chance to be blue; otherwise it inherits one parent's color. Parents can breed again after 5 minutes in Java, 1 minute in Bedrock.
Speed up the grind: feed babies buckets of tropical fish - each use cuts 10% off the remaining 20-minute growth time, so adults recycle into the breeding pool faster.
Scale up: keep every adult, not just blue ones - more breeding pairs means more rolls of the 1/1200 dice per cycle.
When one finally comes out blue, breed it too: blue parents still only give 1/1200 blue babies, so protect your prize with a name tag.
materials: At least 2 axolotls (bucketed from lush caves)
Lots of buckets of tropical fish (warm ocean)
editionNote: Breeding cooldown is 5 minutes in Java but only 1 minute in Bedrock, so Bedrock farms roll the 1/1200 chance five times faster.
versions: Axolotl since 1.17 (Caves & Cliffs Part I); lush cave natural spawning since 1.18.

faq.q: Can blue axolotls spawn in the wild?
faq.a: No. Blue is a breeding-only mutation: every bred baby has a 1 in 1200 (0.083%) chance to be blue. You will never find one in a lush cave.

faq.q: Do two blue axolotls make blue babies?
faq.a: Only at the same 1/1200 rate - otherwise the baby inherits a parent's color, which at least means blue. Blue parents never raise the mutation odds.

faq.q: How many axolotls do I need to breed for a blue one?
faq.a: On average 1200 babies. With several pairs and fish-fed growth acceleration, a dedicated farm gets there - bring a lot of tropical fish.

name: How to Dye Armor in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Leather armor, leather horse armor and wolf armor can be dyed. In Java Edition, craft the item together with 1 or more dyes. In Bedrock Edition, dye water in a cauldron and use the item on the cauldron. Use dyed armor on a cauldron of undyed water to remove the dye.
steps: Get leather armor, leather horse armor or wolf armor. These are the items the wiki lists as dyeable this way.
Get dyes. There are sixteen dyes.
Java Edition: craft the item together with 1 or more dyes in a crafting grid.
Bedrock Edition: dye the water in a cauldron with dye, then use the item on the cauldron. This uses 1 layer of water and does not change the water's color.
To remove the dye, use the dyed leather armor on a cauldron with undyed water (Bedrock). The wiki says this changes the water's color to the armor's dye color and leaves the armor with no dye.
For reference, the default leather armor color is #A06540.
materials: Leather armor, leather horse armor or wolf armor
Bedrock only: a cauldron with water
editionNote: Java: dyeing is done by crafting the item with dye. Bedrock: dyeing uses a cauldron of dyed water, 1 layer per item. Undyeing uses a cauldron of undyed water for leather armor, leather horse armor and wolf armor.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.a: The wiki describes dyeing for leather armor, leather horse armor and wolf armor. It does not list dyeing for other armor sets.

faq.a: Dye the water in a cauldron, then use the armor on the cauldron. It uses 1 layer of water and does not change the water's color.

faq.a: Use the dyed item on a cauldron with undyed water. For leather armor the wiki says this changes the water to the armor's dye color.

faq.a: Yes. Craft it with dye in Java Edition, or use it on a cauldron of dyed water in Bedrock Edition. It cannot be equipped on baby wolves.

name: How to Make a Lead in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft leads from 5 string: one craft gives 2 leads. The old recipe (4 string + 1 slimeball) was replaced in 25w18a (Java) and Preview 1.21.90.21 (Bedrock). Use a lead on a mob to leash it, and use it on a fence to tie the mob there.
steps: Gather 5 string for each craft, which gives 2 leads.
Craft the lead in a crafting table.
Use a lead on a leashable mob to leash it. Each leashed mob needs its own lead. Hostile mobs usually cannot be leashed, and wolves cannot be leashed once angry.
To tie a mob, use the lead on any type of fence: it attaches with a visible knot. A mob tied to a fence tends to stay within 5 blocks of the post.
A lead can stretch a maximum of 12 blocks (16 if the mob is a happy ghast). Past that, or if the mob moves quickly away, the lead breaks and drops as an item.
Remove a lead by using it on the mob again, hitting the knot, or using shears. The lead drops as an item (not in Creative on Java).
No string? Leads can also come from the wandering trader's trader llamas (dropped when a llama is detached), or from chests in woodland mansions, ancient cities and abandoned camps.
editionNote: Both editions use 5 string for 2 leads now. Bedrock: when a chunk unloads with a leashed mob inside, the lead sometimes breaks and drops. The wiki lists the balloon recipe (with lead) for Bedrock and Education only.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.q: How do you make a lead?
faq.a: With 5 string in a crafting table. One craft gives 2 leads. The old recipe was 4 string and 1 slimeball.

faq.q: Do you still need a slimeball?
faq.a: No. The wiki says leads are now crafted with 5 string instead of 4 string and 1 slimeball (Java 25w18a, Bedrock Preview 1.21.90.21).

faq.a: A lead stretches at most 12 blocks (16 for a happy ghast) and breaks if the mob cannot follow or moves quickly away. It also breaks when hit by a projectile or when the fence post is removed or pushed.

faq.a: No. A lead does not break if the attached animal dies.

name: How to Make Smooth Stone in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Smelt stone in a furnace to get smooth stone. Stone itself comes from smelting cobblestone. Mine it with a pickaxe, or it drops nothing. It is renewable and stacks to 64.

Smelt the cobblestone in a furnace to get stone.
Smelt the stone again to get smooth stone. That is two smelting passes from cobblestone.
Mine smooth stone with a pickaxe to collect it. Without a pickaxe it drops nothing.
Or find it in villages: it generates in the butcher's house of plains, savanna and snowy plains villages as slabs and blocks, and a mason's chest can hold it (20.8% per the wiki loot table).
Use it: 3 smooth stone in a row make 6 smooth stone slabs (the stonecutter also makes slabs). A blast furnace takes 5 iron ingots, 1 furnace and 3 smooth stone.

name: How to Get Honeycomb in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Shear a full bee nest or beehive (honey level 5) to get 3 honeycombs. Shearing angers the bees inside, unless there is a lit campfire or soul campfire (or a fire) under it, or you use a dispenser with shears. Honeycomb is used for beehives, candles, honeycomb blocks and waxing copper or signs.
steps: Find a bee nest. Naturally generated nests hold 2-3 bees: 100% of trees in meadows have one, 5% in plains, sunflower plains and cherry groves, 2% in flower forests (Java), 1% in mangrove swamps and 0.2% in forests and birch forests (Java).

Or grow one: oak, birch and cherry trees grown from saplings within 2 blocks of a flower at the same Y level have a 5% chance to grow with a nest of 2-3 bees. Mangroves have a 1% chance with no flower needed.
Wait until it is full (honey level 5). A comparator reads the honey level, with 5 as the maximum.
Put a lit campfire, soul campfire or fire under the nest so the bees do not turn hostile.
Use shears on the full nest: it drops 3 honeycombs and resets to honey level 0.
A dispenser with shears inside can harvest it without angering the bees. The honeycomb pops out as a dropped item.
Use honeycomb on any copper block (or a copper golem) to wax it and stop oxidation, or on signs to stop them being edited. It also crafts beehives, candles and honeycomb blocks.
materials: A lit campfire or soul campfire
Optional: a dispenser for automatic harvesting
Flowers and saplings to grow your own nests
editionNote: Both editions give 3 honeycombs from a full nest or hive. Biome chances differ: flower forests are 2% in Java and 3% in Bedrock, and forests are 0.2% in Java and 0.035% in Bedrock. In Bedrock, oak trees grown in plains can grow a nest regardless of nearby flowers.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.q: Why do bees attack me when I collect honeycomb?
faq.a: Shearing a full nest angers the bees inside. A lit campfire or soul campfire (or a fire) under it keeps them from becoming hostile, and a dispenser with shears does not anger them at all.

faq.q: How do I know a nest is full?
faq.a: A full nest or hive is at honey level 5. A redstone comparator outputs a signal equal to the honey level, up to 5.

faq.q: What happens if I break a nest without Silk Touch?
faq.a: It drops nothing and the bees inside come out angry. With Silk Touch the nest drops itself with the bees inside, and nearby bees do not become angry.

faq.q: What can I do with honeycomb?
faq.a: Craft beehives, candles and honeycomb blocks, and wax copper blocks, copper golems and signs.

keywords: honeycomb minecraft how to get shear bee nest honey level 5 campfire dispenser wax copper

name: How to Make a Campfire in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft a campfire from sticks, coal or charcoal, and any log, stem, wood or hyphae (stripped works too). It cooks up to 4 food items at once with no fuel, pacifies bees, makes a smoke signal and gives light level 15 without spreading fire.
steps: Gather sticks, 1 coal or charcoal, and any log, stem, wood or hyphae (stripped variants work).
Craft the campfire: a stick in the top center, stick-coal-stick across the middle row, and three logs along the bottom row (3 sticks, 1 coal or charcoal, 3 logs, stripped or wood variants included).
Cook on it: use a food item on a lit campfire. Up to 4 items cook at once and no fuel is needed. Each takes 30 seconds (600 ticks), against 10 seconds in a furnace.
Put it within five blocks of a beehive or bee nest, with open air between them, to harvest honey bottles and honeycomb without angering the bees.
Make a smoke signal: smoke rises around 10 blocks. With a hay bale below, it floats up 24 blocks.
It is lit when placed. Relight with flint and steel, a fire charge or a flaming arrow. Put it out with a shovel, a splash water bottle or by waterlogging it. Rain does not extinguish it.
Careful: a lit campfire damages mobs and players standing on it, but does not set them on fire. Mining it drops 2 charcoal, or the campfire itself with Silk Touch.
materials: 3 logs, stems, wood or hyphae (any type)
Optional: hay bale for a taller smoke signal
editionNote: Java: pistons do not interact with campfires. Bedrock: a piston push breaks a campfire (2 charcoal), campfires can also be lit with Fire Aspect, and they can also be put out by water placed above them.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.q: Does a campfire need fuel?
faq.a: No. It cooks up to four food items at once without fuel.

faq.q: How long does food take on a campfire?
faq.a: 30 seconds (600 ticks), against 10 seconds in a furnace and 5 in a smoker.

faq.q: How tall is a campfire smoke signal?
faq.a: Around 10 blocks. With a hay bale below it, 24 blocks.

faq.a: No. Its fire does not spread under any circumstances.
