name: How to Breed Horses in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Tame two horses, then feed each a golden apple or golden carrot to activate love mode. They mate and produce a foal. The foal's health, speed and jump are worked out from both parents' stats by a formula, so breeding good horses can improve the line. Foals take 20 minutes to grow, and feeding them speeds that up.
steps: Tame both parents: taming is required to breed a horse. Repeated mounting eventually makes hearts appear above the horse.
Feed each tamed horse a golden carrot or golden apple. Those activate love mode in tamed horses. Plain apples, wheat and sugar do not.
The horses mate and a foal appears, and breeding gives 1-7 XP. The foal usually has the color and markings of one parent, with a 13/45 chance of random ones.
Stats: health, movement speed and jump height are set at birth, not affected by food. For breeding, the wiki says each stat is calculated by a formula from the parents' stats.

Grow the foal: foals take 20 minutes to mature unless fed. Sugar speeds growth by 30 seconds, wheat 20 seconds, apple and golden carrot by 1 minute, hay bale by 3 minutes and golden apple by 4 minutes.
Keep the best foal and breed it again to improve the line over generations.
Breeding a horse with a donkey gives a mule, which cannot breed.
materials: Fences or leads to keep the parents together
Optional: hay bales, apples or sugar to grow the foal faster
editionNote: Foods and 20-minute foal growth are the same in both editions. Bedrock only: breeding a horse with a donkey unlocks the Artificial Selection achievement, and an untamed adult horse at full health cannot be fed hay.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.q: What do horses eat to breed?
faq.a: Golden carrots or golden apples activate love mode in tamed horses. Apples, wheat, sugar and hay bales heal them and speed foal growth, but do not start breeding.

faq.q: How do I get a faster horse?
faq.a: Stats are set when a horse is born and are not changed by food. When breeding, each foal stat is calculated by a formula from both parents, so breed your best horses together and keep the best foals.

faq.q: Can you breed a horse and a donkey?
faq.a: Yes. The result is a mule. Mules cannot breed.

faq.q: How long until a foal grows up?
faq.a: 20 minutes if not fed. Feeding reduces it: sugar 30 seconds, wheat 20 seconds, apple or golden carrot 1 minute, hay bale 3 minutes, golden apple 4 minutes.

name: How to Make Concrete in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft concrete powder from sand, gravel and a dye, then let it touch water. It turns into concrete on contact. It comes in the sixteen dye colors. Mine concrete with a pickaxe or it drops nothing.
steps: Craft concrete powder (shapeless): 4 sand, 4 gravel and 1 dye of the color you want give 8 concrete powder.
Concrete powder is a gravity-affected block: it falls when the block below is not solid.
Make it touch water: place it into, next to, or let it fall into flowing water, a water source, or (Java only) a waterlogged block. It becomes concrete on contact.
Next to a waterlogged block it must touch a side where water can flow out, such as the open sides of stairs, not the back of stairs or any side of waterlogged leaves.
Mine the concrete with a pickaxe. Without one it drops nothing.
materials: 1 dye of the color you want (makes 8 powder)
editionNote: Waterlogged blocks convert concrete powder in Java only. Bedrock needs real water.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.q: How do you turn concrete powder into concrete?
faq.a: Let it touch water: a water source, flowing water, or a waterlogged block (Java only).

faq.q: Is concrete renewable?
faq.a: Yes, per the wiki, but without glitches sand is renewable only through the wandering trader, so harvesting natural sand is easier.

faq.q: How many colors are there?
faq.a: Sixteen, one per dye color.

faq.q: Does concrete need a pickaxe?
faq.a: Yes. Mined without one it drops nothing.

name: How to Make a Copper Golem in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Place a block of copper (any oxidation stage, waxed works too) and put a carved pumpkin or jack o'lantern on top - the pumpkin must be placed last. The copper block turns into a copper chest and the golem spawns on it, ready to sort your items.
steps: Gather the materials: 1 block of copper (9 copper ingots) and 1 carved pumpkin - shear a regular pumpkin - or a jack o'lantern.
Place the block of copper where you want the golem. Any oxidation stage works, waxed blocks too, and the pattern works horizontally or even upside-down.
Place the carved pumpkin or jack o'lantern last - by hand, with a dispenser, or even let an enderman do it.
The copper block transforms into a copper chest facing the pumpkin's direction and the copper golem spawns where the pumpkin was, matching the block's oxidation stage.

Put it to work: the golem takes up to 16 of the first item it finds in copper chests and files them into nearby wooden chests or trapped chests that are empty or already contain that item type - a fully automatic sorting system.

Maintain it: use a honeycomb to wax it and freeze oxidation, or scrape with an axe to revert one stage. Unwaxed golems take 21-23 in-game days per oxidation stage, and once fully oxidized they turn into a copper golem statue. Scrape the statue with an axe one stage at a time; an unoxidized statue comes back to life.
materials: 1 carved pumpkin (pumpkin + shears) or jack o'lantern
Optional: honeycomb to wax the golem
Optional: copper chests and wooden chests for the sorting setup
editionNote: The build is identical in Java (1.21.9) and Bedrock (1.21.111). When sorting, Java golems cannot tell apart potion contents, tipped arrow types or suspicious stews - Bedrock golems can. Both ignore durability, enchantments and custom names.
versions: Added in Java 1.21.9 and Bedrock 1.21.111. The copper golem lost the 2021 mob vote and finally arrived four years later with a chest-sorting job instead of pressing buttons.

faq.q: Does the copper golem spawn naturally?
faq.a: No. It only exists when a player builds it (copper block + pumpkin placed last), from a spawn egg, or when you reanimate an unwaxed copper golem statue with an axe.

faq.q: What happens when a copper golem fully oxidizes?
faq.a: It freezes into a copper golem statue and drops whatever it was holding. Scrape an unwaxed statue with an axe until it is unoxidized to bring the golem back - waxing with honeycomb at any stage prevents this entirely.

faq.q: How does copper golem sorting work?
faq.a: It opens copper chests, takes up to 16 of the first item type it finds, and places them in nearby wooden or trapped chests that are empty or already contain that item. It remembers up to 9 copper chests and resets after checking 10 empty ones.

name: How to Tame and Ride a Nautilus in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Find a nautilus in any ocean biome between Y 38 and 58 and feed it pufferfish or buckets of pufferfish - each one has a 1/3 chance to tame it. Put a saddle on it to ride: it hits 6.5 m/s underwater and has a chargeable dash.
steps: Find a nautilus: they swim in every ocean biome (any temperature) between Y-levels 38 and 58, in groups of 1-3. In Bedrock 10% spawn as babies, which are already passive.
Tame it: feed pufferfish or buckets of pufferfish. Each one has a 1 in 3 chance of taming, and holding one also tempts the nautilus to follow you.
Interact once and it becomes persistent - it stops counting toward the water creature cap and never despawns.
Saddle it: use a saddle on the tamed nautilus (craftable since 1.21.6 with 3 leather and 1 iron ingot). Remove it later with shears.

Ride it: standard movement controls. The nautilus gains speed in a straight line up to 6.5 m/s, and pressing jump triggers a dash - hold jump to charge a longer one. Your XP bar becomes the dash meter while riding.
Armor it with nautilus armor (copper through diamond as chest loot, netherite via smithing), and heal or breed adults by feeding any fish or bucket of fish - pufferfish heals 2 HP, raw cod heals 4.
Alternative: the zombie nautilus is tamed the same way, is faster (7.15 m/s) and never despawns even on Peaceful - but it is undead, so Instant Health potions hurt it and you cannot breed it.
materials: Pufferfish or buckets of pufferfish (several, 1/3 tame chance each)
Optional: nautilus armor (loot from shipwrecks, ocean ruins or buried treasure)
Optional: any fish for healing and breeding
editionNote: Added in Java 1.21.11 and Bedrock 1.21.130. In Bedrock you cannot go through Nether or End portals while riding a nautilus, and babies spawn naturally 10% of the time.
versions: Nautilus: Java 1.21.11 / Bedrock 1.21.130. Saddles craftable since Java 1.21.6 / Bedrock 1.21.90.

faq.q: How fast is a nautilus?

name: How to Find Buried Treasure in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Buried treasure is a chest buried mainly in beaches, and it always holds a heart of the sea, the only source of one. Find it with a buried treasure map from a shipwreck, then dig where the map leads. In Java the chest is at chunk-relative 9,9 and faces east; in Bedrock it is at 8,8.
steps: Get a map: shipwrecks have up to 3 chests (supply, treasure and map chests), and the wiki says they can contain buried treasure maps. Map chests are in the lower section of the ship.
Follow the map to the treasure. Buried treasure generates in beach biomes (Java and Bedrock) and can also generate underwater.
Find the exact spot: in Java the chest is always at chunk-relative 9 on both X and Z, and faces east. In Bedrock it is at 8 on X and Z.
Dig down. The chest is usually under sand or gravel on beaches, under stone if it generated on an underwater hillside, and sometimes under other terrain blocks like coal ore or diorite.
If the chest is exposed to water it is waterlogged.
Loot: every buried treasure has a heart of the sea. Java pools can also give iron ingots, gold ingots, cooked cod and salmon, Water Breathing potions, TNT, emeralds, prismarine crystals and diamonds.
Use the heart of the sea to craft a conduit.
materials: A buried treasure map (shipwreck map chest)
Something for breathing underwater, if the chest is underwater
editionNote: Java: chunk-relative 9,9 and the chest faces east. Bedrock: chunk-relative 8,8. Bedrock also generates buried treasure in stony shore and mushroom field shore biomes, in addition to beaches and snowy beaches.

faq.q: Is buried treasure the only source of the heart of the sea?

faq.q: Where do I find buried treasure maps?

faq.q: What biomes does buried treasure generate in?

name: How to Make Fireworks in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft a firework rocket from paper and gunpowder: it makes 3 rockets, and up to three gunpowder raise the flight duration. Add firework stars for explosions. For elytra boosting use rockets with no star, since a star makes you take explosion damage.
steps: Craft paper + gunpowder to get 3 firework rockets. Up to three gunpowder can be used, and more gunpowder means a longer flight duration (maximum 3).
For elytra boosting, keep the rocket star-free. A rocket with any firework star hurts you when it explodes.

Boost while gliding: using a rocket on elytra pushes you in the direction you face at 33.5 blocks per second. Boost time is about 1.5, 2.0 and 2.5 seconds for flight durations 1, 2 and 3 (the wiki says it is somewhat random).

For a show, craft a firework star first: gunpowder + a matching dye, plus optional extras. Fire charge gives a large ball, gold nugget a star shape, any head a creeper face, feather a burst, glowstone dust a twinkle and diamond a trail.
Craft paper + gunpowder + firework stars to make the rocket. Any remaining spaces can hold more firework stars (up to seven), and all of them explode almost together. Damage grows with each star.
Launch it by using it on a block, from a dispenser (it flies the way the dispenser faces) or from a crossbow. A crossbow rocket only deals damage if it has an explosion effect.
editionNote: In Java, a crossbow rocket that hits an entity explodes instantly. In Bedrock it passes through the entity, so aim where it will explode.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.q: How many rockets does one craft give?
faq.a: 3, with paper and gunpowder.

faq.q: Do fireworks hurt when I fly with elytra?
faq.a: Only if the rocket has a firework star. Without one it has no explosion.

faq.q: How do I add a trail or twinkle?
faq.a: Add a diamond (trail) or glowstone dust (twinkle) to the firework star.

faq.q: Do crossbow fireworks do damage?
faq.a: Only with an explosion effect. Higher flight duration gives more range, and each star adds damage.

keywords: firework rocket minecraft how to make paper gunpowder firework star elytra boost crossbow

name: How to Get Silk Touch in Minecraft

steps: Enchanting table: enchant tools or books until Silk Touch is offered. It has a maximum level of 1 and a weight of 1, so it is a low-chance offer.
Librarian villagers: check their enchanted book trades for Silk Touch.
Fishing: enchanted books from fishing can carry Silk Touch.
Chests: monster room chests and non-village structure loot can contain it.
Bedrock Edition only: mobs that spawned in a raid can drop Silk Touch.
Apply the book on an anvil. Silk Touch and Fortune cannot be on the same tool.

faq.q: Can Silk Touch and Fortune go on the same pickaxe?

quickAnswer: Craft paper with 3 sugar cane in a row on a crafting table: it yields 3 paper. Paper is needed for books, maps, cartography tables, firework rockets, name tags and banner patterns.

Place 3 sugar cane in a horizontal row on a crafting table to get 3 paper.

Make a map: paper + compass gives an empty map (Java) or an empty locator map (Bedrock).
Make a firework rocket: paper + gunpowder (up to three gunpowder for longer flight), optionally with firework stars.
Zoom a map out: map + paper in a cartography table, which the wiki lists as 8 times more efficient than the crafting table.
Find it in chests: shipwreck supply chests (1-12 paper, ~46%) and map chests (1-10, ~89%), stronghold library chests (2-7, ~88-89%) and village cartographer chests (1-5, ~61%).

name: How to Get XP Fast in Minecraft
quickAnswer: The fastest XP combines a mob farm with furnace banks: common hostile mobs drop 5 XP each, smelting stores XP inside the furnace for one big payout, and quartz mining pays 2-5 XP per ore. Level 30 costs 1,395 XP total and unlocks max-level enchanting.
steps: Hunt hostile mobs: zombies, skeletons, creepers and most hostiles drop 5 XP (plus 1-3 per piece of spawned equipment) as long as they die within 5 seconds of a player hit - fall damage and fire still count if you tagged them.
Mine the right ores: nether quartz pays 2-5 XP per ore, diamond and emerald 3-7, and coal, redstone and lapis smaller amounts. Silk Touch banks the XP inside the ore block for later.

Build a furnace bank: XP from smelting stays stored in the furnace. Smelt cactus (the best payer in Java), food or cobblestone with a hopper unloading it, then take one item from the GUI to collect the entire stored pile at once.
Farm a monster spawner: a dungeon spawner feeding a kill chamber gives steady XP and drops; mining the spawner itself is a one-time 15-43 XP, so cage it, don't break it.
Use a sculk catalyst: mobs dying near sculk convert into sculk blocks that store their XP - mine the sculk to collect it. A catalyst over a mob farm is a passive XP battery.
Collect the quiet sources: trading with villagers, breeding animals, reeling in fish, bottles o' enchanting, disenchanting gear in a grindstone, and challenge advancements in Java all pay XP.
Late game jackpots: the ender dragon drops 12,000 XP the first time (500 when respawned), the wither drops 50, and raid waves with Hero of the Village farms scale even higher.
Spend it at 30: max-level enchanting needs 30 levels (1,395 XP from 0); anvils accept jobs up to level 39. On death you drop 7 XP per level, capped at 100 points - bank levels before risky trips.
materials: A sword (Looting III for drops, XP unaffected)
Furnaces plus fuel for the smelting bank
Torches and food for mining trips
Optional: Silk Touch pickaxe to bank ore XP
editionNote: Core XP sources are shared. In Java, challenge advancements pay XP and cactus is the best smelting payout; in Bedrock, smelting payouts differ slightly. Dying drops 7 XP per level up to 100 points unless keep_inventory is on.
versions: Current for the latest Java and Bedrock releases; the ender dragon's first-kill payout is 12,000 XP, the highest single source in the game.

faq.q: How much XP do I need for level 30?
faq.a: 1,395 experience points from level 0. Levels cost more as they climb: the jump from 27 to 30 alone costs 306, so grind after big expenses, not before.

faq.q: What gives the most XP in Minecraft?
faq.a: The first ender dragon kill: 12,000 XP. After that, mob spawner farms, sculk catalyst setups and furnace banks give the best sustained rates, with nether quartz mining as the best casual option.

faq.q: Do I lose my XP when I die?
faq.a: You drop orbs worth 7 XP per level, capped at 100 points (roughly 7 levels), and the rest vanishes. With the keep_inventory gamerule on, you keep everything.

quickAnswer: Craft a bookshelf with 6 planks and 3 books: planks in the top and bottom rows, books in the middle row. Up to 15 bookshelves around an enchanting table give level 30 enchantments.

Get 6 planks of any wood per shelf.
Craft the shelf: 6 planks and 3 books. Planks fill the top and bottom rows, books fill the middle row.
Enchanting needs up to 15 bookshelves around an enchanting table to reach level 30 enchantments, so plan 45 books and 90 planks.

faq.q: How many bookshelves do I need for level 30 enchantments?

name: How to Make a Piston in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft a piston from any planks, cobblestone, an iron ingot and redstone dust. Add a slimeball to a piston to make a sticky piston. A piston moves up to 12 blocks at once.
steps: Gather the materials: 3 planks of any wood, 4 cobblestone, 1 iron ingot and 1 redstone dust.
Craft the piston: top row planks - planks - planks, middle row cobblestone - iron ingot - cobblestone, bottom row cobblestone - redstone dust - cobblestone.
Make it sticky: combine a slimeball with a piston.
Power it with a redstone signal. It extends in 2 game ticks (0.1 seconds) and pushes at most 12 blocks.
Place it facing you: pistons are always placed facing toward the player.
Break it with any tool; a pickaxe is faster. It always drops itself.
editionNote: Java Edition has quasi-connectivity: a piston can be powered from one block above, which Bedrock lacks. Bedrock has soft inversion (a redstone torch on a powered piston turns off) and a fixed start delay of 2 game ticks. In Java the start delay is 0 or 1 tick.
versions: Per the Minecraft Wiki Piston page. Slime blocks pull and push adjacent blocks since 14w18a.

faq.q: What is the difference between a piston and a sticky piston?
faq.a: A sticky piston (piston + slimeball) can also pull blocks back; a normal piston only pushes.

faq.q: How many blocks can a piston push?
faq.a: Up to 12 blocks at once.

faq.q: How fast does a piston extend?
faq.a: It takes 2 game ticks (0.1 seconds) after its start delay.

faq.q: Can a normal piston pull a slime block?
faq.a: No. Slime and honey blocks only stick for sticky pistons: a normal piston cannot pull them.

keywords: piston minecraft craft sticky piston slimeball redstone planks cobblestone iron push 12 blocks

name: How to Make TNT in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft TNT with gunpowder and sand (or red sand), in a checkerboard. Light it with flint and steel, a fire charge, redstone, fire, a flaming projectile or an explosion. Lit by fire or redstone it explodes after 4 seconds with power 4.
steps: Get gunpowder and sand (or red sand, any mix works).
Craft in a checkerboard: gunpowder in the four corners and the center, sand on the four edges.
Light it: flint and steel, fire charge, a dispenser, a redstone signal, stray fire, a flaming projectile or an explosion.
Wait: primed TNT explodes after 80 game ticks (4 seconds) when lit by fire or redstone, or after 10-30 ticks (0.5-1.5 seconds) when set off by another explosion.
Use physics: primed TNT is affected by gravity and can be pushed by flowing water, lava, pistons and explosions.
Find free TNT: 9 TNT generate in each desert pyramid, and buried treasure chests hold 1-2 TNT (~62.7%).
Underwater, TNT usually cannot destroy blocks.
materials: To prime: flint and steel or a redstone signal
editionNote: In Java Edition, a gravity block such as sand on top of TNT when it is lit falls through it and lets the explosion break blocks underwater. In Bedrock Edition those tricks do not work; only underwater TNT (Education Edition option) can destroy blocks underwater.
versions: Per the Minecraft Wiki TNT page: the fuse was 2 seconds in early versions and became 4 seconds in 20100125.

faq.q: How long is the TNT fuse?
faq.a: 80 game ticks (4 seconds) when lit by fire or redstone, and 10-30 ticks when set off by an explosion.

faq.q: How strong is a TNT explosion?
faq.a: Primed TNT creates an explosion of power 4.

faq.q: Does TNT chain react?
faq.a: Yes. A redstone signal does not power adjacent TNT, but adjacent TNT blocks are activated by the explosion.

faq.q: Where can I find TNT without crafting?
faq.a: Desert pyramids (9 TNT) and buried treasure chests (1-2 TNT at ~62.7%).

name: How to Respawn the Ender Dragon in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Place four end crystals on the edges of the exit portal, one on each side. A sequence of a bit over 30 seconds resets the obsidian pillars and then the dragon respawns at (0, 128, 0). A respawned dragon drops 500 XP instead of the 12,000 of the first kill.
steps: Craft 4 end crystals (glass, an eye of ender and a ghast tear each).
Go to the exit portal at the center of the main End island.
Place one end crystal on each of the four sides of the exit portal, on bedrock or on obsidian placed where the bedrock was.

Stay clear: the crystals point at the tops of the pillars, setting off explosions that reset the obsidian pillars, iron bars and end crystals, and destroying any player-placed blocks on top. Then all crystals point at (0, 128, 0) and the dragon spawns there, and the four crystals explode. The sequence lasts exactly 604 ticks.
Do not destroy any of the four crystals: that cancels the summoning. The crystals on the pillars cannot be destroyed during the sequence.
Pick up the dragon egg first: if you start re-summoning without picking it up, the egg disappears.
Rewards: 500 XP per respawned dragon, and an End gateway on each kill until there are 20.
materials: 4 end crystals (each: 7 glass + 1 eye of ender + 1 ghast tear)
Total: 28 glass, 4 eyes of ender, 4 ghast tears
editionNote: In Bedrock Edition the crystals can be placed one block outward in all or any of the four directions. The dragon egg appears only the first time the dragon is slain in Java Edition, and the first and second time in Bedrock Edition.
versions: Per the Minecraft Wiki Ender Dragon page: respawned dragons have dropped 500 experience since 15w33c.

faq.q: Do I get another dragon egg from a respawned dragon?
faq.a: In Java Edition only the first kill drops it. In Bedrock Edition it appears the first and second time. If you re-summon without picking it up, it disappears.

faq.q: How much XP does a respawned dragon give?
faq.a: 500 XP, compared with 12,000 for the first kill.

faq.q: How many End gateways can generate?
faq.a: Each defeat creates one, and no more generate once there are 20.

faq.q: What cancels the summoning?
faq.a: Destroying any of the four end crystals around the exit portal.

name: How to Make a Snow Golem in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Stack 2 snow blocks vertically and place a carved pumpkin or jack o'lantern on top, last. A snow golem appears. It throws snowballs at monsters (they only damage blazes, but knock mobs back), leaves a snow trail, and takes damage in rain, water and hot biomes unless it has Fire Resistance.
steps: Get 2 snow blocks and a carved pumpkin or jack o'lantern.

Stack the 2 snow blocks vertically, then place the pumpkin on top. A player, dispenser, enderman or command can place it, but not a piston. The pattern also works sideways or upside-down, as long as the pumpkin goes last.

The snow golem moves toward monsters (except ghasts and undead mounts) and throws one snowball per second from up to 10 blocks away, or 16 if it was captured. Snowballs do damage only to blazes, but knock back anything they hit, and they provoke mobs to attack the golem. It never intentionally attacks you.
It leaves a trail of snow where blocks can support it. In Java this happens in any biome; in Bedrock the trail is not generated in hot biomes. If mobGriefing is false, no trail appears.
It takes 1 HP of damage per tick in rain, water and biomes with temperature above 1.0 (such as badlands, deserts and Nether biomes). The Fire Resistance effect lets it survive there. It has 4 HP.
Shear it to remove the pumpkin, which drops as an item. In Java you can only give it a pumpkin again with a command such as /data.
When it dies it drops 0-15 snowballs.
editionNote: Java: the snow trail generates in any biome, and savannas count as hot biomes for damage. Bedrock: no trail in hot biomes (jungles, mushroom fields, savannas, stony peaks, deserts, badlands, Nether), a snowball that hits you gives knockback and makes tamed wolves and trusting foxes attack the golem, and its snowballs can set mobs on fire after passing through lava or fire.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.q: Why did my snow golem die in the desert or the Nether?
faq.a: Snow golems take damage in rain, water and in biomes with a temperature above 1.0, such as badlands, deserts and Nether biomes. Fire Resistance lets them survive in those biomes.

faq.q: Do snow golem snowballs deal damage?
faq.a: Only to blazes. They knock back any mob they hit, and they provoke monsters to attack the golem.

faq.q: Does a snow golem attack me?
faq.a: No, it never intentionally attacks the player. In Bedrock, a snowball that hits you gives knockback and makes tamed wolves and trusting foxes attack the golem.

faq.q: What do snow golems drop?
faq.a: 0 to 15 snowballs when killed, and 1 carved pumpkin when sheared.

name: How to Make an Ender Chest in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft an ender chest from obsidian and an eye of ender. It has 27 slots, all ender chests in the world are linked (even across dimensions), and each player has their own separate contents. Break it with a Silk Touch pickaxe to get the chest back, otherwise it drops 8 obsidian.
steps: Craft the ender chest: 8 obsidian in a ring around 1 eye of ender in the center.
Place the ender chest and open it with the use control. A solid block above it stops it from opening.
Use it like a normal chest, but every ender chest in the world, in any dimension, shares the same contents for you. Other players see their own contents, never yours.
Items inside stay even if you die. If the ender chest is destroyed, its items are not dropped and can be retrieved by accessing or placing another ender chest.
To move it, mine it with a Silk Touch pickaxe: it drops itself. Without Silk Touch it drops 8 obsidian.

Piglins become hostile toward players who open or break an ender chest.
materials: A Silk Touch pickaxe to pick the chest back up
editionNote: Ender chests have 27 slots, per-player contents and a link across all dimensions. They do not combine into double chests and do not interact with hoppers, droppers or comparators. Donkeys, mules and llamas cannot carry them, and the ender dragon can still destroy them.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.q: Can other players open my ender chest?
faq.a: They can open the block, but they see their own contents. Items in your ender chest cannot be seen or taken by other players.

faq.q: Do ender chests work across dimensions?
faq.a: Yes. All ender chests in the world are interconnected, including in different dimensions.

faq.q: Why did my ender chest drop obsidian?
faq.a: Without Silk Touch it drops 8 obsidian. With Silk Touch it drops itself.

faq.q: What happens to my items if the ender chest breaks?

name: How to Make a Hopper in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft a hopper from a chest and 5 iron ingots. It has 5 slots. Unless powered by redstone, it pushes one item into the container it faces, pulls one item from a container above it, and collects dropped items above it. A redstone signal locks all three functions.
steps: Craft the hopper: 5 iron ingots and 1 chest. The chest goes in the center, with iron ingots in the top-left, top-right, middle-left, middle-right and bottom-center slots.
Place it so its output points at the container you want to fill. Its facing is the direction its output points, and it pushes items only into containers in that direction.

It then works on its own: it pushes a single item from its inventory into the container it faces, pulls a single item from a container above it, and collects item entities from the space above it. It first tries to push, then to pull, and if there is no container above, it collects items.
After collecting an item (or stack), a hopper has an 8-game-tick cooldown (0.4 seconds).
Lock it with redstone: while powered, the hopper does not push, pull or collect. A locked hopper can still receive items from droppers, crafters and other hoppers.
Chain hoppers into pipes to move items over distance. Locking one hopper stops a horizontal pipe, but a vertical pipe needs two adjacent hoppers locked.
Read how full a hopper is with a redstone comparator. Hoppers also work with furnaces and brewing stands: a hopper on top of a brewing stand only deposits into the ingredient slot.
editionNote: In Java, pistons cannot move hoppers. In Bedrock, a hopper can only be locked on the input redstone tick. Hoppers also generate above barrels in trial chambers.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.q: How fast is a hopper?
faq.a: After moving or collecting an item it waits 8 game ticks (0.4 seconds). Hoppers collect groups of dropped items all at once, so they collect item entities much faster than they pull from containers.

faq.q: Why won't my hopper fill the chest next to it?
faq.a: A hopper pushes only into the container in the direction its output faces. Check which way it points.

faq.q: How do I stop a hopper?
faq.a: Give it a redstone signal. All three functions stop. A locked hopper can still receive items from droppers, crafters and other hoppers.

faq.q: How many items does a hopper hold?
faq.a: It has 5 slots of inventory.

keywords: hopper minecraft craft 5 iron ingots chest item transfer redstone lock furnace brewing stand

name: How to Make a Compass in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft a compass from iron ingots and redstone dust. It points horizontally toward the Overworld's spawn point. Use it on a lodestone to get a lodestone compass that points to that lodestone, even in the Nether or the End.
steps: Craft the compass: 4 iron ingots in a plus shape (top, left, right and bottom) around 1 redstone dust in the center.
Read it: it points in the horizontal direction of the Overworld's spawn point. It does so in the inventory, in your hand or in an item frame.
If its target is in a different dimension, or is a broken lodestone, it spins in random directions. That is why a plain compass is useless in the Nether and the End.
Craft a lodestone from 8 chiseled stone bricks around 1 iron ingot, or find one: bastion remnant bridge chests (100%) and ruined portal chests (66.7%, 1 to 2).
Use the compass on the lodestone. It now points to that lodestone, shown by an enchantment glint, and this works in the End and the Nether too.
If the lodestone breaks, or you are in another dimension, the compass spins randomly again.

You can also loot compasses: village cartographer's chests (26.3%), ancient city chests (16.5%), stronghold library chests (10.9% Java, 10.5% Bedrock), shipwreck map chests (7.7%) and trial chambers intersection barrels (5.9%).
materials: For a lodestone compass: a lodestone (8 chiseled stone bricks around 1 iron ingot)
editionNote: Both editions use the same compass and lodestone behavior. In Bedrock, the compass also points at its target in the crafting table preview. The stronghold chest chance differs slightly (10.9% Java, 10.5% Bedrock).
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.q: What does a compass point to?
faq.a: The horizontal direction of the Overworld's spawn point.

faq.q: Why does my compass spin in the Nether?
faq.a: Its target is in a different dimension, so it spins randomly. Link it to a lodestone in that dimension.

faq.q: How do I make a lodestone?
faq.a: Craft it from chiseled stone bricks and an iron ingot, or loot it in bastion remnants and ruined portals.

faq.q: Where can I find a compass?
faq.a: In village cartographer's chests, ancient cities, strongholds, shipwrecks and trial chambers, among others.

name: How to Make a Fishing Rod in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft a fishing rod from sticks and string. Cast it into water, wait for the stream of bubbles to reach the bobber and reel in when it bites to get a fish, junk or a treasure item. Durability is 64 in Java and 385 in Bedrock.
steps: Craft the fishing rod: 3 sticks in a diagonal from bottom-left to top-right, and 2 string in the right column, below the top stick.
Cast it into water. After a short wait a stream of bubbles approaches the bobber.

quickAnswer: Craft shears from iron ingots. Use them to shear sheep, mooshrooms, snow golems and bogged, to harvest honeycomb from full beehives, to carve pumpkins and to collect leaves, vines and cobwebs as items. Durability is 238 in Java and 239 in Bedrock.

Open a crafting table. Every armor piece follows the same idea - fill the outline of that piece with diamonds.

materials: 24 diamonds (full set): helmet 5, chestplate 8, leggings 7, boots 4

name: How to Find a Village in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Villages generate in plains, meadow, desert, savanna, taiga and snowy plains biomes. Walk or ride in one direction scanning the horizon, buy an explorer map from a cartographer, or use /locate if cheats are on.
steps: Know where they generate: villages generate in plains, meadow, desert, savanna, taiga and snowy plains biomes. Bedrock Edition adds snowy taiga and sunflower plains. They do not generate in forests, jungles or oceans.

Spawn check: villages are fairly common near spawn. There is about a 1 in 2 chance of at least one within 500 blocks of the world spawn point in Java and about 2 in 3 in Bedrock. If you start in a forest, walk out of it and scan the flat biomes first.
Travel smart: pick one direction and keep going. A boat along a coast, a horse across plains, or an elytra later on all beat wandering in circles.
Climb and scan: at dawn or dusk, get on the highest hill around and look for the regular grid of houses, lit windows and paths - villages are easy to spot from height.
Use a cartographer: any cartographer villager sells explorer maps that lead to a village of a specific type (plains, desert, savanna, taiga or snowy), depending on where he spawned.
Use commands if cheats are on: in Java, /locate structure #village prints the nearest village of any type. In Bedrock, use /locate structure village.
Found one? Secure it: wall or light the village, ring the bell to gather villagers, and consider building your trading hall and iron farm there.
Bonus: 2% of villages generate as abandoned villages. Their villagers are zombie villagers, which you can cure into normal villagers.
editionNote: Bedrock Edition also generates villages in snowy taiga and sunflower plains. The /locate command differs: Java uses /locate structure #village, Bedrock uses /locate structure village. Villages are slightly more common in Bedrock.

name: How to Find Amethyst in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Find amethyst geodes between Y=-58 and Y=30 in the Overworld. Look for their smooth basalt shell and white calcite layer in caves or underwater. Each chunk has a 1 in 24 chance to attempt geode generation, and geodes have a 95% chance to generate with a crack.
steps: Know the target: amethyst geodes generate between Y=-58 and Y=30 in the Overworld. Search underground or underwater for their outer shell.
Explore caves in that height range: geodes have a 95% chance to generate with a crack that exposes their hollow interior.
Spot the shell: the outer layer is smooth basalt (dark grey), the middle ring is calcite (white) - either block peeking out of a cave wall means a geode is behind it.
Dig in: the inside is lined with amethyst blocks and budding amethyst. Amethyst buds and clusters grow only on budding amethyst blocks.
Harvest clusters, not buds: only the fully grown amethyst cluster drops shards. Break it with a pickaxe for 4 shards - by hand or piston you only get 2.
Use Fortune: Fortune III raises the average to 8.8 shards per cluster. Use Silk Touch only if you want to move the cluster block itself for decoration.
Protect budding amethyst: it drops nothing, even with Silk Touch. A piston destroys it instead of moving it. Leave it in place to grow more buds and clusters.
Craft tinted glass: put 1 glass in the center of a crafting table and 1 amethyst shard directly above, below, left and right of it. The 4 shards and 1 glass produce 2 tinted glass.
Craft a spyglass: fill one vertical column of a crafting table with 1 amethyst shard at the top and 1 copper ingot in each of the two slots below it. This produces 1 spyglass; no stick is needed.
Craft a block of amethyst: arrange 4 amethyst shards in a 2 by 2 square to produce 1 block of amethyst.
editionNote: In both editions, budding amethyst is unobtainable in Survival and cannot be moved. In Bedrock, a new amethyst bud can also form in flowing water, replacing the water block.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

name: How to Find a Bastion Remnant in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Bastion remnants generate in every Nether biome except basalt deltas, though parts can extend into them. Look for large blackstone structures. Nether structure regions are 432 by 432 blocks in Java and 480 by 480 in Bedrock; each region can generate a bastion or a fortress, not both.

Wear a gold armor piece to avoid provoking ordinary piglins just by being nearby. Gold does not protect you from piglin brutes, or from piglins angered by opening containers, mining gold or attacking piglins.
Search Nether biomes other than basalt deltas. A bastion can extend into basalt deltas, but cannot start generating there.
Look for large blackstone buildings with ramparts and passages. Explore carefully rather than relying on a fixed search height, and watch for lava and drops.
Expand your search beyond the region containing a fortress. Regions are 432 by 432 blocks in Java and 480 by 480 in Bedrock; moving a fixed distance does not guarantee a new region or a bastion.
With cheats enabled, run /locate structure minecraft:bastion_remnant in Java or /locate structure bastion_remnant in Bedrock while in the Nether to find bastion coordinates.
Identify the variant: bridge, hoglin stables, housing units or treasure room. Treasure rooms have bridges above a lava floor, a magma cube spawner and a central gold-and-loot area.

Iron armor or better, shield, food

name: How to Find Lush Caves in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Look for a naturally generated azalea tree with oak logs and azalea leaves: its rooted dirt leads down toward lush caves. Search beneath humid terrain such as dark forests, jungles and old growth taigas. Player-grown azalea trees do not indicate a cave.
steps: Look for a naturally generated azalea tree: it has oak logs and azalea leaves, sometimes with flowers. Its roots lead toward a lush cave. Trees grown by players can appear anywhere and are not a reliable clue.

Search humid terrain: lush caves commonly generate beneath dark forests, jungles, old growth taigas, wooded badlands and taigas within frozen biomes. They do not generate beneath ordinary forests, plains or savannas, but can sometimes occur beneath oceans and deserts.

Follow rooted dirt below a natural azalea tree. Dig a staircase or check the blocks beneath you before descending so you do not fall into the cave. Rooted dirt continues down toward the lush cave, with hanging roots near its end.
Or go caving: explore any large cave system under humid terrain and watch for moss blocks, cave vines with glow berries, and clay-lined pools - that is the lush cave palette.
Confirm the biome with its vegetation: moss, cave vines with glow berries, spore blossoms and dripleaf around clay-lined pools. Underground light alone is not enough to identify a lush cave.

Look for axolotls in the water: they spawn only in lush caves, with clay less than five blocks below the spawning space. Tropical fish can inhabit the pools, and glow squid can also spawn in the biome.
Explore for moss blocks, azalea bushes, spore blossoms, glow berries, clay and dripleaf plants. These are useful resources to look for throughout the cave.
Use a water bucket to collect an axolotl. Axolotls released after being carried in a bucket do not despawn.
Stay safe: glow berries light much of the biome, but dark pockets still spawn hostile mobs - light the place as you explore.
editionNote: Lush caves and natural azalea-tree clues exist in both editions. Mob spawn tables differ between Java and Bedrock, so do not assume every mob has the same spawn weight or group size.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.q: How do you find a lush cave in Minecraft?
faq.a: Search for naturally generated azalea trees and follow their rooted dirt downward carefully. Azalea trees can also generate inside caves. A player-grown tree does not prove that a lush cave lies underneath.

faq.q: What biomes are above lush caves?

name: How to Find Dripstone Caves in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Explore underground far inland, away from oceans and coasts. Dripstone caves can generate at any altitude and contain dripstone blocks, stalactites and stalagmites. Pointed dripstone alone is not proof of the biome, since it also occurs elsewhere.
steps: Search inland: dripstone caves generate where continentalness is high - far from oceans and coasts. They essentially never appear under ocean biomes.

Explore inland cave systems: elevated mountain valleys can indicate the inland terrain where dripstone caves generate. There is no fixed search height, and a mountain does not guarantee a dripstone cave.
Do not rule out humid terrain: although lush caves often occur below humid biomes, dripstone caves can replace them when those areas are far inland.

Look for widespread dripstone blocks, hanging stalactites, rising stalagmites and small water wells. Pointed dripstone also generates outside this biome, including in trial chambers, so a lone spike is not enough to identify it.
Look for copper ore: dripstone caves generate larger copper ore blobs than other biomes. This does not mean that every deposit is large or that large ore veins are exclusive to this biome.
Watch your head - and feet: falling stalactites hurt, and landing on a stalagmite deals heavy fall damage. Never dig straight up or down here.

Grow pointed dripstone by hanging it directly under a dripstone block with a water source above that block. For a simple lava farm, put a lava source above a support block, hang 1 pointed dripstone below it, and place an empty cauldron directly beneath the tip with only air between them. Lava fills the cauldron over time but does not grow the dripstone.
Watch the aquifers: drowned can spawn in the water inside dripstone caves. Do not assume an underwater passage is safe.
editionNote: Both editions have dripstone caves and larger copper ore blobs in this biome. For dripstone growth, use a water source above a dripstone block; Java also supports a waterlogged block there. An air-only path from the tip to a cauldron works in both editions.
versions: Describes the current Java and Bedrock releases. See the edition note above for differences.

faq.q: How do you find a dripstone cave in Minecraft?
faq.a: Explore underground far inland, away from coasts. Look for widespread dripstone blocks, stalactites, stalagmites and small water wells. There is no fixed altitude to search, and an isolated pointed dripstone formation may occur outside the biome.

faq.q: What is special about dripstone caves?
faq.a: They contain extensive dripstone formations, generate larger copper ore blobs than other biomes, and allow drowned to spawn in their aquifers. Pointed dripstone can also be used in a renewable lava farm with a lava source, support block and cauldron.

faq.q: Do dripstone caves spawn under oceans?
faq.a: Dripstone caves favor high continentalness, so they are essentially never found beneath ocean biomes or bordering a coast. Far inland, they can generate even below humid terrain where lush caves would otherwise occur.

faq.q: Can stalactites kill you?
faq.a: Yes - a falling stalactite deals real damage, and falling onto a stalagmite multiplies fall damage. Mine stalactites from the side and never stand directly under one you break.

name: How to Breathe Underwater in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Four real ways: a water breathing potion (pufferfish + awkward potion, 3 or 8 minutes), a turtle shell helmet (10 extra seconds per dive), a conduit (unlimited breathing in range), and the Respiration enchantment (slower air drain).
steps: Option 1 - water breathing potion: brew an awkward potion (nether wart + water bottle) with a pufferfish at a brewing stand for 3 minutes of water breathing; add redstone to extend it to 8 minutes.
Get pufferfish: fish in any ocean or warm water with a fishing rod - pufferfish are an uncommon catch, so plan on a few minutes of fishing.

Option 2 - turtle shell: breed two seagrass-fed turtles, protect the eggs, and collect 5 scutes when the babies grow up. Craft the 5 scutes into a turtle shell helmet - it gives 10 seconds of water breathing every time you dive.

Option 3 - conduit: the endgame answer. Build a conduit frame underwater (prismarine ring, 16-42 blocks) and conduit power gives unlimited water breathing, night vision and faster mining in a huge radius.
Option 4 - Respiration enchant: Respiration III on a helmet slows your air drain to about 60 seconds of diving - combine it with a turtle shell for 70+ seconds.
Emergency air in Java: doors, signs, ladders, trapdoors and fences placed underwater create air pockets where you can refill your bubbles - a classic Java-only survival trick.
Bubble columns: magma block columns pull you down fast and restore your air as you travel; soul sand pushes you up. They refill bubbles, so build them into your underwater bases.
Do not forget light: underwater visibility is dark - water breathing plus night vision (golden carrot potion) is the real ocean monument combo.
materials: Prismarine + nautilus shells + heart of the sea (conduit route)
editionNote: Air-pocket blocks (doors, signs, ladders) work only in Java - in Bedrock they flood. In Bedrock, waterlogged beds can be used underwater with water breathing. Potions, turtle shells and conduits work identically in both editions.
versions: Water breathing potions have existed since Java 1.7.2 (2013) as brewed potions, the turtle shell arrived with Update Aquatic 1.13 (2018) alongside conduits and bubble columns.

faq.q: How do you make a water breathing potion in Minecraft?
faq.a: Brew a water bottle with nether wart to get an awkward potion, then add a pufferfish: that is a 3-minute water breathing potion. Add redstone dust to extend it to 8 minutes.

faq.q: What helmet lets you breathe underwater?
faq.a: The turtle shell - 5 turtle scutes crafted like a helmet. It grants 10 seconds of water breathing that refreshes every time you surface, and pairs with Respiration III for long dives.

faq.q: Can you breathe underwater forever in Minecraft?
faq.a: Yes, with a conduit: inside its range (up to 96 blocks) conduit power gives permanent water breathing, underwater night vision and faster mining. Outside a conduit, chain 8-minute potions.

faq.q: Do torches give air underwater?
faq.a: In Java, placing a torch, door or sign against your face underwater briefly creates an air pocket that refills your bubbles. None of these work in Bedrock - use bubble columns or potions instead.

keywords: breathe underwater minecraft water breathing potion pufferfish turtle shell scutes conduit respiration enchant air pocket door bubble column night vision

name: How to Find Copper in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Copper ore generates everywhere from Y=-16 to Y=112, peaking at Y=47-48 - just mine around sea level. For serious quantities, go to dripstone caves, where copper blobs reach 52 blocks instead of the usual 16.
steps: Mine at the right height: copper ore generates between Y=-16 and Y=112 and is most common at Y=47-48 - normal hill and cave mining around those levels is all it takes.
Use a stone pickaxe or better: copper ore drops raw copper only with a stone pickaxe or higher; a wooden pickaxe destroys the block.
Smelt it: copper ore drops 2-5 raw copper per block (Fortune multiplies that, up to around 20 with Fortune III). Smelt raw copper in any furnace for copper ingots.

Best biome - dripstone caves: inside dripstone caves the copper blobs grow to 0-52 blocks instead of 0-16, and large copper ore veins generate bigger on average. One dripstone session can yield stacks of copper.
Hunt ore veins: above Y=0, rare ore veins mix copper ore with granite and raw copper blocks - a single vein can hold thousands of ingots.
Below Y=0 the ore becomes deepslate copper ore: same drops, slower to mine.

Know what it is for: copper tools, weapons and armor (the 2025 copper tier between stone and iron), copper golems, lightning rods, spyglasses, brushes, and a whole family of building blocks - copper blocks, grates, bulbs, doors and trapdoors.
Manage oxidation: exposed copper slowly turns from orange to green through four stages. Scrape it with an axe to revert one stage, or combine it with honeycomb to wax it and freeze the color forever.
editionNote: Copper generation is identical in Java and Bedrock, including the larger dripstone-cave blobs. Both editions got the copper tool and armor tier and the copper golem in the 2025 drop.
versions: Copper ore was added in Java 1.17, Caves and Cliffs Part I, on June 8, 2021. The 2025 drop expanded copper into a full tool, weapon and armor tier and added the copper golem.

faq.q: What Y level is best for copper in Minecraft?
faq.a: Y=47-48 is the generation peak, with ore from Y=-16 to Y=112. In dripstone caves the blobs are more than three times bigger, making that biome the best copper source overall.

faq.q: How much raw copper does copper ore drop?
faq.a: 2-5 raw copper per block without enchantments - already the most generous common ore. Fortune raises it further, up to about 20 raw copper with Fortune III.

faq.q: Why is my copper turning green?
faq.a: Oxidation: exposed copper blocks slowly weather through four stages from orange to fully green over a few in-game days. Wax them with honeycomb to lock the color, or scrape with an axe to reverse one stage.

faq.q: Is copper better than iron?
faq.a: No - the copper tier sits between stone and iron. Its real value is building (oxidizing blocks), copper golems, lightning rods and spyglasses. Skip copper tools unless you are early or decorating.

keywords: copper ore minecraft where to find best y level Y48 raw copper smelt dripstone caves oxidation wax honeycomb copper golem lightning rod spyglass

name: How to Find an Ocean Monument in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Ocean monuments generate in deep ocean biomes, at most one per 512x512 block area. The reliable way: buy an ocean explorer map from a journeyman cartographer villager (13 emeralds + compass) - it marks the nearest monument directly.
steps: Get an ocean explorer map: journeyman-level cartographers sell them for 13 emeralds and a compass. This is the intended, guaranteed route - the map marks the monument with a red dot.

Or sail the deep oceans: monuments only generate in deep ocean biome variants (deep ocean, deep lukewarm, deep cold, deep frozen). A boat, night vision potions and a high vantage point help you spot the prismarine silhouette glowing with sea lanterns.
Or use commands: /locate structure minecraft:ocean_monument prints the nearest coordinates.
Know the spacing: at most one monument generates per 512x512 block area, so if you find none in one ocean, keep sailing - every deep ocean region has its shot.
Prepare for the dive: water breathing potions (8 minutes), night vision, good armor, a sword or trident, food, and doors or other air-pocket blocks if you play Java. Milk buckets cure Mining Fatigue.
Expect Mining Fatigue: each of the three elder guardians periodically inflicts Mining Fatigue III for 5 minutes, making blocks nearly unbreakable. Kill the elders first or bring milk.
Kill the three elder guardians: one in the top room, one in each wing. Each drops a wet sponge, plus prismarine shards and a tide armor trim chance.

Loot the monument: the treasure chamber in the central section hides 8 gold blocks inside dark prismarine, sponge rooms hold around 30 wet sponges each, and the whole structure is made of prismarine, prismarine bricks, dark prismarine and sea lanterns.
Plan a guardian farm: guardians spawn only inside the monument's bounding box - draining or flooding it with soul-sand currents turns it into the best XP and prismarine farm in the game.
editionNote: Monument generation and loot are the same in both editions, and milk clears Mining Fatigue in both. Guardian farms built by draining the monument work identically in Java and Bedrock.
versions: Ocean monuments were added in Java 1.8, the Bountiful Update, on September 2, 2014, together with guardians and prismarine. Pocket Edition received them in 0.16.0.

faq.q: Where do ocean monuments spawn in Minecraft?
faq.a: In deep ocean biome variants only, at most one per 512x512 block area. Buy an ocean explorer map from a journeyman cartographer to mark the nearest one, or use /locate structure minecraft:ocean_monument.

faq.q: How do you get rid of Mining Fatigue from an elder guardian?
faq.a: Drink a milk bucket - it clears Mining Fatigue III instantly. The elder guardians reapply it roughly every minute while you are nearby, so kill the three elders (top room and both wings) as fast as possible.

faq.q: What loot is in an ocean monument?
faq.a: 8 gold blocks in the central treasure chamber, wet sponges (around 30 per sponge room, plus one from each elder guardian), prismarine blocks and sea lanterns everywhere, and tide armor trims from elder guardians.

faq.q: Can guardians spawn outside the monument?
faq.a: No - guardians spawn only inside the ocean monument's bounding box, which is exactly why drained monuments make such efficient guardian farms.

keywords: ocean monument minecraft how to find deep ocean explorer map cartographer elder guardian mining fatigue gold blocks sponge room prismarine guardian farm

name: How to Get a Sponge in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Sponges can only be found in ocean monuments. Each elder guardian drops 1 wet sponge, and sponge rooms hold about 30 wet sponges each on average. Dry them in a furnace or in the Nether.
steps: Find an ocean monument: they sit in deep ocean biomes and are the only place sponges are found.
Kill the elder guardians: a monument always has three (one at the top, one in each wing), and each drops 1 wet sponge.
Look for sponge rooms: monuments can have them, and each room contains an average of 30 wet sponges.
Mine sponges by hand or with any tool: a hoe is the quickest.
Dry a wet sponge in a furnace with any fuel. If a bucket is in the fuel slot when it finishes, the water drains into the bucket.
Or place a wet sponge in the Nether: it dries instantly with a puff of steam.
Use a dry sponge: it instantly absorbs flowing and source water up to 6 blocks away (taxicab distance) in all six directions, then turns into a wet sponge.
materials: Furnace or Nether access for drying
editionNote: In Bedrock Edition, a wet sponge placed in any dry Overworld biome dries after a few minutes. In a dry biome a normal sponge that absorbs water dries out immediately with a puff of steam.
versions: Facts come from the Minecraft Wiki Sponge and Ocean Monument pages.

faq.q: Where do sponges come from?
faq.a: Only ocean monuments: elder guardians and sponge rooms.

faq.q: How do I dry a wet sponge?
faq.a: Smelt it in a furnace, or place it in the Nether. In Bedrock a dry biome also works after a few minutes.

faq.q: How far does a sponge absorb water?
faq.a: Up to 6 blocks away by taxicab distance, in all six directions.

faq.q: What tool mines a sponge fastest?
faq.a: A hoe. Any tool or your hand also works.

name: How to Breed Turtles in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Feed seagrass to two turtles on a beach - one returns to its home beach and lays 1-4 eggs. Eggs crack three times and hatch at night in about 4-5 days; protect them from zombies, and each grown baby drops a scute for the turtle shell helmet.
steps: Find turtles: they spawn on beaches (not snowy or stony shores) in small groups. You need two.
Gather seagrass: use shears on seagrass in any ocean or river - punching it drops nothing.
Breed them: hold seagrass and feed both turtles. They enter love mode, and one becomes pregnant and digs in the sand.
The home beach rule: the pregnant turtle always travels back to the beach where it hatched (or where its eggs were placed) to lay. Breed turtles near your base by moving eggs with Silk Touch first.
Protect the eggs: the turtle lays 1-4 eggs in the sand. Zombies, husks, drowned and skeletons actively seek and stomp turtle eggs - fence and light the area, or stand guard.
Wait for the cracks: eggs crack three times on random ticks, more often at night, and typically hatch in 4-5 in-game days. All eggs in one block hatch at once.
Guard the babies: baby turtles are tiny and targeted by many mobs. Keep them fenced until they grow.
Harvest the scutes: when a baby turtle matures into an adult it drops exactly 1 turtle scute - five scutes craft the turtle shell helmet with built-in water breathing.
Scale up: an egg farm with Silk-Touched eggs placed on one protected beach gives you a steady scute pipeline - breed, fence, wait, repeat.
No leads: turtles cannot be leashed - lead them with seagrass in hand (they follow within 10 blocks) or move the eggs with Silk Touch instead.
materials: Fences and torches to protect the eggs
editionNote: Turtle breeding and egg mechanics are identical in Java and Bedrock. In both editions the home-beach behavior, 3-stage cracking and mob-stomping rules are the same.
versions: Turtles were added in Java 1.13, the Update Aquatic, on July 18, 2018, together with scutes, the turtle shell and potion of the Turtle Master. Bedrock got them in 1.5.0.

faq.q: How do you breed turtles in Minecraft?
faq.a: Feed seagrass (cut with shears) to two turtles on a beach. The pregnant one returns to its home beach and lays 1-4 eggs in the sand, which hatch in about 4-5 in-game days, mostly at night.

faq.q: Why won't my turtle lay eggs?
faq.a: It is not on its home beach - pregnant turtles only dig on the beach where they hatched. Wait for it to walk there, or move the eggs it already laid with Silk Touch to your preferred beach: relocated babies adopt the new home.

faq.q: What eats turtle eggs in Minecraft?
faq.a: Zombies, zombie villagers, husks, drowned, skeletons and their variants actively hunt and stomp turtle eggs, and several mobs attack baby turtles. Fence and light the nesting beach.

faq.q: How do you get turtle scutes?
faq.a: Scutes drop only when a baby turtle grows into an adult - one per turtle. There is no other source, so breeding turtles is the only way to craft the turtle shell helmet.

keywords: breed turtles minecraft seagrass turtle eggs home beach hatch night scute turtle shell helmet silk touch zombie stomp egg farm

name: How to Get Blaze Rods in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Blaze rods drop only from blazes, which live in nether fortresses. A blaze drops 0-1 rods (50%) when killed by a player or a tamed wolf, up to 0-4 with Looting III. Blazes need light level 11 or less to spawn, and fortresses can have up to two blaze spawner platforms.
steps: Enter the Nether with gear: armor, a shield, a bow and food. Blazes attack with volleys of three small fireballs and set you on fire.
Find a nether fortress: blazes are found there and nowhere else, and the wiki lists them as the only source of blaze rods.
Locate a blaze spawner: a fortress can generate up to two blaze spawner platforms, each surrounded by nether brick fences and reached by a three-block staircase.
Kill blazes: they drop 0-1 blaze rods by default (50%), 0-2 with Looting I, 0-3 with II and 0-4 with III. They only drop when killed by a player or a tamed wolf.
Farm the spawner: blazes always require light level 11 or less to spawn, so a spawner keeps producing them in the dark. Build a safe killing area.
Use the rods: blaze rods are required to craft brewing stands and blaze powder. Blaze powder fuels brewing stands and is needed to craft eyes of ender.
editionNote: The Minecraft Wiki notes blazes may spawn naturally in fortresses in groups of 2 or 3 in Java Edition and from 1 to 3 in Bedrock Edition.
versions: Per the Minecraft Wiki, blazes are the only source of blaze rods.

faq.q: Where do you get blaze rods?
faq.a: Only from blazes, which are found in nether fortresses and their spawners.

faq.q: What is the blaze rod drop chance?
faq.a: 0-1 by default (50%), up to 0-4 with Looting III, only when killed by a player or a tamed wolf.

faq.q: What are blaze rods for?
faq.a: Brewing stands and blaze powder, which fuels brewing and crafts eyes of ender.

name: How to Get Nether Wart in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Nether wart grows in nether fortress stairwell gardens (about 20 plants) and in housing-unit bastion courtyards (1, 5 or 6 plants). Plant it on soul sand in any dimension - no light or water needed - and harvest at full growth for 2-4 warts.
steps: Find a nether fortress: the standard source. Check the small soul sand gardens beside interior stairwells - about 20 nether wart plants grow there per garden, and fortress chests can hold more.
Or raid a bastion: housing-unit bastion remnants grow nether wart in their central courtyards - exactly 1, 5 or 6 plants per courtyard.
Harvest everything you find: break any mature crop (tall, deep red) for 2-4 nether wart, and younger ones for 1. Take it all - one garden is enough to start an infinite farm.
Use Fortune: a Fortune tool raises the mature drop by +1 per level, up to 7 warts from one fully grown crop. Young crops always drop just 1.
Plant on soul sand: nether wart grows ONLY on soul sand - not soul soil, not dirt. Place the farm anywhere: the Overworld, your base, even the End.
Forget light and water: growth ignores light level and hydration completely. A dark closet works as well as a garden.
Skip the bone meal: bone meal does nothing on nether wart. It grows through 4 stages on random ticks - about 34 minutes from planting to full growth on average.
Scale the farm: each mature crop replants into 2-4 more plants, so every harvest multiplies your field. A few cycles turn 20 warts into hundreds.
Spend it on brewing: nether wart + water bottle = awkward potion, the base of almost every useful potion in the game. It also crafts red nether bricks and nether wart blocks for building.
materials: A nether fortress or bastion remnant
editionNote: Identical mechanics in both editions: soul sand only, 4 stages, no bone meal, Fortune scaling on mature crops. In Java the debug screen shows the exact growth stage (age 0-3).
versions: Nether wart was added in Java Beta 1.9 Prerelease in September 2011, together with blazes and brewing - it has been the foundation of alchemy ever since. Pocket Edition got it in v0.12.1.

faq.q: Where do you find nether wart in Minecraft?
faq.a: In nether fortresses (soul sand gardens near stairwells, about 20 plants, plus chest loot) and in the central courtyards of housing-unit bastion remnants (exactly 1, 5 or 6 plants). It generates nowhere else.

faq.q: Can you grow nether wart in the Overworld?
faq.a: Yes - nether wart grows in any dimension as long as it is planted on soul sand. Light, water and biome are all irrelevant; it grows through 4 stages in about 34 minutes on average.

faq.q: Does bone meal work on nether wart?
faq.a: No - bone meal has no effect. Nether wart advances one stage on random ticks only (10% chance per tick), so patience is the only accelerator.

faq.q: Why won't my nether wart plant?
faq.a: It only plants on soul sand. Soul soil does not work, and neither does farmland or dirt. Bring soul sand back from the Nether and the farm works anywhere.

name: How to Get String in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Kill spiders or cave spiders (0-2 string, up to 0-5 with Looting III), break cobwebs with a sword, or kill striders in the Nether (2-5 string, up to 2-8 with Looting III). Tamed cats, piglin bartering, tripwire and loot chests also give string.
steps: Hunt spiders and cave spiders: they drop 0-2 string by default (0-3 with Looting I, 0-4 with II, 0-5 with III), with a 66.67% chance of at least 1 by default.
Kill striders in the Nether: they drop 2-5 string by default, up to 2-8 with Looting III.
Break cobwebs with a sword: cobwebs also drop string when pushed by a piston or washed away by flowing water (flowing lava destroys them without leaving string).
Break tripwire: it can be broken instantly with any tool and drops string. Five pieces of tripwire generate in every jungle pyramid, and several appear next to dispensers in trial chambers.
Sleep near a tamed cat: it has a 70% chance of giving a gift when you wake up, and 16.13% of gifts are string.
Barter with piglins: a gold ingot has a ~4.26% chance (20 in 469) to return 3-9 string.
Loot chests: monster rooms and woodland mansions (1-8, 57.8%), desert pyramids (1-8, 59%), pillager outposts (1-6, 39.1%).
Use it: bow, fishing rod, crossbow, lead, loom, scaffolding and white wool (4 string).

steps: Kill endermen: they drop 0-1 ender pearls by default (50%), 0-2 with Looting I, 0-3 with II and 0-4 with III. They become hostile if you hit them or look directly at their face, and a carved pumpkin on your head stops the eye-contact trigger.

Trade with an expert-level cleric villager: 5 emeralds for 1 ender pearl.
Loot a woodland mansion: the trapped chest in the fake end portal room always has 2 ender pearls. Trial chambers corridor chests can also hold 1-2.

name: How to Get Obsidian in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Pour water over a lava source block: obsidian forms where flowing water touches still lava. Mine it with a diamond or netherite pickaxe (anything else drops nothing), or barter with piglins (~8.53% for 1 obsidian per gold ingot).
steps: Find a lava source block: lava pools generate on the surface, in caves and in the Nether.
Pour water from a bucket onto the lava source blocks: flowing water touching a still lava source turns it into obsidian. Flowing lava makes cobblestone instead, so aim for the sources.
Mine it with a diamond or netherite pickaxe: obsidian takes 9.4 seconds with a diamond pickaxe and 8.35 with netherite. With a weaker tool it takes longer and drops nothing.

Renewable sources: the 25-obsidian platform in the End regenerates every time an entity enters the End, nether portals generate obsidian when created, and lava can be farmed with cauldrons under pointed dripstone.
Barter with piglins: a gold ingot gives a ~8.53% chance of 1 obsidian, the fastest way to stack it up without mining.
Loot chests: ruined portal chests (1-2 obsidian, ~46%), bastion remnant generic chests (4-6, ~24%), village weaponsmith chests (3-7, ~23%) and nether fortress chests (2-4, ~7%).
editionNote: In Java Edition, a nether portal generated midair creates 4 extra obsidian blocks at the bottom. Blue wither skulls can destroy obsidian, since they ignore blast resistance.
versions: In 1.16 (20w07a) piglins offered obsidian with a ~0.92% chance; in 20w09a it rose to ~8.85% in stacks of 1-5. Today it is ~8.53% (40/469) for a single block, per the Minecraft Wiki Obsidian page.

faq.q: What pickaxe do you need to mine obsidian?
faq.a: Diamond or netherite only. With any other pickaxe obsidian takes far longer and drops nothing when it breaks.

faq.q: Can you make obsidian infinitely?
faq.a: Yes. The End's 25-block obsidian platform regenerates whenever an entity goes through an end portal, nether portal frames regenerate when new portals are created, and lava is renewable via pointed dripstone and cauldrons since 1.17.

faq.q: What is obsidian used for?
faq.a: Nether portal frames (minimum 10 blocks), enchanting tables (4), ender chests (8) and beacons (3). It has a blast resistance of 1,200 and normal explosions cannot destroy it.

faq.q: Does flowing lava make obsidian?
faq.a: No. Obsidian only forms when water touches a lava SOURCE block. Water touching flowing lava makes cobblestone, and lava flowing onto water makes stone.

name: How to Make Glass in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Smelt sand or red sand in a furnace: one block of sand plus any fuel gives one block of glass. You can also buy 4 glass for 1 emerald from librarian villagers.
steps: Gather sand with any shovel: deserts and beaches are the easiest sources. Red sand from badlands works exactly the same.
Craft a furnace from 8 cobblestone if you don't have one.
Smelt the sand: put sand in the top slot and any fuel (coal, charcoal, planks, lava bucket) in the bottom. Each sand block smelts into 1 glass.
Speed it up with a super smelter: a furnace array fed by hoppers turns a desert's worth of sand into stacks of glass automatically.
Alternative: trade with librarian villagers. After the Village & Pillage update they sell 4 glass for 1 emerald in both editions.
Remember: glass drops NOTHING when broken unless the tool has Silk Touch. Always carry a Silk Touch tool if you plan to reposition windows.
materials: Fuel: coal, charcoal, planks or a lava bucket
Silk Touch tool (to move placed glass)
editionNote: Smelting and trading work identically in Java and Bedrock. One quirk: glass has no assigned tool in Java, so every tool breaks it at the same speed. Both editions need Silk Touch for glass to drop itself.
versions: Glass is one of the oldest blocks in the game: added in Java Classic 0.0.19a (June 2009), with furnace smelting of sand since Indev (February 2010). In Pocket Edition it existed from the earliest demos.

faq.q: How do you make glass in Minecraft?
faq.a: Smelt sand or red sand in a furnace with any fuel: 1 sand = 1 glass. It takes 10 seconds per block in a regular furnace, half in a blast... no, a smoker does not smelt sand; use a normal furnace.

faq.q: Why did my glass disappear when I broke it?
faq.a: Glass only drops itself when mined with a Silk Touch-enchanted tool. With any normal tool it shatters and drops nothing, in both editions.

faq.q: What can you craft with glass?

Slimes spawn in swamps and mangrove swamps at night (best on a full moon) or deep underground in slime chunks below Y=40. You can also buy them from wandering traders, get them from sneezing baby pandas, or uncraft a slime block into 9.
steps: Hunt swamps at night: slimes spawn in swamps and mangrove swamps between Y=51 and Y=69 at light level 7 or less. They spawn most often on a full moon and never on a new moon.

Or dig into a slime chunk: about 1 in 10 chunks is a slime chunk, where slimes spawn below Y=40 regardless of light. In Java the chunks depend on the world seed; in Bedrock they're at the same coordinates in every world.
Split them down: big and medium slimes don't drop anything - they split. Only the smallest slimes drop 0-2 slimeballs, and Looting adds 0-1 per level (up to 5 with Looting III).
Let frogs help: frogs eat small slimes whole and each one drops 1 slimeball - a frog pen in a swamp is an easy passive farm.
Watch baby pandas: a sneezing baby panda has a 1/700 chance to drop a slimeball. Slow, but free if you keep pandas.
Buy or uncraft: wandering traders sell 1 slimeball for 4 emeralds, and a slime block crafts back into 9 slimeballs - handy if you have blocks but need balls.
Spend them on: sticky pistons, slime blocks, magma cream, frog breeding -, and breeding frogs (they also shorten tadpole growth by 10%).
materials: A swamp at night or a slime chunk below Y=40
Optional: 4 emeralds for the wandering trader
editionNote: Two Bedrock differences: slime chunks sit at the same coordinates in every world (Java chunks depend on the seed), and killing a wandering trader who is offering slimeballs while you hold an emerald has an 8.5% chance (+1% per Looting level) to drop one.
versions: Slime size is affected by regional difficulty, per the Minecraft Wiki: from 33% for each size at low difficulty to 16% small, 33% medium and 50% big at higher difficulty.

faq.q: Where do slimes spawn?
faq.a: Two places: swamps and mangrove swamps at night between Y=51 and Y=69 (a full moon is best), and slime chunks below Y=40 where light doesn't matter. About 10% of chunks are slime chunks.

faq.q: Why aren't slimes dropping slimeballs?
faq.a: Only the smallest slimes drop slimeballs (0-2 each). Big and medium slimes split into smaller ones when killed - keep fighting until you finish the smallest size.

faq.q: Can you farm slimeballs without slimes?
faq.a: Yes: frogs eat small slimes and drop 1 slimeball each, baby pandas sneeze them out (1/700 chance), wandering traders sell them for 4 emeralds, and slime blocks uncraft into 9.

faq.q: What are slimeballs used for?
faq.a: Sticky pistons, slime blocks and magma cream, and breeding frogs.

name: How to Get a Dried Ghast in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Dried ghasts generate next to nether fossils in soul sand valleys (a 1 in 3 chance per fossil). You can also craft one with 8 ghast tears + 1 soul sand, or barter with piglins (~2.13% per gold ingot). Waterlog it and after about 20 minutes it becomes a ghastling that grows into a happy ghast.
steps: Head to a soul sand valley in the Nether - it's the only biome with nether fossils.
Search the fossils: each nether fossil has a 1/3 chance to generate with a dried ghast next to it. It mines instantly with any tool or your bare hand and always drops itself.
Or craft one: 8 ghast tears around 1 soul sand. Farm tears from ghasts - Looting III raises the drop to up to 4 per ghast.
Or barter: piglins have a 10/469 (~2.13%) chance to hand over a dried ghast per gold ingot - a gold farm plus a bartering setup works long-term.

Hydrate it: place the dried ghast so it's waterlogged (sitting in water). Green particles appear and it visibly rehydrates in stages - partially hydrated around 5 minutes, mostly hydrated around 10, fully hydrated around 15.

Wait for the ghastling: after about 20 minutes underwater it transforms into a ghastling, which grows into a rideable happy ghast. Times vary a little because stages advance on random ticks (about 5.3 minutes each on average).

Don't dry it out: remove the water and it dehydrates back at the same rate, and breaking it reverts it to the dried state instantly. On soul sand or soul soil it makes cracking sounds - eerie but harmless.
materials: Or 8 ghast tears + 1 soul sand for crafting
Or gold ingots for piglin bartering
A water bucket to hydrate it
editionNote: Behavior is identical in both editions now, but the arrival differed: Java added dried ghasts in 1.21.6, while Bedrock previewed them behind the Drop 2 2025 experiment in 1.21.80 and made them vanilla in 1.21.90. The crafting recipe started as ghast tears + bone block in early snapshots and switched to soul sand before release.
versions: Added in Java 1.21.6 and Bedrock 1.21.90 (both June 2025, the Drop 2 of 2025).

faq.q: Where do dried ghasts spawn?
faq.a: In soul sand valleys, next to nether fossils - each fossil has about a 33% chance to generate one beside it. They insta-mine with your bare hand.

faq.q: How long does a dried ghast take to hydrate?
faq.a: About 20 minutes waterlogged to become a ghastling: visible stages at roughly 5, 10 and 15 minutes. Stages advance on random ticks, so real times vary a little around the average.

faq.q: Can you craft a dried ghast?
faq.a: Yes: 8 ghast tears surrounding 1 soul sand. It's the expensive route - bartering (~2.13% per ingot) or fossil hunting is usually cheaper.

faq.q: What happens if the water is removed?
faq.a: It slowly dehydrates back to the dried state at the same rate it hydrated, and breaking the block reverts it instantly. Only a fully hydrated ghast that completes the timer becomes a ghastling.
