name: How to Get Wind Charges in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft them: 1 breeze rod makes 4 wind charges. Breeze rods come from breezes, the jumping mobs from trial chambers spawners (1-2 rods per kill, more with Looting). Wind charges also drop from vaults and ominous vaults in trial chambers.
steps: Find a trial chamber: these copper-and-tuff structures generate underground in the Overworld - our finder guide covers the fastest ways to locate one.
Locate a breeze spawner: breezes only spawn from trial spawners ringed by chiseled tuff in combat chambers (never corridors), one per chamber.
Farm breeze rods: each breeze drops 1-2 breeze rods when killed by a player, and Looting raises the haul. Breezes deflect every projectile except wind charges, so go in with melee.
Craft the charges: place 1 breeze rod in the crafting grid for 4 wind charges. Shapeless, no table needed.
Loot them too: vaults and ominous vaults in trial chambers can eject wind charges directly - free ammo while you farm rods.

Throw and bounce: a wind charge bursts on impact, dealing 1 damage and heavy knockback. Throw one at your feet mid-jump to launch yourself - you only take fall damage below the height where the burst hit you.

Use the tricks: wind charges flip non-iron doors, trapdoors, fence gates, buttons and levers, ring bells, snuff candles, break chorus flowers and shatter decorated pots. You can even deflect them mid-flight with a melee swing, like ghast fireballs.
Watch the cooldown: 0.5 seconds between throws, shown as a white overlay on the item.
materials: Melee weapon for breezes (they deflect arrows)
editionNote: Player and dispenser shots knock back 22% harder than breeze shots but burst in a smaller 2.4-block sphere (breeze shots: 6 blocks). In Bedrock a wind charge that passes through fire or lava sets hit entities alight, and the thrown projectile has a slight offset. Both editions share the same 0.5-second throw cooldown.
versions: Wind charges arrived as experimental content in Java 1.20.3 / Bedrock 1.20.60 and became official with 1.21 (Tricky Trials, June 2024). Early snapshots had breezes drop them directly; the breeze rod crafting recipe replaced that before release.

faq.q: How do you craft wind charges?
faq.a: Put 1 breeze rod anywhere in a crafting grid - it makes 4 wind charges. Breeze rods drop from breezes in trial chambers (1-2 per kill, more with Looting).

faq.q: Do wind charges hurt you?
faq.a: A direct hit deals 1 damage plus knockback. The trick is fall damage: after a burst launches you, you only accumulate fall damage below the height where the burst hit - so you can rocket-jump safely if you land high enough.

faq.q: What can wind charges activate?
faq.a: Non-iron doors and trapdoors, fence gates, buttons and levers all flip; bells ring, candles go out, chorus flowers break and decorated pots shatter. They also bounce back if you hit them with a melee attack or another projectile.

faq.q: Where else do wind charges drop?
faq.a: Vaults and ominous vaults in trial chambers can eject them as loot, so opening vaults while farming breeze rods builds your stack faster.

faq.q: What do wind charges do in Minecraft?
faq.a: They create a wind burst on impact: entities get knocked back and take 1 damage on direct hits, and redstone-weak blocks like buttons, levers, fence gates and non-iron doors flip state. Players use them for movement: a blast at your feet launches you upward and resets fall damage.

faq.q: Do wind charges hurt the player?
faq.a: The knockback affects you too, but fall damage only applies after the burst resets your fall distance. Land the timing right and you take no fall damage at all from huge drops, which is the core of wind charge movement tech.

faq.q: How many wind charges does a breeze rod make?
faq.a: Four per breeze rod. Each breeze drops 1-2 rods (up to more with Looting), so one breeze is worth 4-8 wind charges.

name: How to Get Ice in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Mine it with Silk Touch: ice drops only when the tool has Silk Touch - without it the block just vanishes (or turns into water). Find it frozen on rivers, oceans and lakes in snowy biomes, or farm it by letting water freeze in a snowy biome. Craft 9 ice into packed ice, and 9 packed ice into blue ice.
steps: Get Silk Touch first: ice drops nothing without it - mined normally, the block disappears and becomes water if there's a block underneath. Our Silk Touch guide covers the fastest ways to get the enchantment.

Find natural ice: frozen oceans, frozen rivers and snowy beaches are covered in it; lakes in any snowy biome freeze over too. You'll also see it in frozen peaks, igloo windows (Java) and the ancient city ice box.
Mine with a pickaxe: any Silk Touch tool works, but a pickaxe is fastest.

Farm your own: in a snowy biome, place water source blocks exposed to the sky with a solid block beside them and block light under 10 - they freeze into ice over time via random ticks. No sunlight melts them, only block light above 11.
Upgrade to packed ice: 9 ice in a 3x3 grid make 1 packed ice - it never melts and drops with Silk Touch too. Find it naturally in ice spikes biomes, icebergs and snowy villages.
Then blue ice: 9 packed ice make 1 blue ice - the fastest, rarest tier, also found in icebergs in frozen oceans.
Put it to work: boats hit 40 m/s on ice (1.8x faster on blue ice) and ice works in the Nether, so an ice boat highway there multiplies your Overworld travel speed by 8.
materials: A Silk Touch tool (pickaxe is fastest)
Snowy biome access (frozen ocean, frozen river...)
Water buckets if farming your own
editionNote: Behavior is nearly identical across editions. The small differences: igloos use regular ice windows in Java but packed ice in Bedrock, packed ice generates as piles in snowy villages, and ice's light-filtering differs slightly between editions. Ice never melts from sunlight in either - only block light above 11.
versions: Ice has existed since Java Alpha v1.0.4 (2010). Packed ice arrived in 1.7.2 and blue ice in 1.13, and Silk Touch has always been the only way to collect any of them.

faq.q: How do you pick up ice in Minecraft?
faq.a: Only with a Silk Touch enchanted tool. Without Silk Touch the block drops nothing - it disappears, turning into water if there's a block below it.

faq.q: Does ice melt in Minecraft?
faq.a: Regular ice melts when block light next to it is above 11 (torches, glowstone...) - sunlight never melts it. Packed ice and blue ice never melt at all.

faq.q: How do you make packed ice and blue ice?
faq.a: Craft 9 ice into 1 packed ice, then 9 packed ice into 1 blue ice. Neither crafts back down. Packed ice also generates in ice spikes biomes, icebergs and snowy villages; blue ice appears in icebergs.

faq.q: What is ice used for?
faq.a: Speed. Boats reach 40 m/s on ice (blue ice is 1.8x faster), sprint-jumping in a 2-block corridor is the fastest way to run, water streams over ice move items quicker, and ice highways work in the Nether for 8x Overworld-equivalent travel.

Add delay: use the repeater to cycle 4 delay settings, from 1 to 4 redstone ticks (0.1-0.4 seconds). Repeaters in series build precise timers.
Use it as a diode: signals only flow from back to front, never backward - repeaters stop feedback loops from shorting your circuits.
Lock it: power the side of a repeater with another repeater or a comparator and it freezes in its current state - a one-bit memory cell for doors and traps.

Compare mode (front torch down): the comparator outputs the back input only if it is at least as strong as the side inputs - a minimum-signal gate.
Subtract mode: use the placed comparator once and the front torch pops up. Now it outputs the back signal MINUS the strongest side signal - analog arithmetic for smart circuits.
Preserve levels: unlike a repeater, a comparator passes the exact input strength through (up to 15), which keeps fullness readings and analog lines intact.

Diamond or netherite pickaxe to mine the crying obsidian

name: How to Trade with Villagers in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Give an unemployed villager a job site block (lectern, composter, blast furnace...) and right-click to trade. steps: Find or breed villagers, then place a job site block next to an unemployed one: lectern = librarian, composter = farmer, blast furnace = armorer, smithing table = toolsmith, grindstone = weaponsmith, cauldron = leatherworker, and so on.
Check the offered trades (right-click). Don't like them? Break the job block and place it again - the trades reroll, but ONLY if you have never traded with that villager.

Trade with emeralds and goods. Each trade gives you 3-6 XP and fills the villager's experience bar; a full bar levels it up: novice (stone badge), apprentice (iron), journeyman (gold), expert (emerald), master (diamond).
Leveling unlocks new trades - master librarians sell candles, armorers sell diamond gear, and the best enchanted books sit at the top levels.
Villagers restock up to twice per day while they can reach their job site block (in Bedrock they also need to be linked to a bed).
For permanent discounts, cure a zombie villager next to your trading hall; since 1.20.2 the big discount applies only to the first cure. The Hero of the Village effect from a raid also drops prices.
materials: Villagers (a village, or breed two with beds + food)
Job site blocks: lectern, composter, fletching table, blast furnace, smoker, grindstone, smithing table, cauldron, brewing stand, stonecutter, loom, cartography table, barrel
Emeralds (the universal currency) and sellable goods like wheat, paper, coal or rotten flesh
editionNote: Java and Bedrock differ in the details: Java villagers cap at 10 trades with 2 new ones per level, Bedrock unlocks up to 3 slots per level (7-10 total). Restocking in Bedrock requires a linked bed; in Java only access to the job site. Overusing one trade raises its price through demand in both editions.
versions: Trading as we know it dates to 1.8 (14w02a) and was completely rebalanced in 1.14 (Village & Pillage), which added job site blocks, levels and restocking. Since 1.20.2 the zombie-cure discount no longer stacks - only the first cure gives the big one.

faq.q: Why won't my villager restock its trades?
faq.a: It needs to physically reach its job site block during work hours, and it restocks at most twice per day. In Bedrock it must also be linked to a bed. Trap it in a 1x1 cell and it may never work again.

faq.q: How do I lock in a villager's trades?
faq.a: Trade with it once. From that moment its profession and its full trade list are permanent - even if you break the job block. Before that first trade, breaking and replacing the block rerolls the offers.

Nether-side portals matter too: a ruined portal near your Nether spawn is free obsidian and a landmark.
materials: Flint and steel (or from the chest)
editionNote: Ruined portals generate identically in Java and Bedrock: all biomes in both dimensions, 5% giant variants, the same loot table family including lodestones since 1.21.5. Both editions let you complete the frame and light it.
versions: Ruined portals were added in 1.16 (20w16a, the Nether Update), which is why their loot leans golden. Lodestones joined their chest loot in 1.21.5, making ruined portals a rare source of that wayfinding block.

faq.q: What is inside a ruined portal chest?
faq.a: Gold gear, gold ingots and nuggets, flint and steel, fire charges, obsidian, golden apples, enchanted golden tools, bells and clocks - thematically the leftovers of whoever broke the portal. Since 1.21.5, lodestones can appear too.

faq.q: Can I repair a ruined portal?
faq.a: Yes - that is their secret purpose. Replace the crying obsidian (it does not light) with regular obsidian, fill the gaps, and ignite with flint and steel from the chest. Many speedrunners find their first portal this way.

faq.q: Why is there crying obsidian in the frame?
faq.a: Crying obsidian is decorative and cannot form a working portal - you must mine it out (diamond or netherite pickaxe) and swap in normal obsidian. Save the crying obsidian for respawn anchors.

name: How to Make Beetroot Soup in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Combine 6 beetroots with a bowl to make beetroot soup - 6 hunger and 7.2 saturation, identical stats to mushroom stew. Beetroot comes from village farms or its seeds in chests.
steps: Get beetroot: village farms grow it (plains and desert villages especially), or find beetroot seeds in dungeon, mineshaft and village chests.
Plant the seeds and let them grow through four stages - harvest when the beetroot tops turn dark red.
Craft a bowl from 3 planks.
Place 6 beetroots in the top two rows of the crafting table with the bowl at the bottom.
Eat for 6 hunger and 7.2 saturation - exactly mushroom-stew-tier food.
The bowl comes back after eating, and like all stews it does not stack.
Leftover beetroot? Dye things red, breed pigs, or trade it to farmer villagers.
editionNote: Identical in Java and Bedrock: 6 beetroots + 1 bowl, 6 hunger and 7.2 saturation, non-stacking with the bowl returned. Beetroot itself grows the same way in both editions.
versions: Beetroot soup is a Bedrock original: it debuted in Pocket Edition v0.8.0 and only came to Java in 1.9 (15w31a). The recipe has been 6 beetroots plus a bowl since Pocket v0.9.0.

faq.q: Is beetroot soup worth making?
faq.a: Stat-wise it matches mushroom stew (6 hunger, 7.2 saturation), so it is fine - but 6 beetroots per bowl makes it expensive unless you run a beetroot farm. Most players grow beetroot for red dye and pig breeding instead.

faq.q: Where do I find beetroot seeds?
faq.a: Village farms are the fastest source - just harvest the beetroot already growing there. Seeds also show up in dungeon, mineshaft, woodland mansion and village chests, and end city chests can hold beetroot too.

faq.q: Beetroot soup or mushroom stew?
faq.a: Same hunger and saturation, same bowl back, same no-stacking. Mushroom stew wins on ingredient effort (2 mushrooms vs 6 beetroots), beetroot soup wins if your base is already a beetroot empire.

name: How to Get a Trident in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Tridents cannot be crafted. Kill drowned that spawn holding one: 6.25% of natural drowned carry a trident, and it drops with 8.5% chance in Java or 25% in Bedrock. Trial chamber vaults can also rarely give one.
steps: Find drowned: rivers, oceans and swamps at night, or any zombie that drowns underwater - but note converted zombies never carry tridents.
Hunt the ones holding a trident: 6.25% of naturally spawned drowned have one.
Kill it with Looting III if you can: base drop chance is 8.5% in Java and 25% in Bedrock, and Looting raises it.
Farm it: an ocean ruin or river farm that spawns natural drowned produces tridents over time - converted-zombie farms do not.
Alternative: trial chamber vaults can rarely contain tridents.
Enchant it: Loyalty returns the thrown trident, Riptide launches you in water or rain, Channeling summons lightning in thunderstorms, Impaling adds damage.
Keep it alive: tridents have low durability and cannot be crafted - repair with Mending or combine two on an anvil.
editionNote: The big edition gap is drop rate: 8.5% in Java versus 25% in Bedrock per trident-wielding drowned killed by a player or tamed wolf. Riptide and Channeling work in both, and neither edition lets you craft a trident.
versions: Tridents were added in 1.13 (the Update Aquatic) alongside drowned. Trial chambers (1.21) added vaults as a second rare source, ending eight years of drowned-only farming.

faq.q: Can you craft a trident?
faq.a: No - the trident is famously uncraftable. Your sources are drowned that spawn holding one and, since 1.21, trial chamber vaults. That rarity is why Mending matters so much on a good one.

faq.q: Why does my drowned farm never drop tridents?
faq.a: If your farm converts zombies into drowned, that is the problem: converted drowned never spawn with tridents. Only naturally spawned drowned (6.25% chance) carry them - farms must generate natural spawns.

faq.q: Riptide or Loyalty?
faq.a: They are mutually exclusive, so most players carry two tridents: Loyalty for combat (it returns after every throw) and Riptide for travel, launching you through water and rain. Channeling pairs with Loyalty for thunderstorm lightning.

name: How to Make and Activate a Conduit in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft a conduit from 8 nautilus shells around a heart of the sea, place it underwater, and surround it with 16-42 prismarine-type blocks. An active conduit gives Conduit Power - water breathing, night vision and faster mining - in a 32-96 block radius.
steps: Craft the conduit: 8 nautilus shells in every outer slot with a heart of the sea in the center.
Pick a spot underwater with room for a frame - conduits only activate when the block itself is waterlogged.
Build the activation frame: three 5x5 open squares centered on the conduit (one per axis), made of prismarine, prismarine bricks, dark prismarine or sea lanterns.
Use at least 16 frame blocks to activate; a full 42-block frame maxes the range at 96 blocks.
Touch water or rain within range and you get Conduit Power: water breathing, underwater night vision and faster underwater mining.
Bonus weapon: a fully framed conduit damages drowned, guardians and other hostile water mobs within 8 blocks.
One conduit can anchor an entire underwater base - add frames later to extend coverage.
materials: 16-42 prismarine blocks, dark prismarine, prismarine bricks or sea lanterns
editionNote: Crafting, activation frames and Conduit Power are identical in Java and Bedrock: 8 shells + heart of the sea, 16-42 prismarine-family blocks, 32-96 block spherical range, and the 8-block hostile-mob damage zone in both.
versions: Conduits were added in 1.13 (the Update Aquatic), completing the ocean trilogy with tridents and hearts of the sea. Their recipe and frame mechanics have stayed unchanged since release.

faq.q: What does Conduit Power actually do?
faq.a: It bundles Water Breathing, underwater Night Vision and Haste-like faster mining underwater into one infinite-duration effect - as long as you stay in range and touching water or rain. It is the reason underwater bases are viable.

faq.q: How many prismarine blocks do I need?
faq.a: 16 blocks activate the conduit at 32 blocks of range, and every 7 additional blocks add 16 more range, up to 42 blocks for the full 96-block sphere. Prismarine, bricks, dark prismarine and sea lanterns all count.

faq.q: Is a conduit worth the 8 nautilus shells?
faq.a: For any underwater project, yes - it replaces water-breathing potions forever, lights the depths, speeds mining and even zaps guardians. Farm shells from drowned and wandering traders, and grab the heart from buried treasure.

keywords: conduit minecraft, how to activate conduit, conduit power, nautilus shell heart of the sea, conduit frame prismarine

name: How to Get a Heart of the Sea in Minecraft
shortTitle: Get a Heart of the Sea
quickAnswer: The heart of the sea is found only in buried treasure chests. Get a treasure map from a shipwreck or ocean ruin chest, follow the red X, and dig - every buried treasure holds exactly one heart of the sea.
steps: Find a shipwreck or ocean ruin: their chests can contain a buried treasure map.
Shipwrecks are the reliable source - look for the map chest, usually in the hull section.
Open the map: it shows the area with a big red X marking the treasure.
Travel to the X and stand on it - the map marker fills in as you approach.
Dig down at the X (usually sand or gravel on a beach, sometimes deeper inland) until you hit the chest.
Every buried treasure chest contains exactly one heart of the sea, plus iron, gold, diamonds and potions.
Use it: 1 heart of the sea + 8 nautilus shells crafts a conduit.
Tip: the X chunk is precise - dig a spiral staircase around the exact spot instead of a straight shaft.
materials: Buried treasure map (from shipwrecks or ocean ruins)
editionNote: Identical in Java and Bedrock: hearts of the sea come only from buried treasure chests (one per chest, guaranteed), and treasure maps come from shipwreck and ocean ruin chests in both editions.
versions: The heart of the sea was added in 1.13 (18w15a, the Update Aquatic) together with buried treasure itself. It has exactly one use - the conduit - and has never gained another, keeping it the purest treasure hunt item in the game.

faq.q: Is the heart of the sea in every buried treasure?
faq.a: Yes - every buried treasure chest is guaranteed to contain exactly one heart of the sea. If the chest has none, you dug up the wrong chest (or a player got there first on a server).

faq.q: Where do treasure maps come from?
faq.a: Chests in shipwrecks and underwater ruins. Shipwrecks are the dependable route: each wreck has up to three chests and one of them holds the map. Cartographer villagers sell ocean explorer maps too, but those lead to monuments, not treasure.

faq.q: Can I farm hearts of the sea?
faq.a: Not from one spot - each buried treasure chest is unique to its map, and maps always point to un-looted treasure near their wreck. For multiple hearts you need multiple wrecks, which makes ocean exploration the real farm.

name: How to Find a Shipwreck in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Shipwrecks generate in oceans and on beaches, sometimes even inland or in ice. Sail the ocean watching for wooden masts, and loot up to 3 chests - the map chest in the stern always holds a buried treasure map.
steps: Take a boat out into any ocean biome - shipwrecks generate in all of them, plus beaches, snowy shores and even embedded in ice or inland terrain.
Scan the water for dark wooden shapes: masts, hulls and upright or capsized ships, often with drowned hanging around.
Check the shallows too: many wrecks sit half-buried on beaches, visible from land.
Loot smart: wrecks hold up to 3 chests depending on intact sections - supply chest in the bow, treasure chest in the upper stern, map chest in the lower stern.
The map chest is the prize: it always contains a buried treasure map leading to a heart of the sea.
Watch for drowned while diving - wrecks are their favorite hangout. Bring a door or conduit for air pockets on deep wrecks.
Cheat option: /locate structure minecraft:shipwreck gives exact coordinates.
materials: Air supply plan for deep dives
editionNote: Shipwreck generation and chest layout (bow supply, stern treasure and map chests) are the same in Java and Bedrock, and both editions made them rarer in 1.16. The /locate structure command works in both.
versions: Shipwrecks were added in 1.13 (18w11a, the Update Aquatic) and made somewhat rarer in 1.16. They remain the only reliable source of buried treasure maps in the game.

faq.q: How many chests are in a shipwreck?
faq.a: Up to 3, one per intact section: a supply chest in the bow (food, coal, tools), a treasure chest in the upper stern (iron, gold, diamonds, emeralds), and a map chest in the lower stern (paper, feathers, and always a treasure map). Broken wrecks can hold fewer or none.

faq.q: Can shipwrecks spawn on land?
faq.a: Yes - wrecks generate on beaches and occasionally fully inland or frozen into icebergs, a leftover of Aquatic-era generation. Land wrecks are the easiest loot in the ocean update: no diving, no drowned ambush.

faq.q: Why do shipwrecks matter?
faq.a: Their map chests guarantee a buried treasure map, and buried treasure is the only source of hearts of the sea - the conduit ingredient. Every serious ocean playthrough starts with a wreck.

name: How to Hatch a Dragon Egg
quickAnswer: You can't - in vanilla Minecraft the dragon egg is purely a decorative trophy and there is no way to hatch it. You can only collect it after beating the ender dragon: punch it once to make it teleport, then dig under it, place a torch and break the block so it falls and drops as an item. Hatching is only possible with mods.
steps: Know the truth first. The dragon egg cannot be hatched in vanilla Minecraft - it is a trophy item. Any video showing a hatching egg uses mods or datapacks.
Beat the ender dragon. The egg appears on top of the exit portal after your first dragon kill (in Bedrock, a second kill can drop another one due to a bug).
Don't mine it directly. Punching or mining the egg makes it teleport up to 15 blocks horizontally and 7 vertically. Chasing it around the exit portal is normal.
Use the torch trick. Hit the egg once, find where it landed, dig out the block beneath it, place a torch in the hole and break the block the egg sits on. It falls onto the torch and drops as an item.
Display your trophy. The egg is one of the rarest blocks in the game - only one exists per world in Java. Put it somewhere safe; if it falls into the void or lava, it is gone forever.
materials: Blocks to reach the exit portal top
editionNote: Identical in Java and Bedrock, except Bedrock can drop a second egg from a re-summoned dragon due to a long-standing bug. Neither edition can hatch the egg without mods.
versions: The dragon egg was added in Beta 1.9 Prerelease 4 (2011) alongside the ender dragon as the proof of victory. Mojang has never added a hatching mechanic - it remains a trophy.

faq.q: Can you hatch the dragon egg in vanilla?
faq.a: No. It is decorative only. Mods like Dragon Mounts add baby dragons, but the base game has no hatching mechanic.

faq.q: The egg teleported and I lost it - what now?
faq.a: It teleports within a 31x15x31 area around where you hit it. Search the exit portal area thoroughly; it often ends up inside the bedrock fountain or on the ground nearby.

faq.q: How many dragon eggs can I get?
faq.a: One per world in Java. In Bedrock, defeating the re-summoned dragon can drop a second egg.
