name: How to Get Smite in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Smite goes on swords, axes, spears and maces, and adds 2.5 HP of damage per level against undead mobs - up to +12.5 HP at Smite V. Get it from an enchanting table, enchanted books (librarian villagers, loot chests, fishing) or by combining items on an anvil. It cannot coexist with Sharpness, Bane of Arthropods, Density or Breach.
steps: Enchant directly at the table. Swords, axes, spears and maces can all roll Smite up to level V - put down 15 bookshelves for level 30 rolls and reset with cheap throwaway enchants until Smite appears.

Or use an anvil with a book. Enchanted books with Smite come from librarian trades (the reliable route), dungeon, mineshaft, stronghold and ruined portal chests, fishing treasure, and raid drops from vindicators and pillagers in Bedrock.
Combine on the anvil. Book plus weapon, or two Smite items of the same level to raise it - two Smite IVs make a Smite V. Watch the 'too expensive' cap at 40 levels in survival.

Know what it hits. Undead only: zombies, drowned, husks, zombie villagers, zombified piglins, zoglins, skeletons, strays, bogged, wither skeletons, phantoms and the wither itself. Smite V adds 12.5 HP per hit - the wither melts.

Pick your lane: Smite or Sharpness. They are mutually exclusive (along with Bane of Arthropods, Density and Breach). Sharpness is the generalist; Smite is the specialist for wither fights, zombie farms and Nether fortresses.
materials: Sword, axe, spear or mace to enchant
Anvil + Smite enchanted book (librarian trade, loot or fishing)
XP levels (up to 30 per roll, more for anvil work)
editionNote: Smite works the same in Java and Bedrock: +2.5 HP per level against undead. One Bedrock oddity: a tiny fraction (0.75%) of zombified piglins are not classed as undead and ignore Smite. Since 1.21, Smite is also mutually exclusive with the mace enchants Density and Breach.
versions: Smite has been in the game since enchantments arrived in Beta 1.9 Prerelease 3 (2011). Its +2.5 HP per level bonus has never changed; 1.21 only added the Density and Breach incompatibilities alongside the mace.

faq.q: Smite or Sharpness for the wither?
faq.a: Smite V, no contest. The wither is undead, so Smite V adds +12.5 HP per hit against it - Sharpness V only adds +3 (Java) and works on everything. One wither run pays for the enchant.

faq.q: Can I put Smite and Sharpness on the same sword?
faq.a: Not in survival - they are incompatible. You would need commands. Pick one per weapon; many players keep a Smite axe just for undead and a Sharpness sword for everything else.

faq.q: What is the fastest way to get Smite V?
faq.a: A librarian. Break and replace the lectern until it offers Smite, lock the trade, then buy up to level V - or combine two IV books on an anvil. Cheaper and more predictable than the enchanting table lottery.

name: How to Get Riptide in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Riptide is a trident enchantment that launches YOU when you throw the trident in water or rain - the trident never leaves your hand. Max level III. Get it from an enchanting table, librarian trades, loot chests or anvil combining, but it cannot be combined with Loyalty or Channeling.
steps: Get a trident first. Drowned spawn holding them in rivers and oceans; kill the holder for a chance at the drop - Looting III helps. It is the rarest mainstream weapon in the game.
Enchant the trident. Put it in an enchanting table (tridents are enchantable directly) or use an anvil with a Riptide book from a librarian, ocean ruin or shipwreck chest, or fishing treasure.
Level it to III. Riptide I launches you a short distance; III throws you far - combine two lower-level Riptide items or books on an anvil to climb. Higher level means longer, faster launches.

Use it to fly. Throw it while standing in water or exposed to rain and you launch with it. Throw straight up for height, or sprint-swim and throw forward for speed. Paired with elytra, Riptide III in rain is the fastest transport in the game.

Accept the trade-offs. A Riptide trident cannot be thrown as a normal projectile and never leaves your hand, so it cannot have Loyalty (nothing to return) or Channeling. Each throw costs 1 durability in Java - carry Mending.
materials: Enchanting table, or anvil + Riptide enchanted book
editionNote: Riptide works the same in Java and Bedrock: it only activates in water or rain, and it is mutually exclusive with Loyalty and Channeling. The durability cost per throw is a Java-only rule.
versions: Riptide was added in 1.13 (Update Aquatic, 2018) together with the trident itself. Its behavior has stayed consistent since: launch-only, no projectile, incompatible with the other trident movement enchants.

faq.q: Riptide or Loyalty on my trident?
faq.a: Different jobs. Loyalty makes it a returning ranged weapon for fighting drowned and guardians; Riptide turns it into a movement tool for rain and oceans. Many players carry one of each. They can never be on the same trident.

faq.q: Can I use Riptide in a cauldron or bubble column?
faq.a: You need to be standing in water or exposed to falling rain - a cauldron's water does not count. Bubble columns in open water do, as long as you are inside the water.

faq.q: Is Riptide worth it without elytra?
faq.a: Yes for ocean travel - Riptide III beats any boat. But it truly shines with elytra: throw up, deploy, and you have rain-powered flight with no fireworks.

name: How to Get Channeling in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Channeling is a trident enchantment (max level I) that summons a lightning bolt when your thrown trident hits a mob or other entity during a thunderstorm. Get it from an enchanting table, librarian trades or loot chests. It cannot be combined with Riptide.
steps: Get a trident. Kill drowned that spawn holding one in rivers and oceans - Looting III improves your odds.
Enchant it with Channeling. Enchanting table roll, anvil plus book from a librarian or loot chest, or combine two tridents. Channeling is a single-level enchant: no II or III to chase.
Wait for a thunderstorm. Channeling only fires while it is thundering - rain alone is not enough in Java. Sleep through normal rain, keep an ear out for thunder, and keep the trident ready.

Throw at anything living. When the trident lands on a mob, player, armor stand, boat or even an item frame during the storm, lightning strikes that spot: 5 HP of damage plus fire, on top of the trident hit.

Farm the special effects. Lightning converts pigs into zombified piglins, villagers into witches, creepers into CHARGED creepers (which make zombies, skeletons and creepers drop their heads when they explode) and red mooshrooms into brown ones. In Bedrock, hitting a lightning rod summons a strike even in ordinary rain.
materials: Enchanting table, or anvil + Channeling book
editionNote: Java: lightning only during thunderstorms, on entities or lightning rods. Bedrock: hitting a lightning rod summons lightning during ANY rain, not just thunderstorms - much easier to trigger. Channeling and Riptide are mutually exclusive in both.
versions: Channeling was added in 1.13 (Update Aquatic, 2018) alongside the trident. Its thunderstorm requirement and Riptide incompatibility have been unchanged since release.

faq.q: Channeling or Riptide?
faq.a: Channeling for mob farms and head collecting, Riptide for movement. They cannot share a trident, so most late-game players own two tridents. Loyalty pairs fine with Channeling, by the way.

faq.q: Why won't my Channeling trident summon lightning?
faq.a: It must be actively thundering - not just raining. In Java even a lightning rod needs a thunderstorm; only Bedrock triggers rods in normal rain. Check for thunder sounds and lightning flashes in the sky.

faq.q: How do I get mob heads with Channeling?
faq.a: Strike a creeper with the trident during a thunderstorm to charge it, then get it to blow up next to a zombie, skeleton or another creeper - the victim drops its head. One charged creeper, one head, so plan the blast.

name: How to Get Loyalty in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Loyalty is a trident enchantment (max level III) that makes the thrown trident fly back to your hand after it lands. Higher levels return it faster. Get it from an enchanting table, librarian trades or loot chests. It cannot be combined with Riptide.
steps: Get a trident. Kill drowned that spawn holding one in rivers and oceans - Looting III raises the drop odds.
Enchant it with Loyalty. Enchanting table roll, or an anvil plus a Loyalty book from a librarian, loot chest or fishing treasure.
Raise it to III. Loyalty I leaves you waiting a beat after each throw; III snaps the trident back almost instantly. Combine two same-level Loyalty items or books on an anvil to climb.
Fight at range without losing it. Throw, let it hit, and it returns on its own - no chasing drops into lava, oceans or ravines. It returns to you wherever you have moved, even through walls.

Respect its limits. In Java, a trident thrown into the void is gone forever - there is nothing for it to bounce off, so it never comes back. In Bedrock it returns after about 15 blocks of void. And Loyalty can never share a trident with Riptide.
materials: Enchanting table, or anvil + Loyalty enchanted book
editionNote: Java: throwing into the void destroys the trident even with Loyalty III - the wiki marks this as working as intended. Bedrock: it returns after traveling about 15 blocks into the void, and dispenser-fired tridents do not return at all.
versions: Loyalty was added in 1.13 (Update Aquatic, 2018) with the trident itself. Its return behavior and Riptide incompatibility have been unchanged since.

faq.q: Loyalty or Riptide?
faq.a: Loyalty for combat - a reliable ranged weapon that always comes back. Riptide for movement. They are mutually exclusive, so most players carry two tridents. Loyalty also pairs nicely with Channeling.

faq.q: My Loyalty trident never came back - why?
faq.a: Most likely it fell into the void (Java) with nothing to hit. It can also get stuck if you log out or die in some edge cases. In the End, never throw it into the void below the islands.

faq.q: Does Loyalty III make it return instantly?
faq.a: Nearly - higher levels shorten the wait after impact. III is fast enough for rapid-fire throwing in fights, which is why it is the standard combat build with Impaling.

name: How to Get Impaling in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Impaling is a trident enchantment (max level V) adding 2.5 HP of damage per level. In Java it only boosts damage against aquatic mobs - fish, guardians, squids, turtles, dolphins, axolotls - and NOT drowned. In Bedrock it boosts damage against any mob that is in water or rain.
steps: Get a trident. Drowned with tridents spawn in rivers and oceans; Looting III improves the drop chance.
Enchant it. Enchanting table roll, or an anvil plus an Impaling book from a librarian, loot chest or fishing treasure. Combine same-level books to reach Impaling V.

Know your edition. Java: the bonus only applies to aquatic mobs - guardians, elder guardians, all fish, squids, glow squids, turtles, dolphins, axolotls, tadpoles and nautiluses. Drowned count as pure undead and take nothing extra. Bedrock: ANY mob touching water or rain takes the bonus - players included.

Raid a monument. Impaling V turns elder guardians into four-hit kills and one-shots most fish and squids. It is the enchant that makes ocean monuments, guardian farms and warm-ocean exploring comfortable.

Mind the incompatibilities. Impaling cannot combine with Sharpness, Smite, Bane of Arthropods, Density or Breach - though in survival you would never fit those on a trident anyway, since they belong to swords, axes and maces.
materials: Enchanting table, or anvil + Impaling enchanted book
Loyalty or Riptide partner enchant (separate slots - they stack with Impaling)
editionNote: The huge edition split: Java limits Impaling to aquatic mobs (drowned excluded - marked 'works as intended' on the bug tracker), while Bedrock applies it to anything standing in water or rain. Bedrock also rounds the bonus down to whole numbers per level.
versions: Impaling was added in 1.13 (Update Aquatic, 2018) with the trident. Its Java aquatic-only scope and Bedrock water-or-rain scope have stayed the same since release.

faq.q: Does Impaling work on drowned?
faq.a: In Java, no - drowned are classified as undead, not aquatic, and the bug report was closed as intended behavior. In Bedrock, yes if they are in water or rain. For Java drowned hunting, Smite on a sword does the job.

faq.q: Is Impaling worth it in Java?
faq.a: For ocean content, absolutely: guardian farms, monument raids and warm-ocean loot runs. For general combat in Java it does nothing - it is a specialist enchant, unlike the Bedrock version which is a mini-Sharpness in the rain.

faq.q: Impaling plus Loyalty - do they stack?
faq.a: Yes, they are on different tracks and combine fine: Loyalty brings it back, Impaling makes it hit harder. That is the classic ocean-hunter trident build.

name: How to Get Multishot in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Multishot is a crossbow enchantment (max level I) that fires 3 projectiles in a 10° spread for the price of one arrow. It duplicates tipped arrows, spectral arrows and firework rockets too. It cannot be combined with Piercing, and only the center projectile can be picked back up.
steps: Craft or loot a crossbow. Tripwire hook + 3 sticks + 2 string + 1 iron ingot, or take one from a pillager.
Enchant it with Multishot. Enchanting table roll, or an anvil plus a Multishot book from a librarian or loot chest. One level only - no grinding for higher tiers.

Fire three for one. Each shot throws three copies of your loaded projectile in a fixed 10-degree horizontal spread, but only consumes one arrow from your inventory. The cost: 3 durability points per shot (one per projectile).

Load the fun ammo. Multishot duplicates whatever is loaded: tipped arrows for area effects, spectral arrows to tag whole groups, and firework rockets for triple explosive volleys - three rockets at once is the classic raid-melter.

Know the quirks. Only the center arrow can be recovered after firing, and in Java, damage immunity means a single mob can only be hurt by one arrow per shot - Multishot is for crowds, not single targets. Piercing is mutually exclusive.
materials: Enchanting table, or anvil + Multishot enchanted book
Arrows, tipped arrows or firework rockets to load
editionNote: Multishot behaves the same in Java and Bedrock for the basics (3 projectiles, 10° spread, one arrow consumed). The one-arrow-per-mob limit comes from Java's damage immunity system, so Bedrock mobs can technically catch more than one arrow from a volley.
versions: Multishot was added in 1.14 (Village & Pillage, 2019) together with the crossbow itself. Its spread, ammo cost and Piercing incompatibility have not changed since.

faq.q: Multishot or Piercing?
faq.a: Multishot for crowd control and firework volleys; Piercing for lined-up mobs and shield-piercing shots. They cannot share a crossbow, so pick per weapon - many players keep one of each.

faq.q: Does Multishot work with fireworks?
faq.a: Yes - three rockets per shot, each duplicated for free. Load rockets with firework stars for damage and a Multishot crossbow becomes a grenade launcher that only costs one rocket per volley.

faq.q: Why did only one of my three arrows hurt the zombie?
faq.a: Java's damage immunity: right after taking a hit, a mob briefly cannot take another, so the side arrows bounce off the same target. Aim into groups so each arrow finds its own victim.

name: How to Get Piercing in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Piercing is a crossbow enchantment (max level IV) that lets arrows fly through multiple mobs in a line - level+1 entities per shot - and they are not consumed, so you can pick them back up. It even ignores raised shields. It cannot be combined with Multishot, and it does nothing for firework rockets.
steps: Get a crossbow. Craft one (3 sticks, 2 string, 1 iron ingot, 1 tripwire hook) or take one from a pillager.
Enchant it with Piercing. Enchanting table roll, or an anvil plus a Piercing book from a librarian or loot chest. Combine same-level books to reach Piercing IV.

Line them up. A Piercing arrow passes through the enchantment level's worth of entities, hitting level+1 mobs total - Piercing IV skewers five mobs standing in a row. The arrow keeps flying straight, so aim along the line.

Enjoy infinite arrows. Piercing arrows are never consumed by hits: shoot through the crowd, then walk over and pick your arrow back up. This works with tipped and spectral arrows too - one potion arrow, endless volleys.

Know what stops it. Piercing ignores raised shields, but a closed shulker shell, the wither's half-health armor and a breeze's wind armor still bounce arrows off. And it has zero effect on firework rockets loaded in the crossbow.
materials: Enchanting table, or anvil + Piercing enchanted book
Arrows (tipped and spectral included - you get them back)
editionNote: Piercing works the same in Java and Bedrock: level+1 entities per arrow, shield-ignoring, arrow recovery included. The fireworks limitation applies in both - rockets are not duplicated or pierced.
versions: Piercing was added in 1.14 (Village & Pillage, 2019) with the crossbow. Its shield-piercing behavior and Multishot incompatibility have been consistent since release.

faq.q: Piercing or Multishot?
faq.a: Piercing for lined-up mobs, infinite tipped arrows and shield-piercing PvP shots; Multishot for spread crowds and triple firework volleys. They cannot share a crossbow - keep one of each.

faq.q: Does Piercing really make arrows infinite?
faq.a: Functionally yes: the arrow is never consumed on hit, only lost if it flies somewhere unreachable. One tipped arrow of Harming can serve for an entire raid if you collect it between waves.

faq.q: Does Piercing ignore shields in PvP?
faq.a: Yes - a raised shield does not block a Piercing arrow at all. It is one of the few ways to pressure a turtling player, alongside axes disabling shields in Java.

name: How to Get Quick Charge in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Quick Charge is a crossbow enchantment (max level III) that cuts loading time by 0.25 seconds per level. A normal crossbow loads in 1.25 seconds; Quick Charge III drops it to 0.5 seconds - faster than a bow can even draw.
steps: Get a crossbow. Craft one (3 sticks, 2 string, 1 iron ingot, 1 tripwire hook) or loot it from a pillager.
Enchant it with Quick Charge. Enchanting table roll, or an anvil plus a Quick Charge book from a librarian or loot chest. Combine books to reach level III.

Feel the speed. Each level shaves 0.25 seconds off the 1.25 second load time: 1.0s at I, 0.75s at II and 0.5s at III. A Quick Charge III crossbow fires almost twice as fast as stock - and reloads faster than a fully drawn bow shot cycle.

Pair it right. Quick Charge stacks beautifully with Piercing for raid lines or Multishot for volleys (pick one of those two per crossbow). It also makes firework crossbows viable in real fights - 0.5 seconds between rocket volleys.
Do not chase level IV. Quick Charge stops at III in survival; levels IV and V only exist via commands, where V loads the crossbow instantly. On an anvil, combining beyond III wastes your XP.
materials: Enchanting table, or anvil + Quick Charge enchanted book
Arrows or firework rockets to load
editionNote: Quick Charge works the same in Java and Bedrock: -0.25 seconds per level, capped at III in survival. The instant-load level V trick is a commands-only curiosity in both editions.
versions: Quick Charge was added in 1.14 (Village & Pillage, 2019) alongside the crossbow. Its 0.25-second-per-level reduction has never been rebalanced.

faq.q: Is Quick Charge III better than a bow?
faq.a: For raw speed, yes: 0.5s loads beat a bow's draw-and-fire cycle, and crossbow shots hit instantly at full power. Bows still win on Infinity ammo and Power V burst damage - but a Quick Charge III firework crossbow out-damages most things in crowds.

faq.q: Quick Charge or Multishot?
faq.a: They do different jobs and stack on the same crossbow - Quick Charge is compatible with both Multishot and Piercing. The real choice is Multishot versus Piercing; Quick Charge goes on either build.

faq.q: Why won't my crossbow load instantly with Quick Charge?
faq.a: Instant loading needs level V, which only exists through commands. Survival Quick Charge caps at III and 0.5 seconds - still the fastest ranged reload in the game.

name: How to Get Luck of the Sea in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Luck of the Sea is a fishing rod enchantment (max level III) that raises treasure catches from 5% to 11.3% and cuts junk from 10% to 4.2%. Treasure means enchanted books (Mending included), name tags, saddles, nautilus shells, enchanted bows and rods. Get it from an enchanting table, librarian trades or fishing itself.
steps: Craft a fishing rod. Three sticks and two string - spiders at night supply the string.
Enchant it. An enchanting table can roll Luck of the Sea directly on the rod, or use an anvil with a book from a librarian, a loot chest, or - fittingly - from fishing up treasure with a plain rod.

Fish in open water. For treasure loot tables you need open water: the bobber must sit in water at least 2 blocks deep in every direction, with sky or lily pads above. A dock over deep ocean or a dug 5x5x2 pool both work.

Watch the table shift. Unenchanted fishing gives 5% treasure and 10% junk. Luck of the Sea III flips that to 11.3% treasure and 4.2% junk, with fish barely affected - about 2.1% more treasure and 2% less junk per level.

Farm the good stuff. Treasure rolls include enchanted books (any treasure enchant, including Mending), name tags, saddles, nautilus shells, and enchanted bows and fishing rods. Add Lure III on the same rod to double your catch speed.
materials: Enchanting table, or anvil + Luck of the Sea book
Open water (2+ blocks deep, open sky)
editionNote: Luck of the Sea works identically in Java and Bedrock with the default loot tables: +2.1% treasure and -1.95% junk per level. It combines with Lure on the same rod - they cover different parts of the fishing game and are not mutually exclusive.
versions: Luck of the Sea was added in 1.7.2 (2013) together with Lure, when fishing got its loot-table overhaul. Its per-level rates have stayed the same ever since.

faq.q: Luck of the Sea or Lure?
faq.a: Both, on the same rod - they are compatible. Lure cuts the wait between bites, Luck of the Sea upgrades what each catch is. A Lure III + Luck of the Sea III + Mending rod is the classic fishing endgame.

faq.q: Can I fish up Mending with it?
faq.a: Yes - enchanted books in the treasure table can roll any treasure enchantment, Mending included. It is the slow-but-free route if you have no librarian yet.

faq.q: Why am I only catching fish, no treasure?
faq.a: You are probably not in open water. The game requires a clear 2-block-deep volume around the bobber and direct sky (or lily pads) above - fishing in a cave pool or a 1-block ditch silently disables the treasure table.

keywords: how to get luck of the sea

name: How to Get Lure in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Lure is a fishing rod enchantment (max level III) that cuts the wait between bites by 5 seconds per level. Lure III nearly empties the idle time, roughly doubling your catches per hour. Get it from an enchanting table, librarian trades, loot chests or fishing itself.
steps: Craft a fishing rod. Three sticks plus two string from spiders.
Enchant it with Lure. The enchanting table can roll it directly on the rod, or use an anvil with a Lure book from a librarian, a loot chest or a treasure catch.

Feel the shorter waits. A plain rod makes you wait 5-30 seconds per bite. Each Lure level subtracts 5 seconds from that window, so Lure III pulls the wait down to almost nothing - your bobber barely settles before the next bite.

Pair it with Luck of the Sea. They are compatible and cover both halves of fishing: Lure makes bites come faster, Luck of the Sea makes each catch better. Lure III + Luck of the Sea III + Mending is the classic endgame rod.
Fish in open water. Speed means nothing without the treasure table: the bobber needs water at least 2 blocks deep around it and open sky (or lily pads) above, or you will only ever catch fish.
materials: Enchanting table, or anvil + Lure enchanted book
Open water (2+ blocks deep, open sky)
editionNote: Lure behaves identically in Java and Bedrock: -5 seconds of wait per level, compatible with Luck of the Sea. A commands-only curiosity: beyond level 5 the bite timer never starts and nothing ever bites.
versions: Lure was added in 1.7.2 (2013) together with Luck of the Sea, in the fishing loot overhaul. Its 5-seconds-per-level effect has been stable since.

faq.q: Lure or Luck of the Sea?
faq.a: Both - they stack on the same rod and answer different questions. Lure is quantity (faster bites), Luck of the Sea is quality (more treasure, less junk). If you must pick one for XP and book farming, Luck of the Sea edges it out.

faq.q: Does Lure work in rain?
faq.a: Rain already shortens bite times on its own, and Lure stacks with that bonus - fishing in the rain with Lure III is the fastest catching in the game.

faq.q: Why does nothing bite with my command-enchanted rod?
faq.a: Lure above level 5 (commands only) breaks the bite timer - the wiki confirms fish never bite at all. Survival Lure III is the effective cap.

name: How to Get Frost Walker in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Frost Walker is a boot enchantment (max level II) that freezes water into frosted ice under your feet as you walk, and makes you immune to magma block and campfire damage. It is a treasure enchantment - the enchanting table never offers it, so get the book from librarians, loot chests or fishing. It cannot combine with Depth Strider.
steps: Know it is treasure-only. Frost Walker never appears on the enchanting table. Your routes: librarian villagers (reroll the lectern until the book appears), structure chests, or fishing up enchanted books with Luck of the Sea.
Apply it on an anvil. Book plus boots, any tier - diamond or netherite for lava-lake duty. Combine two Frost Walker I books for level II.

Walk on water. Moving across water freezes a circle (Java) or square (Bedrock) of frosted ice around you with a radius of 2 + level: 3 blocks at I, 4 at II. The ice cracks behind you, so keep moving - standing still drops you in.
Use its hidden perk. Frost Walker boots also make you immune to magma block and campfire damage - handy for Nether floors and hidden-campfire traps.

Choose: Frost Walker or Depth Strider. They are mutually exclusive. Frost Walker turns oceans into roads; Depth Strider makes you fast UNDER water. For long ocean trips most players keep a Frost Walker pair in an ender chest.
materials: Frost Walker enchanted book (librarian, loot or fishing - treasure enchant)
Ender chest (optional - swap boots on long trips)
editionNote: The freeze shape differs: a circle in Java, a square in Bedrock, radius 2 + level in both. The water needs air above it to freeze, and you must be moving on the ground - jumping or flying does not trigger it.
versions: Frost Walker was added in 1.9 (the Combat Update, 2016). It has been a treasure enchantment with the Depth Strider incompatibility since day one.

faq.q: Why won't the enchanting table give me Frost Walker?
faq.a: It is a treasure enchantment like Mending - table-rolls never include it. Librarian lectern rerolling is the reliable route; fishing with Luck of the Sea III works too.

faq.q: Does Frost Walker work on lava?
faq.a: No - it freezes water only. For lava lakes you want a Fire Resistance potion, a strider, or lots of blocks. The magma-block immunity is real though: magma floors stop hurting.

faq.q: Frost Walker or Depth Strider for an ocean base?
faq.a: Frost Walker, usually: you can walk to shore over the water instead of swimming. Depth Strider is better if you build and fight underwater a lot, especially with Respiration and Aqua Affinity.

name: How to Get Flame in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Flame is a bow enchantment (max level I) that sets your arrows on fire: targets burn for 5 fire damage over 5 seconds after the hit. Flaming arrows also light TNT, campfires and candles - but they cannot ignite blocks like trees, and rain or water puts them out mid-flight.
steps: Get a bow. Three sticks plus three string, or take one from a skeleton.
Enchant it with Flame. The enchanting table can roll it directly, or use an anvil with a Flame book from a librarian, loot chest or fishing treasure. One level only - no grinding.

Let fire finish the job. A Flame arrow deals its normal damage, then sets the target alight for 5 seconds: 5 HP of fire damage ticked over that time. Against unarmored mobs that is often a free extra half-health bar.

Use it as a tool. Flaming arrows light TNT from a safe distance, light campfires and candles, and cook dropped meat from animals that die burning - cows and pigs killed by fire drop cooked beef and pork chops.

Know the limits. Flaming arrows ignite ONLY players, mobs, TNT, campfires and candles - no forest fires, no burning trees. Rain and water extinguish the arrow mid-flight, and mobs killed purely by fire drop no XP unless you dealt non-fire damage within the last 5 seconds.
materials: Enchanting table, or anvil + Flame enchanted book
Arrows (or Infinity - Flame stacks with it)
editionNote: Flame behaves the same in Java and Bedrock: 5 HP of fire over 5 seconds, single level, Infinity-compatible. The XP rule matters in both: a kill credited purely to fire grants no experience orbs.
versions: Flame has been in the game since the enchantment system launched in Beta 1.9 Prerelease 3 (2011). Its burn duration and single level have never changed.

faq.q: Flame or Power?
faq.a: Both - they stack. Power V multiplies the arrow hit itself, Flame adds the burn. A Power V + Flame + Infinity bow is the classic general-purpose build; add Punch II if you like spacing, or Unbreaking and Mending for upkeep.

faq.q: Do Flame arrows cook food?
faq.a: Yes - animals that die while burning drop the cooked version of their meat. Hunting cows with a Flame bow gives you steak directly, no furnace needed.

faq.q: Why did my Flame arrow go out?
faq.a: Water and rain extinguish flaming arrows mid-flight - shooting through rain, a waterfall or into water turns it back into a normal arrow. Under a roof or inside the Nether, fire away.

name: How to Get Fire Protection in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Fire Protection is an armor enchantment (max level IV) that cuts fire damage - fire, lava, magma blocks, campfires, blaze shots, flaming arrows - by 8% per level, and shortens burn time by 15% per level. Stack 7 total levels across your armor and you stop catching fire at all. It cannot combine with Protection, Blast Protection or Projectile Protection on the same piece.
steps: Enchant armor at the table. Helmets, chestplates, leggings and boots can all roll Fire Protection up to IV. Turtle shells too. Use 15 bookshelves for level 30 rolls.
Or use an anvil. Fire Protection books come from librarian trades, structure chests and fishing treasure. Combine two same-level books to climb toward IV.

Know what it covers. Standing in fire, swimming in lava, magma blocks, lit campfires, blaze fireballs, flaming arrows and burning zombie hits - 8% less damage per level, so IV on one piece takes 32% off every fire hit.

Exploit the burn-time bonus. Each level also cuts your burning time by 15% (max 60% per piece at IV). Total level 7 across your set - say IV + III - means 100% burn reduction: lava still hurts, but you never keep burning after you get out.

Pick one protection per piece. Fire Protection is mutually exclusive with Protection, Blast Protection and Projectile Protection. A common endgame mix: Protection on three pieces, Fire Protection on one Nether piece.
materials: Armor piece (any tier, turtle shells included)
Enchanting table + bookshelves, or anvil + Fire Protection book
editionNote: Works the same in Java and Bedrock: 8% fire damage reduction per level plus 15% burn-time reduction per level. One trap: blaze and magma cube contact hits count as melee damage, not fire - Fire Protection does nothing for those.
versions: Fire Protection has existed since enchantments launched in Beta 1.9 Prerelease 3 (2011). Its 8%-per-level formula and the burn-time bonus have survived every rebalance since.

faq.q: Fire Protection or Protection for the Nether?
faq.a: Fire Protection if lava is your main fear - it cuts lava damage and, at total level 7+, stops the burning afterward. Protection is the better generalist for fortresses full of wither skeletons and blaze melee. Ideally: one Fire Protection piece, the rest Protection.

faq.q: Does Fire Protection work against the blaze fireball?
faq.a: Yes - blaze projectiles are fire damage and get reduced. But a blaze bumping into you deals melee damage, which Fire Protection does not touch.

faq.q: Can I become fully fireproof?
faq.a: For burning, yes: total Fire Protection level 7 across armor pieces gives 100% burn-time reduction - you take no afterburn at all. Direct lava and fire contact still deals reduced damage, so pair with a Fire Resistance potion for true immunity.

name: How to Get Blast Protection in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Blast Protection is an armor enchantment (max level IV) that cuts explosion damage by 8% per level - creepers, TNT, ghast fireballs, beds in the Nether, end crystals, wither skulls, even firework rockets - and in Java adds 15% explosion knockback resistance per level. It cannot combine with Protection, Fire Protection or Projectile Protection.
steps: Enchant armor at the table. Any armor piece can roll Blast Protection up to IV with a full bookshelf setup.
Or use an anvil. Blast Protection books come from librarian trades, structure chests and fishing treasure. Combine same-level books up to IV.

Count what it blocks. Creeper hugs, charged creepers, TNT, ghast fireballs, beds and respawn anchors used in the wrong dimension, end crystals, the wither's spawn explosion and its skulls, firework rockets, and wind charges - 8% off per level, 32% at IV.

Use the knockback bonus. In Java each level also grants 15% explosion knockback resistance, stacking across pieces - a full Blast Protection set barely moves when a creeper pops next to you. Essential for crystal PvP and end crystal fights.

Place it where explosions live. It is mutually exclusive with the other protections, so dedicate one piece to it: it shines in the End (crystals), the Nether (beds, ghasts), ancient city runs (shrieking panic creepers) and PvP servers with crystals.
materials: Enchanting table + bookshelves, or anvil + Blast Protection book
editionNote: Damage reduction is identical in Java and Bedrock (8% per level, 32% at IV). The 15%-per-level explosion knockback resistance is a Java side effect. Blast Protection also covers wind charge and Wind Burst damage since 1.21.
versions: Blast Protection has existed since enchantments launched in Beta 1.9 Prerelease 3 (2011). The list of covered explosions has only grown - beds, respawn anchors, wind charges and Wind Burst joined over the years.

faq.q: Blast Protection or Protection?
faq.a: Protection for everyday everything; Blast Protection when explosions are the threat - end crystal PvP, mining with beds in the Nether, wither fights, creeper farms. One Blast Prot piece in a Protection set is the classic compromise.

faq.q: Does Blast Protection stop ghast fireballs?
faq.a: Yes - ghast fireball damage is explosion damage, so it gets cut by 8% per level. The direct impact of the fireball is also covered because the whole hit is tagged as an explosion.

faq.q: Does it help against the warden's sonic boom?
faq.a: No - the sonic boom is not explosion damage. Only Resistance, wolf armor and witch-level resistance reduce it. Bring a Turtle Master potion instead.

name: How to Get Projectile Protection in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Projectile Protection is an armor enchantment (max level IV) that cuts projectile damage by 8% per level: arrows, thrown tridents, shulker bullets, llama spit, blaze fireballs and wind charges. It does nothing against splash potions, fireworks or the warden's sonic boom, and it cannot combine with Protection, Fire Protection or Blast Protection.
steps: Enchant armor at the table. Any armor piece can roll Projectile Protection up to IV with 15 bookshelves.
Or use an anvil. Books come from librarian trades, structure chests and fishing treasure. Combine same-level books up to IV.

Know what it blocks. Skeleton and pillager arrows, drowned tridents, shulker bullets in end cities, llama spit, blaze fireballs and breeze wind charges - 8% less per level, 32% at IV. The direct hit of a ghast fireball or wither skull counts too, but their explosions do not (that is Blast Protection's job).

Know what slips through. Splash potions of Harming, the dragon's fireball breath, firework rockets and the warden's sonic boom are NOT projectile damage - Projectile Protection ignores them completely.

Choose it for ranged metas. It is mutually exclusive with the other protections. Put it on one piece when your server is bow-heavy, when farming skeletons, or before an end city run where shulker bullets rain from every wall.
materials: Enchanting table + bookshelves, or anvil + Projectile Protection book
A skeleton to not fear anymore
editionNote: Works the same in Java and Bedrock: 8% projectile damage reduction per level, no side effect. It is the only specialized protection with no bonus perk - Blast gets knockback resistance, Fire gets shorter burn time, Projectile gets nothing extra.
versions: Projectile Protection has existed since enchantments launched in Beta 1.9 Prerelease 3 (2011). Its coverage list grew with new projectiles - shulker bullets in 1.9, wind charges in 1.21.

faq.q: Projectile Protection or Protection?
faq.a: Protection covers projectiles too (plus everything else) at 4% per level, so it is the generalist. Projectile Protection doubles that to 8% but ONLY for projectiles - pick it when ranged damage is what actually kills you: skeleton farms, end cities, bow PvP.

faq.q: Does it work against drowned tridents?
faq.a: Yes - thrown tridents are projectile damage. Drowned melee slaps are not, so keep your distance and let the enchant work.

faq.q: Does Projectile Protection block shulker bullets?
faq.a: Yes - shulker bullets are projectile damage and get reduced by 8% per level. The levitation effect still applies though, so keep an eye on your landing.

name: How to Get Density in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Density is a mace-only enchantment (max level V) that adds half a heart of smash attack damage per block fallen, per level - so Density V adds 2.5 hearts per block of drop. Get it from the enchanting table, librarian trades, fishing loot, or ominous vaults in trial chambers. It cannot combine with Smite, Bane of Arthropods or Breach.
steps: Get a mace first. Density only goes on maces, so you need a heavy core from an ominous vault plus a breeze rod from a breeze in the trial chambers.
Enchant at the table. Maces can roll Density up to V directly. Use 15 bookshelves for level 30 rolls.
Or find the book. Density books come from librarian trades of any level, fishing treasure, and ominous vaults - ominous vaults are the most reliable source of high levels.

Understand the math. Smash attacks scale with fall distance, and Density multiplies that scaling: +0.5 hearts per block fallen per level. At Density V, dropping 10 blocks adds 25 hearts on top of the base smash damage.

Pick your damage school. Density competes with Smite, Bane of Arthropods and Breach for the same slot. Density is the one-shot specialist: pair it with Wind Burst so every kill relaunches you for the next smash.
materials: Enchanting table + bookshelves, or anvil + Density book
editionNote: Identical in Java and Bedrock: +0.5 hearts per block fallen per level, up to level V. Technically also incompatible with Sharpness and Impaling, but no survival weapon can hold both, so you will never see that conflict.
versions: Density arrived with the mace in Java 1.21 and Bedrock 1.21.0 (2024) as one of its three signature enchantments, alongside Breach and Wind Burst.

faq.q: Density or Breach on my mace?
faq.a: Density for PvE one-shots - its fall-distance bonus reaches absurd numbers fast. Breach only outperforms it against heavily armored targets (players in netherite, high-armor mobs) on flat ground. Most players run Density and keep a Breach mace for PvP.

faq.q: Can Density go on a sword?
faq.a: No - Density is mace-only. Smite and Bane of Arthropods are the sword-and-axe equivalents in its exclusivity group.

faq.q: How much damage does Density V add?
faq.a: 2.5 extra hearts per block fallen. A 5-block drop adds 12.5 hearts; a 10-block drop adds 25. Combined with the mace's own fall scaling, well-aimed smashes delete nearly any mob in one hit.

name: How to Get Breach in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Breach is a mace-only enchantment (max level IV) that ignores 15% of the target's armor effectiveness per level - Breach IV cuts 60% of their armor damage reduction, natural mob armor included. Get it from the enchanting table, librarian trades, fishing, or ominous vaults. It cannot combine with Smite, Bane of Arthropods or Density.
steps: Get a mace. Breach only enchants maces: craft one from a heavy core (ominous vault) and a breeze rod (breezes in trial chambers).
Enchant at the table. Maces can roll Breach up to IV with a full bookshelf setup.
Or find the book. Librarian trades, fishing treasure and ominous vaults all carry Breach books.

Know what it pierces. Each level ignores 15% of the target's armor damage reduction - leather to netherite, plus the natural armor points of mobs like zombies and shulkers. Breach IV treats full netherite like it is barely there.

Know what it does NOT pierce. Breach ignores only raw armor. Protection enchantments on that armor and the Resistance effect still apply at full strength - a Protection IV opponent is far less vulnerable than a plain netherite one.
Use it where armor matters. Breach shines in PvP and against armored mobs. Against unarmored targets it does nothing, which is why most players keep it as a second mace next to Density.
materials: Enchanting table + bookshelves, or anvil + Breach book
An armored friend to test on (consensually)
editionNote: Works the same in Java and Bedrock: 15% armor-effectiveness reduction per level, max IV. Beyond level VI there is no practical effect. Remember: enchantment-based protection (Protection, Resistance) is unaffected - only armor points and armor toughness are pierced.
versions: Breach arrived with the mace in Java 1.21 and Bedrock 1.21.0 (2024). It is the armor-counter counterpart to Density's raw damage.

faq.q: Breach or Density for PvP?
faq.a: Breach. Netherite armor turns Density's fall bonus into chip damage, while Breach IV strips 60% of that armor off every hit - including flat-ground hits where Density adds nothing. Keep Density for PvE farming.

faq.q: Does Breach work on the warden?
faq.a: The warden has no armor points, so Breach gives no bonus against it - or against any unarmored mob. Bring Density or Smite instead.

faq.q: Does Breach ignore Protection IV?
faq.a: No - Breach only reduces the damage reduction from armor points and toughness. Protection enchantments and the Resistance effect apply at full strength on top of whatever armor remains.

name: How to Get Sweeping Edge in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Sweeping Edge is a Java Edition sword enchantment (max level III) that boosts sweep attack damage to 50%/67%/75% of your sword's damage against surrounding mobs. It does nothing on the mob you hit directly, and it does not exist in Bedrock. Get it from the enchanting table, librarian trades, fishing, or structure chests.
steps: Check your edition. Sweeping Edge is Java Edition only - Bedrock swords have no sweep attacks at all, so the enchantment does not exist there.
Enchant a sword at the table. Any sword can roll Sweeping Edge up to III. Use 15 bookshelves for level 30 rolls.
Or find the book. Librarian trades, fishing treasure, monster room chests, ocean ruins chests and other non-village structure loot all carry it.

Learn the sweep. On Java, standing still on the ground and attacking with your cooldown at 84.8% or higher triggers a sweep: mobs in a small area around your target take the sweep damage and get knocked back.
Do the math. Sweep damage is 1 + sword damage x level/(level+1): III means 75% of your sword's damage splashes to nearby mobs. A Sharpness V diamond sword sweeps 8.5 hearts per swing into the crowd.
Use it in crowds. Sweeping Edge shines in mob farms, zombie sieges and raid waves - anywhere enemies pack together. For single targets it adds zero damage.
materials: Enchanting table + bookshelves, or anvil + Sweeping Edge book
editionNote: JAVA EDITION ONLY. Bedrock has no sweep attack mechanic and no Sweeping Edge enchantment. On Java, the bonus applies only to surrounding mobs, never to the mob you hit directly.
versions: Sweeping Edge has existed since the Combat Update (Java 1.9, 2016), which introduced attack cooldowns and sweep attacks. It has been Java-exclusive ever since.

faq.q: Why can't I get Sweeping Edge on Bedrock?
faq.a: Because it does not exist there. Sweep attacks themselves are a Java-only mechanic - Bedrock swords swing differently, so the enchantment has nothing to boost. Mojang has tested combat changes, but as of now Sweeping Edge remains Java-only.

faq.q: Does Sweeping Edge increase damage on my main target?
faq.a: No - only the surrounding mobs caught in the sweep take the boosted damage. Your direct target takes the sword's normal hit. Pair it with Sharpness, which boosts both.

faq.q: Sweeping Edge or Sharpness?
faq.a: Not a choice - they stack on the same sword. Sharpness raises your direct hit (which also raises the sweep, since sweep damage scales off sword damage), and Sweeping Edge raises the splash percentage. The classic mob-farm sword has both.

name: How to Get Bane of Arthropods in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Bane of Arthropods is a weapon enchantment (max level V) that adds 2.5 hearts of damage per level against spiders, cave spiders, bees, silverfish and endermites, and slows them with Slowness IV for a few seconds. Get it from the enchanting table, librarian trades, fishing, or structure chests. It cannot combine with Sharpness, Smite, Density or Breach.
steps: Enchant at the table. Swords and spears can roll Bane of Arthropods up to V; in Bedrock, axes and maces too (in Java, axes and maces need an anvil + book). Use 15 bookshelves for level 30 rolls.
Or find the book. Librarian trades, fishing treasure and non-village structure chests all carry it. In Bedrock, raid mobs can drop enchanted books as well.
Know your targets. It works against exactly five mobs: spiders, cave spiders, bees, silverfish and endermites. Each level adds 2.5 hearts against them - Bane V adds 12.5 hearts per hit.
Use the slow. Every hit also inflicts Slowness IV for a random 1 to 1.5 seconds at level I, growing by 0.5 seconds per level up to 3.5 seconds at V. Spiders barely crawl toward you.

Decide where it fits. It is mutually exclusive with Sharpness, Smite, Density and Breach. Sharpness wins as the generalist, Smite for undead farms - Bane's real home is a cave spider XP farm sword, where cave spiders melt and stop in place.
materials: Enchanting table + bookshelves, or anvil + Bane of Arthropods book
A cave spider spawner to conquer
editionNote: Both editions add 2.5 hearts per level, but Bedrock rounds damage down, making levels I, III and V slightly weaker than Java. In Bedrock, axes and maces get it directly at the table; in Java they need an anvil. In Java, offhand spear charge attacks do not apply it (known bug MC-308270).
versions: Bane of Arthropods has existed since enchantments launched in Beta 1.9 Prerelease 3 (2011). Spears joined its item list in the 26.x updates.

faq.q: Bane of Arthropods or Sharpness?
faq.a: Sharpness for almost everything: +0.5 to 3 hearts against ALL mobs. Bane adds far more (+2.5 per level) but only against five arthropod mobs. Keep one Bane sword for spider and cave spider farms; put Sharpness on your everyday blade.

faq.q: Does Bane of Arthropods work on shulkers or the warden?
faq.a: No - despite the buggy look, shulkers are not arthropods. The full list is spiders, cave spiders, bees, silverfish and endermites. For everything else the enchantment adds zero damage.

faq.q: Is Bane of Arthropods good for cave spider farms?
faq.a: It is THE enchantment for them. The 2.5-hearts-per-level bonus plus Slowness IV means cave spiders die in one hit and never reach you through the farm gaps - much better than Smite or Sharpness there.

name: How to Get Curse of Binding in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Curse of Binding is a treasure enchantment (level I only) that locks an item into your armor slot - you cannot take it off until you die, the item breaks, or you enter Creative mode. It comes from fishing, librarian trades, and structure chests. It is a curse, not a bonus: think twice before putting it on.
steps: Know what it does. A cursed item equipped in an armor slot cannot be removed in survival. Ever. Not with a grindstone, not with a crafting table - those just give it back still cursed.
Find it as treasure. Curse of Binding never appears on the enchanting table. Look in fishing loot, librarian trades (any level), non-village structure chests, and - in Bedrock - raid mob drops.
Learn the escape routes. Three ways out: die (the item drops), break the item (only if it has durability), or switch to Creative. With keep_inventory on, only breaking works.

Beware the special cases. Carved pumpkins and mob heads have no durability, so death is the ONLY way out - in hardcore that means never. The same applies to elytra, which have durability but are painful to break. One mercy: placing a cursed pumpkin or head as a block and mining it removes the curse.

Use it on purpose. It is mostly a trolling tool (dispenser a cursed pumpkin onto a friend), but it has real uses: locking armor onto players in adventure maps, or onto mobs so they never swap for better dropped gear.
materials: Nothing to craft - it is a treasure enchantment
Fishing rod, librarian villager, or structure chests
An armor piece you are VERY sure about
A friend with a sense of humor (for the pumpkin trick)
editionNote: Identical in Java and Bedrock: the item stays on until death, breaking, or Creative. Mobs wearing cursed gear are also stuck with it - a zombie in a cursed leather helmet will not swap it for netherite.
versions: Curse of Binding arrived in the Exploration Update (Java 1.11, 2016; Bedrock 1.1, 2017) alongside Curse of Vanishing and the totem of undying.

faq.q: How do I remove Curse of Binding?
faq.a: Die, break the item, or go Creative - those are the only ways. For cursed carved pumpkins and mob heads specifically, place the block and mine it: the curse is removed when it drops as an item.

faq.q: Does the grindstone remove Curse of Binding?
faq.a: No - grindstones cannot remove curses. The item comes out still cursed, same with crafting-grid combining. Curses are permanent; only the escape routes (death, breaking, Creative) work.

faq.q: Can I die on purpose to remove it?
faq.a: Yes, that is the standard fix - store your valuables, jump off something tall, and pick the freed item back up. With keep_inventory on, though, the item stays on your corpse-self, so you must break it instead.

what does curse of binding do

name: How to Get Curse of Vanishing in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Curse of Vanishing is a treasure enchantment (level I only) that makes the item disappear forever when you die - no death drop, no corpse run. It comes from fishing, librarian trades, and structure chests, and it can appear on almost any gear. It is a curse: the main skill is knowing how to work around it.
steps: Know what it does. When you die holding a cursed item, it vanishes from the world instead of dropping. Nothing - not even a hopper - can recover it.

Find it as treasure. It never comes from the enchanting table. Fishing loot, librarian trades (swamp librarians with the trade rebalance datapack), non-village structure chests and, in Bedrock, raid drops.

Learn the exceptions. The item does NOT vanish if you manually dropped it before dying, or if it sits inside a shulker box or bundle in your inventory - the curse cannot see inside containers. With keep_inventory on, it never triggers at all.
Accept it cannot be cleansed. Grindstones and crafting combining cannot remove curses. Once an item is cursed, it stays cursed until it vanishes or breaks.

Exploit it. Vanishing has real uses: it prevents enemies from looting your gear in PvP, and mapmakers use it for one-life items. For everyday gear, though, treat it as a warning label on otherwise nice loot.
materials: Nothing to craft - it is a treasure enchantment
Fishing rod, librarian villager, or structure chests
A shulker box or bundle (to smuggle it through death)
editionNote: Same behavior in Java and Bedrock: vanish on death, containers and manual drops exempt, keep_inventory disables it. In Bedrock it can also appear on the recovery compass - a uniquely cruel combination.
versions: Curse of Vanishing arrived in the Exploration Update (Java 1.11, 2016; Bedrock 1.1, 2017) together with Curse of Binding.

faq.q: How do I remove Curse of Vanishing?
faq.a: You cannot - grindstones and crafting cannot strip curses. The practical workaround is not removal but routing: keep the item inside a shulker box or bundle, where the curse cannot trigger, or drop it before a risky fight.

faq.q: Does Curse of Vanishing work in a shulker box?
faq.a: No - items inside shulker boxes or bundles survive death normally. This is intended behavior (Mojang marked the bug report as works-as-intended) and the standard way to protect cursed loot.

faq.q: Is Curse of Vanishing ever useful?
faq.a: Yes - in PvP it denies your killer the loot, since your best sword vanishes instead of dropping for them. Adventure maps also use it to enforce single-use items. Outside that, it is a tax on treasure loot.
