name: How to Breed Axolotls in Minecraft (Blue Axolotl Guide)
quickAnswer: Feed two axolotls a bucket of tropical fish each and they enter love mode: a baby spawns with 1-7 XP. Every baby has a 1 in 1,200 chance to be the ultra-rare blue variant - the ONLY way to get one. Parents need 5 minutes between breeds in Java (1 minute in Bedrock).
steps: Catch your axolotls. Scoop them with a water bucket in lush caves - they come in pink, brown, gold, cyan and wild. Two is the minimum breeding pair.
Farm tropical fish. Find them in warm oceans, lush caves and mangrove swamps, and catch each one ALIVE with a water bucket. Raw or cooked tropical fish does NOT work - only living ones in buckets.
Set up a pool. Axolotls need water: dig a breeding pond near your base, at least a few blocks deep, with no open route to the sea.
Feed one bucket of tropical fish to each parent. Hearts appear, they swim together, and a baby axolotl spawns with a puff of XP.
Chase the blue one. Each baby rolls a 1/1200 chance for the blue variant; otherwise it inherits a random parent's color. Blue never spawns naturally - breeding is the only path.
Speed up the grind: babies take 20 minutes to grow, but each bucket of tropical fish fed to a baby cuts 10% off the remaining time. In Bedrock parents can rebreed after just 1 minute.
materials: Lots of tropical fish buckets (a warm ocean trip or a fish farm)
A safe water pond with walls
Patience - 1/1200 odds means hundreds of babies
editionNote: Follow range differs: axolotls follow bucket-holders within 10 blocks in Java, 16 in Bedrock. Rebreed cooldown is 5 minutes in Java vs 1 minute in Bedrock - Bedrock is the faster blue-farm platform. One trap in both: picking up a fed axolotl before it mates resets its willingness, so feed again if you bucket it mid-courtship.
versions: Axolotls and the blue variant arrived in Caves & Cliffs Part I (1.17, 2021). Before 1.17.1 the blue one was even rarer in practice; the 1/1200 breeding chance has been stable since.

faq.q: Can blue axolotls spawn naturally?
faq.a: No - wild lush-cave spawns are only pink, brown, gold, cyan and wild. Blue exists exclusively as a 1/1200 breeding roll, which is what makes it the game's classic flex pet.

faq.q: Do two blue parents guarantee blue babies?
faq.a: No - even two blue parents produce a random parent's color UNLESS the baby hits the 1/1200 blue roll. Every baby rolls blue independently, whatever the parents look like.

faq.q: Why won't my axolotls breed?
faq.a: Three usual suspects: you fed raw tropical fish instead of a living bucket; the parents are still on cooldown (5 min Java / 1 min Bedrock); or you bucketed a fed axolotl before it reached its mate, which resets its willingness - feed it again.

name: How to Make a Banner in Minecraft (Loom Guide)
quickAnswer: Craft a banner with 6 matching wool + 1 stick, then use a loom (2 string + 2 planks) with dyes to add patterns - up to 6 layers in survival. Special pattern items (creeper charge, skull charge, thing, flow, guster...) unlock unique designs, and a plain banner plus a shield combines into a custom shield.
steps: Craft the base banner: 6 wool of one color in the top two rows + 1 stick in the bottom middle. The wool color becomes the background.
Craft a loom: 2 string over 2 planks. It is also the shepherd villager's job site block.
Open the loom: banner in the left slot, dye in the middle, optional banner pattern item on the right. Pick a design from the list - the preview shows exactly what you get.
Layer patterns: each pass through the loom adds one pattern layer, up to 6 in survival. The last layer goes on top, so plan the order (background shapes first, icons last).

Hunt special patterns: flower charge (oxeye daisy), creeper charge (creeper head), skull charge (wither skeleton skull), thing (enchanted golden apple), snout (piglin banner pattern from bastions), globe (cartographer trade), flow and guster (trial chambers).
Use the result: place banners as decoration, copy finished designs by crafting banner + same-color blank banner, or combine one with a shield to carry your colors into battle.
materials: Dyes of every color you plan to use
Optional: banner pattern items for rare designs
editionNote: Nearly identical in Java and Bedrock. Java survival banners cap at 6 pattern layers; Bedrock allows more via commands. Both have the same loom interface and pattern list, including the 1.21 flow and guster patterns.
versions: Banners arrived in 1.8 (2014) with crafting-table recipes; the loom replaced that system in 1.14 (Village & Pillage, 2019). Flow and guster patterns came with trial chambers in 1.21.

faq.q: How many layers can a banner have?
faq.a: Six in survival. Each loom pass adds one layer and the game counts them in the tooltip. Commands and the creative inventory can go beyond, but survival stops at 6.

faq.q: How do I put my banner on a shield?
faq.a: Craft the banner together with a plain (unpatterned) shield in the crafting grid - the shield takes the banner's full design. This works once per shield and the shield keeps its durability.

faq.q: Can I wash a mistake off a banner?
faq.a: Yes - use the banner on a cauldron with water to remove the TOP layer only (it costs one water level in Java). Everything below stays, so mistakes are never fatal.

name: How to Use a Bundle in Minecraft (Inventory Guide)
quickAnswer: Craft a bundle with 1 string on top of 1 leather. In your inventory, left-click items onto it (or pick the bundle up and click it on the items) to store a whole stack's worth of mixed items in one slot. Right-click to take items out, and scroll to pick which one.
steps: Craft the bundle: 1 string in the top-middle slot and 1 leather right below it. It needs no crafting table - the 2x2 inventory grid is enough. Combine it with any dye for one of 16 colors.

Understand capacity: a bundle holds what adds up to ONE normal stack. Items that stack to 64 take 1 slot each (64 sticks fill it), items that stack to 16 take 4 slots each (16 ender pearls fill it), and one unstackable item like a sword fills the whole bundle.
Insert items: with the inventory open, left-click the items onto the bundle - or pick up the bundle and left-click it onto the items. Both directions work.

Take items out: hover over the bundle and right-click to grab the most recently added item. Scroll the mouse wheel (or right stick on a controller) to highlight a different slot first, then right-click.
Throw from the hotbar: hold the bundle in hand and press use/right-click to toss the most recent stack out in front of you - handy for passing items to a friend or into lava.
Nest for mega-storage: bundles can go inside other bundles (each costs 1/16 of the outer bundle plus its contents) and inside shulker boxes. Shulker boxes can NOT go inside bundles.
materials: A shulker box for the ultimate portable storage combo
editionNote: Same storage rules in Java and Bedrock. Only the controls differ: a mouse uses right-click + scroll wheel, controllers use the Take-half button + right stick, and touch screens use taps (tap the bundle, tap the item, tap an empty slot).
versions: Bundles were finally released in Java 1.21.2 and Bedrock 1.21.40 (October 2024, the Bundles of Bravery drop) after about four years stuck as an experimental feature. The recipe was simplified to string + leather in the same update.

faq.q: Can a bundle hold a shulker box?
faq.a: No. Shulker boxes cannot go inside bundles, but bundles can go inside shulker boxes - that is the classic endgame inventory setup.

faq.q: Do bundles stack?
faq.a: No, one bundle per inventory slot. You can however nest bundles inside other bundles, at the cost of 1/16 of the outer bundle's space each.

faq.q: What happens if a bundle is destroyed?
faq.a: Its contents spill out as items, just like a broken shulker box - you do not lose them.

faq.q: Is a bundle better than a shulker box?
faq.a: Different jobs. A shulker box stores 27 stacks of one type each; a bundle stores ONE stack mixed across many types. Bundles shine early-game for cleaning up scattered loot.

name: How to Use a Crafter in Minecraft (Autocrafting Guide)
quickAnswer: The crafter crafts automatically every time it receives a redstone pulse. Fill its 3x3 grid (hoppers and droppers can feed it from any side), click empty slots to disable the ones your recipe does not use, then send a signal: the result ejects from the front, or lands directly in a container it faces.
steps: Craft it: 5 iron ingots, 1 crafting table, 2 redstone dust and 1 dropper.
Open the GUI: nine slots in a 3x3 grid, just like a crafting table. Click an empty slot to disable it - disabled slots cannot be filled, which is how you lock a shaped recipe in place.
Feed ingredients with hoppers or droppers pointing into any side. The crafter fills empty enabled slots in reading order (left to right, top to bottom), topping up the smallest matching stack first.
Send a redstone pulse. Four game ticks (0.2s) later, one crafted item ejects from the front face. A steady signal only crafts once - use a clock or repeated pulses for continuous crafting.

Point the front face into a chest, barrel or another container to auto-store results. If that container is full or refuses the item, the crafter drops it into the world instead. Recipe byproducts (empty bottles from honey blocks, buckets from cake) eject right after the main item.
Read it with a comparator: the output signal strength equals the number of slots that are disabled OR contain an item (0-9), regardless of stack size - perfect for detecting a fully loaded crafter.
materials: 5 iron ingots + 1 crafting table + 2 redstone dust + 1 dropper per crafter
Hoppers and/or droppers to feed ingredients
A redstone clock, button or lever for the trigger signal
Optional: comparator for load detection, chest for output
editionNote: Core behavior is identical in both editions. In Java, crafters ignore quasi-connectivity (unlike droppers and dispensers) and pistons cannot move them; in Bedrock pistons can push them.
versions: Added in Java 1.21 and Bedrock 1.21.0 (2024). Before that it existed behind the Update 1.21 experimental toggles in Java 1.20.3 and Bedrock 1.20.50.

faq.q: Why won't my crafter craft?
faq.a: Three usual suspects: the redstone signal is constant instead of pulsing (use a clock), the items do not match a recipe shape, or a disabled slot is blocking an ingredient.

faq.q: Can hoppers pull items out of a crafter?
faq.a: Yes - a hopper underneath removes ingredients from the grid, not the crafted result. The result only leaves through the front face when it crafts.

faq.q: Can a crafter feed another crafter?
faq.a: Yes. A crafter facing a second crafter inserts its output directly, which lets you chain multi-step recipes automatically.

name: How to Get Blue Ice in Minecraft (Fastest Ice)
quickAnswer: Mine blue ice with any Silk Touch tool (a pickaxe is fastest) - without Silk Touch it drops nothing. Find it at the underwater base of icebergs in frozen oceans, craft 9 packed ice into 1 blue ice (81 regular ice total), or buy it from a wandering trader for 6 emeralds.
steps: Get Silk Touch first. Blue ice breaks instantly into nothing without it. Any Silk Touch tool works, but a pickaxe mines it fastest.
Hunt icebergs in frozen ocean biomes: blue ice generates along their underwater base and in big arching formations nearby. Rarely, a whole iceberg is made of blue ice - a jackpot.
Craft it instead: fill the 3x3 grid with packed ice to get 1 blue ice. Since packed ice is 9 regular ice, one blue ice costs 81 ice - an ice farm makes this painless.
Buy it from wandering traders: they sell 1 blue ice for 6 emeralds. Prices are steep, but it saves the trip.
Loot natural piles: blue ice also generates in some snowy plains village houses and inside ancient cities.

Put it to work: blue ice is the slipperiest block in the game (boats hit about 72.7 m/s versus 40 on regular ice), it never melts near light, items slide much further in water streams above it, and lava flowing over soul soil next to blue ice generates basalt.
materials: OR 81 regular ice (9 packed ice) per blue ice block
OR 6 emeralds per block from a wandering trader
editionNote: Identical generation and crafting in both editions. Bedrock bonus: a wandering trader currently offering blue ice has a 25% chance (+1% per Looting level) to drop one when killed while you hold an emerald.
versions: Added in Java 1.13 (Update Aquatic, 2018) and Bedrock 1.4.0. It has been renewable ever since packed ice became craftable in the same release; ancient cities added another natural source in 1.19.

faq.q: Does blue ice melt?
faq.a: No. Unlike regular ice, blue ice never melts, even right next to torches or glowstone - same as packed ice.

faq.q: Is blue ice faster than packed ice?
faq.a: Yes. Boats top out around 72.7 m/s on blue ice versus 40 m/s on ice or packed ice, and items in water streams slide further. For long ice roads, blue ice is worth it.

faq.q: Can you craft blue ice back into packed ice?
faq.a: No - blue ice is not a storage block. The conversion is one-way, so spend your ice wisely.

keywords: how to get blue ice minecraft

name: How to Use a Brush in Minecraft (Archaeology Guide)
quickAnswer: Craft a brush with a feather on top, a copper ingot in the middle and a stick on the bottom. Hold use on suspicious sand or suspicious gravel for about 4.8 seconds and an item slowly emerges - pottery sherds, diamonds, sniffer eggs and more, depending on the structure. You can also brush armadillos for scutes.
steps: Craft the brush in a vertical line: feather, copper ingot, stick. It has 64 uses in Java (65 in Bedrock).

Find suspicious blocks: suspicious sand generates in desert temples, desert wells and warm ocean ruins; suspicious gravel in cold ocean ruins and trail ruins. They look almost identical to normal sand/gravel - look for the slightly rougher texture.
Hold the use button on a suspicious block. Do NOT break it - broken suspicious blocks drop nothing. Brushing takes 96 game ticks (4.8 seconds) per block.
Watch the item emerge: a little item pokes out of the block in stages, then pops out, and the block turns into regular sand or gravel. If you stop mid-brush, the block slowly resets.

Know what is inside: loot depends on the structure - desert pyramids give sherds, diamonds and TNT; trail ruins hide sherds, templates and colored glass; ocean ruins hide sherds and sniffer eggs (warm ruins only for eggs).

Bonus use: hold the brush on an armadillo to make it drop an armadillo scute. This costs 16 durability, so a fresh brush yields 4 scutes in Java (5 in Bedrock). Enchant with Unbreaking or Mending to make it last.
materials: 1 feather + 1 copper ingot + 1 stick per brush
Several spare brushes for a big dig site (or Mending)
Shovel to clear the normal sand/gravel around the suspicious blocks
editionNote: Brushing works the same in both editions. Two small differences: the brush has 64 durability in Java and 65 in Bedrock, so armadillo brushing yields 4 vs 5 scutes per brush.
versions: Added in Java 1.20 and Bedrock 1.20.0 (Trails & Tales, 2023) together with the archaeology system. Armadillo brushing arrived later in Java 1.20.5 / Bedrock 1.20.80.

faq.q: Can I mine suspicious sand with a shovel?
faq.a: You can, but it drops nothing - the loot only comes out by brushing. Always brush suspicious blocks, never break them.

faq.q: How do I tell suspicious sand from normal sand?
faq.a: Suspicious blocks have a subtly rougher, speckled texture and are not affected by gravity. When in doubt, tap the brush on the block: if the brushing animation digs in, it is suspicious.

faq.q: Where do I find sniffer eggs?
faq.a: Only by brushing suspicious sand in warm ocean ruins - each block has a 1/15 chance (6.7%) to hide one. Cold ruins and trail ruins use suspicious gravel instead and never give eggs.

name: How to Tame an Allay in Minecraft (Find, Befriend & Duplicate)
quickAnswer: Allays cannot be tamed like a wolf, but giving one any item (use it on the allay) makes it follow you and fetch dropped copies of that item. Find them caged at pillager outposts or jailed in woodland mansions - and duplicate them with an amethyst shard while they dance to a jukebox.
steps: Find an allay: they only spawn during world generation - 50% chance of 1-3 in the dark oak cages at pillager outposts, and 50% chance of 1-3 in the jail cells inside woodland mansions. Break them out.
Befriend it: hold ANY item and press use on the allay. It takes the item, starts following you (within 64 blocks) and searches for dropped copies of that same item within 32 blocks of you.
Take the item back with an empty hand (use on the allay) if you want it to stop following or change jobs.

Automate collection with a note block: if a playing note block sounds within 16 blocks, the allay delivers items there for 30 seconds instead of to you. Repeat the note to keep it locked on - the classic farm sorting trick.

Duplicate your allay: play any music disc in a jukebox so it dances, then give it an amethyst shard. It splits into two allays and the shard is consumed. Both allays get a 5-minute cooldown before duplicating again.
Keep it safe: allays have 20 health, regenerate 2 HP per second and cannot be hurt by their owner. A lead ties them to a fence - but a leashed allay will not follow you through portals.
materials: Any item to hand over (the one you want collected)
Amethyst shard + jukebox + any music disc (for duplication)
Note block (optional, for farm delivery points)
editionNote: Behavior is nearly identical. Bedrock extras: allays teleport to you through nether portals, and using a lead or name tag on an allay gives the item to it. In Java a name tag always performs its naming function instead.
versions: Added in Java 1.19 and Bedrock 1.19.0 (The Wild Update, 2022) after winning the Minecraft Live 2021 mob vote. Amethyst duplication arrived in the same update.

faq.q: Can you tame an allay like a wolf or cat?
faq.a: Not exactly - there is no tame button. Giving it an item makes it YOUR allay: it follows you, works for you and cannot be damaged by you. Taking the item back releases it.

faq.q: Why won't my allay pick up items?
faq.a: Three common reasons: the mob_griefing game rule is false, the drops are further than 32 blocks from you, or you are more than 64 blocks away so it is not following.

faq.q: Can an allay find any item?
faq.a: It collects dropped copies of the exact item it holds - it ignores enchantments and custom names, and it cannot fetch items stored inside shulker boxes.

name: How to Use the Mace in Minecraft (Smash Attack Guide)
quickAnswer: The mace is slow on the ground but deadly from above: fall at least 1.5 blocks and hit a mob mid-fall for a smash attack - +4 damage per block for the first 3 blocks fallen, +2 for the next 5, then +1 per block, with NO upper cap. A successful smash also cancels your fall damage.
steps: Get the mace first: craft it from a breeze rod and a heavy core (trial chambers loot). See our how-to-get-mace guide.
On the ground it is mediocre: 6 damage per hit with the slowest attack speed in Java (0.6). Use it like an axe for panic swings, not as your main DPS.
The real move is the smash attack: fall 1.5+ blocks and attack before landing. Any fall counts - jump off a ledge, pillar up and drop, or bounce in with a wind charge.

Damage scales with distance fallen: +4 per block for the first 3 blocks, +2 per block for the next 5, then +1 per block forever. A 10-block drop already hits like a netherite sword crit - and from a tall tower it one-shots almost anything.
Landing a smash resets your fall height, so you take zero fall damage. It also knocks back everything within 2.5 blocks (not you).

Enchant it: Density adds +0.5 damage per level per block fallen (best for pure smash damage), Breach shreds armored targets, and Wind Burst bounces you back up after a smash so you can chain attacks. Repair with breeze rods in an anvil - one rod restores 25%.
materials: Wind charges (optional, for ground smash setups)
Density, Breach or Wind Burst enchanted books
editionNote: Bedrock smash attacks are even stronger: there is no attack cooldown, and smash attacks work during elytra flight. In Java you must unequip the elytra before the hit lands, and the slow 0.6 attack speed applies to normal swings. Neither edition can smash with Slow Falling active.
versions: Added in Java 1.21 and Bedrock 1.21.0 (Tricky Trials, 2024) alongside the trial chambers, the breeze and the mace-exclusive enchantments Density, Breach and Wind Burst.

faq.q: How much damage can a smash attack do?
faq.a: There is no cap. After the first 8 blocks (+22 damage), every extra block fallen adds +1 - a 100-block drop adds over 110 damage on top of the base 6, enough to one-shot nearly any mob in the game.

faq.q: Does the smash attack work with elytra?
faq.a: Descending with an elytra counts as fallen blocks. In Bedrock the smash works mid-flight; in Java you must unequip the elytra before the hit connects.

faq.q: Density or Breach - which is better?
faq.a: Density multiplies smash damage and wins for one-hit drops. Breach ignores a big chunk of armor and wins against players or armored mobs in prolonged fights. You cannot put both on one mace.

name: How to Make Mud Bricks in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft packed mud from 1 mud + 1 wheat, then craft 4 packed mud into 4 mud bricks. Mud comes from water bottles on dirt (or mangrove swamps). Mud bricks also make stairs, slabs and walls - the perfect brown desert-ruin building block.
steps: Get mud: use a water bottle on any dirt block (dirt, coarse dirt or rooted dirt), or dig it straight out of a mangrove swamp with a shovel.
Craft packed mud: 1 mud + 1 wheat anywhere in the grid makes 1 packed mud. Wheat comes from any small wheat farm.
Craft mud bricks: 4 packed mud in a 2x2 square gives 4 mud bricks. Any pickaxe mines them - other tools drop nothing.
Expand the set: mud bricks craft (or stonecut) into mud brick stairs, slabs and walls - the stonecutter wastes nothing.
Alternative source: mud bricks generate naturally inside trail ruins, so archaeology trips double as a building-material run.
Scale up with automation: a dispenser firing water bottles at dirt makes mud hands-free - see our clay farm guide for the full dripstone cell design that also renews the raw material.
materials: Mud (water bottle + dirt, or a mangrove swamp)
Any pickaxe for harvesting placed bricks
editionNote: Identical recipes and behavior in Java and Bedrock.
versions: Added in Java 1.19 and Bedrock 1.19.0 (The Wild Update, 2022) alongside mud, mangrove swamps and the mud-to-clay dripstone mechanic.

faq.q: What is the difference between mud, packed mud and mud bricks?
faq.a: Mud is the raw block (from dirt + water bottle). Packed mud is mud + wheat - a building block itself. Mud bricks are 4 packed mud crafted together - the polished brick version with stairs, slabs and walls.

faq.q: Are mud bricks renewable?
faq.a: Fully. Dirt is renewable (coarse dirt + hoe), water bottles are endless, and wheat grows in days - so a mud brick supply never runs dry.

faq.q: Do mud bricks need a specific pickaxe?
faq.a: Any pickaxe works, even wooden. Mining them with anything else (or bare hands) breaks the block without dropping it.

keywords: how to make mud bricks minecraft

name: How to Find the Deep Dark in Minecraft
quickAnswer: The deep dark is a sculk-covered cave biome in the deepslate layer, usually under mountains (jagged, frozen and stony peaks are your best bet). Dig down to around Y=-52 beneath a big mountain and branch-mine - the floor turning to sculk means you found it. No normal mobs spawn there; the danger is the warden.
steps: Pick the right surface: the deep dark favors low-erosion regions, which in practice means BIG mountains. Frozen peaks, jagged peaks and stony peaks are the classic markers; it can appear under other terrain too, but mountains are the reliable hunt.
Descend into the deepslate layer: the biome lives down around Y=-52 and below, occasionally reaching higher under tall mountains. Staircase down - never dig straight.

Watch for the floor change: grey sculk patches with glowing sculk veins, sculk sensors and shriekers mean you have arrived. The biome is almost lightless - no glow lichen, just catalysts and lava glow.
Notice the silence: no regular hostile mobs spawn in the deep dark. The only spawns are wardens (from shriekers) plus the odd monster room mob. Quiet does not mean safe.
Sneak from here: sculk sensors hear your footsteps. Crouch everywhere, carpet or wool your path, and never set off a sculk shrieker three times - that summons the warden.
Loot the prize: the deep dark is the ONLY biome where ancient cities generate. Follow the sculk and you will often find one nearby - see our ancient city guide for the loot runs.
materials: Iron or better pickaxe plus torches
Wool blocks or carpet (they muffle vibrations)
Food, and a water bucket for escapes
Night vision potions help a lot in the lightless biome
editionNote: Same generation and mechanics in Java and Bedrock.
versions: Added in Java 1.19 and Bedrock 1.19.0 (The Wild Update, 2022) together with ancient cities, sculk and the warden.

faq.q: What Y level is the deep dark?
faq.a: It generates in the deepslate layer, most commonly around Y=-52 and deeper, though under very tall mountains it can reach up into the stone layer.

faq.q: Is the deep dark only under mountains?
faq.a: Most often, yes - it favors low-erosion regions, which usually means mountain ranges. It can generate under other biomes too; mountains are just the reliable way to hunt it.

faq.q: Do mobs spawn in the deep dark?
faq.a: No regular mob spawning happens there at all. The only threats are the warden summoned by sculk shriekers and mobs from monster rooms that overlap the biome.

keywords: how to find deep dark minecraft

name: How to Get Pointed Dripstone in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Mine pointed dripstone in dripstone caves with any tool (a pickaxe is fastest), or buy 2 for 1 emerald from wandering traders. To grow your own: hang one under a dripstone block with a water source above - it lengthens about one growth step every 5 in-game days.
steps: Find a dripstone caves biome underground - it generates at any height, but caves with giant stalactite columns are the jackpot. Every spike is harvestable pointed dripstone.
Mine it with anything; a pickaxe is fastest. Breaking any segment drops the whole column below it, so harvest from the bottom up.
Buy spares: wandering traders sell 2 pointed dripstone for 1 emerald when the trade shows up.
Set up a farm: place a dripstone block, put a water source directly above it (in Java a waterlogged block works too), and hang a pointed dripstone underneath.
Wait: each random tick can advance the stalactite one growth step, averaging 5 in-game days (about 100 minutes) per step. It grows to several blocks and can merge with a stalagmite below.
Harvest the tip and leave the base hanging - it regrows forever. Scale with rows: our dripstone farm and lava farm guides use the same cells for infinite dripstone, lava and clay.
materials: Dripstone block + water source for the farm
1 emerald per 2 dripstone at the wandering trader (optional)
editionNote: Growing works the same in both editions (Java also accepts waterlogged blocks as the water source). Bedrock bonus: a wandering trader offering the trade has a 25% chance (+1% per Looting level) to drop 2 dripstone when killed while you hold an emerald.
versions: Added in Java 1.17 and Bedrock 1.17.0 (Caves & Cliffs Part I, 2021). The mud-to-clay conversion arrived later in 1.19.

faq.q: Does pointed dripstone regrow?
faq.a: Yes - a stalactite hanging under a dripstone block with water above it keeps growing forever, roughly one growth step per 5 in-game days. Harvest the tip, keep the base.

faq.q: What is pointed dripstone used for?
faq.a: Lava and water farming (cauldrons fill from drips), converting mud to clay, stalactite drop traps, and pure decoration in cave builds.

faq.q: Do stalactites hurt when they fall?
faq.a: Yes - breaking the block a stalactite hangs from drops it, and the falling spikes damage whatever they land on. Stalagmites also multiply fall damage if you land on them. Handle with care.

keywords: how to get pointed dripstone minecraft

name: How to Make a Soul Torch in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft 4 soul torches from coal or charcoal + a stick + soul sand or soul soil stacked vertically. They glow a spooky cyan at light level 10 (dimmer than normal torches) and - best part - piglins run away from them.
steps: Gather soul sand or soul soil in the Nether: soul sand fills the soul sand valley, soul soil is the valley's ash block (also in bastions). Silk Touch is NOT needed.
Craft vertically: coal or charcoal on top, stick in the middle, soul sand or soul soil on the bottom - that makes 4 soul torches.
Use them as mood lighting: the flame burns cyan-blue and the light level is 10 versus a normal torch's 14 - dimmer, so mobs can still spawn further out. It is atmosphere, not coverage.
Weaponize them against piglins: piglins avoid soul fire light - soul torches, soul lanterns and soul campfires all repel them. Line your nether routes to keep piglins at distance.
Craft the family: a soul torch + 8 iron nuggets makes a soul lantern (light 10, hangable); soul soil + sticks + logs makes the soul campfire. Same piglin-repelling effect.
Snow golem trick: soul torches do not melt snow or ice, so they are the safe lighting for frozen builds and ice roads.
materials: 1 soul sand or soul soil (Nether, soul sand valley)
editionNote: Identical recipe and behavior in Java and Bedrock.
versions: Added in Java 1.16 and Bedrock 1.16.0 (Nether Update, 2020) alongside soul lanterns, soul campfires and the soul sand valley.

faq.q: Do soul torches keep mobs away?
faq.a: Only piglins. The light level 10 is too dim to fully mob-proof an area (normal torches glow at 14), but piglins actively avoid soul fire light sources - that is the real utility.

faq.q: Soul torch vs lantern - which is better?
faq.a: A soul lantern is brighter? No - both glow at 10. The lantern is hangable and prettier; the torch is cheap and needs no iron. Both repel piglins and avoid melting snow.

faq.q: Can you make soul torches without going to the Nether?
faq.a: No - soul sand and soul soil are Nether-only blocks. One quick soul sand valley trip gives you a lifetime supply.

keywords: how to make soul torch minecraft

name: How to Get Pink Petals in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Pink petals grow on the ground in cherry grove biomes - break them with anything (they drop one item per petal in the spot, up to 4). Farm them with bone meal: each use adds a petal to the spot, and at 4 petals it pops off a free copy.
steps: Find a cherry grove - the pink-leafed mountain biome. Pink petals generate scattered on the grass there, 1 to 4 per block.
Break them by hand or with any tool: they break instantly and drop exactly as many items as petals were placed in that spot.
Farm them: use bone meal on a pink petal block and the petal count rises by 1. Once it holds 4, each extra bone meal pops off a copy of the petal - infinite petals from one starter.
Java only bonus: bone meal on grass blocks inside a cherry grove also grows fresh pink petals nearby (this does not work on Bedrock).
Craft pink dye: one pink petal makes one pink dye, shapeless - the cheapest pink dye in the game.

Bonus use: bees pollinate pink petals and can be bred with them. Oak, birch and cherry saplings grown within 2 blocks of pink petals have a 5% chance to sprout a bee nest with 2-3 bees - free honey starter.
materials: Nothing to collect them - bare hands work
Bone meal for farming (a composter or skeleton drops keep you stocked)
Saplings (oak, birch or cherry) if you want the bee nest trick
editionNote: The bone-meal-on-grass trick that grows new petals in cherry groves is Java only (Bedrock bug MCPE-168074). Everything else works the same in both editions.
versions: Added in Java 1.20 and Bedrock 1.20.0 (Trails & Tales, 2023) together with the cherry grove biome.

faq.q: Can you farm pink petals?
faq.a: Yes - bone meal adds petals to an existing pink petal block, and at the maximum of 4 petals each extra bone meal drops a free copy. One petal plus bone meal is infinite petals.

faq.q: What are pink petals used for?
faq.a: Decoration (up to 4 petals per block on most dirt-type blocks), pink dye, breeding bees, and the 5% bee nest chance on saplings grown next to them.

faq.q: Do pink petals regrow naturally?
faq.a: No natural regrowth, but they are renewable through bone meal - on the petals themselves in both editions, and on cherry grove grass in Java.

keywords: how to get pink petals minecraft

name: How to Grow Glow Berries in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Plant glow berries on the underside of any solid block and the cave vine grows downward - each new vine block has an 11% chance of carrying berries. The fast way: bone meal ANY part of the vine and it instantly produces berries.
steps: Get starter glow berries from lush caves (harvest with the use button - no need to break the vine) or from our glow berries guide's other sources.
Plant them on the bottom face of any full solid block. They grow downward one block at a time, no light or water requirements.
Wait for growth: each random tick has a 10% chance to extend the vine (about 11 minutes per block on average), and each NEWLY grown block has an 11% chance to bear berries.
Skip the waiting: use bone meal on any block of the vine and it sprouts berries instantly. This is the core of every glow berry farm.
Harvest with the use button so the vine stays and keeps producing; breaking the vine only drops a berry if that segment had one, and Fortune does not help.
Use shears on the bottom tip to stop a vine at the exact length you want - perfect for lighting designs, since berry-bearing vines glow at light level 14.
Extra uses: feed two foxes glow berries to breed them, compost them at a 30% fill chance, or eat them in a pinch (2 hunger points).
materials: At least 1 glow berry (from lush caves)
Any solid block to hang the vine from
editionNote: Growth and bone meal mechanics are identical in both editions. Eating one restores 2 hunger; saturation differs slightly (0.4 Java, 1.2 Bedrock).
versions: Glow berries were added in Java 1.17 and Bedrock 1.17.0 (Caves & Cliffs Part I, 2021); lush caves started generating naturally in 1.18.

faq.q: Do existing cave vines grow berries over time?
faq.a: No - only newly grown vine blocks can spawn with berries (11% chance each). An old bare vine stays bare forever unless you use bone meal on it.

faq.q: What is the fastest glow berry farm?
faq.a: A row of long vines plus bone meal. Each bone meal on any segment makes that segment produce a berry instantly, so one long vine turns a bone meal supply into a berry supply.

faq.q: Do cave vines give off light?
faq.a: Yes - any vine segment carrying glow berries emits light level 14, as bright as a torch, which is why they double as cave lighting.

keywords: how to grow glow berries minecraft

name: How to Get Calcite in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Calcite forms the middle layer of amethyst geodes (between the smooth basalt shell and the amethyst core) and also generates in white strips across stony peaks mountains. Mine it with any pickaxe - without one it drops nothing.
steps: Hunt an amethyst geode: calcite is the white ring between the outer smooth basalt and the inner amethyst blocks. Geodes spawn underground and are often exposed in caves, aquifers and even underwater ravines.
Strip-mine the calcite layer: one geode yields stacks of it, and while you are there you can grab amethyst shards and smooth basalt too.
Check stony peaks: in mountain biomes with bare stone summits, calcite generates in long surface strips you can quarry with zero digging.
Always use a pickaxe - even a wooden one works. Bare hands or other tools destroy the block with no drop.
Plan your supply: calcite is NOT renewable, so every block in the world is finite. Big white builds mean visiting several geodes.
Use it for clean white builds: calcite is a pure matte white block, softer and weaker than most stone - perfect for walls, statues and trim, not for blast-proofing.
materials: A boat helps - geodes often surface in oceans
editionNote: Identical generation and drops in Java and Bedrock.
versions: Added in Java 1.17 and Bedrock 1.17.0 (Caves & Cliffs Part I, 2021); the stony peaks strips arrived with the new mountains in 1.18.

faq.q: Is calcite renewable?
faq.a: No - there is no farm, trade or craft for calcite. The world generates a finite amount in geodes and stony peaks strips, so stockpile it.

faq.q: Where is calcite most common?
faq.a: Amethyst geodes are the densest source (an entire layer per geode). Stony peaks mountains have visible surface strips that are easier to spot from a distance.

faq.q: What is calcite used for?
faq.a: Pure decoration. It has no crafts, but its clean white texture makes it one of the most popular building blocks for modern and Greek-style builds.

name: How to Get Tuff in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Tuff generates in huge ore blobs below Y=0 - mine deep and you will hit entire caves of it. Use any pickaxe, then run it through a stonecutter for the full polished and brick family, the same blocks trial chambers are built from.
steps: Mine below Y=0: tuff appears in ore blobs anywhere from Y=-64 up to Y=0, in every biome. Any deep mining session runs into it - it is basically the gravel of the deepslate layer.
Use a pickaxe: like most stone, tuff drops nothing without one. Wooden pickaxe works.
Follow the iron veins: below Y=0, large iron ore veins come wrapped in tuff (with raw iron blocks at the core). Spotting tuff patches at deepslate level can lead you to serious iron.
Loot trial chambers: these copper-and-tuff structures are built from tuff bricks and also have tuff in chests - sightseeing and supplies in one trip.
Stonecut everything: one tuff block in a stonecutter converts cleanly into polished tuff, tuff bricks, chiseled variants, slabs, stairs and walls - no wasted material.
Build with the family: tuff's grey-green tones pair perfectly with copper, which is exactly why Mojang built the trial chambers out of them.
materials: A stonecutter to unlock the decorative variants
editionNote: Same generation and crafting in Java and Bedrock.
versions: Tuff was added in Java 1.17 and Bedrock 1.17.0 (Caves & Cliffs Part I, 2021); the polished and brick variants arrived in 1.21 with the trial chambers.

faq.q: What Y level is tuff found at?
faq.a: Between Y=-64 and Y=0, in every biome, as large ore blobs. It also wraps the big iron veins that generate below Y=0.

faq.q: Is tuff renewable?
faq.a: No, but it is absurdly abundant - blobs of up to 864 blocks generate twice per chunk below Y=0, so you will never run out in practice.

faq.q: What can you make with tuff?
faq.a: Via crafting or the stonecutter: polished tuff, tuff bricks, chiseled tuff, and slab/stair/wall versions of each - the complete trial chambers palette.

name: How to Make Mud in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Use a water bottle on any dirt, coarse dirt or rooted dirt block and it turns into mud. Natural mud fills mangrove swamps. Mud crafts into packed mud and mud bricks, and dries into clay over a pointed dripstone.
steps: Craft water bottles: fill glass bottles at any water source or cauldron.
Use a bottle on dirt: right-click dirt, coarse dirt or rooted dirt with the water bottle. The block becomes mud.
Automate it: a dispenser loaded with water bottles converts dirt on its own, which is how automatic mud farms work (dispensers even hit the bottom face, which players cannot).
Or dig it naturally: mangrove swamps are carpeted in mud, and it also shows up in trail ruins and some trial chambers entrances. A shovel is fastest.
Craft the building blocks: mud + wheat makes packed mud, and 4 packed mud make 4 mud bricks - a full warm-brown brick palette with stairs, slabs and walls.

Dry it into clay: place mud on top of a block with a pointed dripstone hanging underneath and it converts to clay (about 17.6% chance, 45/256, each time the stalactite's uppermost block gets a random tick). This makes mud the renewable clay pipeline - see our clay farm.
Know the quirks: mud is slightly shorter than a full block - entities sink into it a little (no slowdown, unlike soul sand), sand drops as an item on it, and hoppers can pull items through it.
materials: A shovel for natural mud in mangrove swamps
Wheat for packed mud, pointed dripstone for clay
editionNote: Conversion and crafting are the same in both editions; the mud-to-clay conversion does not happen in the Nether.
versions: Added in Java 1.19 and Bedrock 1.19.0 (The Wild Update, 2022) with the mangrove swamp.

faq.q: Can you turn mud back into dirt?
faq.a: Indirectly, yes: grow an azalea tree on mud and the mud below becomes rooted dirt, which you can hoe into normal dirt.

faq.q: Is mud renewable?
faq.a: Yes - water bottles on dirt make infinite mud, and water is infinite. That also makes clay renewable through the dripstone drying trick.

faq.q: Does mud slow you down like soul sand?
faq.a: No. You sink a few pixels into mud, but movement speed is normal - it is safe for paths and farms.

name: How to Get the Bolt Armor Trim in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Bolt armor trim smithing templates drop from standard vaults and chests in trial chambers. Once you have one, duplicate it with 7 diamonds + a copper block, then apply it at a smithing table with any armor piece and a trim material.
steps: Find trial chambers and earn trial keys from the trial spawners - each spawner you defeat has a chance to eject a key.
Open standard vaults: the bolt armor trim is a vault and chest drop inside trial chambers. More chambers, more vaults, better odds.
Duplicate your first template immediately: 7 diamonds + 1 block of copper (waxed works too) + the template crafts 2 templates - never risk your only copy.
Apply it at a smithing table: template + any armor piece + any trim material (iron, gold, diamond, emerald, lapis, redstone, quartz, amethyst, netherite or copper).
Pick your colors: the trim material sets the color - diamond blue, gold yellow, redstone red - over the bolt pattern's lightning lines.
Want the rarer sibling? Flow armor trim comes from OMINOUS vaults, which need ominous trial keys from ominous trial spawners - see our bad omen guide.
materials: Trial keys from defeated trial spawners
A smithing table, armor piece and trim material
editionNote: Identical loot sources and recipes in Java and Bedrock.
versions: Added in Java 1.21 and Bedrock 1.21.0 (Tricky Trials, 2024) alongside the flow armor trim.

faq.q: What is the difference between bolt and flow armor trims?
faq.a: Both are trial chambers trims. Bolt comes from standard vaults and chests; flow only comes from ominous vaults behind ominous trial keys, making flow the rarer flex.

faq.q: Can you duplicate armor trims?
faq.a: Yes - every smithing template duplicates with 7 diamonds plus its theme block. For bolt that block is copper, so stock up on both.

faq.q: Do armor trims change stats?
faq.a: No - trims are purely cosmetic. The bolt trim adds lightning-styled lines in whatever material color you choose.

name: How to Get Bad Omen in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Since 1.21, Bad Omen only comes from drinking an ominous bottle - dropped by pillager raid captains (the ones with the banner) or looted from vaults. Carry it into a village to start a raid, or near a trial spawner to trigger an ominous trial.
steps: Find a raid captain: pillager outpost leaders and patrol captains wear an ominous banner on their head. Kill one outside a raid and it drops an ominous bottle.
Or loot vaults: standard vaults in trial chambers can contain ominous bottles too.
Drink it: the bottle gives Bad Omen at level I-V for 100 minutes. Higher-level bottles come from higher-difficulty captains and ominous vaults.

Trigger a raid: walk into a village with Bad Omen and it becomes Raid Omen - the raid starts after 30 seconds. On Java, levels above II add an extra wave and stronger raider gear, and Hero of the Village matches your omen level.
Trigger an ominous trial instead: bring Bad Omen near a trial spawner and it transforms into Trial Omen (15 minutes per level), converting nearby spawners into ominous trial spawners.
Cash in: ominous trial spawners drop ominous trial keys, which open ominous vaults - the only source of the heavy core and the flow armor trim.
Change your mind? Drink milk (or die) to clear the effect before you walk somewhere unfortunate.
materials: An ominous bottle from a raid captain or vault
Combat gear for the raid or ominous trial you are about to start
Milk bucket as an emergency exit
editionNote: Big edition split: on Java the omen level upgrades raids (extra wave, better gear, stronger Hero of the Village). On Bedrock the level only affects trial spawners - raids ignore it.
versions: Bad Omen exists since Java 1.14 and Bedrock 1.11 (Village & Pillage); the ominous bottle mechanic replaced automatic Bad Omen from captains in Java 1.21 and Bedrock 1.21.0.

faq.q: Why did killing a pillager captain not give me Bad Omen?
faq.a: Since 1.21 captains drop an ominous BOTTLE instead of applying the effect - you choose when to drink it. No more accidental raids when you walk home through a village.

faq.q: What does Bad Omen do in trial chambers?
faq.a: Near a trial spawner it becomes Trial Omen, turning spawners ominous: harder fights, but they drop ominous trial keys for ominous vaults - heavy cores, flow trims and better loot.

faq.q: How do you get rid of Bad Omen?
faq.a: Drink milk, die, or simply let the 100 minutes run out. It also converts away once it becomes Raid Omen or Trial Omen.

keywords: how to get bad omen minecraft
bad omen raid omen trial omen

name: How to Grow a Mangrove Tree in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Plant a mangrove propagule on dirt, mud, clay or a moss block - on land or underwater - and wait or use bone meal. Propagules hang from mangrove leaves: bonemeal the leaves to grow one, and harvest it once fully grown.
steps: Find a mangrove swamp and look for propagules hanging under mangrove leaves. If none are grown, bonemeal the leaves to force one.
Wait until the hanging propagule is fully grown (4 stages) - only fully grown propagules drop as items. Breaking it early gives nothing.
Plant the propagule on any dirt variant (except dirt paths), mud, clay or a moss block. It is amphibious: it works planted underwater too.
Leave at least 6 empty blocks above it and room for the roots, which spread up to 5 blocks sideways and need solid ground within 11 blocks below (mud does not count as solid).
Wait like a normal sapling (you must stay nearby) or bonemeal the planted propagule to grow the tree instantly, even without light.
Harvest mangrove logs, roots and leaves - the tree also generates moss carpet on nearby mud. Each leaf bonemeal cycle gives more propagules for a full farm.
materials: 1+ mangrove propagules from a mangrove swamp
Dirt, mud, clay or moss blocks to plant on
Bone meal (optional, to grow propagules and trees instantly)
editionNote: Identical in Java and Bedrock.
versions: Mangrove trees and propagules arrived in 1.19 (The Wild Update) on both editions.

faq.q: Can I plant a hanging propagule directly on leaves?
faq.a: No - a propagule hanging from leaves never grows into a tree. Pick it once fully grown and plant it on the ground (or underwater).

faq.q: Why won't my mangrove tree grow?
faq.a: Check the root room: the roots need a solid block (not mud) within an 11-block depth below and up to 5 blocks to the sides, plus 6 empty blocks above the propagule. Tight spots fail silently.

keywords: how to grow mangrove tree minecraft propagule plant underwater mangrove swamp sapling bonemeal roots

name: How to Make a Splash Potion in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Add gunpowder to any regular potion in a brewing stand to turn it into its splash version - throwable, and it affects every entity near the impact. Splash potions are the only way to give effects to mobs or other players.
steps: Brew the normal potion first - for example an awkward potion + magma cream gives a Potion of Fire Resistance.
Get gunpowder: creepers drop 0-2 (no Looting needed to start), ghasts and witches drop it too, and it appears in dungeon, temple, shipwreck and village chests.
Put the finished potion in a brewing stand with gunpowder as the ingredient. Wait 20 seconds.
Out comes the splash version: throw it with the use button. The closer an entity is to the impact, the stronger and longer the effect.

Classic uses: Splash Potion of Harming or Poison against enemies, Splash Healing in team fights, Splash Fire Resistance for a friend in lava, and Splash Weakness (plus a golden apple) to cure zombie villagers.
Add dragon's breath to a splash potion to upgrade it into a lingering potion, which leaves an effect cloud on the ground.
materials: A brewing stand and blaze powder as fuel
1 gunpowder per batch of up to 3 potions
editionNote: Identical recipe on both editions. On Java, effect strength scales with distance from the impact; Bedrock splash potions work the same way in practice.
versions: Splash potions exist since Java Beta 1.9 / 1.0.0 and Bedrock 0.12 (the brewing update).

faq.q: Can I make a splash water bottle?
faq.a: Yes - brewing gunpowder into a water bottle gives a splash water bottle, which extinguishes fire and damages blazes (1 heart per hit).

faq.q: Does making a potion splash change its duration?
faq.a: The potion keeps its base duration, but entities further from the impact point get a weaker version. Hit your target as close as possible.

keywords: splash potion minecraft how to make gunpowder brewing stand throwable weakness harming fire resistance lingering

name: How to Breed Sniffers in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Feed torchflower seeds to two sniffers and they breed, laying a sniffer egg as an item. The egg hatches in 10 minutes on a moss block (20 minutes anywhere else). Sniffers never spawn naturally - your first egg comes from brushing suspicious sand in warm ocean ruins.
steps: Get your first sniffer: brush suspicious sand in warm ocean ruins until a sniffer egg pops out, then place it and wait for it to hatch (10 min on moss, 20 min elsewhere).
You need two sniffers to breed - hatch a second egg from the ruins, or breed once you already have a pair.
Collect torchflower seeds: sniffers dig them up themselves (50/50 with pitcher pods), or grow and harvest torchflowers.
Hold the seeds to lead both sniffers close together, then feed each of them a torchflower seed.
Hearts appear and the pair produces a sniffer egg item plus 1-7 experience - no waiting for a baby to grow this way.
Place the egg on a moss block for the fastest hatch (10 minutes, two crack stages). Moss from shipwrecks, lush caves or a moss farm works; note pale moss blocks do NOT speed it up.
materials: Torchflower seeds (sniffers dig them up, or farm torchflowers)
A moss block to hatch the egg faster
editionNote: Identical in Java and Bedrock. On Java, sniffer eggs hatch without random ticks, so randomTickSpeed does not affect them.
versions: Sniffers arrived in 1.20 (Trails & Tales) on both editions, after winning the 2022 mob vote.

faq.q: Can sniffers spawn in the wild?
faq.a: No - every sniffer comes from a sniffer egg, either brushed from suspicious sand in warm ocean ruins or bred from two sniffers.

faq.q: What do sniffers dig up?
faq.a: Torchflower seeds and pitcher pods with equal odds. They dig only while on the ground, not leashed, in water, tempted, panicking, or in a boat or minecart.

keywords: how to breed sniffers minecraft torchflower seeds sniffer egg hatch moss 10 minutes warm ocean ruins suspicious sand

name: How to Get a Saddle in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft it: 3 leather + 1 iron ingot on a crafting table (since 1.21.6). Before that update, saddles came from fishing (0.8%), ravager drops, strider jockeys, village trading and structure chests like nether fortresses and dungeons.
steps: Craft it (1.21.6+): place leather in the top-center slot and leather, iron ingot, leather across the middle row - 3 leather and 1 iron ingot per saddle.
Fish for one: saddles are a treasure catch with a 0.8% chance per attempt, improved by Luck of the Sea.
Kill a ravager during a raid: it always drops a saddle, and Looting does not change that.
Kill a strider jockey in the Nether (a zombified piglin riding a strider): the strider always drops the saddle it wears.
Trade with a master-level leatherworker villager, who sells a saddle for emeralds.
Loot chests: nether fortresses, bastion remnants and village tannery chests can still hold saddles.
Remove one without killing the mob: since 1.21.6, using shears on a saddled mob takes the saddle off safely.
materials: Or a fishing rod with Luck of the Sea for the old-school route
editionNote: Saddles became craftable in Java 1.21.6 and Bedrock 1.21.90 (3 leather + 1 iron ingot), and the same update lets shears remove a saddle from a mob without killing it. The 1.21.6 update also removed saddles from monster room, ancient city, desert pyramid, jungle pyramid and stronghold altar chests, so chest hunting now means nether fortresses, bastions and village tanneries. Fishing odds (0.8%) and the ravager drop are identical in both editions.
versions: Craftable since 1.21.6 (Java) / 1.21.90 (Bedrock), the Chase the Skies drop. On older versions use fishing, ravagers or chest loot.

faq.q: Can you craft a saddle in Minecraft?
faq.a: Yes, since 1.21.6: 3 leather plus 1 iron ingot, with the leather in the top-center slot and leather-iron-leather across the middle row. Before 1.21.6 saddles were loot-only.

faq.q: What is the fastest way to get a saddle?
faq.a: Craft it from 3 leather and 1 iron ingot - both farmable in minutes. Without crafting, killing a ravager during a raid guarantees one, and master leatherworker villagers sell them for emeralds.

faq.q: How do you get a saddle off a pig or horse?
faq.a: Since 1.21.6, use shears on the saddled mob to remove the saddle without hurting it. On equines and camels you can also open their inventory and take it out of the saddle slot.

keywords: how to get a saddle minecraft saddle recipe craft saddle fishing saddle

name: How to Ride a Strider in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Put a saddle on an adult strider and steer it with a warped fungus on a stick (fishing rod + warped fungus). Striders walk on lava at 4.24 m/s (Java) or 3.71 m/s (Bedrock), making them the best Nether transport.
steps: Get a saddle: craft one with 3 leather + 1 iron ingot, or kill a strider jockey whose strider always drops its saddle.
Craft a warped fungus on a stick: fishing rod + warped fungus from warped forests (or huge warped fungi).
Find a strider walking on the Nether lava seas and use the saddle on it.
Hop on and hold the warped fungus on a stick: the strider walks toward wherever you point it.
Use the stick for a speed boost: 7 to 49 seconds in Java, a flat 16 seconds in Bedrock, costing 1 durability per boost.
Breed striders with warped fungus to build your own herd near a lava lake.
materials: Fire resistance potion recommended for the lava seas
editionNote: Striders are faster in Java (4.24 m/s on lava vs 3.71 in Bedrock) and their boost lasts a random 7-49 seconds, while Bedrock gives a fixed 16 seconds. Out of lava, striders shiver, turn purple and slow down in both editions.
versions: Striders exist since 1.16 (Nether Update). Baby striders cannot be ridden, only adults.

faq.q: Can striders survive out of lava?
faq.a: They survive but hate it: they shiver, turn purple-gray and move slowly. Rain and water hurt them, so keep your strider on lava or dry land and never let it touch water.

faq.q: How do you control a strider?
faq.a: With a warped fungus on a stick, exactly like pigs with a carrot on a stick. Hold it and the strider walks in the direction you look; right-click for a boost that consumes durability.

faq.q: Do saddles come back off a strider?
faq.a: Yes: use shears on the saddled strider to remove the saddle (since 1.21.6), or kill the strider and it always drops the saddle it wears.

keywords: how to ride a strider minecraft warped fungus on a stick nether lava transport strider saddle

name: How to Get a Spyglass in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft it: 1 amethyst shard on top of 2 copper ingots in a vertical line. The spyglass zooms your view to 1/10 of your normal FOV, perfect for scouting terrain, bases and distant mobs.
steps: Get an amethyst shard: mine fully grown amethyst clusters inside an amethyst geode with any pickaxe (Fortune increases drops).
Get 2 copper ingots: smelt raw copper from copper ore, common in dripstone caves and around Y=48.
Craft vertically: amethyst shard in the top slot, then copper ingot, then copper ingot below it.
Use it from your hotbar: hold use to zoom to 1/10 of your FOV (7 degrees at the Java default of 70).
Combine with a high render distance or a tall tower to scout ocean monuments, villages and bastions from far away.
editionNote: The default zoom differs slightly because default FOV differs: 7 degrees in Java (from 70) and 6 degrees in Bedrock (from 60). Crafting and behavior are otherwise identical.
versions: Spyglasses exist since 1.17 (Caves & Cliffs Part 1). Amethyst geodes generate in every overworld chunk region, so there is always one within a reasonable walk.

faq.q: What does a spyglass do in Minecraft?
faq.a: It narrows your field of view to one tenth of normal, acting like a telescope. A square vignette appears while scoping, and you move slower, so it is for scouting, not fighting.

faq.q: Can you enchant a spyglass?
faq.a: No. The spyglass has no durability and no enchantments; it works forever once crafted.

faq.q: Where do I find amethyst for a spyglass?
faq.a: In amethyst geodes: round structures underground (and sometimes exposed in oceans) with smooth basalt, calcite and amethyst blocks. Only fully grown clusters drop shards; the budding amethyst block itself cannot be moved.

keywords: how to make spyglass minecraft spyglass recipe amethyst shard copper zoom telescope

name: How to Raid an Ocean Monument in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Bring water breathing potions, night vision, good armor and milk. Kill the 3 elder guardians first (top room and both wings) to end the Mining Fatigue III, then loot the treasure chamber (8 gold blocks in dark prismarine) and the sponge rooms (~30 wet sponges each).
steps: Prepare: water breathing potions (8 min), night vision, depth strider boots, a door or conduit for air pockets, and milk buckets against Mining Fatigue.
Expect the curse: every elder guardian within 50 blocks applies Mining Fatigue III for 5 minutes, making mining nearly impossible. Milk clears it briefly.
Kill the elder guardian in the topmost room first, then the one in each wing. Use a bow in open water or a sword up close; thorns armor hurts, so watch your health.
Loot the treasure chamber in the central section: 8 blocks of gold encased in dark prismarine.
Find the sponge rooms (opening only in the floor): about 30 wet sponges per room, the only sponge source in the game.
Farm guardians afterward: they only spawn in and around the monument, dropping prismarine shards, prismarine crystals and fish.
materials: Depth Strider boots and Respiration helmet
editionNote: The raid works the same in Java and Bedrock. In Bedrock the Mining Fatigue particle comes from a separate elder guardian ghost entity, and guardians spawn slightly differently, but the 3 elder guardians and loot are identical.
versions: Ocean monuments exist since 1.8 (Bountiful Update). They remain the only sponge source and the only guardian spawn location.

faq.q: How do you get rid of Mining Fatigue in an ocean monument?
faq.a: Kill all 3 elder guardians: one in the top room and one in each wing. Until then they reapply Mining Fatigue III every minute within 50 blocks. Milk buckets clear the effect for a few seconds of mining at a time.

faq.q: What loot is in an ocean monument?
faq.a: 8 gold blocks in the central treasure chamber, around 30 wet sponges per sponge room, and unlimited prismarine shards and crystals from farming guardians. Elder guardians also drop wet sponges, tide armor trims (20%) and prismarine loot.

faq.q: Can you drain an ocean monument?
faq.a: Yes, and the sponges you win are the tool for it: dry them in the Nether or a furnace and they each absorb up to 65 water blocks. Draining the whole monument is a classic mega-project that turns it into a guardian farm.

keywords: ocean monument raid minecraft elder guardian mining fatigue sponge room gold treasure chamber

name: How to Use Shulker Boxes in Minecraft
quickAnswer: A shulker box is a portable chest: it keeps all 27 slots of items inside when you break it. Craft one with 2 shulker shells + 1 chest, place it, fill it, mine it with a pickaxe and carry your whole inventory anywhere.
steps: Get shulker shells from shulkers in end cities (bring Looting III for more drops).
Craft: chest in the middle, one shulker shell above and one below.
Place the box and fill its 27 slots, the same space as a single chest.
Break it with any tool (pickaxe is fastest): the box drops as an item with everything still inside.
Carry dozens of filled boxes in your inventory: that is thousands of item slots in your pocket.
Dye boxes any color by crafting them with a dye, and store a filled box in your ender chest for a portable storage network.
Note: you cannot put a shulker box inside another shulker box.
editionNote: Shulker boxes behave the same in Java and Bedrock: contents survive breaking, pistons and explosions. Creative instant-mining also drops the filled box.
versions: Shulker boxes exist since 1.11 (Exploration Update). Before end cities are reachable, use donkeys or llamas with chests as portable storage.

faq.q: Do shulker boxes keep items when broken?
faq.a: Yes, that is their whole point. Mining a shulker box drops the box as an item with all 27 slots of contents stored inside it, and placing it again restores access to everything.

faq.q: Can you put a shulker box inside a shulker box?
faq.a: No. Shulker boxes cannot contain other shulker boxes, which is the only nesting limit. But you can put filled shulker boxes inside an ender chest for effectively infinite portable storage.

faq.q: How many items fit in a shulker box?
faq.a: 27 stacks: up to 1,728 of most blocks (27 slots x 64). A full inventory of filled shulker boxes holds over 60,000 items.

keywords: shulker box minecraft how to use portable storage shulker box recipe ender chest

name: How to Hatch a Sniffer Egg in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Place the sniffer egg on the ground and wait: it hatches in 20 minutes, or 10 minutes on a moss block. The egg cracks twice before a snifflet pops out. No torch, light level or special biome required.
steps: Get a sniffer egg: brush suspicious sand in warm ocean ruins (see the sniffer egg guide) or breed two sniffers with torchflower seeds.
Place the egg on any block; unlike turtle eggs it needs no sand and no Silk Touch to pick back up.
For double speed, place it on a moss block: 10 minutes instead of 20.
Wait through two cracking stages, like a turtle egg. Stay nearby: chunks must be loaded for the timer to run.
Meet your snifflet: the baby sniffer takes 40 minutes to grow up, or feed it torchflower seeds to speed growth.
Adult sniffers dig up torchflower seeds and pitcher pods for ancient plant farming.
materials: Sniffer egg (brushed from suspicious sand in warm ocean ruins)
Torchflower seeds (optional, to grow the snifflet faster)
editionNote: Hatching works identically in Java and Bedrock: 10 minutes on moss, 20 minutes anywhere else, and the egg floats without a supporting block in both editions.
versions: Sniffers and their eggs exist since 1.20 (Trails & Tales), the first mob vote winner to reach the game.

faq.q: How long does a sniffer egg take to hatch?
faq.a: 20 minutes on most blocks, 10 minutes on a moss block. The egg visually cracks twice before hatching into a snifflet.

faq.q: Does a sniffer egg need light or heat to hatch?
faq.a: No. Unlike turtle eggs (which need night) or dragon eggs (which do not hatch at all), sniffer eggs hatch anywhere in any light level. Only moss speeds it up.

faq.q: What do you do with a sniffer after it hatches?
faq.a: Let it grow up (40 minutes, faster with torchflower seeds) and it sniffs out torchflower seeds and pitcher pods, the ancient plants you cannot get any other way. Breed two adults with torchflower seeds for more eggs.

keywords: how to hatch sniffer egg minecraft sniffer egg hatch time moss block snifflet

name: How to Barter with Piglins in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Throw a gold ingot at an adult piglin (or use it on them) and they examine it for 6 seconds, then throw back a random item: ender pearls, obsidian, fire resistance potions, quartz, soul speed books and more. Wear gold armor so they do not attack you.
steps: Find piglins: they live in crimson forests and nether wastes, and guard bastion remnants. Only adult piglins barter - babies pocket the gold, and piglin brutes ignore it.
Wear at least one piece of gold armor: any gold piece stops adult piglins from attacking on sight.
Bring stacks of gold ingots, farmed from a gold farm or mined as nether gold ore.
Drop an ingot near an adult piglin or use it directly on them. Baby piglins do not barter; they just steal the ingot.
Wait 6 seconds while the piglin examines the gold, then catch the thrown item. Full cycle: about 6 seconds per ingot in Java, 8 in Bedrock.

Best drops: ender pearls (2-4 at ~2.1% (about one pearl drop per 16 ingots)), splash and drinkable fire resistance potions, obsidian and crying obsidian, nether quartz, soul speed enchanted books (~1.1%) and iron boots.
Build a bartering farm: trap piglins on hoppers, pipe gold in, and collect chests full of pearls and potions automatically.
Stay safe: never open chests, mine gold blocks, or attack piglins nearby while bartering - it angers every piglin around. In Bedrock an angered piglin finishes the barter instantly before attacking.
Use it for speedrunning: bartering is the standard speedrun route to ender pearls - far faster than hunting endermen.
materials: One piece of gold armor (helmet is cheapest)
Hoppers and chests for a farm (optional)
editionNote: The bartering cycle is 6.05 seconds in Java and 8 seconds in Bedrock. If a piglin zombifies mid-barter, Java drops the ingot immediately while Bedrock keeps it held until the zombified piglin dies.
versions: Bartering exists since 1.16 (Nether Update). The loot table was rebalanced once in 1.16.2 and has been stable since.

faq.q: What is the best item from piglin bartering?
faq.a: Ender pearls: bartering is one of the fastest pearl sources in the game, at roughly 2.1% per ingot in stacks of 2-4. Speedrunners build entire strategies around it. Soul Speed books and fire resistance potions are the other premium drops.

faq.q: Why do piglins attack me when I barter?
faq.a: You are missing gold armor, you opened a chest or mined gold near them, or you hit one. Adult piglins tolerate players wearing at least one gold piece, but breaking containers or gold blocks nearby enrages them regardless.

faq.q: Can baby piglins barter?
faq.a: No. Baby piglins pick up the gold ingot and run off with it, so keep babies out of your bartering setup or your gold disappears with no return.

faq.q: What can you get from bartering with piglins?
faq.a: Ender pearls (2-4), obsidian, fire resistance potions and splash potions, nether quartz, iron nuggets, string, gravel, leather, soul speed enchanted books and iron boots, water bottles, and dried ghasts - each gold ingot buys one random item.

faq.q: Why won't the piglin take my gold?

name: How to Raid Trial Chambers in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Find trial chambers underground, walk within 14 blocks of each trial spawner to trigger a wave scaled to your player count, defeat every mob, and collect the reward per player: trial keys, wind charges and loot. Keys open vaults; ominous bottles upgrade the run to ominous trials with better vaults and the heavy core.
steps: Locate trial chambers underground between Y=-20 and Y=40, usually in deepslate layers. Cartographer villagers can sell a trial chambers map.
Gear up: full iron or better, shield, food and blocks. Copper and tuff corridors mean you are in.
Trigger each trial spawner by stepping within 14 blocks with line of sight; it spawns a limited wave scaled to nearby players.
Defeat the whole wave: the spawner ejects a reward for every player (trial keys ~half the time, plus potions, arrows and wind charges) and enters cooldown.
Use trial keys on vaults: each vault opens once per player, so everyone in the group gets their own loot.
For the hard mode: drink an ominous bottle, walk up to a spawner with Trial Omen and it becomes an ominous trial spawner dropping ominous keys for ominous vaults, the only source of the heavy core.
Kill breezes for breeze rods: they craft into wind charges and the mace.

Prioritize the breeze. Breezes fire wind charges that deal no direct damage but hurl you into the air - the fall hurts. Deflect the charge back with a well-timed hit, then rush it while it repositions. Breeze rods become wind charges and, with a heavy core, the mace.

Handle the spawners smart. Spawners have a cooldown after defeat and cannot be mined for anything useful, so clear, loot, and move on. Narrow doorways and shield corners turn bad rooms into easy ones.
Take the trophies. Heavy core + breeze rod = mace, the smash weapon. Flow and bolt armor trims, wind charges, and ominous bottles for your raid farm round out a full clear.
materials: Sword and bow (spawners mix melee and ranged mobs)
Ominous bottles for ominous trials (optional, endgame)
Food, torches and blocks for safety
Bad Omen (ominous bottle) for the ominous run
Empty inventory rows - vaults pay out a lot
editionNote: Vaults open once per player in both editions, up to 128 players per vault. Trial spawner scaling and rewards work the same in Java and Bedrock.
versions: Trial chambers exist since 1.21 (Tricky Trials). Ominous trials and the heavy core arrived in the same update.

faq.q: How do trial spawners work?
faq.a: They activate when a player gets within 14 blocks with line of sight, summon a limited wave scaled to the number of players, and once every mob dies they eject one reward per player and go on cooldown. Rewards include trial keys, wind charges, potions and arrows.

faq.q: What is the difference between a vault and an ominous vault?
faq.a: Normal vaults open with trial keys from normal trial spawners. Ominous vaults need ominous keys from ominous trial spawners, which only appear when you approach a spawner with the Trial Omen effect (from drinking an ominous bottle). Ominous vaults hold the best loot, including the heavy core for the mace.

faq.q: Can you farm trial chambers?
faq.a: Yes: trial spawners reactivate after their cooldown, and each player gets rewards separately, so a group can cycle spawners indefinitely. Vaults are once per player, so bring friends for more openings.

faq.q: How do trial keys work?
faq.a: Defeat a trial spawner's wave and it has a 50% chance to eject a trial key for every participating player. Each player uses their own key on a vault, and the vault gives everyone separate loot - no fighting over drops. Ominous spawners drop ominous keys at 30% for the better ominous vaults.

faq.q: Are trial chambers worth it?
faq.a: Yes - the mace (heavy core + breeze rod) exists nowhere else, ominous vaults have the game's best enchanted golden apple odds at 22.5%, and the armor trims are exclusive. It is also simply the best structured combat content in the mid game.

faq.q: How do I survive the breeze?
faq.a: Do not tank the fall - tank nothing: dodge sideways, and hit the wind charge to deflect it back, which blows the breeze open for a sword rush. Feather Falling IV and a water bucket remove most of the danger while you learn the rhythm.

name: How to Raid an Ancient City in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Sneak everything. Ancient cities at Y=-51 in the deep dark are full of sculk sensors and shriekers: four shrieker activations summon the warden. Crouch, break shriekers with a hoe, throw snowballs to distract sensors, and loot chests for echo shards, swift sneak books and the exclusive ward and silence armor trims.
steps: Find an ancient city in a deep dark biome at Y=-51, usually under mountains. Bring wool, a hoe, snowballs and night vision.
Crouch everywhere: sneaking makes no vibrations, so sculk sensors and shriekers ignore you.
Break every sculk shrieker you see with a hoe (fastest tool). Four activations of naturally generated shriekers summon a warden.
Throw snowballs away from you to distract sensors and shriekers while you cross open areas or loot.
Loot the chests: echo shards (recovery compass), swift sneak enchanted books, disc fragments for music disc 5, and the ward and silence armor trims found nowhere else.
Hunt the rare prize: ancient city chests have one of the highest enchanted golden apple chances of any structure.
If a warden spawns, do not fight it: lose line of sight, stay silent and let it burrow back after 60 seconds of no vibrations.
editionNote: Ancient city loot and warden spawning are the same in Java and Bedrock. Ice box chests are a separate loot table worth checking in both editions.
versions: Ancient cities exist since 1.19 (The Wild Update). Swift sneak, echo shards and the two trims remain exclusive to them.

faq.q: How many shrieker activations summon the warden?
faq.a: Four per player. Each player has their own warning level that rises when they activate a naturally generated sculk shrieker, and at the fourth activation a warden emerges. Shriekers you place yourself never summon one.

faq.q: What loot is exclusive to ancient cities?
faq.a: Echo shards (for the recovery compass), swift sneak enchanted books, disc fragments (music disc 5), and the ward and silence armor trims. The chests also carry one of the best enchanted golden apple rates in the game.

faq.q: What is the safest way to explore an ancient city?
faq.a: Crouch constantly, cover your approach with wool (wool blocks and carpets do not transmit vibrations), break shriekers first with a hoe, and use snowballs to pull sensor attention away. Never run, never place or break blocks near sensors without sneaking.

name: How to Get the Pigstep Music Disc in Minecraft

Play it in a jukebox and enjoy the only Lena Raine disc obtainable as loot: 2:28 of electronic hip-hop, added with the Nether Update.

versions: Pigstep exists since 1.16 (Nether Update), composed by Lena Raine. It remains the rarest-feeling disc because bastions are dangerous and its drop chance is low.

faq.q: Which bastion chests have Pigstep?
faq.a: All bastion chest types can roll it: bridge, hoglin stable, generic housing and treasure room chests. Treasure rooms have the densest loot overall, so always clear them fully.

name: How to Enchant Elytra in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Elytra skip the enchanting table: use an anvil with enchanted books. The winning combo is Unbreaking III + Mending, making your wings last effectively forever. The only other options are Curse of Binding and Curse of Vanishing.
steps: Get enchanted books: Mending from librarian trading or loot, Unbreaking III from the enchanting table, trading or loot.
Place the elytra in the anvil's first slot and the book in the second. Elytra cannot be enchanted on the enchanting table directly.
Apply Unbreaking III first, then Mending. Anvil costs rise with each working, so combine books cheaply first if you can.
Result: Unbreaking III stretches flight time to about 4 seconds per durability point (roughly 29 minutes total), and Mending repairs with XP while you fly with XP gain.
Avoid the curses: Curse of Binding locks the elytra on until death, Curse of Vanishing deletes it on death. Never accept them outside hardcore jokes.
Maintain the wings: repair on an anvil with phantom membranes if Mending is not active, before durability hits 1 and they stop working.
editionNote: Identical in Java and Bedrock: anvil-only enchanting, same four legal enchantments, same durability behavior.
versions: Elytra enchanting rules have been stable since 1.9. Unbreaking III giving roughly 4 seconds of flight per durability point is the long-standing balance.

faq.q: What enchantments can elytra have?
faq.a: Exactly four: Unbreaking (up to III), Mending, Curse of Binding and Curse of Vanishing. No Protection or custom flight enchantments exist. Unbreaking III + Mending is the universal best setup.

faq.q: Why can't I put my elytra in the enchanting table?
faq.a: By design: elytra are not armor and cannot roll enchantments at the table. Every enchantment must come from an enchanted book applied on an anvil, and armor trims do not work on them either.

faq.q: How long do elytra last with Unbreaking III?
faq.a: About 4 seconds of flight per durability point, around 28 minutes and 48 seconds of continuous gliding, versus roughly 7 minutes unenchanted. Add Mending and XP from any source keeps them alive indefinitely.

quickAnswer: Loot ancient city chests: the ward armor trim generates in most chest types there (everything except ice box chests). Duplicate your first one with 7 diamonds + 1 cobbled deepslate, then apply it on a smithing table with any armor piece and trim material.
