faq.a: Terracotta is flat color; glazed terracotta is made by smelting dyed terracotta and has a unique repeating pattern per color (creeper face on cyan, flower on white, and so on).

faq.q: Where can I find terracotta without crafting it?
faq.a: The badlands (mesa) biome: entire mountains of red, orange, yellow, brown, white and light gray terracotta. Savanna villages also generate with some.

faq.q: Does terracotta burn?
faq.a: No. Terracotta is a fired clay block: it does not catch fire and has stone-level blast resistance, which makes it a safe roofing material.

faq.q: Can you turn terracotta back into clay?
faq.a: No. Smelting clay into terracotta is one-way, so only smelt what you need.

name: How to Make Stone in Minecraft

steps: Mine cobblestone with any pickaxe. It drops when you mine natural stone without Silk Touch, so every mining trip produces it.
Place a furnace and add any fuel: coal, charcoal, logs, planks, or a lava bucket.
Put cobblestone in the top slot of the furnace. Each cobblestone smelts into 1 stone.
Speed it up with a blast furnace: it smelts stone-related blocks twice as fast, ideal for big building projects.
Use stone for stone bricks (4 stone in a 2x2 square), stone slabs and stairs, redstone repeaters and comparators, and as a clean building block.

faq.a: Cobblestone is the rough block that drops when you mine stone. Smelting it turns it back into smooth gray stone, which is needed for stone bricks, repeaters, and comparators.

faq.q: How do you get stone without a furnace?

name: How to Repair Tools in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Three ways: combine two damaged tools of the same type in the crafting grid (free, but loses enchantments), repair on an anvil with the tool's material or a matching tool (keeps enchantments, costs XP), or use the Mending enchantment so XP orbs repair the item automatically.
steps: Crafting grid repair: place two damaged tools of the same type and material anywhere in the grid. The result adds their remaining durability plus a 5% bonus, but all enchantments are lost. Good for unenchanted tools only.
Grindstone repair: combine two damaged tools of the same type in a grindstone. Same free repair, and it strips non-curse enchantments, refunding some XP. Useful for clearing bad enchantments.

Anvil repair with material: put the tool in the left slot and its material in the middle (diamonds for diamond tools, iron ingots for iron tools, and so on). Each material item restores 25% durability and enchantments are kept, but it costs XP levels.
Anvil combine: merge two enchanted tools of the same type to add their durabilities together and combine or keep enchantments. The prior-work penalty makes repeated repairs cost more each time.
Mending: apply a Mending enchanted book to your best tools at an anvil. Held or worn items with Mending repair themselves from XP orbs, making them effectively permanent.
Netherite note: netherite tools repair with netherite ingots on an anvil, which is expensive, so Mending is the real answer for endgame gear.
materials: Two damaged tools of the same type (grid/grindstone repair)
Anvil + repair material (diamonds, iron ingots, etc.) or a matching tool
editionNote: Repair mechanics are the same in Java and Bedrock: grid combining gives a 5% durability bonus, anvil material repair restores 25% per item, and the anvil prior-work penalty applies in both. Mending works identically in both editions.

faq.q: Why do my enchantments disappear when I repair?
faq.a: You used the crafting grid: grid repair always strips enchantments. Use an anvil to keep them, or a grindstone if you actually want them removed (it refunds some XP).

faq.q: What is the cheapest way to repair a diamond pickaxe?
faq.a: Anvil with diamonds: each diamond restores 25% durability. But the prior-work penalty grows, so for a good pickaxe the cheapest long-term answer is a Mending book and an XP source.

faq.q: Can you repair tools infinitely?
faq.a: Only with Mending. Anvil repairs stop working once the operation cost passes 39 levels (Too Expensive), and every repair raises that cost.

faq.q: What material repairs what tool?
faq.a: The tool's own material: wooden planks for wood tools, cobblestone for stone tools, iron ingots for iron, diamonds for diamond, gold ingots for gold, netherite ingots for netherite. Elytra repairs with phantom membranes, and shears with iron ingots.

name: How to Make a Cobblestone Generator in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Place water and lava so flowing water touches a lava source from the side: where they meet, cobblestone forms instantly and forever. Mine it, and a new block regenerates in the same spot, giving infinite cobblestone.
steps: Gather 1 water bucket and 1 lava bucket. Lava is common in caves and the Nether; water anywhere.
Dig a trench 4 blocks long and 1 deep. Dig one more block down at one end (so water flows there).
Place the water source at the deeper end; it flows 1-2 blocks into the trench.
Place the lava source at the opposite end of the trench. Where the flowing water meets the lava source from the side, a cobblestone block appears.
Mine that cobblestone block with any pickaxe. A new one forms immediately in the same spot: infinite cobblestone.
Upgrade the design: put a hopper and chest under the mining spot to auto-collect, or mine from below with the block between you and the lava so drops never burn.
Stone and basalt variants: lava flowing DOWN onto water makes stone instead, and lava flowing over blue ice on soul soil makes basalt (1.16+).
editionNote: Cobblestone generators work identically in Java and Bedrock: water flowing into a lava source from the side generates cobblestone, lava flowing down onto water generates stone, and lava over blue ice above soul soil generates basalt in both editions.

faq.q: Why does my generator make obsidian instead of cobblestone?
faq.a: The water touched the lava SOURCE block directly from above or the lava touched the water source. Cobblestone only forms where flowing water meets the side of a lava source; water hitting a lava source head-on makes obsidian and consumes the lava.

faq.q: Can you make an infinite stone generator?
faq.a: Yes: let lava flow DOWN onto a water stream from above. That contact makes stone, which is great because stone (not cobblestone) is what stone bricks and repeaters need.

faq.q: How do you make a basalt generator?
faq.a: Place soul soil, put blue ice on top, and let lava flow over the blue ice. Basalt forms where lava meets blue ice above soul soil (1.16+).

faq.q: Does a cobblestone generator ever run out?
faq.a: Never, as long as the lava and water sources stay in place. Only the water touching the lava source directly (making obsidian) breaks it, and that only happens if you mine the wrong block.

quickAnswer: The safe automatic design: bees fill a bee nest or beehive to honey level 5, an observer watches the block and fires a dispenser holding glass bottles (for honey bottles) or shears (for honeycomb). Dispenser harvesting never angers the bees, so no campfire is needed.
steps: Get bees and a home for them: lure bees with flowers to your farm spot, or move a bee nest at night with Silk Touch while the bees are inside. Craft beehives (6 planks + 3 honeycomb) for extra colonies.

Build the harvester: place a dispenser facing the hive, and load it with glass bottles (honey bottles) or shears (honeycomb).

Automate it: place an observer watching the hive (its face on the hive, redstone dot pointing into the dispenser circuit). When the honey level hits 5, the hive's state change triggers the observer and fires the dispenser.
Collect the output: put a hopper under or beside the hive/dispenser line feeding into a chest, so bottles and honeycomb stack up automatically.

materials: Bees (2+ to breed a colony) and bee nests or beehives

faq.q: Do bees get angry when a dispenser harvests honey?
faq.a: No. Harvesting with a dispenser (bottles or shears) is the only collection method that never angers bees, even without a campfire. That is what makes automatic honey farms safe.

faq.q: How long does a hive take to fill?
faq.a: Each bee trip adds 1 honey level after pollination, and a hive needs 5 levels. With 3 bees per hive and flowers nearby, a hive fills roughly every 30-60 minutes of daytime activity.

faq.q: Honey bottles or honeycomb - which should I farm?
faq.a: Honey bottles (glass bottles in the dispenser) if you want honey blocks or food; honeycomb (shears in the dispenser) if you need beehives, candles or wax for copper. Load the dispenser with the right tool and the farm does the rest.

faq.q: Do bees work at night or in rain?
faq.a: No. Bees stay inside their nests at night and during rain, so farms only produce during clear daytime. Build the farm indoors? Bees also need sky access or at least to pathfind to flowers - enclosed farms work if bees can reach the flowers inside.

name: How to Make a Circle in Minecraft (Any Diameter)
quickAnswer: Minecraft has no round blocks, so circles are built by hand from a pixel pattern: pick a diameter, place the pattern for one quarter, mirror it to the other three, and fill or leave hollow. Odd diameters center on one block; even diameters center on the gap between four blocks.
keywords: how to make a circle in minecraft circle guide pixel circle diameter chart sphere build
materials: A flat area or scaffolding for tall builds
Optional: a circle generator chart open on a second screen
steps: Pick your diameter in blocks. Small circles (5-15 blocks) suit towers and wells; 20-50 for domes; 50+ for arenas.
Mark the center: for odd diameters (7, 9, 11...) it is a single block; for even diameters (8, 10, 12...) it is the intersection between 4 blocks.
Build the straight sides first: from the center, measure half the diameter along each axis and place the 4 edge midpoints.
Fill the curved quadrants: starting from an edge midpoint, step diagonally inward, following the pattern - for a small circle the steps go 2 blocks straight, 1 diagonal, 2 straight, mirrored.
Mirror each quarter to the other three. If one quarter looks wrong, fix it before copying - symmetry is what makes it read as a circle.
Fill the interior for a disc, or leave the ring hollow for walls. For a sphere, stack horizontal circles whose diameters shrink toward the top and bottom.
Step back at least the circle's diameter in blocks to check the shape: circles only look round from a distance.
versions: Building technique, identical in every version and edition of Minecraft.
editionNote: Works the same in Java and Bedrock - blocks are blocks.

faq.q: What is the smallest circle that looks round?
faq.a: About 7 blocks in diameter. Below that (5 or 3) the shape reads as a diamond; use it deliberately for small details like wells or lily pads.

faq.q: How do I make a perfect sphere?
faq.a: Think of it as a stack of horizontal circles: the widest circle sits at the middle height, and each layer above and below uses a smaller diameter, mirrored top to bottom. A 9-block sphere uses diameters 5-7-9-7-5 across its 5 layers.

faq.q: Any trick for huge circles?
faq.a: Build one quadrant flat on the ground first, screenshot it or count its rows, then reproduce that row-by-row plan on all four sides. For very large builds, external circle generator tools print the exact row lengths for any diameter.

name: How to Allocate More RAM to Minecraft (Java)
quickAnswer: In the Minecraft Launcher go to Installations, edit your installation, open More Options and change the -Xmx value in JVM Arguments (for example -Xmx4G for 4 GB). Vanilla runs fine on 2 GB; heavy modpacks want 6-8 GB. Never give Minecraft more than half your total RAM.
keywords: allocate more ram minecraft java launcher jvm arguments xmx modpack lag fix how much ram
materials: A PC with enough free RAM - check your total before assigning
A 64-bit Java installation (the launcher bundles one by default)
steps: Check your total RAM first: 8 GB systems should assign at most 4 GB to Minecraft; 16 GB systems can go up to 8 GB.
Open the Minecraft Launcher and go to the Installations tab.
Hover your installation (or the modpack profile) and click the three dots > Edit.
Click More Options to reveal the JVM Arguments field.
Find -Xmx2G near the start and change the number: -Xmx4G for 4 GB, -Xmx6G or -Xmx8G for big modpacks. Do not touch anything else in the line.
Save and launch. In-game, press F3: the top right shows memory usage - if it sits near 100% and stutters, raise the value one step.
For servers, the same flag goes in the start command: java -Xmx4G -jar server.jar nogui.
More is not always better: over-allocating makes Java garbage collection spikes worse. If 8 GB still stutters, the bottleneck is elsewhere (shaders, view distance, CPU).
versions: Applies to all Java Edition versions through the official launcher. Bedrock manages memory automatically - there is no RAM setting.
editionNote: Java Edition only. Bedrock (Windows, console, mobile) allocates memory on its own.

faq.q: How much RAM does vanilla Minecraft need?
faq.a: The default 2 GB is enough for vanilla with modest view distance. Assign 4 GB if you use big render distances, high-resolution texture packs or shaders.

faq.q: What about modpacks?
faq.a: Light packs run on 4 GB, medium packs on 6 GB, and huge kitchen-sink packs on 8 GB. Assigning more than 8-10 GB usually hurts rather than helps.

faq.q: Minecraft says 'out of memory' even after raising it?
faq.a: Make sure you edited the installation you actually launch, that you are on 64-bit Java (32-bit caps around 1.5 GB), and that other apps are not eating the RAM you just assigned.

name: How to Change Your Minecraft Name (Java and Bedrock)
quickAnswer: Java: sign in at minecraft.net, open your profile and change your Profile Name - you can do it once every 30 days, free. Bedrock: your in-game name is your Xbox gamertag; change it at xbox.com - the first change is free and later changes cost money.
keywords: how to change minecraft name username java bedrock gamertag profile name 30 days
materials: Access to the Microsoft account that owns your Minecraft copy
A new name that is not taken (3-16 characters for Java)
steps: Java Edition: go to minecraft.net and sign in with your Microsoft account.
Open your profile page and find the Profile Name section.
Enter the new name and save. Names are 3-16 characters: letters, numbers and underscores only.
Wait before re-changing: Java allows one name change every 30 days.
Your old name does not transfer with you on servers: server owners recognize you by your account ID, so your inventory, homes and bans follow the account, not the name.
Bedrock Edition: your display name is your Xbox gamertag. Change it at xbox.com (Social > Gamertag) or on an Xbox console.
The first gamertag change is free; after that, Xbox charges a fee per change, so pick carefully.
After changing, restart the game and your launchers so the new name shows everywhere.
versions: The 30-day Java cooldown and Microsoft-account profile page apply to current Minecraft: Java Edition. Bedrock naming follows Xbox gamertag rules on all platforms.
editionNote: Java and Bedrock names are completely separate systems: changing one never changes the other.

faq.q: Do I lose my worlds or server progress if I change my name?
faq.a: No. Worlds live on your device, and servers track your account ID, not your name. Your progress, inventories and permissions follow the account.

faq.q: Can two players have the same name?
faq.a: On Java, no: profile names are unique and you cannot take one that is in use. Xbox gamertags can be shared - duplicates get a numeric suffix shown after the name.

faq.q: Can I change my name back?
faq.a: Yes, as long as nobody else has taken the old name - but the 30-day cooldown (Java) or the paid fee (Bedrock, after the first free change) still applies.

name: How to Make a Water Elevator in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Build a 1x1 water column of source blocks, then swap the floor block: soul sand makes a bubble column that blasts you upward, and a magma block makes a whirlpool that pulls you down. Every block of the column must be a water source - grow kelp up through flowing water to convert it.
keywords: water elevator minecraft bubble column soul sand magma block kelp source blocks how to build
materials: 1 soul sand (up elevator) and/or 1 magma block (down elevator)
Water buckets (2+ for an infinite source, or 1 plus kelp)
Kelp to convert flowing water into source blocks
Building blocks and signs or a door to hold the water in
steps: Build a 1x1 vertical shaft with walls, from the bottom floor to the top exit. Hold the water in with signs, trapdoors or a door at the entrance.

Fill the shaft with water so every block is a source block: the fast way is to place one water source at the bottom, then plant kelp and grow it to the top - growing kelp turns each flowing block into a source.
Break the kelp from the bottom: the whole column stays as source water.
Up elevator: replace the floor block of the shaft with soul sand. After a second, bubbles appear - step in and you shoot to the top.
Down elevator: use a magma block instead. The whirlpool pulls you down fast and you land safely on the magma block (it deals no damage while you stand still in the column).
Combine both: two adjacent shafts, one soul sand for up, one magma for down, sharing walls.
Add a water source at the top entrance so you can also swim in from the top, and light the shaft so drowned cannot spawn in it.
versions: Bubble columns were added in the Update Aquatic (Java 1.13 / Bedrock 1.5). The mechanic is identical in both editions.
editionNote: Works the same in Java and Bedrock. In Bedrock, entering the top of an up-column is slightly smoother at high speeds.

faq.q: Why are there no bubbles?
faq.a: Almost always a flowing-water block in the column. Every single block between the soul sand or magma and the surface must be a source block - grow kelp all the way up and break it to fix gaps.

faq.q: Does the magma block hurt?
faq.a: Standing on magma deals 1 damage per tick - but sneaking negates it, and in a down elevator you only touch it for an instant. Use a hopper minecart or carpet under the exit if you want zero risk.

faq.q: Can I go up faster?
faq.a: Bubble columns are already the fastest vertical transport in vanilla. Dolphin's grace, Depth Strider or a swiftness potion add a small boost inside the column.

name: How to Teleport in Minecraft (Commands and Survival)
quickAnswer: With cheats on, open chat and run /tp @s X Y Z to teleport to coordinates, or /tp @s PlayerName to jump to another player. Without cheats, teleporting means ender pearls, chorus fruit or portals - there is no free teleport in survival.
keywords: how to teleport minecraft tp command coordinates ender pearl chorus fruit cheats survival
materials: Cheats enabled for command teleporting (or operator on a server)
Chorus fruit for short random hops
steps: Command teleport: enable cheats, open chat and type /tp @s 100 64 -250 to teleport to those coordinates. Use ~ for relative jumps: /tp @s ~50 ~ ~ moves you 50 blocks east.
Teleport to a player: /tp @s Alex sends you to Alex. On servers, /tp Alex Steve teleports one player to another (operator only).
Bring something to you: /tp @e[type=cow,limit=1] @s teleports the nearest cow to you - handy for lost pets with name tags.
Bedrock extras: /tp also accepts facing angles, and both editions support /teleport as an alias of /tp.
Survival teleport 1: throw an ender pearl. You land where it lands and take 5 fall damage - wear Feather Falling and never pearl into unloaded gaps.
Survival teleport 2: eat chorus fruit for a random 8-block teleport in any direction, including through walls and downward. It can save you from a cave-in or drop you into lava.
Survival teleport 3: portals. Nether travel moves you 8 overworld blocks per nether block, so a portal pair is the fastest long-distance 'teleport' without cheats.
Safety: before teleporting, note your current coordinates (F3 on Java, or the world 'show coordinates' setting on Bedrock) so you can always teleport back.
versions: /tp has existed since Java Classic (modern form since 1.3.1) and in Bedrock since early versions. Ender pearls teleport since Beta 1.9; chorus fruit since 1.9.
editionNote: Command syntax is the same in both editions. In Java, F3 shows coordinates; in Bedrock, enable Show Coordinates in world settings - no cheats needed for that toggle.

faq.q: How do I teleport without cheats?
faq.a: Ender pearls, chorus fruit and nether portals are the only vanilla options. Many multiplayer servers add /home, /spawn and /tpa commands - check the server's help menu.

faq.q: Why does /tp kill me sometimes?
faq.a: You can teleport into blocks or over the void: the command does not check safety. Aim a few blocks above ground (Y is the middle coordinate) and pick a spot you have seen.

faq.q: Can I teleport to my bed?
faq.a: Not with vanilla commands - there is no bed coordinate lookup. Die with keep_inventory off and you respawn at your bed; otherwise note the bed's coordinates and /tp there.

name: How to Find Your Way Home in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Write down your base coordinates (F3 on Java, Show Coordinates on Bedrock) and navigate back to them. A compass always points to world spawn, a recovery compass to your last death, and a lodestone-linked compass to any base you choose.
keywords: find your way home minecraft lost how to get back coordinates compass lodestone recovery compass
materials: Coordinates of your base - write them down before exploring
Optional: recovery compass or a lodestone-linked compass
Torches or trail markers for cave systems
steps: Before exploring: stand at your base door and screenshot the coordinates. Java: press F3 and read the XYZ line. Bedrock: enable Show Coordinates in world settings (no cheats needed).
To return, walk so your current X and Z approach the base values - Y (height) rarely matters on the surface.
Compass: a normal compass points to world spawn. If your base is near spawn, follow it; if not, it is still a fixed reference point you can navigate from.
Lodestone compass: use a compass on a lodestone placed at your base and it points to that lodestone forever - the true 'point me home' item, working in any dimension.
Recovery compass: craft one with echo shards from an ancient city; it points to your last death spot, not your base - perfect for corpse runs.

Lost without coordinates: climb high at sunrise and look for terrain you remember, check your maps, or retrace with torches. As a last resort, dying respawns you at your bed (you lose your items unless keep_inventory is on).
Prevention habits: sleep in a bed to set spawn, carry 8+ torches and place them always on the same side in caves (right going in, left coming out), and make a map of the area around base.
versions: Compasses point to world spawn since Alpha. Lodestones arrived in 1.16 (Nether Update) and the recovery compass in 1.19 (The Wild Update).
editionNote: Everything works the same in both editions. Coordinate display differs: F3 on Java, the Show Coordinates toggle on Bedrock.

faq.q: My compass spins randomly - why?
faq.a: It is lodestone-linked and its lodestone was broken, or you are in a different dimension from the lodestone. Normal compasses only break logic near the world border or in other dimensions, where they spin uselessly.

faq.q: Do compasses work in the Nether?
faq.a: Normal compasses and clocks spin randomly in the Nether and the End. Lodestone compasses work everywhere as long as their lodestone is in the same dimension.

faq.q: I died far away and lost everything - how do I get back?
faq.a: A recovery compass points exactly to your death spot. Without one, note that items despawn after 5 minutes of loaded time - run, and the timer only ticks while the chunk is loaded.

name: How to Crawl in Minecraft (1-Block Spaces)
quickAnswer: Crawling is automatic: close a trapdoor over yourself, or swim or fly into a 1-block-high gap, and your character drops to a 0.625-block-tall crawl that fits through single-block spaces. There is no crawl key - the pose triggers whenever your head would hit a block.
keywords: how to crawl minecraft 1 block gap trapdoor crawling swift sneak sneak under
materials: A trapdoor (any wood) for the classic crawl trigger
Optional: a piston or fence gate as alternatives
Swift Sneak leggings to crawl faster
steps: Place a trapdoor on the floor-level block at the entrance of your 1-block gap and flip it open vertically.
Walk into the trapdoor and close it over yourself (right-click): your character instantly drops into the crawling pose.
Move forward into the 1-block space. You travel at sneaking speed and fit anywhere a single block of air exists.
Other triggers: swim into a 1-block gap (you stay prone), fly in with an elytra, throw an ender pearl into the gap, or have a piston push a block over you.
To stop crawling, move into a space at least 1.5 blocks high: you stand up automatically.
Crawl faster: Swift Sneak leggings (ancient city loot) raise crawl speed - at Swift Sneak III you crawl nearly at walking pace.
Uses: 1-block mob-proof tunnels, secret bases, strip mining with a 1x1 profile, and reaching items under slab floors.
versions: Crawling became an automatic mechanic in Java 1.14 (it started as a swimming side-effect in 1.13). Bedrock added proper crawling in the 1.20 updates.
editionNote: Both editions crawl automatically now. Java triggers are slightly more generous (more block types force the pose); the trapdoor method works everywhere.

faq.q: Is there a crawl button?
faq.a: No. Crawling is not a keybind like sneaking - your character crawls only when a block forces the pose, and stands up when there is headroom again.

faq.q: Can mobs follow me into a 1-block tunnel?
faq.a: Most cannot: zombies and skeletons are too tall. Baby zombies, silverfish, endermites and cave spiders fit - light the tunnel and you are safe from everything else.

faq.q: Does crawling make you slower than sneaking?
faq.a: Same base speed as sneaking. Swift Sneak enchantments speed both up, which is why they are the best leggings enchantment for tunnel networks.

name: How to Make Tinted Glass in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft 1 glass block with 4 amethyst shards to get 2 tinted glass: a glass variant that blocks 100% of light while staying see-through. It is the only mob-proof transparent block and, unlike normal glass, it always drops itself when broken.
keywords: tinted glass minecraft recipe amethyst shards block light mob spawning see through dark window
steps: Find an amethyst geode (they generate underground from Y=70 down, often exposed in caves and oceans) and mine amethyst clusters with any pickaxe - fully grown clusters drop 4 shards.
Smelt sand into glass in a furnace.
Place the glass in the center of the crafting grid with amethyst shards above, below, left and right.
Collect 2 tinted glass per craft.
Build with it: tinted glass looks like smoked glass but blocks ALL light - daylight and torchlight stop dead at the block.

Control light with it: mobs spawn in the dark space behind tinted glass just like behind any solid block, so its real uses are dark rooms you can see into or out of, hiding light sources, and mob farms with viewing windows.
Break it freely: tinted glass drops itself with any tool or bare hands - no Silk Touch needed, unlike normal glass.
versions: Tinted glass was added in 1.17 (Caves & Cliffs Part I) on both editions.
editionNote: Identical recipe and behavior in Java and Bedrock.

faq.q: Does tinted glass block mob spawning?
faq.a: No - it blocks light, not spawning. A room behind tinted glass stays dark and mobs CAN spawn there, exactly like behind stone. That is what makes it perfect for mob-farm viewing windows and dark rooms you can still see out of.

faq.q: Tinted glass vs stained glass - what is the difference?
faq.a: Stained glass is colored but transparent to light; tinted glass is neutral smoked glass that blocks light entirely. Stained is decoration, tinted is a light-control tool.

faq.q: Do I need Silk Touch?
faq.a: No - tinted glass always drops itself, even broken by hand. It is one of the most forgiving building blocks in the game.

name: How to Use a Lodestone in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft a lodestone from 8 chiseled stone bricks + 1 iron ingot, place it at your base, and use a compass on it: that compass points to the lodestone from anywhere in the same dimension. It is the only way to make a compass track a custom point.
keywords: lodestone minecraft how to use compass link custom waypoint chiseled stone bricks recipe navigation
materials: 8 chiseled stone bricks (stonecutter or 2 stone brick slabs stacked)
1 compass per waypoint you want to track
steps: Craft chiseled stone bricks: run stone bricks through a stonecutter, or stack 2 stone brick slabs.
Craft the lodestone: fill the crafting grid with 8 chiseled stone bricks and put 1 iron ingot in the center. (The recipe was cheapened from netherite to iron in the Spring to Life update.)
Place the lodestone somewhere permanent - your base entrance is ideal. It needs a pickaxe to mine back.
Hold a compass and use it (right-click) on the lodestone. The compass enchants-glints and locks to that block.
Follow it home: the linked compass points at the lodestone from any distance, as long as you are in the same dimension.
Make one per dimension: a lodestone compass only works in the lodestone's dimension, so keep separate linked compasses for your overworld base, nether hub and end gateway.
If the lodestone breaks, every compass linked to it spins randomly - replace the lodestone and re-link them.
versions: Lodestones were added in 1.16 (Nether Update). The recipe changed from a netherite ingot to an iron ingot in 1.21.5 (Spring to Life).
editionNote: Same crafting and linking in Java and Bedrock. Lodestones also generate in ruined portal chests.

faq.q: Does a lodestone compass work in other dimensions?
faq.a: No - it must be in the same dimension as its lodestone. A nether lodestone compass is useless in the overworld and vice versa.

faq.q: Can other players use my lodestone?
faq.a: Only if they link their own compass to it. Lodestones are not beacons - each compass is linked individually, and there is no limit to how many compasses point at one lodestone.

faq.q: What happens if I lose the linked compass?
faq.a: Craft a new compass and right-click the lodestone again. Linking is free and instant - the lodestone never runs out.

name: How to Hatch Turtle Eggs in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Turtle eggs only hatch on sand, red sand or suspicious sand, and almost all progress happens at night - on average 4-5 nights, with 90% hatched within 7 nights. Stay within 128 blocks or they pause, and fence them in: zombies go out of their way to trample them.
keywords: how to hatch turtle eggs minecraft how long turtle egg hatching night sand trample zombie
materials: Turtle eggs (breed two turtles with seagrass - the female lays 1-4 eggs on her home beach)
Sand, red sand or suspicious sand to place them on
Fences or walls to protect the clutch
Torches to keep hostile mobs away
steps: Breed two turtles with seagrass: one becomes pregnant and digs at her home beach to lay 1-4 eggs.
Leave the eggs where they are, or move them with a Silk Touch tool - any other tool (or a piston) destroys them. Moving a cracked egg with Silk Touch resets its growth stage.
The eggs must sit on sand, red sand or suspicious sand: on any other block they never hatch.
Wait through the nights. Eggs crack visibly 3 times before hatching, and about 95% of all cracking happens in a short window just before dawn (around 3-4 am in-game).
Stay close: eggs make zero progress when no player is within 128 blocks horizontally. Build your base near the beach or AFK nearby.
Protect the clutch: zombies and their variants actively pathfind to turtle eggs and jump on them. Fence the area and light it up.
When the cluster hatches, all eggs in it hatch at once and the babies always face south. Babies drop one scute when they grow up - 5 scutes craft a turtle shell helmet.
versions: Turtle eggs were added in the Update Aquatic (Java 1.13 / Bedrock 1.5). The night-hatching mechanic is the same in both editions.
editionNote: Identical hatching in Java and Bedrock.

faq.q: How long do turtle eggs take to hatch?
faq.a: 4-5 nights on average, 90% within 7 nights. Daytime barely counts: almost all cracking happens in the pre-dawn window, so sleeping through nights does not skip progress - the eggs advance at the end of each night regardless.

faq.q: Why won't my turtle eggs hatch?
faq.a: The three usual reasons: they are not on sand-type blocks, you are more than 128 blocks away (they pause), or they are glitched from a Silk Touch move - re-place them and wait through a few full nights nearby.

faq.q: Do turtle eggs hatch faster on their home beach?
faq.a: No - beach location does not matter, only the sand block and your proximity. Turtles must breed on their home beach, but the eggs hatch at the same speed anywhere on sand.

name: How to Get a Bell in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Bells cannot be crafted: steal one from a village meeting point with any pickaxe, find one in a ruined portal chest, or buy one from an armorer villager. Ring a bell during a raid and every raider within 32 blocks glows (Java).
keywords: how to get a bell minecraft bell recipe village armorer trade ruined portal raid glowing
materials: Any pickaxe to mine a bell quickly (bare hands work, just slower)
Or emeralds for trading with an armorer villager
steps: Fastest option: find a village and look for the bell at the meeting point - usually on a wooden frame near the well or center. Mine it with a pickaxe and it drops itself.
Loot option: bells appear in ruined portal chests - check them while exploring.
Renewable option: trade with an armorer villager, who sells bells for emeralds at higher levels. This is the only renewable source, since bells have no crafting recipe.
Place the bell on the side, top or bottom of a block and right-click to ring it.
Village defense: ringing a bell sends nearby villagers running to their beds - ring it at nightfall to get everyone indoors before zombies arrive.
Raid radar (Java): if a bell rings while raid mobs are within 32 blocks, every raider gets the Glowing effect - visible through walls. Ring repeatedly during raids to track the last hidden pillagers.
In Bedrock, village bells ring automatically when a raid starts; the Glowing trick is Java-only.
versions: Bells were added in 1.14 (Village & Pillage) on both editions. The Glowing effect on raiders is Java Edition only.
editionNote: Obtaining works the same everywhere. The raid Glowing highlight is Java-only; Bedrock bells ring on their own when a raid begins.

faq.q: Can you craft a bell?
faq.a: No. There is no recipe: villages, ruined portal chests and armorer trades are the only sources.

faq.q: Do villagers need a bell?
faq.a: Villages generate with one at the meeting point, and villagers gather around it. Removing it does not break the village, but villagers can claim beds without it - it is mostly a rally and alarm tool for you.

faq.q: Why does the bell ring by itself?
faq.a: In Bedrock it rings automatically when a raid starts. In both editions, villagers can ring claimed bells, and redstone pulses trigger bells too.

name: How to Make a Carpet in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Place 2 wool of the same color side by side in a crafting grid to get 3 carpets of that color. Re-dye white carpets by surrounding a dye with 8 carpets, and use carpets for decoration, fuel-free floor mob-proofing tricks and llama saddles.
keywords: how to make carpet minecraft recipe wool dye carpet colors craft floor decoration
materials: 2 wool of one color per craft (sheep or string crafting)
Optional: dyes to recolor white carpets
A crafting table (or the 2x2 inventory grid - it fits)
steps: Get wool: shear sheep for 1-3 wool without killing them, or craft 4 string into 1 wool.
Place 2 wool of the same color anywhere side by side in a crafting grid.
Take the 3 carpets from the output - each craft turns 2 wool into 3 carpets.
All 16 colors work: the carpet color always matches the wool you used.
To recolor: dye the sheep before shearing (permanent colored wool), or craft white carpets and surround 1 dye with 8 carpets to dye all 8 at once.
Place carpets on any solid surface. They sit one pixel above the block - mobs cannot spawn on carpet-covered floors, and you can hide light sources or hoppers underneath.

Extras: carpets decorate llamas like saddles (each color gives a different pattern), work as fuel for 0.33 smelts each, and let you walk over fences (jump onto a carpet on top of a fence, while animals cannot pass).
versions: Carpets have existed since Java 1.6.1 and Bedrock Alpha 0.8.0. Recipe and behavior are the same everywhere.
editionNote: Identical in Java and Bedrock.

faq.q: Can mobs spawn on carpets?
faq.a: No - carpets are non-spawnable blocks, so a carpeted floor is a spawn-proof floor that still looks soft. This makes them great for dark builds and mob-farm interiors.

faq.q: What is the most efficient carpet color?
faq.a: All colors cost the same. For large floors, dye the sheep instead of the wool: one dye colors a sheep forever, and every shearing after that gives colored wool for free.

faq.q: Why can I jump a fence with carpet but my horse cannot?
faq.a: A carpet on top of a fence gives players a step up but mobs read the fence as a full 1.5-block wall. It is the classic animal-pen door: you hop over, livestock stays in.

name: How to Make a Glow Item Frame in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Combine 1 item frame with 1 glow ink sac anywhere in the crafting grid to get a glow item frame: a frame that makes the item inside it shine bright, visible in the dark. Glow ink sacs drop from glow squids in dark underwater caves.
keywords: glow item frame minecraft recipe glow ink sac glow squid how to craft display items light
materials: 1 glow ink sac per frame (glow squid drops)
Any crafting grid - the recipe is shapeless
steps: Craft an item frame first: 8 sticks around 1 leather.
Get glow ink sacs: glow squids spawn in dark water underground and below Y=30; kill them for 1-3 sacs.
Combine the item frame and the glow ink sac anywhere in a crafting grid (shapeless recipe).
Place the glow item frame on a wall, floor or ceiling and put any item inside.
The item inside glows with a bright outline and stays readable in complete darkness - the frame itself does not emit light, so it does not affect mob spawning.
Uses: glowing map walls, item labels on chests you can read at night, enchanted-book displays and shop signs that pop.
Rotate the item inside with right-click like a normal frame; punch the frame once to pop the item out, twice to break it (it always drops itself).
versions: Glow item frames were added in 1.17 (Caves & Cliffs Part I) on both editions.
editionNote: Identical recipe and behavior in Java and Bedrock.

faq.q: Does a glow item frame light up the room?
faq.a: No - the item inside is bright and self-lit, but the frame emits no actual light level. It will not melt snow or stop mobs.

faq.q: Can I convert an existing item frame?
faq.a: Not directly: use a glow ink sac on a placed normal item frame to turn it into a glowing one, or craft a new glow item frame. You can also apply a regular ink sac to a glow frame to revert it.

faq.q: Where do glow squids spawn?
faq.a: In total darkness in water below Y=30 - aquifers, underground lakes and deep ocean caves. They stop spawning when you light the water, so hunt before you glow-lichen the place.

name: How to Change Your Minecraft Skin (Java and Bedrock)
quickAnswer: Java: upload a skin PNG at minecraft.net (Profile > Skin) or in the launcher's Skins tab - free, unlimited, instant. Bedrock: use the in-game Dressing Room to pick or import a skin. Choose the Classic (4px arms) or Slim (3px arms) model to match your PNG.
keywords: how to change minecraft skin java bedrock upload skin png dressing room classic slim model free
materials: A skin PNG file (64x64, or 64x32 classic format)
The right model choice: Classic or Slim arms
steps: Get a skin: download one from a skin site, make your own in an editor, or use our Skins gallery for ideas. Save the PNG.
Java, method 1: sign in at minecraft.net, open Profile > Skin, choose Classic or Slim model, upload the PNG and save. It applies to your account immediately.
Java, method 2: open the Minecraft Launcher > Skins tab > New Skin, pick the model and browse to your PNG.
Bedrock: launch the game, open Dressing Room on the main menu, pick a skin you own or import your own PNG (import works on Windows, mobile and most platforms; consoles are more limited).
Pick the right model: a Slim PNG on the Classic model shows black patches on the arms - if your skin looks wrong, switch models first.
Your skin follows your account: every device and server where you log in shows the new skin. No restart needed beyond relogging.
Keep a small library: the launcher (Java) and Dressing Room (Bedrock) both store multiple skins so you can swap whenever you like.
versions: Skin uploading applies to current Minecraft on both editions. The Slim (3px arm) model exists since Java 1.8.
editionNote: Java skins are account-wide PNG uploads. Bedrock skins live in the Dressing Room and can include marketplace items - some of those cost Minecoins, but classic skin import is free.

faq.q: Why does my skin have black or broken arms?
faq.a: Model mismatch: you uploaded a Slim (3-pixel arms) skin as Classic (4-pixel), or the reverse. Change the model at upload time and it fixes itself.

faq.q: Can I use a custom skin on Bedrock consoles?
faq.a: Console Bedrock (PlayStation, Xbox, Switch) does not allow PNG imports - you choose from Dressing Room items there. Windows and mobile Bedrock do allow importing your own PNG.

faq.q: Do other players see my skin?
faq.a: Yes, on any online server - everyone sees the skin tied to your account. In offline or cracked environments skins often fail to load, which is a server-side issue, not yours.

name: How to Get a Cape in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Official capes cannot be crafted, bought or custom-made: Mojang grants them for events and promotions (event servers, Minecraft Live, migrations), and once a promotion ends the cape is gone forever. Every account has the default Pan Cape - anything claiming to sell you a cape is a scam.
keywords: how to get a cape minecraft free mojang cape events pan cape elytra cape scam migration
materials: A Mojang/Microsoft account in good standing
Participation in whatever cape promotion is currently live (they are time-limited)
Zero money - official capes are never sold
steps: Check what you already own: everyone has the Pan Cape (the golden pancake design) - equip it from your minecraft.net profile (Java) or the Dressing Room (Bedrock).

Watch official channels: Mojang announces cape promotions on minecraft.net, the launcher and Minecraft Live. Past capes came from event servers, Twitch/TikTok campaigns, account migrations and real-life events.
Claim during the promotion: capes are granted by playing an event server, redeeming a code from an official campaign, or automatically to qualifying accounts. Each promotion explains its own steps.
Accept that old capes stay locked: MINECON capes, the Migrator cape and similar were one-time promotions. They cannot be obtained anymore, by anyone, at any price.
Wear it: on Java, pick the cape on your minecraft.net profile; on Bedrock, equip it in the Dressing Room. The cape also reskins your elytra when you wear one.
Bedrock extra: the Dressing Room also sells cosmetic capes for Minecoins - those are character-creator items, separate from the official Java-style capes.
Never buy a 'cape account' or 'cape code' from a stranger: capes cannot be transferred between accounts, so any cape for sale is a scam or a stolen account.
versions: Capes apply to current Minecraft on both editions. Official capes earned on one edition usually sync to the other through your Microsoft account.
editionNote: Java equips capes on the minecraft.net profile page; Bedrock uses the Dressing Room. Mod capes (OptiFine and similar) only show to players using the same mod.

faq.q: Can I make or upload a custom cape?
faq.a: No - unlike skins, capes cannot be custom-made. Only Mojang can grant one, and only through time-limited promotions. Mods can show unofficial capes, visible only to users of that mod.

faq.q: Can I buy a cape?
faq.a: Not from Mojang, ever. Sites or people selling capes sell either nothing, a stolen account, or a mod cape that only mod users can see. Do not pay for one.

faq.q: I joined an event but did not get the cape?
faq.a: Promotions sometimes take days to roll out and require claiming (redeeming a code or finishing a task). Check the event's official page and your minecraft.net profile before assuming it failed - and after the deadline, there is no way in.

name: How to Install Shaders in Minecraft (Java)
quickAnswer: Install Iris (recommended) or OptiFine - both free - then drop a shader pack ZIP into the shaderpacks folder and enable it in Video Settings > Shaders. Shaders are Java Edition only; Bedrock has its own Vibrant Visuals setting.
keywords: how to install shaders minecraft java iris optifine shaderpacks folder vibrant visuals free
materials: Iris (with Fabric) or OptiFine - both free downloads
A shader pack ZIP (BSL, Complementary, Sildur's...)
A PC with a decent GPU - shaders are heavy
steps: Choose your loader: Iris + Sodium is the modern pick (better performance and mod compatibility); OptiFine is the classic all-in-one. Both are free - never pay for shaders or installers.

For Iris: run the Fabric installer for your Minecraft version, then drop the Iris and Sodium JARs into the mods folder. For OptiFine: download the JAR matching your game version and run it - it creates a launcher profile.
Launch the game once with that profile, then close it. A shaderpacks folder appears inside your .minecraft directory.
Download a shader pack (it comes as a ZIP - do not unzip it) and move the ZIP into the shaderpacks folder.
In-game: Options > Video Settings > Shaders, select the pack, click Done. The world relights itself with the new look.
Tune performance: shader packs have Low/Medium/High presets. If your FPS drops hard, lower the preset before blaming your PC.
Bedrock players: shaders as such do not exist - the built-in Vibrant Visuals graphics setting (on supported devices) is the official equivalent.
versions: Shader support via OptiFine/Iris works on all current Java versions. Iris updates faster on new releases; OptiFine sometimes lags behind version updates.
editionNote: Java Edition only. Bedrock (Windows, console, mobile) cannot install shader packs - use Vibrant Visuals or marketplace looks instead.

faq.q: Are shaders free?
faq.a: Yes. Iris, OptiFine and every major shader pack (BSL, Complementary, Sildur's) are free. Sites charging for shader downloads or 'premium installers' are scams - get everything from the official pages.

faq.q: Shaders vs texture packs - what is the difference?
faq.a: Texture packs change how blocks look; shaders change the lighting, shadows, water and sky. They stack: most people run both together.

faq.q: My game crashes with shaders - what now?
faq.a: Update your graphics drivers first. Then try Iris instead of OptiFine (or vice versa), pick the Low preset, and check the pack matches your Minecraft version. Old packs on new versions are the most common crash cause.

name: How to Play Minecraft with Friends (Every Way)
quickAnswer: Same edition required: Bedrock players add each other as Xbox friends and join from the Friends tab; Java players open their world to LAN or join the same server IP. Realms is the paid always-on option on both editions; free server hosting works for Java.
keywords: how to play minecraft with friends multiplayer java bedrock lan server realms join world cross platform
materials: The same edition as your friends: Java with Java, Bedrock with Bedrock
An online Microsoft account for Bedrock friend play
steps: Check editions first: Java (PC only) and Bedrock (Windows, consoles, mobile) cannot play together. This is the #1 reason 'it does not work'.
Bedrock, easiest way: everyone signs in with a Microsoft account, one player opens their world with Multiplayer enabled, friends find it in the Friends tab and join. No IP needed.
Same house, any edition: open the world to LAN (Java: Esc > Open to LAN; Bedrock: Multiplayer settings) and others join from the LAN section.
Java servers: one player runs or rents a server, shares the IP, everyone adds it under Multiplayer > Add Server. Free hosting options exist - see our servers section.
Realms: Mojang's official subscription server - always online, works on both editions (separate Realms for Java and Bedrock), one player pays and invites the rest for free.
Match versions: if a friend cannot join, check everyone runs the same game version - version mismatch is the second most common join failure.
On public servers, friend each other and use /tpa or the server's party system to play together instead of hunting coordinates.
versions: Applies to current Java and Bedrock. Realms is a paid Mojang subscription; everything else listed here is free.
editionNote: Cross-edition play (Java with Bedrock) is impossible in vanilla. Some unofficial proxy servers bridge them, but that is server-side work - not something clients can fix.

faq.q: Can Java and Bedrock players play together?
faq.a: Not in vanilla - they are different codebases. Some community servers run a proxy (Geyser) that lets Bedrock clients join Java servers, but the server owner must set that up.

faq.q: Why can I not see my friend's world?
faq.a: Run the checklist: same edition, same version, the host has Multiplayer toggled on (Bedrock) or opened to LAN (Java), you are Xbox friends (Bedrock online), and nobody's firewall or parental settings block multiplayer.

faq.q: Is Realms the only always-online option?
faq.a: No: a rented or self-hosted server stays online without the host playing. Realms is just the simplest - the others are free or cheaper but need more setup.

name: How to Back Up Your Minecraft World
quickAnswer: Your world is a folder: Java keeps it in .minecraft/saves, Bedrock in the com.mojang/minecraftWorlds folder. Copy the world folder somewhere safe and you have a full backup - restore by copying it back. Do it before updates, mods and experiments.
keywords: how to backup minecraft world saves folder restore copy java bedrock where are worlds stored
materials: Access to your game files (file explorer on PC)
Free disk space for the copy
Optional: cloud storage or a USB drive for off-machine copies
steps: Java (Windows): press Win+R, type %appdata%\.minecraft\saves and hit Enter. Each folder there is one world.
Java (Mac/Linux): saves live in ~/Library/Application Support/minecraft/saves (Mac) and ~/.minecraft/saves (Linux).
Bedrock (Windows): worlds are in %localappdata%\Packages\Microsoft.MinecraftUWP_8wekyb3d8bbwe\LocalState\games\com.mojang\minecraftWorlds.

Bedrock (mobile): on Android the same com.mojang folder lives in internal storage (games/com.mojang/minecraftWorlds) if the game is set to External/Application storage; iOS keeps it inside the app's files - use the Files app.
Close the game, then copy the whole world folder to your backup spot. Copying while playing can corrupt the copy.
To restore: put the folder back where it came from and restart the game. The world appears in the list with its original name.
Habit: back up before big updates, before adding or removing mods (Java), and monthly in general. Servers: copy the world folder while the server is stopped.
versions: Folder locations are current for the official launcher and Bedrock installs. Third-party launchers keep their own instance folders with a saves directory inside.
editionNote: Java worlds and Bedrock worlds are not interchangeable - a backup can only be restored to the same edition.

faq.q: Can I move a world from Java to Bedrock?
faq.a: Not directly - the formats differ. Community converters exist, but they are unofficial and lossy; keep backups in their original edition.

faq.q: My world disappeared - is the backup enough?
faq.a: If the folder still exists in saves, the world is there - the list sometimes hides worlds after version issues. If the folder is gone, only a real backup copy (or file-recovery tools) can bring it back.

faq.q: How big are world folders?
faq.a: Fresh worlds are a few MB; long-played worlds with lots of exploring reach hundreds of MB to several GB. Check size before picking a cloud plan, but any USB stick handles most worlds.

name: How to Update Minecraft (Every Platform)
quickAnswer: Java updates itself through the launcher: just pick the Latest Release installation and play. Bedrock updates through your device's app store (Microsoft Store, Play Store, App Store or the console's game menu). Servers must be updated separately with the new server JAR.
keywords: how to update minecraft latest version launcher java bedrock console mobile server update
materials: The official launcher (Java) or your device's store (Bedrock)
A world backup before big updates (recommended)
steps: Java: open the Minecraft Launcher - it downloads new versions automatically. In the Installations tab, the Latest Release installation always points at the newest version.
Java, stay on an old version: create a separate installation pinned to your version (useful for mods and servers that have not updated).
Bedrock on Windows: open the Microsoft Store > Library > Get updates.
Bedrock on mobile: update from the Play Store (Android) or App Store (iOS) like any app.
Bedrock on consoles: highlight the game, press the options/menu button and choose Check for Updates - consoles usually auto-update when online.

Servers: the server does not update with your client. Download the new server JAR (Java) or Bedrock server build, stop the server, swap the file and start it again. Clients and server must match versions to play together.
Before updating a world you care about: back it up. Worlds upgraded to a new version usually cannot go back to the old one.
versions: Applies to the current release channels. Java snapshots and Bedrock previews are separate opt-in tracks for testing upcoming updates.
editionNote: Java updates live in the launcher; Bedrock updates live in each platform's store. There is no in-game update button on Bedrock.

faq.q: Why is my game not updating?
faq.a: Java: make sure you launch the Latest Release installation, not a pinned old one. Bedrock: stores sometimes hold updates for hours by region - check the store page manually and restart the device.

faq.q: Will updating break my mods?
faq.a: Usually yes, temporarily: mods are built per version. Keep a pinned installation on your modded version until your mods update - this is exactly what the Installations tab is for.

faq.q: My friends updated and I cannot join their world?
faq.a: Versions must match. Either update to their version or ask them to host on yours. Realms always runs the latest version, so Realms players must stay current.

name: How to Make a Super Smelter (Auto Furnace)
quickAnswer: A super smelter is a row of furnaces fed automatically: hoppers on top load items to smelt, hoppers on the side load fuel, and hoppers underneath pull the results into a chest. Feed it once and walk away - it smelts stacks while you play.
keywords: super smelter minecraft auto furnace array hoppers automatic smelting how to build xp
materials: Furnaces (any count - 8 to 16 is a good start)
3 hoppers per furnace plus 1-2 input and 1-2 output chests
Fuel: dried kelp blocks, coal blocks or lava buckets
steps: Place a row of furnaces side by side, one block apart or touching - the design works either way.
Run a hopper line into the TOP of each furnace: place hoppers facing down into them and connect the line back to one input chest. This line carries the items to smelt.
Run a second hopper line into the BACK or SIDE of each furnace for fuel. Connect it to a fuel chest.
Place a hopper under each furnace facing into a collection line that ends in the output chest.
Balance the load: hoppers distribute items unevenly - put a minecart-with-hopper track above the top line for even spread, or simply overfill the input chest so every furnace stays busy.
Fuel it efficiently: dried kelp blocks smelt 20 items each and farm themselves; a lava bucket smelts 100. Load the fuel chest and the system runs for hours.
XP trick: furnaces bank the XP of everything they smelt. Pull one item out manually from any furnace after a big run and all the stored XP floods into you.
versions: Hopper-fed furnace arrays work identically in all current versions. Minecart distribution behaves slightly differently per edition - the overfilling method avoids that entirely.
editionNote: Works in Java and Bedrock. Hopper timing differs slightly, which is why the overfilled-input design is recommended for both.

faq.q: Why does the first furnace get everything?
faq.a: Hoppers push into the first available slot, so the nearest furnace fills first. Either overflow the input (simple) or use a hopper-minecart on a rail over the furnaces (even).

faq.q: Is a blast furnace or smoker better for a super smelter?
faq.a: They smelt their categories (ores / food) twice as fast but only those categories. Mixed input needs regular furnaces; dedicated arrays with blast furnaces for ores and smokers for food are the fastest setup.

faq.q: How do I collect the XP?
faq.a: XP accumulates inside each furnace as it smelts. Manually take out any single finished item and the furnace dumps all its stored XP on you - one claim after a long session is a huge level boost.

name: How to Show Coordinates in Minecraft (Java and Bedrock)
quickAnswer: Java: press F3 - your X, Y and Z are in the debug screen. Bedrock: enable Show Coordinates in the world settings (no cheats needed). X/Z are your horizontal position, Y is height - diamonds live around Y=-59.
keywords: how to show coordinates minecraft f3 java bedrock xyz enable coordinates world settings
materials: Bedrock: world settings access (owner or operator)
No cheats required on either edition
steps: Java: press F3 in-game. The debug overlay appears - look for the XYZ line near the top left. Press F3 again to hide it.
Read it right: X runs east(+)/west(-), Y is height, Z runs south(+)/north(-). Your block position is the rounded-down value.
Java extras: F3 + G shows chunk borders, F3 + B shows hitboxes, F3 + Q lists all debug shortcuts. On some laptops F3 needs Fn + F3.
Bedrock: open the world settings (pause > Settings, or the pencil icon on the world list) and toggle Show Coordinates on. They display permanently at the top left.
Bedrock without cheats: the Show Coordinates toggle is a world setting, not a cheat - achievements stay enabled. The copy-coordinates button next to it puts your position in chat.
Use them: write down base coordinates, mark diamonds level (Y=-59 in current versions), and navigate back home by walking toward your saved X and Z.
Multiplayer: server rules may hide the F3 coordinates (reduced debug info). Bedrock servers and Realms respect the world setting controlled by the owner.
versions: F3 debug screen since early Java; Show Coordinates toggle in Bedrock since 1.8. Both work in all current versions.
editionNote: Java shows coordinates via F3 with no setting needed. Bedrock needs the world toggle, which the world owner controls - on Realms ask the owner to enable it.

faq.q: F3 does nothing - why?
faq.a: On laptops the function row often needs Fn + F3. Some keyboards map F3 to brightness or volume - check your Fn lock. In-game, make sure no chat window is open.

faq.q: Why does my server hide coordinates?
faq.a: Java servers can enable reducedDebugInfo, which strips coordinates from F3 for everyone. It is a server-side rule - only the owner can change it (gamerule reducedDebugInfo false).

faq.q: What Y level should I mine at?
faq.a: For diamonds in current versions, Y=-59 (just above bedrock, watching for lava). For iron, mountain tops and Y=16; for coal, high mountains; for ancient debris in the Nether, Y=15.

name: How to Install Mods in Minecraft (Java)
quickAnswer: Java: install a mod loader (Fabric, Forge or NeoForge) from its official site, run the installer, drop the mod .jar files into the mods folder and launch the loader profile. Mods must match your Minecraft version and loader. Bedrock cannot run mods - it uses add-ons.
keywords: how to install mods minecraft java fabric forge neoforge mods folder curseforge modrinth mod loader
materials: A mod loader: Fabric, Forge or NeoForge
Mod .jar files from CurseForge or Modrinth
Mods matching your exact Minecraft version
steps: Pick a loader: Fabric is light and updates fast, NeoForge/Forge run the big classic mods. Check which loader each mod requires - mods are not cross-compatible between loaders.
Download the installer only from the official site: fabricmc.net, files.minecraftforge.net or neoforged.net. Avoid re-upload sites that bundle junk.
Run the installer with Minecraft closed, choose your game version and install the client. It creates a new profile in the Minecraft Launcher.
Download your mods from CurseForge or Modrinth. Every mod page lists the game version and loader it supports - both must match your install.

Open the mods folder: launch the loader profile once and use the Mods button on the title screen, or go straight to .minecraft/mods (%appdata%\.minecraft on Windows). Create the folder if it does not exist.
Drop the .jar files into mods. On Fabric, most mods also need the Fabric API mod - install it the same way.
Launch the Fabric/Forge/NeoForge profile. The Mods menu lists what loaded; a crash at startup almost always means a version or loader mismatch - remove the newest mod and check versions.
versions: Loaders track each Minecraft release. Fabric usually updates within hours of a new version; NeoForge and Forge take longer. Always match mod, loader and game version.
editionNote: Java Edition only. Bedrock (Windows, console, mobile) does not support mods - it uses add-ons from the Marketplace or .mcpack files.

faq.q: Are mods free?
faq.a: Yes. Mods on CurseForge and Modrinth are free. Any site charging for a mod or a 'premium mod installer' is a scam.

faq.q: Can I use mods on a server?
faq.a: Only if the server runs the same loader and mods. Client-side mods (minimap, performance) work on any server that allows them.

faq.q: Do mods disable achievements?
faq.a: No. Java advancements keep working with mods installed.

name: How to Install Texture Packs (Resource Packs)
quickAnswer: Java: download the pack .zip and drop it (without unzipping) into the resourcepacks folder via Options > Resource Packs > Open Pack Folder, then move it to the Selected column. Bedrock: open the .mcpack file and it imports itself; activate it in Settings > Global Resources.
keywords: how to install texture packs resource packs minecraft java bedrock mcpack resourcepacks folder
materials: Java: from CurseForge or Modrinth; Bedrock: also the Marketplace
A pack matching your Minecraft version
steps: Download a pack from CurseForge, Modrinth or the Marketplace. Java packs are .zip files - do not unzip them.
Java: launch the game and go to Options > Resource Packs > Open Pack Folder. The resourcepacks folder opens.
Copy the .zip into that folder, return to the game and move the pack from the Available column to Selected with the arrow. Click Done - the game reloads with the new textures.
Order matters: packs higher in the Selected list override lower ones. Put your main pack on top.
Bedrock: double-click the .mcpack file (or open it with Minecraft) and it imports automatically. Activate it in Settings > Global Resources, or per world in the world settings.
Marketplace packs on Bedrock install from the Marketplace itself and activate the same way.
versions: Packs are version-sensitive: a pack built for a much older release can show missing or purple-black textures on new blocks. Pack pages list the supported versions.
editionNote: Java calls them resource packs (they can also change sounds and fonts); 'texture pack' is the old name for the same thing. Bedrock uses .mcpack files and Marketplace content.

faq.q: Do texture packs disable achievements?
faq.a: No. Resource packs are cosmetic on both editions - achievements stay enabled.

faq.q: The pack shows in Available but nothing changes?
faq.a: Move it to the Selected column with the arrow and press Done. If textures look broken, the pack targets a different Minecraft version.

name: How to Make a Minecraft Server (Free)
quickAnswer: Java, free: download the official server .jar from minecraft.net, run it once, set eula=true in eula.txt, run it again - your server is live. Friends on your network join via your local IP; friends over the internet need port 25565 forwarded, or use a free host like Aternos instead.
keywords: how to make a minecraft server free java server jar eula port forwarding 25565 aternos realms host
materials: A PC that can stay on while you play
Java installed (same Java your game uses)
Router access for port forwarding (only for internet play)
steps: Create an empty folder for the server and download server.jar into it from minecraft.net/download/server - the official, free download.
Run it: java -Xmx2G -Xms2G -jar server.jar nogui. It stops right away and generates eula.txt and the server files.
Open eula.txt and change eula=false to eula=true (you accept the Minecraft EULA). Save the file.
Run the command again. The world generates and the console prints 'Done' - the server is running. Type stop to shut it down cleanly.
Join from the same PC with the address localhost, or from other devices on your home network with your PC's local IP.
Friends over the internet: forward TCP port 25565 on your router to your PC and share your public IP. server.properties holds the settings (motd, difficulty, max players).
No router access? Use a free host like Aternos (ad-supported) or a tunnel like playit.gg. Realms is Mojang's paid option with the simplest setup of all.
versions: The server .jar matches each game release - take the latest, unless you play modded, then match your mods' version. Bedrock has its own official dedicated server for Windows and Linux.
editionNote: Java and Bedrock servers are separate: a Java server does not accept Bedrock players without unofficial proxies. Consoles and mobile can only join Bedrock servers or Realms.

faq.q: Is running a server free?
faq.a: Yes - the official server .jar is free, and hosts like Aternos are free (ad-supported). Realms is Mojang's paid subscription. Never pay for 'server installer' downloads.

faq.q: How much RAM does a server need?
faq.a: 1-2 GB is fine for a few friends on vanilla. Raise it with -Xmx4G if you add mods or many players.

faq.q: Can I add mods to my server?
faq.a: Yes - install Fabric or NeoForge on the server and every player needs the same mods on their client.

name: How to Install Minecraft Maps (Java and Bedrock)
quickAnswer: Java: unzip the download and copy the world folder (the one containing level.dat) into .minecraft/saves - it appears in your Singleplayer list. Bedrock: double-click the .mcworld file and Minecraft imports it automatically.
keywords: how to install minecraft maps download worlds java saves folder level.dat mcworld bedrock import
materials: Java: file access to your .minecraft folder
The Minecraft version the map was made for
steps: Download maps from CurseForge or Modrinth. Java maps come as a .zip with a world folder inside; Bedrock maps are .mcworld files.
Java: unzip the download. Inside is a folder that directly contains level.dat - that folder is the world.
Open your saves folder: Windows %appdata%\.minecraft\saves, macOS ~/Library/Application Support/minecraft/saves, Linux ~/.minecraft/saves.
Copy the world folder into saves and start Minecraft - the map appears in the Singleplayer list.
Bedrock: open the .mcworld file (double-click, or share it to Minecraft on mobile). It imports itself and shows up in your world list.
Check the map's required version: adventure and parkour maps with command blocks often only work on the exact version the creator lists.
versions: Maps made in newer versions will not open in older game versions. Older maps usually upgrade on first open, but command-block contraptions can break across big updates.
editionNote: Console players (PlayStation, Xbox, Switch) cannot import map files - only Marketplace worlds or Realms. Map import works on Windows, mobile and Java on any OS.

faq.q: The map does not appear in Singleplayer?
faq.a: Usually nested folders: saves must contain the world folder that directly holds level.dat - not a zip, and not a folder inside a folder.

faq.q: Are maps free?
faq.a: Community maps on CurseForge and Modrinth are free. Marketplace worlds on Bedrock can cost Minecoins.

name: How to Find Your Minecraft World Seed
quickAnswer: Java: run /seed in chat (needs cheats or operator). Bedrock: open the world settings - the seed is listed there and viewing it needs no cheats. Use the seed when creating a world to generate the same terrain again.
keywords: how to find world seed minecraft java seed command bedrock world settings same world recreate
materials: Java: cheats enabled or operator on the server
Bedrock: access to the world settings
steps: Java singleplayer with cheats: open chat (T) and run /seed. The seed appears in chat - click it to copy it.
Java without cheats: press Esc > Open to LAN > Allow Cheats: ON > Start LAN World, then run /seed. Cheats turn off again when you quit the world.
Java on a server: only operators can run /seed - ask an admin.
Bedrock: pause > Settings (or the pencil icon next to the world in the list) and scroll the Game section - the seed is shown there in plain sight, and looking at it does not affect achievements.
Use it: when creating a new world, paste the number into the Seed field to generate the same terrain.
Share it with friends so they spawn in the same world layout - handy with our famous seeds lists.
versions: A seed only reproduces the same world on the same edition and roughly the same version - world generation changed at 1.18, so seeds from before generate different terrain today.
editionNote: Java and Bedrock seeds are not interchangeable: the same number produces a different world on each edition.

faq.q: Can I get the seed of a very old world?
faq.a: Yes - /seed works on any Java world you can open, and Bedrock always shows the seed in settings, no matter when the world was created.

faq.q: Does checking the seed disable achievements?
faq.a: No. Viewing it on Bedrock is free; on Java, /seed needs cheats, but Java has no achievement lockout anyway.

name: How to Enable Cheats in Minecraft
quickAnswer: New world: turn on Allow Commands (Java) or Activate Cheats (Bedrock) in the creation screen. Existing Java world: Esc > Open to LAN > Allow Cheats: ON - commands work until you quit. Existing Bedrock world: toggle Activate Cheats in the world settings, which permanently disables achievements for that world.
keywords: how to enable cheats minecraft allow cheats open to lan activate cheats bedrock achievements commands
materials: A singleplayer world (servers need operator permissions instead)
Java: Esc menu for the LAN trick
Bedrock: access to the world settings
steps: New world (Java): Create New World > Game > Allow Commands: ON before generating the world.
New world (Bedrock): flip the Activate Cheats toggle in the creation screen - the game warns that achievements will be disabled for that world.
Existing Java world: press Esc > Open to LAN, set Allow Cheats: ON and start the LAN world. Commands work until you close the world - repeat the trick each session.
Existing Bedrock world: world settings > Activate Cheats. The change is permanent for that world: achievements stay off even if you turn cheats back off later.
What cheats unlock: /gamemode, /give, /tp, /time set, /weather, /seed and the full command list.
On Realms and servers, cheats come from operator permissions (/op from the owner), not from these world toggles.

Newer Java versions also let you toggle cheats at any time from the World Options menu in a singleplayer world. The Open to LAN trick is temporary and, per the Minecraft Wiki, its menu changed after Java 26.3, so look for the cheats option in the LAN screen or World Options.
versions: The Open to LAN trick works in every modern Java version. Java never blocks advancements for cheats; Bedrock blocks achievements the moment cheats turn on.
editionNote: Java keeps advancements with cheats on. Bedrock disables achievements per world the moment you activate cheats - there is no way to re-enable them on that world.

faq.q: Do cheats disable achievements?
faq.a: Bedrock: yes, permanently for that world. Java: no - advancements keep working.

faq.q: Can I enable cheats on someone else's server?
faq.a: No. You need operator permissions from the server owner - there is no client-side trick.

name: How to Keep Inventory When You Die
quickAnswer: Run /gamerule keep_inventory true (needs cheats) and you keep your items and XP when you die. Turn it back off with /gamerule keep_inventory false. On Bedrock it is also a world toggle: Activate Cheats > Keep Inventory.
keywords: how to keep inventory minecraft gamerule keepinventory true die keep items command
materials: Cheats enabled (Java: Open to LAN trick works)
Bedrock: also available as a world toggle in settings
steps: Java: open chat (T) and run /gamerule keep_inventory true. The game confirms the rule changed.
No cheats on your Java world? Press Esc > Open to LAN > Allow Cheats: ON, start the LAN world and run the command. The gamerule stays saved in the world even after cheats turn off again.
Bedrock: world settings > Activate Cheats, then scroll to the Keep Inventory toggle and turn it on. Activating cheats disables achievements on that world.
From now on, dying costs you nothing: you respawn with your full inventory and experience levels.
To go back to normal, run /gamerule keep_inventory false (or flip the Bedrock toggle off).
Server owners: the same command works from the server console or as an operator.
versions: keep_inventory exists in every version that has gamerules - practically all modern Java and Bedrock versions.
editionNote: Bedrock hides it behind the cheats toggle, which disables achievements. Java has no achievement lockout - advancements keep working.

faq.q: Does keep_inventory count as cheating?
faq.a: It is a built-in game rule Mojang put in the game - on Java it does not even cost you advancements. On Bedrock, any cheat toggle disables achievements for that world.

faq.q: Do I lose XP with keep_inventory on?
faq.a: No. You keep your items and your experience levels when you die.

name: How to Set Your Spawn Point in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Sleep in a bed (Overworld) or click a charged respawn anchor (Nether) to set your respawn point. With cheats, /spawnpoint sets it exactly where you stand. Without any of these you respawn at world spawn.
keywords: how to set spawn point minecraft bed respawn anchor spawnpoint command world spawn
materials: A bed (3 wool + 3 planks) for the Overworld
A respawn anchor + glowstone for the Nether
steps: Overworld: place a bed and sleep in it (right-click it; you can only fall asleep at night or in a thunderstorm, but in Java 1.15 and later right-clicking by day still sets your spawn). The chat confirms 'Respawn point set'.
Your bed spawn stays until the bed is broken or blocked - then you respawn at world spawn with a 'bed missing or obstructed' message.
Nether: beds explode there. Use a respawn anchor instead: craft it with 6 crying obsidian + 3 glowstone, place it and charge it with glowstone blocks (up to 4 charges).
Click the charged anchor to set your Nether spawn. Each death uses one charge - recharge with more glowstone.
With cheats: /spawnpoint sets your spawn exactly where you stand, in any dimension. /spawnpoint @p X Y Z sets precise coordinates.
World spawn itself only moves with /setworldspawn (cheats) - useful for server lobbies and adventure maps.
versions: Respawn anchors were added in 1.16 (Nether Update) and work the same in all current versions.
editionNote: Beds set spawns identically on Java and Bedrock. Respawn anchors exist on both editions too - just never right-click a bed in the Nether or the End.

faq.q: Why did I respawn at world spawn?
faq.a: Your bed was broken or blocked, or your respawn anchor ran out of charges. The death message tells you which one happened.

faq.q: Can I have spawns in several places?
faq.a: Only one personal respawn point at a time - the last bed slept in or anchor clicked wins. Compass plus lodestone helps you navigate between bases.

name: How to Find Slime Chunks in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Slimes spawn below Y=40 in special 'slime chunks' - about 1 in 10 chunks, regardless of light. Java: your chunks depend on the world seed (press F3+G to see chunk borders). Bedrock: slime chunks are the same fixed coordinates in every world. Slimes also spawn in swamps at night (Y=51-69).
keywords: how to find slime chunks minecraft slime farm y level swamp java bedrock chunk borders f3 g
materials: Java: F3 debug screen (F3 + G for chunk borders)
Your world seed (/seed) for chunk-finder tools
A pickaxe to dig down to Y=40 or below
steps: Underground method (both editions): slimes spawn below Y=40 in slime chunks, about 1 in 10 chunks, in any light level. Dig out a large room under Y=40 and see where slimes appear.
Java: press F3 + G to draw chunk borders in the world. A chunk runs 16x16 blocks; the debug screen also shows your current chunk.
Java: your slime chunks depend on the world seed. Run /seed, then plug the seed into a free chunk-finder map tool to mark every slime chunk around your base.
Bedrock: slime chunks sit at the same fixed coordinates in every world - any Bedrock slime-chunk map works without knowing your seed.
Swamp method: slimes spawn on the surface in swamps and mangrove swamps between Y=51 and Y=69 when the light level is 7 or less. They are most common on a full moon and never spawn on a new moon.
Farming tip: light up nearby caves to free the mob cap, then stand 24-32 blocks from your slime-chunk platform so slimes keep spawning.
versions: Slime chunk mechanics are stable across current versions. Swamp spawning (Y=51-69, light 7 or less, moon phases) works the same on Java and Bedrock.
editionNote: Java slime chunks are seed-based; Bedrock slime chunks are fixed coordinates shared by every world. Swamp spawning is identical on both.

faq.q: Do slimes need darkness in slime chunks?
faq.a: No - below Y=40 they spawn at any light level. Only the swamp surface spawns care about light (7 or less).

faq.q: Why is my slime farm empty?
faq.a: Usually the mob cap is full of cave mobs, or you are standing too close (slimes do not spawn within 24 blocks of you). Light up caves around the farm.

name: How to Play Older Versions of Minecraft
quickAnswer: Java: Minecraft Launcher > Installations > New Installation > pick any version from the dropdown (back to the oldest alphas) and play it. Bedrock has no official version switcher - only Java can downgrade.
keywords: how to play older versions minecraft downgrade launcher installations old version java alpha beta
materials: An installation per version you want to keep
steps: Open the Minecraft Launcher and go to the Installations tab.
