faq.q: Is the warped forest safe?
faq.a: It is the safest Nether biome: only endermen and striders spawn naturally (no ghasts, piglins or hoglins), and endermen stay neutral unless you look them in the eye.

name: How to Find a Soul Sand Valley in Minecraft
quickAnswer: The soul sand valley is the third most common Nether biome (about 17%) - a gray-blue wasteland of soul sand and soul soil with soul fire, giant Nether fossils and basalt pillars. It can border any Nether biome except warped forests. Ghasts and skeletons spawn constantly here, which makes it the best spot for a ghast tear farm - and dried ghasts sit near the fossils.
keywords: how to find soul sand valley minecraft nether biome ghast farm fossils dried ghast soul soil where
materials: A bow and plenty of arrows for ghasts
Boots with Soul Speed if you have them - the whole floor slows you down
steps: Walk the Nether until the fog turns cyan: the soul sand valley covers about 17% of the dimension and can border any biome except the warped forest.

Confirm the biome: a floor of soul sand and soul soil (gravel on the coasts), blue soul fire scattered around, giant bone fossils poking out of the terrain and basalt pillars running floor to ceiling.
Listen: the wind and ghostly voices in the ambience are unique to this biome.
Watch the sky: ghasts spawn here at high rates along with skeletons - keep a bow ready and never fight near a ledge.
Farm ghast tears: the valley's open floor and constant ghast spawns make it the classic ghast farm location - kite them over soul soil and collect the drops.
Look for dried ghasts: they generate as small block-like creatures near the Nether fossils - pick one up to rehydrate your own happy ghast at home.
Collect soul soil for soul torches and soul campfires, and soul sand for nether wart farms and bubble elevators.
Move smart: soul sand slows you to a crawl - Soul Speed boots fix that, and a boat on ice or a strider beats walking.
versions: Soul sand valley generation is the same on Java and Bedrock. Verified against minecraft.wiki as of 26.x.
editionNote: Cyan fog, bone fossils, ghasts overhead: the valley is creepy, slow and worth it - tears, fossils, dried ghasts and all the soul blocks you will ever need.

faq.q: Where is the soul sand valley in Minecraft?
faq.a: In the Nether - it covers about 17% of the dimension and can border any Nether biome except the warped forest. Look for cyan fog, soul sand and soul soil, soul fire and giant fossils.

faq.q: What spawns in the soul sand valley?
faq.a: Ghasts and skeletons at high rates, plus endermen occasionally. The constant ghast spawns make it the best place to farm ghast tears and the 'Uneasy Alliance' rescue.

faq.q: Where do dried ghasts spawn?
faq.a: In soul sand valleys, near the giant Nether fossils. Pick one up and rehydrate it in water at home to grow a happy ghast.

name: How to Find Basalt Deltas in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Basalt deltas are the second rarest Nether biome (about 16%) - a jagged gray wasteland of basalt and blackstone, shallow lava pools and magma blocks, with ash drifting through the air. It can border any Nether biome except crimson forests. Magma cubes spawn everywhere here, making it the best magma cream farm - and bastion remnants never generate in it.
keywords: how to find basalt deltas minecraft nether biome magma cube farm basalt blackstone ash where
materials: Fire Resistance potions - lava pockets are everywhere
Good boots: the terrain is jagged and full of holes
A pickaxe for basalt, blackstone and the boosted ores
steps: Explore until the fog turns dull lilac: basalt deltas cover about 16% of the Nether and can border any biome except the crimson forest.
Confirm the biome: jagged spikes and terraces of basalt and blackstone, shallow lava deltas 1-3 blocks deep, magma blocks everywhere and gray ash particles floating in the air.
Watch your step: the terrain is some of the roughest in the Nether - jagged drops, hidden lava pools and magma blocks. Sprint-jumping is a bad idea; Fire Resistance is a good one.
Farm magma cubes: they spawn here at very high rates in every size - the best magma cream farm in the game, and froglight fuel if you bring frogs.
Mine the bonus ores: Nether quartz, Nether gold and even ancient debris generate more frequently here to compensate for the scarce netherrack.
Stock up on blocks: basalt (for polished basalt and basalt generators) and blackstone (for stone-tier tools, furnaces and brewing stands in the Nether).
Structures: Nether fortresses and ruined portals generate here, but bastion remnants never do - look elsewhere for pigstep and snout trims.
Mushrooms grow on the basalt, so brown and red mushrooms are free - grab some for stew.
versions: Basalt deltas generation is the same on Java and Bedrock. Verified against minecraft.wiki as of 26.x.
editionNote: Lilac fog, ash, lava deltas and magma cubes on every ledge: hostile terrain, excellent loot - the Nether's quarry and magma farm in one.

faq.q: Where are basalt deltas in Minecraft?
faq.a: In the Nether - the second rarest biome at about 16% of the dimension, bordering any Nether biome except the crimson forest. Look for lilac fog, ash particles and jagged basalt and blackstone terrain with shallow lava pools.

faq.q: What spawns in basalt deltas?
faq.a: Magma cubes in huge numbers and all sizes, plus ghasts occasionally. No piglins or hoglins - and bastion remnants never generate in this biome.

faq.q: What are basalt deltas good for?
faq.a: Magma cube farms (the best in the game), boosted ore rates (quartz, gold and ancient debris), and bulk basalt and blackstone for building.

name: How to Find Nether Wastes in Minecraft
quickAnswer: The Nether wastes is the most common Nether biome - about 36% of the dimension - so you almost certainly spawned in it. It is the classic barren netherrack landscape with lava seas, glowstone on the ceiling, and blobs of quartz, gold and blackstone. It generates in thin strips that always separate the biome pairs that cannot touch: crimson forest from basalt deltas, and warped forest from soul sand valley.
keywords: nether wastes biome minecraft how to find netherrack lava sea quartz gold blackstone most common
materials: A pickaxe - the whole biome is netherrack and ore
Fire Resistance potions for the lava seas
Gold armor for the piglins that wander through
steps: You are probably already in it: the Nether wastes covers about 36% of the dimension, making it the most common Nether biome - most portals open onto it.
Confirm the biome: barren netherrack as far as you can see, lava seas and falls, glowstone blobs on the ceiling, and gravel or soul sand along the coasts.

Look for it in strips: unlike the patchy Nether biomes, the wastes generate in thin bands - a strip of wastes always separates crimson forests from basalt deltas and warped forests from soul sand valleys, the pairs that can never touch.
Mine the visible ores: blobs of Nether quartz and Nether gold generate exposed in the netherrack - the easiest early Nether resources, plus blackstone for stone-tier tools.
Watch the mobs: ghasts, zombified piglins, magma cubes, piglins and striders all spawn here, with the occasional enderman. Wear one gold piece and keep a bow for ghasts.
Ancient debris hides unexposed inside the terrain - the wastes are as good a place as any to bed-mine or TNT-mine at Y=15.
Use the lava seas: striders spawn on them, and a warped fungus on a stick turns the biggest ocean in the game into a highway.
Navigational tip: if you find the wastes thinning into a band, the next biome over is one of the four specialty biomes - follow the strip to change scenery.
versions: Nether wastes generation is the same on Java and Bedrock. Verified against minecraft.wiki as of 26.x.
editionNote: It is the Nether's default wallpaper - but the exposed quartz and gold, the ghast hunting grounds and the strider lava seas make the wastes worth knowing on purpose.

faq.q: What is the Nether wastes biome?
faq.a: The most common Nether biome (about 36% of the dimension): barren netherrack with lava seas, ceiling glowstone, exposed quartz and gold ore, blackstone, and gravel and soul sand coasts. It fills the gaps between the other four Nether biomes.

faq.q: What mobs spawn in the Nether wastes?
faq.a: Ghasts, zombified piglins, magma cubes, piglins, striders on the lava seas, and the occasional enderman - nearly every Nether mob can appear here.

faq.q: Why do crimson forests never touch basalt deltas?
faq.a: Because a thin strip of Nether wastes always generates between them - the same goes for warped forests and soul sand valleys. The wastes are the Nether's separator biome.

name: How to Find a Jungle in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Jungles generate in semi-warm, high-humidity regions bordering forests, plains, deserts, wooded badlands, birch forests and dark forests. From the air look for towering 2x2 jungle trees over 30 blocks tall with vines everywhere. It is the only biome family with melons, cocoa beans, parrots, ocelots and pandas - and lush caves are common underneath.
keywords: how to find jungle minecraft biome jungle trees bamboo cocoa melon parrots ocelots pandas where
materials: An elytra or boat for scouting (optional but fast)
Shears for vines and an axe for jungle wood
Cookies or seeds for parrots once you arrive
steps: Search in semi-warm, wet regions: jungles generate at high humidity, bordering forests, plains, deserts, wooded badlands, birch forests and dark forests.
Regular jungles are often separated from sparse jungles or bamboo jungles by rivers - follow rivers through warm regions.
Jungles can be flat, hilly or mountainous: at high erosion they touch mangrove swamps and windswept savannas; inland they climb mountains, where the peaks are always stony.
Spot it from the air: a dense, uneven canopy of giant 2x2 jungle trees (30+ blocks) draped in vines - the tallest, shaggiest forest in the game.
Confirm the biome: jungle bushes and cocoa pods on the small trees, ferns, vines on everything, melon patches on the ground (exclusive to jungles) and single bamboo stalks scattered about.
Meet the exclusives: parrots, ocelots and pandas spawn only in jungle biomes - bring seeds for parrots and fish for ocelots.
Dig with care: lush caves are common underneath jungles thanks to the humidity - an easy way to find one without searching for an azalea tree.
Harvest the biome kit: jungle saplings, cocoa beans, melons, bamboo and vines all regrow at home - one trip sets up five farms.
Still stuck? Use /locate biome minecraft:jungle (or bamboo_jungle, sparse_jungle) with cheats enabled for exact coordinates.
versions: Jungle generation is the same on Java and Bedrock. Verified against minecraft.wiki as of 26.x.
editionNote: Warm, wet, giant trees: the jungle is five farms in one biome - wood, cocoa, melons, bamboo and parrots - with a lush cave bonus underneath.

faq.q: Where do jungles spawn in Minecraft?
faq.a: In semi-warm regions with high humidity, bordering forests, plains, deserts, wooded badlands, birch forests and dark forests. They range from flatland to mountains with stony peaks, and lush caves are common underneath.

faq.q: What only spawns in jungles?
faq.a: Melon patches, cocoa pods, parrots, ocelots and pandas are all jungle exclusives - plus the tallest trees in the game, the giant 2x2 jungle trees.

faq.q: What is the difference between jungle, sparse jungle and bamboo jungle?
faq.a: The regular jungle has the giant trees and full density. The sparse jungle is a thinner, more open edge variant. The bamboo jungle swaps the canopy for dense bamboo stalks with podzol and is the best panda territory.

name: How to Find a Swamp in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Swamps generate in flat, temperate terrain near sea level at very high erosion, replacing rivers and sitting between plains, forests, taigas and windswept hills - never directly on the ocean. Look for shallow murky water, lily pads, vine-covered oaks and blue orchids (which grow nowhere else). Slimes spawn on the surface at night, and witch huts hide in the deeper swamps.
keywords: how to find swamp minecraft biome slime witch hut blue orchid lily pad frogs where
materials: A boat - half the biome is shallow water
A sword for the night slimes
A name tag for a frog or two (temperate orange frogs live here)
steps: Search in flat temperate regions at very high erosion: swamps sit near sea level between plains, sunflower plains, forests, taigas and ranges of windswept hills or windswept savannas.
Swamps replace rivers in these areas and never directly border the ocean - though their waterways usually connect to one.
Temperature decides the neighbor: at higher temperatures swamps border mangrove swamps; at cold ones they end abruptly at frozen rivers.
Spot it: flat, shallow gray-green water with lily pads, sparse vine-covered oaks standing in the water, seagrass on the bottom and sugar cane on the shores.
Confirm with the exclusive flower: blue orchids grow only in swamps - if you see one, you are standing in one. Firefly bushes grow here too.
Slimes spawn on the surface at night, most during a full moon - the easiest overworld slime source without digging out a slime chunk.
Look for witch huts on stilts in the water: the witch's cauldron and the guaranteed black cat are the giveaway - a classic witch farm location.
Collect the biome kit: blue orchids, lily pads, vines, mushrooms (huge mushrooms appear in Bedrock), clay from the shallow water, and temperate frogs.
Still stuck? Use /locate biome minecraft:swamp with cheats enabled for exact coordinates.
versions: Swamp generation is the same on Java and Bedrock; huge mushrooms are Bedrock-only here. Verified against minecraft.wiki as of 26.x.
editionNote: Flat, wet, high erosion: the swamp is the slime-and-witch biome with the exclusive blue orchid - ugly, useful and easy to farm.

faq.q: Where do swamps spawn in Minecraft?
faq.a: In flat terrain near sea level at very high erosion, in temperate to cold regions between plains, forests, taigas and windswept hills. They replace rivers, never touch the ocean directly, and border mangrove swamps where it is warmer.

faq.q: What is special about the swamp biome?
faq.a: Slimes spawn on the surface at night (peaking at full moon), witch huts generate here, blue orchids grow exclusively in swamps, and it is the home of the temperate orange frog.

faq.q: How do I farm slimes in a swamp?
faq.a: Light up a flat area of the swamp, wait for night (ideally a full moon), and slimes spawn on the surface at any light level below 7 - no slime chunk digging needed. Higher moon phases mean more slimes.

name: How to Make an Awkward Potion in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Brew an awkward potion by adding nether wart to a water bottle in a brewing stand. It has no effect on its own, but it is the base for almost every effect potion in the game.
steps: Craft a brewing stand from 1 blaze rod and 3 cobblestone, and fuel it with blaze powder.
Craft glass bottles from 3 glass and fill them with water at any water source or cauldron.
Find nether wart: it grows in Nether fortress stairwell rooms and in bastion remnant housing units.
Place up to 3 water bottles in the bottom slots of the brewing stand.
Put 1 nether wart in the ingredient slot on top.
Wait 20 seconds. The water bottles turn into awkward potions.
Leave the awkward potions in the stand and add an effect ingredient (like a golden carrot for Night Vision or a magma cream for Fire Resistance) to brew a real potion.
materials: 1-3 water bottles (3 glass each, filled with water)
editionNote: In Java Edition the awkward potion is the only base potion that accepts an effect ingredient, so brewing nether wart first is mandatory for everything except the potion of Weakness. In Bedrock Edition, mundane and thick potions can also be imbued with effect ingredients, but the nether wart route is still the standard one. The recipe is identical in both editions.

faq.q: What does an awkward potion do?
faq.a: Nothing by itself. Drinking it gives no effect. Its only purpose is to serve as the base for brewing effect potions like Swiftness, Strength or Night Vision.

faq.q: Where do I find nether wart?
faq.a: Nether wart grows in Nether fortress stairwells on soul sand and in the housing units of bastion remnants. Take the soul sand too so you can farm it back home; it grows in any dimension.

faq.q: Which potion does not need an awkward potion?
faq.a: The potion of Weakness is the only one: it brews by adding a fermented spider eye directly to a water bottle, with no nether wart step.

name: How to Get a Potion of Luck in Minecraft
quickAnswer: The potion of Luck exists only in Java Edition and has no brewing recipe: you can only get it from the Creative inventory or with commands. It boosts your fishing luck for 5 minutes.
steps: Open a Java Edition world with cheats enabled, or switch to Creative mode.
In Creative, search 'luck' in the inventory and take the potion of Luck (splash and lingering versions are there too).
With commands, use /give @s minecraft:potion[minecraft:potion_contents={potion:"minecraft:luck"}] for the drinkable version.
Drink it to get the Luck effect for 5 minutes.
Go fishing while the effect is active: Luck increases the weight of treasure loot and reduces junk, so you catch more name tags, enchanted books and saddles.
For a survival-legal taste of Luck, get the Hero of the Village effect and stand near a fletcher: it can gift you arrows of Luck.
materials: Java Edition (the potion does not exist in Bedrock)
A fishing rod to make use of the effect
editionNote: The potion of Luck is exclusive to Java Edition and cannot be brewed or obtained in Survival: it was kept in the game for mapmakers after Mojang considered removing it in 1.9. Bedrock Edition has no Luck potion at all. The only survival way to touch the effect is the arrow of Luck that fletcher villagers gift you while you have Hero of the Village (also Java only).

faq.q: Can you brew a potion of Luck?
faq.a: No. There is no brewing recipe in any version. In Java Edition it comes only from the Creative inventory or commands; in Bedrock it does not exist.

faq.q: What does the Luck effect actually do?
faq.a: Luck improves loot tables that use quality, and right now that only means fishing: it raises your chance of treasure catches and lowers junk. It does not affect mob drops or chest loot.

faq.q: How long does the potion of Luck last?
faq.a: The drinkable and splash versions last 5 minutes, the lingering potion 1 minute 15 seconds, and arrows of Luck 37 seconds.

name: How to Get a Potion of Decay in Minecraft
quickAnswer: The potion of Decay is exclusive to Bedrock Edition and cannot be brewed: get it from the Creative inventory or with commands. It inflicts Wither II for 40 seconds, which can kill anything it hits.
steps: Open a Bedrock Edition world (mobile, console or Windows) with cheats enabled, or switch to Creative mode.
In Creative, search 'decay' in the inventory: you will find the potion, splash potion, lingering potion and arrow of Decay.
With commands, use /give @s potion 1 44 or the potion feature equivalent for your version to get the drinkable potion of Decay.
Drink or throw it to apply Wither II for 40 seconds (10 seconds for the lingering cloud).
Use splash potions of Decay against tough mobs: unlike Poison, Wither can kill its target and also hurts undead mobs.
In Survival, the closest legal option is the Wither effect itself: fight the wither, touch a wither rose, or eat suspicious stew made with a wither rose.
materials: Bedrock Edition (the potion does not exist in Java)
A target worth using Wither II on
editionNote: Potions of Decay are Bedrock Edition exclusive: they exist in the Creative inventory but have no brewing recipe and cannot be obtained in Survival. Java Edition has no potion of Decay at all. The Wither effect they deliver is stronger than Poison in two ways: it can kill the victim (Poison leaves you at half a heart) and it damages undead mobs like zombies and skeletons.

faq.q: Can you brew a potion of Decay?
faq.a: No. Even in Bedrock Edition there is no brewing recipe. It only exists in the Creative inventory or through commands, and Java Edition does not have it in any form.

faq.q: What is the difference between Wither and Poison?
faq.a: Wither acts slower per tick but can reduce you to zero hearts and kill you, while Poison always stops at half a heart. Wither also works on undead mobs, which Poison cannot hurt.

faq.q: How long does the potion of Decay last?
faq.a: Both the drinkable and splash versions apply Wither II for 40 seconds. The lingering potion cloud applies it for 10 seconds, which is still enough to finish most mobs.

name: How to Find Blackstone in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Blackstone generates only in the Nether: mine it in basalt deltas, dig below the lava sea level anywhere in the Nether (Y 5-31), loot bastion remnants, or barter with piglins for 8-16 blocks at a time.
steps: Enter the Nether with at least an iron pickaxe (blackstone drops only with a pickaxe; any tier works).
Easiest bulk source: find a basalt deltas biome, the grey ash-filled one. Blackstone is everywhere there, mixed with basalt.
In other Nether biomes, dig underground: blackstone ore blobs replace netherrack up to Y-level 31 (36 in Bedrock), including below the lava sea, so tunnel carefully.
Raid a bastion remnant: large parts of its structure are blackstone and polished blackstone, free for the taking if you survive the piglin brutes.
No mining trip needed: barter gold ingots with piglins. Each ingot has about an 8.5% chance of returning 8-16 blackstone.
Use it like cobblestone: blackstone crafts stone tools, furnaces and brewing stands, and smelts into polished blackstone variants for building.
materials: Fire Resistance potion recommended for digging near lava
editionNote: Blackstone generates in all Nether biomes in both editions, but the ore blobs reach Y 31 in Java and Y 36 in Bedrock, and the giant basalt deltas blobs are Java-only. One quirk shared by both: blackstone works as a cobblestone substitute for tools, furnaces and brewing stands, but it cannot craft dispensers, droppers, pistons or other mechanical blocks.

faq.q: What Y-level is blackstone most common?
faq.a: Blackstone ore blobs generate between Y 5 and Y 31 (Y 36 in Bedrock) in every Nether biome, so digging just under the lava sea level is the classic spot. In basalt deltas it generates at all heights right on the surface.

faq.q: Can blackstone replace cobblestone in every recipe?
faq.a: Almost. It makes stone tools, furnaces and brewing stands, and repairs stone tools in an anvil, but it cannot be used for dispensers, droppers, pistons or the other mechanical blocks that require cobblestone.

faq.q: What is gilded blackstone?
faq.a: Gilded blackstone is a rare variant found in bastion remnants with gold flecks embedded. Mining it without Silk Touch usually drops gold nuggets instead of the block, and piglins get angry when you take it.

name: How to Make Packed Mud in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft packed mud by combining 1 mud block and 1 wheat anywhere in the crafting grid. Four packed mud then craft into 4 mud bricks, the base of the mud brick building set.
steps: Get mud: use a water bottle on a dirt block (coarse dirt and rooted dirt work too) to convert it, or dig it up in a mangrove swamp.
Get wheat: grow it from seeds on farmland, or loot it from village farms and chests.
Open your inventory crafting grid or a crafting table.
Place 1 mud and 1 wheat anywhere in the grid; the recipe is shapeless.
Take the packed mud. It drops itself even when broken by hand, though a pickaxe is faster.
To build with it, craft 4 packed mud into 4 mud bricks, then make mud brick stairs, slabs and walls.
You can also find ready-made packed mud generating naturally in trail ruins.
materials: 1 mud (water bottle + dirt, or mined in mangrove swamps)
editionNote: The packed mud recipe is identical in Java and Bedrock and was added in 1.19 alongside mangrove swamps. In both editions it also generates as part of trail ruins, so archaeology players usually have some lying around. Wheat is the only organic binder that works; hay bales or other crops cannot substitute it.

faq.q: What is packed mud used for?
faq.a: Mainly to craft mud bricks: 4 packed mud make 4 mud bricks, which then become stairs, slabs and walls. It is also a nice textured building block on its own.

faq.q: How do I get mud without finding a mangrove swamp?
faq.a: Point a water bottle at any dirt, coarse dirt or rooted dirt block and use it: the block turns into mud and you get the empty glass bottle back. Works in any biome, any dimension.

faq.q: Is the packed mud recipe shapeless?
faq.a: Yes. The mud and the wheat can sit anywhere in the crafting grid, so you can craft it in your 2x2 inventory grid without a crafting table.

name: How to Find Azalea in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Azalea bushes grow naturally on moss blocks inside lush caves. On the surface, spot an azalea tree (an oak-like tree with azalea leaves) and dig down through its rooted dirt to reach the lush cave below.
steps: Explore cave openings until you find a lush cave: look for glow berries lighting the dark, moss floors, clay pools and vines.
Pick azalea bushes straight off the moss blocks; the flowering variant with pink blossoms grows there too.
Or hunt from the surface: wander until you see an azalea tree, a single oak-like tree with pale azalea leaves mixed in.

Dig a staircase beside the azalea tree, checking for rooted dirt scattered beneath it. Natural roots occupy a 5x5 cross-section centred on the tree and lead toward the lush cave below; do not dig straight beneath your feet.
To farm azalea at home, use bone meal on a moss block: each block in the surrounding area has a 15% chance to sprout an azalea or flowering azalea.
Place azalea on dirt, grass, moss, mud, clay, farmland or rooted dirt, and use bone meal on the bush for a 45% chance to grow your own azalea tree.
materials: Bone meal (optional, to farm or grow azalea trees)
Torches and food for lush cave exploring
editionNote: Azalea behaves the same in Java and Bedrock: it generates in lush caves, grows from bone-mealed moss, and turns into an azalea tree with bone meal at a 45% chance as long as there is a clear 3x5x3 space above it. Leftover azalea composts well too: 65% chance to raise the composter level.

faq.q: What does an azalea tree mean on the surface?
faq.a: It points to a lush cave below. Explore beneath the tree with a safe staircase and follow the rooted dirt toward the cave. The roots can be scattered across a 5x5 area, not one uninterrupted column.

faq.q: Does azalea grow into a tree on its own?
faq.a: No. Unlike saplings, azalea never grows by itself: you have to use bone meal on the bush, and even then it only has a 45% chance per attempt. It needs 3x5x3 blocks of clear space above it.

faq.q: What is the difference between azalea and flowering azalea?
faq.a: They are separate blocks with the same uses, but the flowering variant has pink blossoms, works as a flower for bees, and can breed bees. Both grow on moss in lush caves and come from bone-mealed moss blocks.

name: How to Get Deepslate in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Mine below Y=0 in the Overworld with any pickaxe. An ordinary pickaxe drops cobbled deepslate; Silk Touch drops the original deepslate block. You can also smelt cobbled deepslate in a furnace to get deepslate.
steps: Head underground in the Overworld and check your Y coordinate. Deepslate replaces stone in the transition from Y=8 to Y=0 and dominates below Y=0.
Make a staircase down rather than digging straight beneath your feet. Bring light, food and spare pickaxes for the return trip.
Mine the dark grey rock with a pickaxe. Even a wooden pickaxe works for the base block, but ores embedded in it can need a higher tool tier.
Choose the drop you need: without Silk Touch you get cobbled deepslate; with Silk Touch you get deepslate itself.
If you already have cobbled deepslate, put it in a furnace with fuel to smelt it into deepslate.
For building variants, use a stonecutter. Current 26.x versions accept regular deepslate as well as cobbled deepslate for the decorative family.
materials: Any pickaxe (better tiers speed up gathering)
Silk Touch pickaxe or furnace and fuel for regular deepslate
Torches, food and blocks for a safe staircase
editionNote: The mining drops and smelting route work in Java and Bedrock. Regular deepslate became a stonecutter input in Java 26.1 and Bedrock 26.10; on older versions, use cobbled deepslate instead. Deepslate takes twice as long to mine as stone with the same tool.

faq.q: What is the difference between deepslate and cobbled deepslate?
faq.a: Deepslate is the natural, directional rock block. Cobbled deepslate is its rough mining drop when you do not use Silk Touch. Smelting turns the cobbled block back into deepslate.

faq.q: Can a wooden pickaxe mine deepslate?
faq.a: Yes, a wooden pickaxe can harvest the base deepslate block. That does not mean it can harvest every deepslate ore: the ore still has its own required pickaxe tier.

faq.q: Can I turn regular deepslate into bricks or tiles?
faq.a: In current versions, use the stonecutter. Java 26.1 and Bedrock 26.10 added regular deepslate as an input for cobbled and decorative variants. On earlier versions, begin with cobbled deepslate.

name: How to Get Milk in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Use an empty bucket on a cow, mooshroom or goat to get a milk bucket. Hold the use button to drink it and clear all your status effects, including helpful potion effects. Drinking returns the empty bucket.
steps: Bring an empty bucket. Milk is collected from an animal, not crafted or scooped from a placed liquid.
Find a cow, mooshroom or goat and select the empty bucket in your hotbar.
Use the bucket on the animal to fill it with milk.
To clear status effects, select the milk bucket and hold use until you finish drinking.
Check which effects you want to keep before drinking: milk removes positive effects such as Strength and Fire Resistance as well as harmful effects.
Keep the returned empty bucket for the next refill, or save milk buckets as ingredients for cake.
editionNote: The basic collection and effect-clearing steps work in Java and Bedrock. Beacon and conduit effects can return while you remain in range: almost immediately in Bedrock and after a few seconds in Java. Milk is not an extinguisher and does not put out fire.

faq.q: Does milk remove good potion effects too?
faq.a: Yes. It clears all status effects, so drinking it also removes buffs such as Strength, Speed and Fire Resistance. Check your active effects before using it.

faq.q: Can I place milk like water?
faq.a: No. Milk buckets are drinks and crafting ingredients, not placeable fluid blocks. Hold use to drink one, or use it in a recipe such as cake.

faq.q: Why did Mining Fatigue or another effect come back?
faq.a: Milk clears your current effects but does not remove the source. If a mob or an area effect applies it again, you can be affected again.

faq.q: Does milk stop a player from burning?
faq.a: No. Burning is not a status effect. Use water or another safe way to extinguish the fire; milk can even remove an existing Fire Resistance effect.

name: How to Get a Bee Nest in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Find a bee nest on a tree and break it with a Silk Touch tool to collect it intact. Meadows are a useful starting point because their naturally generated trees have a 100% nest chance. You can also grow oak, birch or cherry saplings near flowers for a 5% chance per tree.
steps: Look for trees in a meadow. Each naturally generated tree there has a bee nest, but meadows can have few trees; plains, sunflower plains and cherry groves are alternatives.
Bring a tool enchanted with Silk Touch before breaking the nest. Without it the nest drops nothing and bees can become angry.
If you want to move the bees too, wait until they have returned inside, then collect the nest with Silk Touch. Bees already inside stay in the dropped nest.
To generate nests at home, plant oak, birch or cherry saplings with a flower within two blocks, including diagonally, on the same Y level.
Grow the sapling, naturally or with bone meal, and check the tree. Each qualifying tree has a 5% chance to generate a nest containing two or three bees; repeat with more saplings if it fails.

After placing the nest, leave its entrance accessible and provide flowers. Harvest a full nest with shears for three honeycombs or a glass bottle for honey; use unobstructed campfire smoke below it to avoid angering the bees.
materials: A tool with Silk Touch to collect the nest
Oak, birch or cherry saplings and flowers for the renewable route
Bone meal (optional, to grow trees faster)
Campfire plus shears or glass bottles for harvesting
editionNote: The flower-and-sapling method works in both editions. Natural flower forest trees have a 2% nest chance in Java and 3% in Bedrock. A carpet above a campfire still lets its smoke calm bees in Java, but blocks that calming effect in Bedrock. Campfire smoke is for harvesting; use Silk Touch to move the nest.

faq.q: Can I craft a bee nest?
faq.a: No. Bee nests come from trees, including newly grown trees under the right conditions. Beehives are the craftable alternative, made with planks and honeycombs.

faq.q: Does Silk Touch keep the bees inside?
faq.a: Yes, any bees inside the nest remain inside the dropped block. Bees outside are not collected with it. Wait until they are home if you want to move the whole colony.

faq.q: Why did my sapling not make a bee nest?
faq.a: For oak, birch and cherry, the flower must be within two blocks on the same Y level. Even with the right setup, the chance is only 5% per tree, so most attempts will not create a nest.

faq.q: Can a mangrove tree generate a bee nest?
faq.a: Yes. A mangrove grown from a propagule has a 1% chance to generate a nest with two or three bees, without needing a flower nearby.

name: How to Make Planks in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Put one log or Nether stem in any crafting slot to get four matching planks. No crafting table is needed. Bamboo is the exception: one block of bamboo makes two bamboo planks.
steps: Break a tree log by hand or use an axe to gather it faster. For crimson or warped planks, collect the corresponding huge fungus stem in the Nether.
Open your inventory crafting grid and put one log or stem in any slot. The recipe is shapeless and works in the small 2x2 grid.
Take the four matching planks. Stripped logs, wood blocks, stripped wood, stems and hyphae also work for their matching wood type.
For bamboo planks, first obtain a block of bamboo, then put that block in a crafting slot. Each block gives two planks, not four; stripped bamboo blocks work too.
Use four planks in a square to make a crafting table and unlock the larger 3x3 grid.
Keep the wood types consistent when making wood-specific blocks such as doors, stairs and slabs. Generic recipes such as sticks and a crafting table allow mixed types.
materials: One log or stem for four planks
Or one block of bamboo for two bamboo planks
editionNote: The basic recipe works in Java and Bedrock. Available wood types depend on your version. Crimson and warped planks do not burn, cannot fuel a furnace and cannot make boats. Overworld planks can fuel a furnace, smelting 1.5 items per plank.

faq.q: Why can I not make planks from a stick?
faq.a: Sticks cannot be turned back into planks. Start with a log, wood block, stem, hyphae or block of bamboo.

faq.q: Do I need a crafting table to make planks?
faq.a: No. Put the raw wood block in any slot of your inventory crafting grid. One log or stem makes four matching planks.

faq.q: Can I mix different plank types in a recipe?
faq.a: For generic items such as sticks and a crafting table, yes. Wood-specific products such as doors, stairs, slabs and fences require matching planks.

faq.q: Why does bamboo give only two planks?
faq.a: That is the bamboo recipe: one block of bamboo or stripped bamboo yields two bamboo planks. Ordinary logs and Nether stems yield four.

name: How to Make a Bowl in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Use three planks in a crafting table to make four bowls. Place two planks at the left and right of one row, then the third in the middle of the row below, making a V shape.
steps: Get three planks of any type; mixed plank types are allowed.
Open a crafting table. The recipe needs three columns, so it does not fit in the inventory 2x2 grid.
Place a plank in the middle-left slot, one in the middle-right slot and one in the bottom-middle slot. Leave the centre empty.
Take all four bowls from the output. This is a shaped recipe, not three planks placed anywhere.
Use bowls in mushroom stew, rabbit stew, beetroot soup or suspicious stew recipes. You can also use an empty bowl directly on a red mooshroom to get mushroom stew.
After eating a bowl-based meal, save the empty bowl that is returned and use it again.
editionNote: The recipe gives four bowls in both Java and Bedrock. Empty bowls stack to 64. As furnace fuel, each bowl smelts half an item in Java or one item in Bedrock, so the fuel value differs by edition.

faq.q: How many bowls do three planks make?
faq.a: Four bowls. Put the three planks in a V shape in a crafting table.

faq.q: Can I use Nether planks for a bowl?
faq.a: Yes. Any plank type works, and you can mix types. Crimson and warped planks can be crafted into bowls even though the planks themselves cannot fuel a furnace.

faq.q: Do bowls disappear when I eat stew?
faq.a: No. Eating the meal leaves an empty bowl, which you can reuse.

faq.q: Can I make bowls in the inventory crafting grid?
faq.a: No. The shaped recipe is three slots wide, so you need the crafting table 3x3 grid.

name: How to Get Rooted Dirt in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Dig beneath an azalea tree to find rooted dirt leading toward a lush cave. It drops itself without Silk Touch, and a shovel gathers it fastest. For a renewable source, grow an azalea tree with bone meal on a suitable ground block.
steps: Look for an azalea tree on the surface. Its oak-like trunk and azalea leaves mark a route toward a lush cave.

Dig a staircase beside the trunk and inspect the blocks below. Rooted dirt replaces scattered blocks in a 5x5 area centred on the tree down toward the lush cave; it is not necessarily one solid column.
Break the rooted dirt by hand or with a tool. A shovel is fastest and Silk Touch is not needed.
For a renewable supply, place an azalea or flowering azalea on dirt, coarse dirt, mud, muddy mangrove roots, clay or moss and use bone meal to grow a tree.
When the tree grows, the block under its trunk becomes rooted dirt. Collect that block and repeat with another bush and a suitable ground block.
For hanging roots, leave space underneath a rooted dirt block and apply bone meal. Alternatively, use a hoe on it to get a hanging roots item and turn the block into ordinary dirt.
materials: Azalea or flowering azalea and bone meal for renewable rooted dirt
A suitable ground block for growing the tree
editionNote: The basic gathering and azalea-tree method work in Java and Bedrock. Rooted dirt does not need Silk Touch. Grass and mycelium cannot spread onto it. Using a water bottle converts it into mud, while a hoe converts it into dirt and drops hanging roots.

faq.q: Can I craft rooted dirt?
faq.a: There is no crafting-grid recipe. Find it below natural azalea trees or create it by growing an azalea tree with bone meal on a suitable ground block.

faq.q: Do I need Silk Touch to collect rooted dirt?
faq.a: No. It drops itself when broken with any tool or by hand. Use a shovel to gather it faster.

faq.q: Does every azalea tree create a long root column?
faq.a: No. Natural trees generate rooted dirt down toward lush caves. A tree you grow creates a single rooted dirt block beneath its trunk, not a whole underground column.

faq.q: How do I get hanging roots from rooted dirt?
faq.a: Use bone meal on the block with free space below to grow hanging roots. Using a hoe also drops a hanging roots item while converting the rooted dirt to normal dirt.

name: How to Make Coarse Dirt in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Combine two dirt and two gravel in a checkerboard pattern to craft four coarse dirt. It drops itself without Silk Touch. Grass and mycelium cannot spread onto it, making it useful for permanent dirt paths and rough landscaping.
steps: Collect two ordinary dirt blocks and two gravel blocks.
Open the inventory crafting grid or a crafting table. Arrange dirt and gravel in a 2x2 checkerboard: dirt/gravel on one row, gravel/dirt on the next.
Take four coarse dirt. This is a shaped recipe; placing the ingredients in a line will not work.
Place it for a rough soil surface that grass and mycelium will not take over. Saplings, flowers and several other plants can still grow on it under their usual conditions.
To turn it into normal dirt, leave air above it and use a hoe once. Use the hoe again if you want farmland.
Alternatively, use a shovel to make a dirt path, or use a water bottle to turn the block into mud.
materials: Hoe, shovel or water bottle (optional, for conversion)
editionNote: The checkerboard recipe and self-drop work in Java and Bedrock. A shovel is fastest for gathering placed coarse dirt, but any tool or your hand works. Unlike grass blocks, coarse dirt does not need Silk Touch to stay intact.

faq.q: Does grass spread onto coarse dirt?
faq.a: No. Neither grass nor mycelium spreads onto it. That makes coarse dirt useful when you want a permanent brown soil surface.

faq.q: Can I turn gravel into dirt with this recipe?
faq.a: Two dirt plus two gravel make four coarse dirt. Hoe those four blocks to get four normal dirt, turning the two gravel inputs into two extra dirt blocks.

faq.q: Do I need a crafting table?
faq.a: No. The 2x2 checkerboard fits in the inventory crafting grid.

faq.q: Why does a hoe not make farmland immediately?
faq.a: The first use turns coarse dirt into normal dirt, provided there is air above it. Use the hoe again on the dirt to make farmland.

name: How to Get Podzol in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Find podzol in an old growth taiga or bamboo jungle and collect it with Silk Touch. For a renewable supply, grow a large spruce tree from four spruce saplings in a 2x2 square; suitable ground around the tree becomes podzol.
steps: Search an old growth taiga or bamboo jungle for the brown, leaf-covered ground blocks.
Use a Silk Touch tool to collect podzol intact. A shovel is fastest; without Silk Touch you get ordinary dirt.
To make podzol at home, plant four spruce saplings in a 2x2 square on suitable ground with enough space for a large tree.
Let the tree grow or use bone meal. The large spruce converts nearby topmost dirt, grass, moss and other suitable ground blocks into podzol.
Collect the new podzol with Silk Touch and replant more large spruce trees as needed. Podzol does not spread on its own.
Use it to plant mushrooms even in bright light. To make farmland instead, use a shovel to turn podzol into dirt path before tilling the path with a hoe.
materials: Silk Touch tool (a shovel is fastest)
4 spruce saplings for the renewable method
Suitable ground and room for a large spruce tree
editionNote: Both editions support Silk Touch gathering and large-spruce generation. The exact ground-conversion footprint differs: Java can reach six blocks toward positive X/Z and five toward negative X/Z; Bedrock reaches at most five horizontally in each direction. Podzol does not become dirt merely because a solid block sits on top.

faq.q: Can I craft podzol?
faq.a: There is no crafting-grid recipe. Grow a large spruce tree to convert suitable ground into podzol, then collect it with Silk Touch.

faq.q: Why does podzol drop dirt?
faq.a: You mined it without Silk Touch. Any Silk Touch tool preserves the podzol block; a shovel is fastest.

faq.q: Does podzol spread like grass or mycelium?
faq.a: No. It does not spread to nearby dirt, and grass or mycelium cannot spread onto it.

faq.q: Can I grow mushrooms on podzol in daylight?
faq.a: Yes. Podzol allows mushrooms at any light level. Huge mushrooms still need the usual room to grow.

name: How to Get Mycelium in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Find mycelium in a mushroom fields biome and mine it with Silk Touch. Without Silk Touch it drops dirt. Place the collected block beside ordinary dirt with enough light and it can spread, giving you a renewable supply.
steps: Find a mushroom fields biome and look for the purple-grey ground beneath the mushrooms.
Collect at least one mycelium block with a Silk Touch tool. A shovel is fastest; mining by hand or without the enchantment gives dirt.
At your base, place the mycelium beside ordinary dirt. Coarse dirt, rooted dirt and podzol are not valid spread targets.
Keep light level at least nine above the source mycelium and at least four above the target dirt, with no light-blocking cover on the dirt.
Wait for random ticks to spread mycelium, then collect extra blocks with Silk Touch while leaving a source block to continue spreading.
Use the blocks for mushrooms and Nether fungi at any light level. Avoid covering your source with opaque blocks: mycelium can die and revert to dirt.
materials: Silk Touch tool (a shovel is fastest)
Access to a mushroom fields biome
Ordinary dirt and enough light for spreading
editionNote: The Silk Touch and spread methods work in Java and Bedrock. Mycelium cannot be tilled directly into farmland: first use a shovel to make dirt path, then a hoe. Sniffers cannot dig on mycelium, even though they can dig on some other soil blocks.

faq.q: Can I craft mycelium?
faq.a: No. Start with a block from mushroom fields collected using Silk Touch, then let it spread to ordinary dirt.

faq.q: Why is my mycelium not spreading?
faq.a: Check that the target is ordinary dirt, the source has light level nine or higher above it, the target has at least four, and the target has no light-blocking cover. Spreading also needs random ticks, so it is not instant.

faq.q: Does mycelium make any biome safe from monsters?
faq.a: The block does not turn your location into mushroom fields. The biome and the ground block are separate, so replacing your base floor with mycelium does not give it mushroom-fields spawning rules.

faq.q: Why did mycelium turn into dirt?
faq.a: Covering it with an opaque block can kill it when it receives a random tick. Keep your source exposed and sufficiently lit if you want it to keep spreading.

name: How to Dry a Sponge in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Place a wet sponge in the Nether to dry it instantly, or smelt it in a furnace with fuel. A dry sponge can absorb water again; a wet sponge cannot. In Bedrock, dry Overworld biomes also dry wet sponges after a few minutes.
steps: Collect your wet sponges after draining water. Any tool or your hand works; a hoe is fastest.
For instant drying without fuel, take the wet sponges to the Nether and place each one. It turns into a dry sponge with a puff of steam.
Break the dry sponges and return to your water-draining project.
If you prefer to stay in the Overworld, put a wet sponge in the furnace input and add fuel. Take the dry sponge from the output.
To recover water too, make sure an empty bucket is in the fuel slot when drying finishes. This works after the furnace has already consumed fuel and is still burning.
Reuse the dry sponge near water. It becomes wet again after absorbing water, so repeat the drying process as needed.
materials: Nether access, or a furnace and fuel
editionNote: Nether drying and furnace drying work in Java and Bedrock. Bedrock also dries a placed wet sponge after a few minutes in a dry Overworld biome; this is not a Java mechanic. Dropped sponge items do not absorb water: place the block.

faq.q: What is the fastest way to dry many wet sponges?
faq.a: Place them in the Nether, where each wet sponge dries instantly without using fuel. Then collect them with a hoe or another tool.

faq.q: Can a wet sponge absorb more water?
faq.a: No. Dry it first. Once a dry sponge absorbs water it becomes wet and stops absorbing until you dry it again.

faq.q: Why does my wet sponge not dry in a desert?
faq.a: Passive drying in dry Overworld biomes is a Bedrock feature. In Java, use a furnace or place the wet sponge in the Nether.

faq.q: Does a sponge remove lava?
faq.a: No. Sponges absorb water, not lava.

name: How to Get Hanging Roots in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Use bone meal on rooted dirt with empty space underneath to grow hanging roots, then collect them with shears. You can also use a hoe on rooted dirt to get a hanging roots item directly while turning the block into ordinary dirt.
steps: Get rooted dirt from beneath a natural azalea tree or by growing an azalea tree with bone meal.
Place rooted dirt above an empty space where the hanging roots can appear.
Use bone meal on the rooted dirt to grow hanging roots underneath.
Use shears to collect the roots. Breaking them by hand destroys them without giving you the item.
For a second collection method, use a hoe on rooted dirt: it turns into dirt and drops a hanging roots item, without needing shears.
Place your collected hanging roots on the underside of a block for decoration. They cannot be placed on a block's top or side.
materials: Bone meal and shears for growing and harvesting
Or a hoe to get the item directly
editionNote: Shears work in Java and Bedrock. Bedrock also lets any Silk Touch tool collect hanging roots; do not rely on that route in Java. Composting a hanging roots item has a 30% chance to raise the composter level.

faq.q: Why did my hanging roots drop nothing?
faq.a: Ordinary tools and your hand do not collect them. Use shears, or use a Silk Touch tool in Bedrock. Hoeing rooted dirt is a separate way to get the item.

faq.q: Can I grow hanging roots without a lush cave?
faq.a: Yes. Put rooted dirt above a free space and apply bone meal anywhere you want to build.

faq.q: Does a hoe make farmland from rooted dirt?
faq.a: The first use turns rooted dirt into ordinary dirt and drops hanging roots. It does not immediately make farmland.

faq.q: Where can I place hanging roots?
faq.a: Only on the underside of a block. They are a hanging decoration, not a plant for the top surface.

name: How to Get Nylium in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Mine crimson nylium in a crimson forest or warped nylium in a warped forest with a Silk Touch pickaxe. To make more, place netherrack beside existing nylium, leave air above the netherrack and use bone meal on the netherrack.
steps: Find the matching Nether forest: crimson nylium is the red ground in crimson forests; warped nylium is the blue-green ground in warped forests.
Bring a pickaxe with Silk Touch. A normal pickaxe gives netherrack, and breaking nylium without a pickaxe gives nothing.
Collect at least one block of the type you want and place it beside netherrack at your base.
Leave air above the netherrack and apply bone meal to that netherrack block, not the nylium. It converts to the nearby nylium type.
Keep crimson and warped seed blocks separate if you need one colour: when both are nearby, either type can be chosen with an equal chance.

For huge fungi, plant crimson fungus on crimson nylium or warped fungus on warped nylium and apply bone meal. Avoid leaving opaque blocks above your nylium, which can cause it to decay into netherrack.
materials: Netherrack and bone meal for conversion
Existing crimson or warped nylium as the starting block
editionNote: Both editions allow netherrack conversion beside existing nylium. Making more nylium from mined netherrack is not the same as making its source fully renewable: the wiki identifies renewable portal-generated netherrack as a Bedrock-specific route. Nylium does not spread automatically like grass.

faq.q: Why does my nylium drop netherrack?
faq.a: Your pickaxe needs Silk Touch to preserve nylium. An ordinary pickaxe drops netherrack instead.

faq.q: Which block should receive the bone meal?
faq.a: Use it on the netherrack beside nylium, with air above. Bone meal on nylium itself grows Nether vegetation rather than being the same conversion step.

faq.q: Can warped fungus grow huge on crimson nylium?
faq.a: No. Match the fungus and ground: warped fungus needs warped nylium, and crimson fungus needs crimson nylium.

faq.q: Can nylium turn back into netherrack?
faq.a: Yes. An opaque block above it can make it decay when a random tick occurs. Keep your seed blocks uncovered.

name: How to Make a Snow Block in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Put four snowballs in a 2x2 square to craft one snow block. The recipe fits in your inventory crafting grid. Unlike thin snow layers, full snow blocks do not melt near ordinary light sources or in dry biomes.
steps: Collect snowballs with a shovel from snow. Breaking a full snow block with a shovel without Silk Touch gives four snowballs.
Open your inventory crafting grid or a crafting table.
Put one snowball in each slot of a 2x2 square and take the snow block.
Place full blocks for snowy builds where thin snow would melt. Snow blocks and powder snow are different blocks.
To collect a placed snow block intact, use Silk Touch. For snowballs, use a shovel without Silk Touch; breaking without a suitable tool can drop nothing.
For a snow golem, stack two snow blocks and place a carved pumpkin or jack o'lantern on top last.
materials: Silk Touch tool (optional, to collect intact snow blocks)
editionNote: The four-snowball recipe works in Java and Bedrock. Full snow blocks do not melt from nearby light-emitting blocks or dry biomes. This does not mean a snow golem is safe in every biome: the mob has its own temperature and water damage rules.

faq.q: Do I need a crafting table for snow blocks?
faq.a: No. Four snowballs in a 2x2 square fit in the inventory grid.

faq.q: Do snow blocks melt next to torches?
faq.a: No. Full snow blocks do not melt near light-emitting blocks. Thin snow layers have different melting rules.

faq.q: Is a snow block the same as powder snow?
faq.a: No. A snow block is a solid building block crafted from snowballs. Powder snow is a separate block with different collection and movement mechanics.

faq.q: How many snowballs do I need for a snow golem?
faq.a: Eight snowballs make the two snow blocks. You also need a carved pumpkin or jack o'lantern, placed last.

name: How to Get Basalt in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Mine basalt with any pickaxe in basalt deltas or soul sand valleys. To generate it at home, make lava flow into an empty space directly above soul soil and beside blue ice. Soul sand and ordinary ice are not substitutes.
steps: Find basalt in basalt deltas terrain or the tall pillars in soul sand valleys. Bring a pickaxe and watch for exposed lava.
Mine the basalt with any pickaxe. Other tools do not give the block.
For a generator, place soul soil under the intended output space and blue ice beside that space.
Arrange a lava source so lava flows into the output space. When flowing lava reaches the space above soul soil and adjacent to blue ice, it becomes basalt.
Mine the generated basalt with a pickaxe and allow more lava to flow into the space. Keep a safe standing position away from the lava.
Use a stonecutter to make polished basalt, or smelt basalt in a furnace to make smooth basalt. These are different decorative variants.
materials: Soul soil, blue ice and lava for a generator
Stonecutter or furnace and fuel (optional, for variants)
editionNote: The generator uses the same key ingredients in Java and Bedrock: flowing lava, soul soil below and blue ice beside the output. Basalt can be oriented like a log when placed. Polished basalt comes from stonecutting; smooth basalt comes from smelting.

faq.q: Why is my basalt generator not working?
faq.a: Check the output space, not just the lava source: it needs soul soil directly below and blue ice adjacent. Lava must flow into that space. Soul sand, regular ice and packed ice are not the required ingredients.

faq.q: Do I need Silk Touch for basalt?
faq.a: No. Any pickaxe drops basalt itself. A wooden pickaxe works for the base block.

faq.q: How do I make smooth basalt?
faq.a: Smelt basalt in a furnace with fuel. Using a stonecutter makes polished basalt instead.

faq.q: Can I generate basalt outside the Nether?
faq.a: Yes. The lava, soul soil and blue ice arrangement is not limited to the Nether biome.

name: How to Get Packed Ice in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Collect packed ice with a Silk Touch tool from ice spikes, frozen peaks or frozen-ocean icebergs. You can also fill a crafting table with nine regular ice blocks to make one packed ice. Packed ice does not melt near light sources.
steps: Look for packed ice in ice spikes, frozen peaks or the icebergs of a frozen ocean.
Use a Silk Touch tool to collect the block; a pickaxe is fastest. Without Silk Touch it drops nothing and does not become water.
For crafting, gather nine regular ice blocks with Silk Touch.
Fill all nine slots of a crafting table with ice to get one packed ice block.
Use packed ice for boat tracks or slippery surfaces that stay frozen near light sources.
If you need blue ice, combine nine packed ice in another full 3x3 crafting grid. Keep in mind that neither recipe can be reversed into its original blocks.
materials: Silk Touch tool (a pickaxe is fastest)
9 ice and a crafting table for each crafted packed ice
editionNote: Both editions support Silk Touch gathering and the nine-ice recipe. Packed ice is a solid block and does not melt near light sources. It can support mob spawning, so a packed-ice floor alone does not make a build spawn-proof.

faq.q: Can I mine packed ice without Silk Touch?
faq.a: You can break it, but it drops nothing. Use any tool with Silk Touch to collect it intact.

faq.q: Can I turn packed ice back into regular ice?
faq.a: No. The nine-ice crafting recipe is one-way; packed ice is not a reversible storage block.

faq.q: Does packed ice melt in the Nether?
faq.a: Packed ice does not melt near light sources and can be used for ice tracks in all three dimensions. It does not behave like regular ice that can turn into water.

faq.q: How much regular ice makes one blue ice?
faq.a: Using the crafting chain, nine ice make one packed ice and nine packed ice make one blue ice, so one blue ice costs 81 regular ice.

name: How to Get Magma Blocks in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Mine magma blocks with any pickaxe, or craft one from four magma cream in a 2x2 square. Look near Nether lava, in basalt deltas or below underwater bubble columns. Magma blocks pull water columns downward and can hurt you when you stand on them.
steps: Bring a pickaxe. Without one, breaking magma blocks gives no drop.
Look near Nether lava or in basalt deltas; underwater magma in the Overworld is another source, but watch for downward bubble columns.
Mine the block while standing on safe ground. Sneaking prevents magma-floor damage, but it does not make underwater exploration free of drowning risk.
For a crafting route, put four magma cream in a 2x2 square in your inventory or crafting table to get one magma block.
To make a downward water elevator, place the magma block beneath a column of water source blocks. Flowing water alone does not make the complete bubble column.
Keep a safe exit beside the bottom of the column. Do not assume carpet will protect you: thin blocks can still allow magma damage.
materials: Or 4 magma cream per crafted magma block
Water source blocks for a downward bubble column
editionNote: The crafting recipe and downward bubble column work in Java and Bedrock. Sneaking, Frost Walker or Fire Resistance can prevent magma-block damage. Magma blocks do not destroy dropped items or cook the animals they kill.

faq.q: Do I need Silk Touch for magma blocks?
faq.a: No. Any pickaxe drops the magma block intact.

faq.q: Does magma push me up or pull me down underwater?
faq.a: It creates a downward bubble column. Soul sand is the block used for an upward column.

faq.q: Does carpet stop magma damage?
faq.a: Do not rely on it. Thin blocks such as carpet do not prevent magma from damaging entities above them.

faq.q: Can I turn a magma block back into magma cream?
faq.a: The four-magma-cream recipe is not a reversible storage recipe. Gather magma cream separately if that is what you need.

name: How to Get Netherrack in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Mine the red rock that makes up most Nether terrain with any pickaxe. Netherrack drops itself without Silk Touch. You can also find patches around ruined portals in the Overworld, then smelt it into individual nether bricks.
steps: Enter the Nether through a portal and look for the common red netherrack terrain. Ruined portals in the Overworld can provide a small supply without a Nether trip.
Mine it with any pickaxe. Other tools or your hand do not give the block.
Watch your footing: netherrack is easy to break and can hide lava or an open drop behind it.
Use it as a cheap temporary building block, or put it in a furnace with fuel to get the nether brick item.
For nylium, place netherrack beside crimson or warped nylium with air above, then apply bone meal to the netherrack.
If you light its top with flint and steel, the fire burns indefinitely and rain does not put it out. Keep flammable builds away from that fire.
materials: Nether access or an Overworld ruined portal
Furnace and fuel (optional, for nether brick items)
editionNote: Mining and smelting work in Java and Bedrock. Bedrock can generate new netherrack with floating Nether portals, making it renewable; this is not the same as ordinary Java portal generation. Smelting gives a nether brick item, not a nether bricks building block.

faq.q: Can I mine netherrack with a wooden pickaxe?
faq.a: Yes. Any pickaxe harvests it, without needing Silk Touch.

faq.q: Can I get netherrack without entering the Nether?
faq.a: Look for a ruined portal in the Overworld. Netherrack generates around those structures.

faq.q: Why did smelting not give a nether bricks block?
faq.a: A furnace turns one netherrack into one nether brick item. The building block is a separate crafting recipe using those items.

faq.q: Does rain put out fire on netherrack?
faq.a: No. Fire on its top burns indefinitely and is not put out by rain. It can still spread to nearby flammable blocks.

name: How to Make Sandstone in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Put four sand in a 2x2 square to make one sandstone. Use four red sand instead for red sandstone. To make the smooth variant, smelt the matching sandstone in a furnace; stonecutting makes cut or chiseled variants, not smooth sandstone.
steps: Collect four sand for each sandstone block, or four red sand for each red sandstone. Keep the two recipes separate.
Open the inventory crafting grid or a crafting table. Fill a 2x2 square with the same sand type and collect one sandstone.
For a mining route, look beneath desert or beach sand for regular sandstone. Mine it with any pickaxe; other tools do not give the block.
Put sandstone in a furnace with fuel to make smooth sandstone. Red sandstone similarly smelts into smooth red sandstone.
Use a stonecutter on regular sandstone for cut sandstone, chiseled sandstone, slabs, stairs or walls. Use smooth sandstone as the input for smooth stairs and slabs.
Place sandstone where you need a solid sandy-looking build that does not fall under gravity. You cannot craft it back into sand.
materials: 4 sand or 4 red sand per block
Furnace and fuel for smooth sandstone
editionNote: The sand recipes and smelting routes work in Java and Bedrock. Regular sandstone generates under desert and beach sand and in structures such as desert pyramids. Red sandstone natural generation has edition-specific details, so crafting from red sand is the dependable route in both editions.

faq.q: How do I make smooth sandstone?
faq.a: Smelt regular sandstone in a furnace with fuel. Four sand make sandstone first, then the furnace makes it smooth. Red sandstone makes smooth red sandstone the same way.

faq.q: Is cut sandstone the same as smooth sandstone?
faq.a: No. They are separate blocks. A stonecutter makes cut sandstone from sandstone, while a furnace makes smooth sandstone.

faq.q: Can I turn sandstone back into sand?
faq.a: No. The four-sand recipe is one-way, so sandstone is not a reversible storage block.

faq.q: Does sandstone fall like sand?
faq.a: No. Regular, red and smooth sandstone are solid building blocks that are not affected by gravity.

name: How to Make a Quartz Block in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft four nether quartz in a 2x2 square to make one block of quartz. Smelt that block in a furnace for smooth quartz, or use a stonecutter for pillars, bricks and chiseled quartz. Quartz blocks cannot be crafted back into nether quartz.
steps: Collect four nether quartz for each block you need.
Put them in a 2x2 square in the inventory crafting grid or a crafting table and take one block of quartz.
For smooth quartz, put the block of quartz in a furnace with fuel. Smooth quartz is not the same block as ordinary quartz.
For decorative shapes, put an ordinary quartz block in a stonecutter: choose quartz pillar, quartz bricks, chiseled quartz, stairs or slabs.
Without a stonecutter, four quartz blocks in a 2x2 square give four quartz bricks; two quartz blocks stacked vertically give two quartz pillars.
Mine placed quartz blocks with any pickaxe. Keep spare nether quartz for redstone recipes, because you cannot unpack the block back into its ingredients.
materials: Furnace and fuel for smooth quartz
editionNote: The base 2x2 recipe and smelting work in Java and Bedrock. Java allows multiple ordinary quartz-block variants as inputs for crafting quartz stairs and slabs, while Bedrock uses the basic block of quartz. Using the basic block or a stonecutter avoids that recipe difference.

faq.q: Is smooth quartz made in a stonecutter?
faq.a: No. Smelt a block of quartz in a furnace to make smooth quartz. A stonecutter makes decorative variants such as pillars and chiseled quartz.

faq.q: Can I get nether quartz back from a quartz block?
faq.a: No. It is not a reversible mineral-storage block.

faq.q: Do I need Silk Touch to mine quartz blocks?
faq.a: No. Any pickaxe collects a placed quartz block; mining without a pickaxe gives nothing.

name: How to Make End Stone Bricks in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Put four end stone in a 2x2 square to craft four end stone bricks. A stonecutter also turns one end stone into one end stone bricks block. Mine them with any pickaxe, and do not assume they are dragon-proof like raw end stone.
steps: Gather end stone and mine it with a pickaxe, or collect existing end stone bricks from an End city or End ship.
For the crafting recipe, arrange four end stone in a 2x2 square in your inventory or crafting table.
Take four end stone bricks. The conversion keeps the same number of blocks.
For smaller quantities, put one end stone in a stonecutter and select end stone bricks.
Put the bricks in the stonecutter to make stairs, walls or two slabs per block.
Use a pickaxe when changing your build. Keep raw end stone where resistance to the ender dragon matters: the dragon can destroy the brick variant.
materials: 4 end stone for 4 end stone bricks
editionNote: The 2x2 recipe and stonecutter route work in Java and Bedrock. End stone bricks are decorative and can be destroyed by the ender dragon, unlike raw end stone. Any pickaxe collects the bricks; other tools give no drop.

faq.q: Do end stone bricks need a furnace?
faq.a: No. Use the 2x2 crafting recipe or a stonecutter. Smelting is not the conversion route.

faq.q: Can a wooden pickaxe mine end stone bricks?
faq.a: Yes. Any pickaxe collects the block.

faq.q: Are end stone bricks immune to the ender dragon?
faq.a: No. The dragon can destroy end stone bricks even though raw end stone resists its block destruction.

name: How to Make Nether Bricks in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Smelt netherrack into nether brick items, then craft four items in a 2x2 square for one nether bricks block. For red nether bricks, combine two nether brick items and two nether wart in a diagonal 2x2 pattern. Smelting the ordinary block makes cracked nether bricks.
steps: Mine netherrack and put it in a furnace with fuel. Each netherrack makes one nether brick item.
Arrange four nether brick items in a 2x2 square in the inventory or crafting table to get one nether bricks block.
For red nether bricks, put two brick items on one diagonal of a 2x2 square and two nether wart on the other diagonal. This makes one red block.
For cracked nether bricks, smelt an ordinary nether bricks block in a furnace. Do not confuse this with smelting netherrack into the item.
Use a stonecutter with ordinary nether bricks for stairs, slabs, walls or the chiseled variant. Two nether brick slabs stacked vertically also craft one chiseled block.
Collect placed nether bricks with any pickaxe. Nether fortresses offer an alternative source of the ordinary blocks.
materials: 4 netherrack and furnace fuel per ordinary block
2 nether brick items + 2 nether wart per red block
editionNote: The basic, red and cracked recipes work in Java and Bedrock. Any pickaxe collects the blocks; mining without one gives nothing. Nether brick items and nether bricks blocks are different ingredients.

faq.q: Why does my nether bricks recipe not work?
faq.a: Use four nether brick items, not four netherrack. Smelt the netherrack first.

faq.q: Can I dye nether bricks red?
faq.a: No. Craft the red variant with two nether brick items and two nether wart in a diagonal 2x2 pattern.

faq.q: Are cracked nether bricks made in a stonecutter?
faq.a: No. Smelt the ordinary nether bricks block in a furnace.

name: How to Get Andesite in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Mine andesite in the Overworld with any pickaxe, or craft one diorite and one cobblestone into two andesite. Four andesite in a 2x2 square make four polished andesite. A stonecutter also makes polished blocks and building shapes.
steps: Look for gray, mottled andesite patches among stone in the Overworld.
Mine the blocks with any pickaxe. Silk Touch is not required, and mining without a pickaxe gives nothing.
If you have diorite, combine one diorite with one cobblestone in the crafting grid to get two andesite.
For polished andesite, arrange four ordinary andesite in a 2x2 square and take four polished blocks.
A stonecutter can convert one andesite into one polished andesite, avoiding batches of four.
Use the stonecutter for stairs or two slabs per block. Ordinary andesite also makes walls; polished andesite has stairs and slabs but no wall variant.
editionNote: Mining, the diorite-plus-cobblestone recipe, polishing and stonecutting work in Java and Bedrock. No furnace is needed. Ordinary andesite has a wall variant; polished andesite does not.

faq.q: Do I need Silk Touch for andesite?
faq.a: No. Any pickaxe drops the andesite block.

faq.q: How do I make polished andesite?
faq.a: Craft four andesite in a 2x2 square for four polished blocks, or cut a single andesite in a stonecutter.

faq.q: Can I smelt cobblestone into andesite?
faq.a: No. Smelting cobblestone makes stone. Craft andesite from diorite and cobblestone instead.

name: How to Get Diorite in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Mine diorite in the Overworld with any pickaxe, or craft two cobblestone and two nether quartz in an alternating 2x2 pattern for two diorite. Four diorite in a 2x2 square make four polished diorite; a stonecutter can polish one block at a time.
steps: Look for white and gray speckled diorite patches among stone in the Overworld.
Mine the diorite with any pickaxe. Silk Touch is not needed; breaking it without a pickaxe gives no drop.
For the crafting route, arrange two cobblestone on one diagonal and two nether quartz on the other diagonal of a 2x2 square. Take two diorite.
Arrange four diorite in a 2x2 square to craft four polished diorite. No furnace or fuel is required.
For a single polished block, put one diorite in a stonecutter and choose polished diorite.
Use the stonecutter to make stairs or two slabs per block. Ordinary diorite also makes walls; polished diorite has no wall variant.
editionNote: The mining, crafting and polishing routes work in Java and Bedrock. Both ordinary and polished diorite need a pickaxe to drop. Polishing is crafting or stonecutting, not smelting.

faq.q: Do I need Silk Touch to collect diorite?
faq.a: No. Any pickaxe collects the block without Silk Touch.

faq.q: Can I make polished diorite in a furnace?
faq.a: No. Craft four diorite in a 2x2 square for four polished blocks, or convert one block in a stonecutter.

faq.q: What can I make with spare diorite?
faq.a: Combine one diorite with one cobblestone for two andesite, or with one nether quartz for one granite.

name: How to Get Granite in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Mine granite in the Overworld with any pickaxe, or combine one diorite and one nether quartz for one granite. Craft four granite in a 2x2 square for four polished granite, or use a stonecutter to polish individual blocks.

faq.a: No. One diorite and one nether quartz make one granite. The four-block polishing recipe gives four polished granite.

name: How to Make Mossy Cobblestone in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Combine one cobblestone block with one vine or one moss block in a crafting grid to make one mossy cobblestone block. Use a moss block, not moss carpet. A stonecutter turns the finished block into stairs, slabs or walls.
steps: Gather cobblestone for the base ingredient.
Get vines or moss blocks. Either is a valid second ingredient; you do not need both.
Place one cobblestone and one vine or moss block anywhere in the inventory crafting grid or a crafting table.
Take one mossy cobblestone block. Repeat for each block you need.
To make stairs, slabs or walls, put the finished mossy block in a stonecutter. Each block gives one stair, one wall or two slabs.
Use a pickaxe to collect placed blocks. The stonecutter shapes mossy blocks but does not add moss to ordinary cobblestone.
materials: 1 vine OR 1 moss block per output block
editionNote: The vine and moss-block recipes work in current Java and Bedrock. The recipe is shapeless, so ingredient positions do not matter. Use the ordinary moss block rather than moss carpet.

faq.q: Can a stonecutter make mossy cobblestone from cobblestone?
faq.a: No. Craft the mossy block first, then use the stonecutter for stairs, slabs or walls.

name: How to Make Polished Blackstone in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft four blackstone in a 2x2 square for four polished blackstone. Four polished blocks in another 2x2 square make four polished blackstone bricks. A stonecutter can make either variant directly from one blackstone; smelt the brick variant for cracked bricks.

editionNote: The crafting, stonecutting and cracked-brick smelting routes work in Java and Bedrock. Polished blackstone, polished blackstone bricks and chiseled polished blackstone are separate blocks. Use the recipe book or stonecutter labels to select the right one.

faq.a: No. Craft four blackstone in a 2x2 square or use a stonecutter. The furnace makes cracked bricks from the brick variant.

faq.q: Can the stonecutter skip the polishing step?

faq.q: Do I lose blocks when crafting polished blackstone?

name: How to Make Deepslate Bricks and Tiles in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft four cobbled deepslate in a 2x2 square for four polished deepslate, then four polished blocks in 2x2 for four deepslate bricks. Another 2x2 of bricks gives four deepslate tiles. A stonecutter makes bricks or tiles directly from cobbled deepslate.

Arrange four polished deepslate in a 2x2 square to make four deepslate bricks.
For deepslate tiles, arrange four deepslate bricks in another 2x2 square. This gives four tile blocks.
For a shorter route, put one cobbled deepslate in a stonecutter and choose one deepslate bricks or one deepslate tiles block directly.
Smelt deepslate bricks or deepslate tiles in a furnace with fuel for their matching cracked variant.

faq.q: Do the 2x2 recipes reduce my block count?

name: How to Make Tuff Bricks in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Craft four tuff in a 2x2 square for four polished tuff, then four polished tuff in 2x2 for four tuff bricks. A stonecutter turns one ordinary tuff directly into one tuff bricks block. Use two tuff brick slabs stacked vertically for chiseled tuff bricks.

Arrange four tuff in a 2x2 square in the inventory crafting grid or a crafting table. Take four polished tuff.
Arrange four polished tuff in a 2x2 square. Take four tuff bricks.
For single blocks or a shorter route, put one ordinary tuff in a stonecutter and choose tuff bricks directly. Polished tuff is also a valid input.
Use a stonecutter with tuff bricks to make one stair, one wall or two slabs per block.
For chiseled tuff bricks, stack two tuff brick slabs vertically in the crafting grid, or choose the chiseled brick variant in the stonecutter.
Mine placed tuff bricks with any pickaxe. No Silk Touch or furnace is needed.

faq.q: Do I need to smelt tuff for bricks?

name: How to Make Glazed Terracotta in Minecraft

name: How to Make Stained Glass in Minecraft

faq.a: The stained glass recipe is a batch recipe: put eight ordinary glass around one dye for eight stained glass.

faq.q: Why did my stained glass disappear when I broke it?
faq.a: Stained glass and stained panes drop nothing unless you use a Silk Touch tool.

name: How to Make Iron Bars in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Put six iron ingots in two full horizontal rows of a crafting table to make sixteen iron bars. Use ingots, not nuggets or raw iron. Any pickaxe collects placed bars, but you cannot smelt the bars back into ingots or nuggets.

name: How to Stop Phantoms in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Sleep in a bed. Phantoms spawn only at night or in thunderstorms, and only once you have gone 3 in-game days without sleeping in a bed or dying. One night in a bed resets the timer. You can also avoid them by staying under a roof or below Y=64, keeping tamed cats nearby, or turning off the spawn_phantoms game rule (doinsomnia in Bedrock).
steps: Sleep in a bed. Entering a bed resets the timer that phantoms depend on. Phantoms need at least 3 in-game days since you last slept in a bed or died, so one bed night every 3 days is enough.
Stay under cover. Phantoms only spawn when you are above sea level (Y=64) with open sky directly above you. A solid roof over your head stops new spawns, and so does working underground below Y=64.
Keep tamed cats close. Cats hiss at a phantom that is attacking a player, and phantoms try to stay at least 16 blocks away from cats.
Remember that phantoms spawn at night or during a thunderstorm, 20 to 34 blocks above you, and attack by diving from the sky. Fight them with a bow or sword when they dive.
If you use commands or a cheats-enabled world, turn them off with /gamerule spawn_phantoms false in Java Edition, or /gamerule doinsomnia false in Bedrock Edition.
In Java 26.3, a straw bed also stops phantoms from spawning, the same way a regular bed does.
materials: A roof or a base below Y=64
Cheats enabled, for the game rule (optional)
editionNote: The 3-day rule and the cat behavior work the same in Java and Bedrock. The game rule is named spawn_phantoms in Java Edition and doinsomnia in Bedrock Edition, and it needs cheats. In Bedrock, phantoms also keep away from ocelots. Phantoms are afraid of cats since Java 18w44a and Bedrock beta 1.8.0.8.
versions: Phantoms were added in Java Edition 1.13. The doInsomnia game rule arrived in Java 19w36a and Bedrock beta 1.6.0.6. Straw beds (Java 26.3, snapshot 3) also prevent phantoms from spawning.
