name: How to Make Charcoal in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Smelt any log or wood in a furnace with any fuel. Each log gives 1 charcoal and 0.15 XP. Charcoal burns as long as coal does and makes torches, soul torches, campfires and fire charges. You can also get 2 charcoal by breaking a campfire without Silk Touch.

Take the charcoal from the output slot. Each log makes 1 charcoal and gives 0.15 XP.
Craft with it: charcoal + stick makes 4 torches, and charcoal + stick + soul sand or soul soil makes 4 soul torches.
Make a campfire from a stick, charcoal and any log, or a fire charge from blaze powder, charcoal and gunpowder.

name: How to Set a World Border in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Run /worldborder set <distance> to make the border that wide (width and length in blocks), and /worldborder center <x> <z> to move its middle. It is Java Edition only and needs permission level 2. By default the border is 59,999,968 blocks wide and centered on 0, 0.
steps: Open chat as an operator (permission level 2, or cheats on in a single-player world).
Set the size: /worldborder set 2000 makes a 2000 x 2000 border. The distance is the width and length in blocks.
Center it: /worldborder center 0 0 moves the middle of the border. The default center is 0, 0.
Shrink or grow it slowly by adding a time in seconds: /worldborder set 500 600 changes the size over 600 seconds. The animation keeps running even if the game is paused.
Change it relative to the current size with /worldborder add, and read the current size with /worldborder get.
Tune the damage: /worldborder damage amount sets damage per second per block outside the buffer (default 0.2), and /worldborder damage buffer sets the safe distance (default 5 blocks).
Tune the warning: /worldborder warning distance (default 5 blocks) and /worldborder warning time (default 15 seconds) control when the screen tints red.
editionNote: The world border is exclusive to Java Edition. The command only affects the dimension where you run it, so run it in the Nether and the End too if you want a border there. Bedrock Edition has no /worldborder command.
versions: The default border is 29,999,984 blocks from the origin on each side (59,999,968 wide).

faq.q: What is the command for a world border?
faq.a: /worldborder set <distance> sets the width and length in blocks. Use /worldborder center <x> <z> to move it.

faq.q: Does the world border exist in Bedrock?
faq.a: No. The world border and the /worldborder command are exclusive to Java Edition.

faq.q: How big is the default world border?
faq.a: 29,999,984 blocks from the origin in each direction, so 59,999,968 blocks wide.

faq.q: Does a world border work in the Nether and the End?
faq.a: Each dimension has its own border. The command only affects the dimension you run it in.

faq.q: What happens outside the world border?
faq.a: Players outside it (except in Creative or Spectator mode) take constant damage once they are more than 5 blocks past the border, and they usually cannot interact with blocks or entities out there. Entities cannot spawn naturally outside it.

name: How to Get Cocoa Beans in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Break cocoa pods that grow on jungle logs in jungle and sparse jungle biomes. A fully grown pod drops 3 cocoa beans. Plant them on the side of any jungle log to farm more. In Bedrock Edition you can also fish in jungle biomes or find them in bonus chests.
steps: Travel to a jungle or sparse jungle biome and look for orange or green pods on the sides of jungle tree trunks. Pods only generate on naturally generated jungle logs, not on trees grown from saplings.
Break a fully grown (orange) pod. Any item works, but an axe is fastest. It drops 3 cocoa beans. Fortune does not increase the drop. Breaking a pod in its first two stages gives only 1 bean.
Plant a bean by placing it on the side of a jungle log, jungle wood, stripped jungle log or stripped jungle wood. The log does not need to be part of a tree.
Wait for it to grow. A pod has three stages (small green, bigger tan, large orange), and each random tick has a 20% chance to advance it, about 5 minutes 41 seconds per stage on average.
Harvest the orange pods and replant. This makes a steady farm from a few jungle logs.
Use the beans: brown dye, cookies, and as a dye for wool, collars, leather armor, beds, glass, terracotta, shulker boxes and candles.
editionNote: In Java Edition cocoa beans only come from naturally generated cocoa pods. In Bedrock Edition they also drop from fishing in jungle, bamboo jungle and sparse jungle biomes, and 40% of bonus chests contain 1-2 beans. In Bedrock, cocoa beans can stand in for brown dye in many recipes.

name: How to Get Gravel in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Dig gravel with a shovel from riverbeds, shallow ocean floors, stony shores and windswept gravelly hills, or from stone-level gravel pockets underground. It is renewable through piglin bartering. Silk Touch always drops the block; without it there is a 10% chance of flint instead.

quickAnswer: Use a honeycomb on the copper block (or craft the block with a honeycomb) to wax it. Waxed copper never oxidizes. Use an axe to remove wax first and then oxidation, one layer per use. Covering copper or keeping it away from water does not stop oxidation.
steps: Get honeycomb from beehives or bee nests with shears, or from a bee farm.
Right-click an unwaxed copper block with a honeycomb, or craft the block with a honeycomb, to turn it into its waxed variant. Waxed blocks look the same as unwaxed ones.
Wax each block you want to keep. Oxidation only uses random ticks, so you cannot slow it by covering the blocks or by keeping water away.
To remove wax, use an axe on the waxed block. The honeycomb is not returned.
To clean oxidation, use an axe on an exposed, weathered or oxidized copper block. Each use removes one layer, going back one stage at a time. The axe removes wax first, then oxidation.
A lightning strike on a non-waxed copper block removes all oxidation from it and may clean nearby blocks.
Oxidation goes through four stages: unoxidized, exposed, weathered and oxidized.
Remember that oxidation can change behavior: only unoxidized copper blocks craft back into copper ingots, and copper bulb light level drops with oxidation (15, 12, 8, 4).
editionNote: Oxidation is random-tick based in both editions. In Java Edition, groups of unwaxed copper blocks oxidize far more slowly than single blocks spaced at least 4 blocks apart, because nearby lower-oxidation blocks hold the others back.
versions: Waxing and axe scraping apply to all oxidizing copper blocks and to copper golems.

faq.a: Wax it with a honeycomb. Waxed copper never oxidizes.

faq.a: No. Oxidation relies only on random ticks, and covering copper with other blocks does not prevent it.

faq.a: No. The honeycomb is not returned.

name: How to Use Structure Blocks in Minecraft
quickAnswer: Get a structure block with /give @s minecraft:structure_block (or from the Operator Utilities tab in Java Creative), place it, and open it in Creative mode with permission level 2. Use Save mode to copy an area (up to 48x48x48 in Java, 64x384x64 in Bedrock) and Load mode to paste it back, with rotation if you want.

Open its screen. It only opens in Creative mode and with permission level 2 or higher.
Pick a mode: Save, Load, Corner or Data.

Save mode: type a structure name, set the relative position (offset) and size, and save. The maximum structure size is 48x48x48 in Java and 64x384x64 in Bedrock. In Java the origin must be at most 48 blocks away in all directions.
Load mode: enter the saved structure's name and place it. You can rotate it. In Java Edition, structures are searched in the world's generated/structures folder first, then in data packs.

Use Corner mode for automatic size calculation: place corner blocks at the opposite corner, then press Detect in the save block. Data mode is deprecated (replaced by the jigsaw block) and only works during natural generation of a few vanilla structures; in Java it is hidden unless you hold Alt while switching from Corner mode.
Use structure void blocks inside the area: they are ignored when the structure is saved, so the blocks already at that spot are kept when the structure is loaded.
editionNote: Limits differ by edition: 48x48x48 in Java and 64x384x64 in Bedrock. In Bedrock Edition only save-mode structure blocks are obtainable through the inventory commands, and saved structures can also be kept in memory or a separate file.
